docs.title: Vision
docs.summary: Simple for simple folk, an absolute unit for power users. Concretely, four people:
docs.semanticSummary: Founding product vision for Hoplight covering who it's for, the five pillars, what we are not, and the taste bar. It is the authority for product intent, not as-built implementation detail. Who it's for names four personas: the first-timer needing a five-minute fix, the multi-platform botmaker, the large-worldbook lore architect, and the archivist of uncarded RP logs. The five pillars require lossless multi-format conversion with escrowed platform fields, interview-driven creation, an honest offline Doctor with optional staged AI fixes, local-first privacy with no account or telemetry, and an agent that works on frontier and weak local models with user-chosen personas. What we are not rules out being a chat frontend, card host, community platform, or RoleCall-only funnel; every platform is first-class. The taste bar demands Table Read or Doctor output that beats skilled unaided work, with specific over generic, playable over poetic, and anti-slop as a core mechanic rather than marketing language.

anchors.summary: Defines four concrete user personas the product must serve without forcing power-user complexity on beginners. The first-timer found a broken Discord card and must succeed in under five minutes without reading docs. The botmaker publishes community cards and currently juggles multiple platform formats, token budgets, and slop avoidance by hand. The lore architect maintains roughly three-hundred-entry worldbooks and needs trigger debugging, consistency checks, and real version history. The archivist holds years of RP logs with characters that were never formalized as cards. The framing is simple for simple folk and powerful for advanced users.

States five non-negotiable product pillars. Every format must import and export losslessly with semantic round-trip equivalence and platform-specific fields held in escrow rather than dropped, aiming to be the reference implementation other tools test against. Creation is interview-driven with adaptive depth, quick-pick chips, freeform input, visible assembly, and temperament modes. The Doctor runs free offline deterministic checks for token waste, format errors, contradictions, and slop banks, while AI treatment is optional, staged, and approved fix by fix with plain-language proof. Local first means readable disk files, encrypted local keys, no account, no server, no telemetry, and a single executable as the whole product. The agent must run well on frontier models and acceptably on small local models, with user-chosen working styles such as collaborator, terse, detail-hound, challenger, or hype.

Explicit non-goals that bound the product. Hoplight is not a chat frontend; the Test Stage auditions content and does not replace SillyTavern or RoleCall as play hosts. It is not a card hosting site or community platform; files are the social layer and people share where they already gather. It is not a RoleCall funnel: lineage may be RC-branded, but every platform is a first-class export target, and favoritism toward RoleCall would lose SillyTavern users. Winning is defined as making the content, not hosting the show.

Sets the craft quality bar for generated or treated content. A card from the Table Read or treated by the Doctor should be visibly better than what a skilled human produces unaided in an hour. Preferences are specific over generic, playable over poetic, and every token must earn its place. Anti-slop is a core mechanic implemented through banks, detectors, and rewrite passes, not merely marketing language about quality.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.summary: Hoplight is a Bun and TypeScript application rooted in `src/`. The canonical engine is shared by three surfaces: the command-line interface, the loopback React Studio, and Kit's terminal interface. No surface owns a private format conversio
docs.semanticSummary: This page defines Hoplight's implemented architecture and the boundaries contributors must preserve. Source boundaries assign the shared engine to src/core, entity schemas to src/entities, drop-in adapters to src/formats, durable local storage to src/studio, sealed-script analysis to src/sandbox, the primary loopback React application to src/ui, Kit's agent loop to src/kit, and the command surface to src/cli.ts. Canonical model and formats explains the hub-and-spoke superset, original source escrow, sparse platform profiles, same-format re-projection, cross-format loss reports, and folder-discovered adapters. Storage and mutation describes the folder database, contained paths, atomic writes, revisions, pure previews, and verified durable application. The three surfaces are the scriptable hoplight CLI, the local desktop Studio with separately enabled remote access, and source-checkout Kit, all sharing one engine while Kit remains absent from release binaries until its build and smoke gates exist. Effects and trust boundaries require fail-closed parsing, sealed imported scripts, deliberate network paths, and encrypted provider credentials that never enter content or model-visible records. Kit checks the initial provider request host but does not yet revalidate runtime redirects. Decisions and future systems points to ADR-001 onward and says specs remain planned rather than implemented until source, tests, and a user entry point prove otherwise.

anchors.summary: Hoplight is a Bun and TypeScript repository rooted in src, with three user surfaces built on one shared engine. src/core owns canonical entities, detection, conversion, coverage, and semantic engines. src/entities owns per-kind schemas and pure capabilities. src/formats contains one drop-in adapter folder per external family. src/studio is the durable local folder database. src/sandbox owns sealed-script analysis and user-invoked benches. src/ui contains the loopback server and React Studio. src/kit contains the source-checkout agent loop, provider adapters, discovery, staged drafts, and transcript ledger. src/cli.ts is the command entry. Dependencies point inward: surface code may depend on engine code, while engine code must never depend on a surface.

Every supported file maps through the canonical model in src/core/canonical.ts; no format converts directly to another format. The canonical body is a superset of interoperable wire fields. Each imported entity also retains its parsed source snapshot and unmapped fields in original escrow, while sparse profiles preserve platform-specific overrides. Same-format export re-projects edits over that source twin so untouched details survive. Cross-format export carries only supported canonical meaning and reports escrowed, dropped, shadowed, or warned paths rather than silently claiming portability. Format adapters are folders under src/formats and expose detect, toCanonical, and fromCanonical. The loader discovers those folders, and the registry, CLI formats listing, Studio import surfaces, and support matrix all consume the same live adapter set.

Studio storage is a folder database rather than an opaque application database. Each piece is saved as readable JSON beneath a per-kind and per-id path. The storage layer contains paths to the studio root, writes atomically, supports keep-both collision behavior, and compares expected revisions before saving so concurrent edits fail visibly. Semantic capability operations remain pure: they produce previews and validation evidence without touching disk. A separate apply path performs the authorized durable mutation, then re-reads the saved entity to verify the result and produce trustworthy post-write evidence. This separation lets CLI, Studio, and Kit share edit logic without granting preview code an accidental write path.

Hoplight exposes three faces over the same engine. The hoplight command is the scriptable CLI for conversion, inspection, validation, labeling, discovery, and Studio launch. Studio is the local desktop experience: a React client served by a Bun loopback server, with the remote-access sidecar remaining an explicit opt-in. Kit is the source-checkout conversational surface. It connects a configured model provider, progressively discovers content and documentation tools, accumulates staged changes with warnings and platform impact, and applies only through the same durable storage boundary. Kit is real source code but is not yet part of distributed release binaries; release claims must wait for a defined bundle, binary inclusion, and installed-artifact smoke test.

Untrusted files and requests are parsed once at their boundary and rejected when unreadable. Imported Lua, macros, and regex payloads remain inert data during import, conversion, storage, preview, and agent use. Execution exists only in the explicit Lua or regex test benches on the isolated sandbox origin, and no additional execution path is allowed. Network effects are deliberate and auditable: remote Studio access is opt-in, Kit checks the initial provider request URL against the configured host, and update checks target fixed GitHub release infrastructure. The current Kit fetch path does not revalidate runtime redirects, so its host gate is not an end-to-end redirect policy. Hoplight has no accounts, telemetry, proxying, or background upload. Provider credentials are encrypted at rest and are configuration, never content: they must not appear in canonical entities, prompts, tool observations, exports, transcripts, or the ledger.

Consequential architectural choices begin with ADR-001 in docs/decisions and continue through the repository's current decision records. Detailed contracts for implemented and future areas live under specs. A specification, roadmap entry, or design description does not by itself establish a shipped capability. Future systems remain explicitly planned until matching source code exists, tests prove the contract, and users have a real entry point. Reference documentation must describe that implemented state honestly rather than converting architectural intent into a release claim.

docs.title: Conventions
docs.summary: These are the repository's binding implementation rules. They describe current enforced practice, not an idealized future toolchain.
docs.semanticSummary: This page states Hoplight's binding current implementation rules. Code requires strict TypeScript boundary narrowing, exact per-kind runtime decoders for handwritten canonical interfaces, explicitly declared open escrow bags, UI-independent core logic, typed errors, consistent naming, and the scoped TS/TSX pictograph gate. defineExhaustiveShape<T>() rejects missing and extra keys, narrowed unions, coercion, any at any nesting depth, and never during typecheck. Tests use Bun across authored src and scripts, begin bug fixes at a failing public boundary, prove semantic same-format round trips, remain deterministic, and do not treat synchronization warnings as clean proof. CLI defines the unfinished automation target for convert, inspect, validate, label, formats, and version. Repository requires useful release-history subjects and behavioral evidence while forbidding gate bypasses. Documentation separates built reference behavior from labeled plans and moves with source. Working method requires inspecting the owning system and Git state, fixing the real owner, reporting verification limits, and obtaining independent review without self-approval.

anchors.summary: TypeScript runs in strict mode, and untrusted values are narrowed at entry. Handwritten domain interfaces may remain rich internal contracts, but separate fail-closed runtime schemas must exhaust their canonical types. defineExhaustiveShape<T>() infers concrete schemas before demanding exact input and output parity, rejecting missing and extra keys, narrowed unions, coercion, any at any nesting depth, and never during typecheck. src/entities/runtime-schema.ts composes the strict per-kind decoders used by storage, HTTP, format-corpus verification, and Kit draft validation. Unknown keys are accepted only inside extension or escrow bags whose contracts explicitly declare openness. Core logic cannot depend on UI, perform effects at import, or conceal authority in a singleton. Code throws Error objects or typed errors, and user-facing boundaries translate failures plainly.

Bun is the test runner, and bun run test discovers every authored test under src and scripts. Bug fixes begin with a regression at the public boundary that reproduces the reported behavior before the repair. Same-format adapter fixtures must parse, serialize, and reparse without semantic loss, protecting the Round-Trip Law at the format boundary. Tests remain deterministic by avoiding live network access, uncontrolled clocks, and unseeded randomness. A nominally green result that still prints framework synchronization warnings is not clean verification and must not be represented as such.

The target automation contract covers the non-interactive data commands convert, inspect, validate, label, formats, and version. JSON mode must emit exactly one JSON value to stdout, while human diagnostics go to stderr. Exit code 0 means success, 1 means invalid user input or invalid content, and 2 means an unexpected internal failure. help and the long-running ui server are outside this JSON contract. The section explicitly says implementation is incomplete: until all commands comply and command-matrix tests land, docs/reference/cli.md remains the authority for current syntax and behavior rather than this target being treated as shipped proof.

Commit subjects must name the affected area and remain useful in Mainstage release history; WIP, misc, and context-free fix subjects are rejected. Conventional prefixes are welcome but optional. The exact [skip release] text is the only machine-read commit marker. User-facing behavioral changes carry tests or recorded live verification. Hooks and gates are repository policy: contributors repair the underlying failure rather than bypassing a hook or weakening a check to force passage.

Reference pages state built behavior only. Planned work belongs under specs or in a roadmap section that labels it as planned, preventing intent from masquerading as a shipped surface. Documentation changes in the same change as its source so contracts and user guidance stay aligned. Generated indexes and semantic summaries are navigation aids, not authority: they cannot transform an inaccurate source page into truth.

Before editing, inspect the implementation, its callers and tests, release configuration, documentation, and Git state, then name both the governing authority and user-visible outcome. Bugs and known contracts begin with an honest failing test at the nearest public boundary. A genuinely novel design may use a bounded spike until its contract is understood, but completion still requires behavioral proof. Repair the owning boundary rather than creating a parallel schema, registry, state authority, or compatibility path. When code and docs disagree, classify the claim as IMPLEMENT, REWRITE, DELETE, or RETAIN. Verification progresses through focused, adjacent, and complete supported checks, with warnings and skips reported rather than counted as clean. Substantial or high-risk work receives independent adversarial review; authors cannot approve their own semantic summaries, security claims, migrations, or release evidence.

docs.title: ADR-001: Runtime - Bun + TypeScript, Node-compatible core
docs.summary: **Status:** accepted
docs.semanticSummary: Accepted ADR choosing TypeScript everywhere with Bun as the toolchain for dev runtime, bun test, bundling, and bun build --compile single-file executables as primary distribution. Core packages core, formats, lore, presets, macros, regexkit, and assembly must not use Bun-only APIs and must stay runnable under Node for npm publish and embedding. apps, agent, and ai may use Bun APIs where they matter for spawn, file IO speed, and compile. Why: one-file no-install distribution is the top goal; TypeScript matches VAUDEVILLE extraction surface and zod dual use as validation and docs; Node-compat core keeps npm and embedding open and de-risks Bun stalls. Consequences: CI runs core package tests under both Bun and Node; a lint rule bans bun star imports inside packages except an allowlist of ai and agent. Status is accepted.

anchors.summary: TypeScript is used everywhere. Bun is the toolchain for development runtime, test runner via bun test, bundler, and bun build --compile for single-file executables as primary distribution. Core packages named core, formats, lore, presets, macros, regexkit, and assembly must not use Bun-only APIs so they remain runnable under Node for npm publish and embedding by other tools. apps plus agent and ai may use Bun APIs where they matter for spawn, file IO speed, and compile.

The top stated distribution goal is one file with no install pain as the anti-SillyTavern-setup answer; bun build --compile is the most direct path on all three OSes. TypeScript is chosen because the entire VAUDEVILLE extraction surface is TS and because zod schemas double as validation and documentation. Node-compatible core keeps the npm and embedding door open and de-risks Bun: if Bun stalls, only apps need porting.

CI must run core package tests under both Bun and Node so Node-compat claims stay proven. A lint rule bans bun colon star imports inside packages except an allowlist covering the ai and agent packages, which are permitted to use Bun-only APIs where they matter.

docs.title: ADR-002: License, AGPL-3.0-or-later
docs.summary: **Status:** accepted
docs.semanticSummary: Accepted ADR selecting AGPL-3.0-or-later for the whole repo to keep code genuinely open while preventing closed commercial exploitation. Context forced the choice because openness and anti-enclosure pull against each other under a permissive license. Decision allows the copyright holder to sell commercial licenses to parties who cannot comply with AGPL, following Grafana, Qt, and pre-SSPL MongoDB dual-licensing. Why AGPL fits: OSI-approved open source without source-available stigma; forks and hosted services must publish complete source under same terms so commercial actors stay away or negotiate; copyright holder is not bound by their own license for other closed projects. Rejected PolyForm-NC FSL BUSL as source-available, MIT Apache as allowing closed forks, and MIT core plus AGPL app as weaker where it matters most though revisitable. Consequences: LICENSE verbatim AGPL text, LICENSING.md plain explanation and commercial contact, license audit fails build on copyleft restricted deps, no CLA is a live constraint so outside contributions cannot merge without forfeiting commercial dual-license option, no per-file SPDX headers.

anchors.summary: The project needed a license that keeps the code genuinely open and usable by anyone while preventing a third party from closing it up and selling it. Those two goals pull against each other under a permissive license, which forced a deliberate decision rather than a default choice.

AGPL-3.0-or-later applies to the whole repository. The copyright holder retains the right to sell commercial licenses to anyone who cannot or will not comply with the AGPL. This dual-licensing model is the same pattern Grafana, Qt, and pre-SSPL MongoDB used for open core plus commercial terms.

AGPL is a real OSI-approved open-source license without source-available stigma. It prevents closed commercial exploitation in practice because any fork or hosted service must publish its complete source under the same terms, which commercial actors rarely accept; they either stay away or negotiate a separate license. The copyright holder is not bound by their own license, so the same code can still be used in their other closed projects.
topics: holder not bound by own license

anchors.summary: PolyForm-NC, FSL, and BUSL are closer to the literal anti-commercial requirement but are source-available rather than open source and invite community suspicion this choice exists to avoid. MIT and Apache allow closed commercial forks outright. MIT core plus AGPL app is a cleaner engine adoption story but weakens the guarantee where it matters most; revisitable per-package later because relicensing toward MIT stays open to the copyright holder while the reverse is not.

LICENSE carries verbatim AGPL-3.0 text; LICENSING.md explains it in plain terms and carries the commercial contact. bun run license:audit fails the build if a copyleft or restricted dependency is introduced. No CLA is in place and this is a live constraint: dual licensing depends on the copyright holder owning all code; the first merged outside contribution without a contributor agreement ends that option. Until a CLA exists, outside contributions cannot be merged without forfeiting commercial licensing. Per-file SPDX headers were considered and are not adopted; the repo-level LICENSE governs.

docs.title: ADR-003: Distribution - single executable + self-updater; installer later
docs.summary: **Status:** accepted
docs.semanticSummary: Accepted ADR for distribution strategy. Primary v0.1 path is single-file executables per OS win x64, mac arm64 and x64, linux x64 built by bun build --compile and attached to GitHub Releases so users download one file and run with no Node, git, or install steps. Self-updater vaud upgrade checks Releases, downloads the new binary, verifies SHA-256 via a minisign-signed checksums file, and swaps atomically; later app face reuses the mechanism with UI; passive behavior is at most one non-blocking new-version notice per day and never auto-install without consent. Later signed desktop installers via Tauri bundler when apps/studio ships at M6, and package managers winget scoop brew when asked. npm publishes core packages for embedders and npx vaud works as secondary path not the documented default. Why: SillyTavern node plus git install is the top onboarding pain so download one file must be engineering truth; GitHub Releases provides free bandwidth where the audience already is. Consequences: release CI builds binary matrix checksums and signature on every tag; Windows SmartScreen will complain about unsigned exes until a code-signing cert is bought; binary size about 50-90MB from Bun runtime is accepted and documented.

anchors.summary: Primary v0.1 distribution is single-file executables for win x64, mac arm64 and x64, and linux x64 via bun build --compile on GitHub Releases with download-one-file run and no Node git or install steps. Self-updater vaud upgrade checks Releases, downloads, verifies SHA-256 from a minisign-signed checksums file, and swaps atomically; UI reuses later; at most one non-blocking new-version notice per day and never auto-install without consent. Later: signed Tauri installers when studio ships M6; winget scoop brew manifests when someone asks. npm core packages and npx vaud are secondary not the documented default.

SillyTavern's node plus git install is the single most cited onboarding pain in this hobby. Download one file is the marketing headline so it must be the engineering truth. GitHub Releases offers free bandwidth and the audience already lives there.

Release CI builds a matrix of binaries plus checksums plus signature on every tag. Windows SmartScreen will complain about unsigned exes; buy a code-signing cert when budget allows and document the More info Run anyway path until then as an M1 ticket. Binary size of roughly 50-90MB because Bun embeds its runtime is accepted and must be documented.

docs.title: ADR-005: Canonical superset model + escrow envelope
docs.summary: **Status:** accepted
docs.semanticSummary: Accepted ADR establishing Hoplight's canonical superset and escrow model. Its schema-authority note records that ADR-011 supersedes the original Zod-under-packages/core wording: current domain contracts are handwritten interfaces in src/entities/<kind>/schema.ts paired with exhaustive adjacent runtime decoders. The Decision retains one canonical model per content type, carries fields without a canonical home in origin-keyed escrow, merges escrow for semantically identical same-format round trips, and requires honest reports for cross-format loss or recovery through tolerated extension fields. Why not "just use chara_card_v3 internally" explains that V3 covers cards only and cannot represent all RoleCall, Risu, Backyard, lorebook, preset, or persona meaning. Precedents in the author's own earlier code identifies RoleCall unsupportedFields and origin plus VAUDEVILLE normalizers as earlier forms of the pattern. Consequences requires codec capability tables to drive conversion reporting and the generated support matrix, while changes to canonical domain contracts demand a migration note, fixture sweep, and explicit design review. ADR-005's superset, escrow envelope, and Round-Trip Law remain accepted even though ADR-011 now owns runtime schema authority.

anchors.summary: The decision text defines one canonical superset per content type and an origin-keyed escrow envelope for fields without a canonical home. Its parse and serialize equations require reports at both boundaries. Same-format serialization merges escrow so the result remains semantically identical under the Round-Trip Law. Cross-format serialization expresses supported meaning, reports escrowed or dropped fields, and preserves escrow where the target permits extension fields, allowing later recovery. The section's historical statement places Zod schemas in packages/core, but the document's schema-authority note explicitly supersedes that detail through ADR-011. Current authority is handwritten domain interfaces under src/entities/<kind>/schema.ts paired with exhaustive runtime decoders; the superset and escrow behavior itself is unchanged.

V3 is card-only and still lossy against RoleCall details palette sprites and depth-injections, Risu extensions, and Backyard fields. Lorebooks, presets, and personas need models V3 does not define. A superset with escrow means the project never argues with a format author about whose fields matter.

anchors.text: Precedents in the author's own earlier code
anchors.summary: RoleCall LorebookEntry unsupportedFields and origin fields are this escrow pattern in miniature. VAUDEVILLE normalizers already unify V1 V2 V3 rcpersona and RoleOut into a common shape. This ADR promotes that established habit into a system-wide law rather than inventing a new approach.

Every codec ships a capabilities table mapping canonical field to native, escrow, or dropped that powers honest conversion reports and the docs format-support matrix which is auto-generated and never hand-maintained. core schema changes are the most expensive changes in the repo: they require a migration note, a fixture sweep, and explicit design review.

docs.title: ADR-006: AI - BYOK + local, and an agent built for weak models
docs.summary: **Status:** accepted
docs.semanticSummary: Accepted ADR for AI posture and weak-model agent design. BYOK first with Anthropic, OpenRouter, OpenAI, Gemini, and any OpenAI-compatible endpoint covering Ollama LM Studio koboldcpp for local; no Vaudeville-operated inference, no account, no proxy; keys in local vault OS keychain or encrypted file. AI is optional: Converter, inspection, validation, deterministic Doctor checks, and project management work with zero keys; first key ask is at first AI moment never at install. Agent must survive weak models using Orison lessons: tiny always-on tools with deferred schemas, resource verbs over vaud URIs, prompted XML tool-calling fallback one tool per iteration, spill store for big results, explicit samplers, staged edits with validate-before-commit never writing user files directly. Model roles are user-mappable per interview treatment test-stage and bulk audits with a sane single-model default. Eval harness at M2 before agent feature work with golden tasks replayable transcripts and model matrix requiring success-rate and tokens-per-task movement. Why: local-first BYOK matches privacy pitch and audience that owns keys; weak-model constraints also make frontier behavior cheaper and more reliable.

anchors.summary: BYOK first: Anthropic, OpenRouter, OpenAI, Gemini, plus any OpenAI-compatible endpoint for Ollama LM Studio koboldcpp local; no Vaudeville-operated inference account or proxy; keys in OS keychain or encrypted file. AI is optional so Converter inspection validation deterministic Doctor and project management need zero keys; first key ask is at first AI moment never install. Agent must survive weak models via tiny always-on tools with deferred schemas, resource verbs ls read write search over vaud URIs, prompted XML fallback with one tool per iteration, spill store to disk handles, explicit samplers with max_tokens room for tool args, and staged edits validate-before-commit never writing user files directly. Model roles are user-mappable across interview treatment test-stage and bulk audits with a sane single-model default. Eval harness at M2 before agent feature work uses golden tasks, replayable transcripts, and a model matrix; agent changes must move success-rate and tokens-per-task numbers.

Local-first plus BYOK is the only stance consistent with the privacy pitch and with an audience that already owns keys and local rigs. Weak-model constraints are not charity: they make frontier-model behavior cheaper and more reliable too, which is Orison's measured lesson.

docs.title: ADR-007: Renderer policy (shell vanilla, per-app freedom, chat surfaces re-evaluated at spec time)
docs.summary: **Status:** accepted · 2026-07-05 **Context owners:** the shell (`src/ui/`), every app folder, the future Table Read and agent surfaces
docs.semanticSummary: Accepted ADR on renderer policy dated 2026-07-05. Context: shell and then-current surfaces were vanilla TS plus DOM with five runtime dependencies and one compiled exe per ADR-001 and ADR-003, while roadmap chat surfaces M4 Table Read and agent packages are classically React-shaped. Two facts prevent a stack war: Table Read and agent engines are UI-agnostic with zero rendering code and one event protocol; the app contract manifest plus mount is renderer-agnostic so an app folder may bundle its own library. Decision: shell and editor shelf-class surfaces stay vanilla TS plus DOM; every app folder has renderer freedom; when Table Read and agent chat surfaces reach implementation their specs must include a renderer assessment with React on the table against streaming updates, virtualized long lists, deep interactive state webs, and component-ecosystem needs; if two or more criteria hold React is the default for that surface otherwise vanilla; engines never acquire a renderer dependency. Consequences: no restart of prior layers; two rendering idioms may coexist bounded by folders-as-schema; this is the standing answer that React is decided per-surface at spec time. Note ADR-008 later supersedes the deferral of chat-surface choice while keeping the engine rule.

anchors.summary: Shell and then-current Library Workbench Press Settings setup surfaces were hand-built vanilla TS plus DOM with five runtime dependencies and one compiled exe. Roadmap also promises chat-shaped surfaces: M4 Table Read conversational interview and agent system packages agent REPL test chat with Studio later at M6. Chat runtimes are classically React-shaped for streaming state and live lists, and comparable apps RoleCall Marinara Lumiverse frontend render chat with React 19. Two facts avoid a stack war: Table Read spec locks the engine as UI-agnostic with zero rendering code and one event protocol shared by CLI and Studio; agent packages follow the same rule so studio may not own private engine capabilities; renderer choice never touches engine design. App contract of manifest plus mount is renderer-agnostic; an app folder may bundle its own rendering library and the shell neither knows nor cares.

Shell and editor shelf-class surfaces stay vanilla TS plus DOM because form and card complexity does not justify a framework runtime. Every app folder has renderer freedom: bundling a framework inside one app is an add not a rewrite and needs no shell change. When Table Read and agent chat surfaces reach implementation their specs must include a renderer assessment against sustained streaming updates, long virtualized lists, deep interactive state webs, and concrete component-ecosystem needs, with React explicitly on the table. If two or more criteria hold, default for that surface is React with Bun-native TSX baked into the exe; otherwise vanilla, with the event protocol keeping a later swap cheap. Engines never acquire a renderer dependency under any outcome.

No restart scenario exists: converter, canonical model, engines, shell, editors, and tokens CSS serve both renderer outcomes unchanged. The repo may eventually carry two rendering idioms isolated per app folder; that cost is accepted and bounded by folders-as-schema. This ADR is the standing answer to whether Studio should be React: the question is only ever asked per-surface with written criteria at the moment the surface is specced.

docs.title: ADR-008: React UI layer for structural rendering safety
docs.summary: **Status:** accepted · 2026-07-05 **Supersedes:** ADR-007's "decide per chat surface later." ADR-007's engine rule is carried forward unchanged and hardened here.
docs.semanticSummary: Accepted ADR dated 2026-07-05 that supersedes ADR-007's deferral of chat-surface renderer choice while carrying forward and hardening the engine rule. Context: Hoplight renders untrusted card and extension text, so direct DOM construction makes HTML-sink safety depend on caller convention; React escapes text by default and repository gates ban explicit escape hatches. Roadmap chat and agent surfaces plus agent-context plans require serializable UI state; closure-held vanilla DOM is agent-opaque while store-driven React matches comparable production apps. Decision: UI layer is React 19 plus TSX transpiled natively by Bun with no Vite or Next, bundled into the same single exe; Zustand for shell store plus one store per app; no URL router; CSS Modules over tokens with no Tailwind; whole UI converts to one idiom; app contract v2 is React component export plus manifest including agentSurface descriptor; engine rule forbids renderer imports in converter canonical model engines and star-core files; react react-dom and zustand are direct dependencies covered by license audit while new dependencies follow normal review without a special commit trailer; dangerouslySetInnerHTML and raw HTML sinks are banned outside an allowlist. Consequences: rewrite bounded by pure cores as spec; ordinary text is escaped by default and the sink gate enforces escape-hatch policy; established tooling lowers maintenance cost; framework churn risk accepted with engine immune.

anchors.summary: Two constraints crystallized after ADR-007. Hoplight renders untrusted card and extension text, so direct DOM construction makes HTML-sink safety depend on every caller; React escapes text by default and gates ban explicit escape hatches. Roadmap chat and agent surfaces plus per-surface context require serializable UI state; closure-held vanilla DOM is agent-opaque while store-driven React matches comparable production applications.

UI layer is React 19 plus TSX transpiled natively by Bun without Vite or Next and bundled into the same single exe. State is Zustand with one shell store plus one store per app surface; navigation is state-driven with no URL router. Styling is CSS Modules over the existing token system with no Tailwind. The UI converts whole shell and every app folder to one idiom; until conversion lands, vanilla surfaces remain the behavioral spec. App contract v2 is a React component export plus manifest including an agentSurface descriptor of state selector and offered actions so every surface is agent-readable by construction. Engine rule unchanged and hardened: converter, canonical model, engines, and every star-core.ts stay pure framework-less TS; a renderer import there is a guardrail violation. React, react-dom, and zustand are direct dependencies covered by license audit; new dependencies follow normal review without a special commit trailer. dangerouslySetInnerHTML and raw HTML-injection sinks are banned by repo gates outside an explicit sanctioned allowlist.

Editor slice 1 and the current shell are rebuilt in React during conversion; their behavior and pure tested cores are the spec so the rewrite is bounded. Ordinary text rendering is escaped by default, while repository gates separately enforce the raw-HTML escape-hatch ban. Established tooling and contributor familiarity reduce maintenance cost. React version churn is accepted and bounded because the engine remains isolated.

docs.title: ADR-009: Distinct origin for test-bench execution
docs.summary: **Status:** accepted in design; packaged-host proof BLOCKED; 2026-07-09 **Context owners:** `src/sandbox/lua/`, `src/sandbox/regex/`, `src/ui/server.ts`, `src/ui/sandbox-host.ts`, desktop entries **Audit IDs:** SANDBOX-001 (Plan 017)
docs.semanticSummary: Accepted-in-design ADR for a distinct origin for test-bench execution; packaged-host proof remains BLOCKED as of 2026-07-09. Context: Risu Test Bench runs untrusted Lua and regex previews in dedicated Workers with resource ceilings; historically workers shared the UI loopback origin which is only an availability boundary not an origin boundary. Decision chooses a second loopback listener on an ephemeral port as a sandbox-only origin serving only worker.js, regex-worker.js, and glue.wasm with CORS for the UI origin, never exposing /api, studio paths, session-token HTML, arbitrary static, or secret source maps. UI injects vaude-sandbox-origin meta; API token stays only in vaude-session and trusted apiFetch. Lua and regex wires are value-only protocols with size and rule caps. Rejected same-path sandbox, allow-same-origin iframe, CORS-only, and deferred helper process. Measured results automate unit allowlist protocol and packaged asset build but not packaged WebView2 probes. Consequences: HTTP-layer origin separation is implementable; do not claim full sandbox isolation in release notes until WebView2 matrix is green; Plans 005 and 016 remain load-bearing. STOP honesty: Plan 017 full Done is BLOCKED until packaged measurements exist.

anchors.summary: Risu Test Bench runs untrusted Lua in a dedicated Worker with Plan 016 resource ceilings for timeout, heap, host-state, and wire size. Regex previews run in a dedicated terminable Worker with a 750 ms wall-clock ceiling. Plan 005 authenticates the loopback API with a per-launch bearer X-Vaude-Token and meta vaude-session. Historically the worker module was served from the same loopback origin as the UI and /api. A same-origin Worker is an availability boundary (killable thread), not an origin boundary. If a future engine bundler WebView or bridge bug exposes web capabilities, same-origin placement increases blast radius for same-origin APIs, storage, or credentials. This is defense-in-depth architecture, not evidence of a current same-origin exploit.

Before a public Windows release, check the freshly built dist/Vaude.exe not the development server: open Workshop Test Bench, run return 42, and run a Regex Bench preview. Both must finish without a worker-load error. Record build version and result in release notes. Automated suite already proves distinct loopback authority, allowlist CSP CORS, API denial, token absence, and protocol; this acceptance specifically covers installed WebView2 runtime.

In-scope assets if sandbox shares the app origin: per-launch API token leak into script state worker globals messages logs or URLs; mutating /api routes via cross-origin-less fetch with ambient authority; studio filesystem write or delete through authenticated routes; trusted cookies and localStorage shared with the worker. Out of scope: arbitrary untrusted native-code isolation, giving Lua DOM fetch or fs access, and auto-running scripts on import.
topics: out of scope native Lua DOM

anchors.summary: Chosen boundary is a second loopback listener where distinct port equals distinct origin. Primary UI API server stays on 127.0.0.1 configured port with Host Origin token gating from Plan 005. Sandbox-only server binds 127.0.0.1 on an ephemeral port and serves only GET sandbox worker.js, regex-worker.js, and glue.wasm plus CORS preflight for the UI origin. Sandbox host must not expose /api, studio paths, index HTML with session token, arbitrary static files, or source maps with secrets. UI HTML injects meta vaude-sandbox-origin which is public not a secret; API token stays only in meta vaude-session and trusted apiFetch. Browser UI loads workers from sandbox origin when meta is present; Bun tests keep module-relative worker paths. Lua wire protocol is a versioned value-only tagged union with allowlisted keys, Plan 016 size budgets, no token fields, no functions handles or ports except the Worker channel. Regex worker accepts values only and rejects oversized input, more than 500 rules, and malformed rows or options before the core engine. Nested sections reject weaker isolation alternatives and document origin alias fail-closed behavior.

children.summary: Reject same-path sandbox as same origin; reject iframe allow-same-origin; reject CORS alone as non-auth. Defer helper child process until measured need for packaging cost.
Distinct 127.0.0.1 ports are distinct origins. Host checks fail closed on aliases. Sandbox origin never authorizes API calls without token and correct Origin.

anchors.summary: Unit checks automated: sandbox handler allowlist serves only the two workers plus wasm and returns 404 for /api and traversal; value protocol rejects wrong version unknown type secret keys and oversized payloads; worker run without token in messages via protocol encode parse. Packaged asset build is automated by bun run scripts/build-desktop.ts. Not run or not measured in this implementation pass: packaged WebView2 origin probe on Windows, self.crossOriginIsolated and storage visibility in WebView, and credentialed API fetch from a sandbox-origin worker in the packaged host.

startUi starts both listeners and stop tears both down. Packaged exe uses the same dual-listen path; sandbox serves both packaged worker bundles plus wasm. If sandbox listen fails, UI can fall back to the matching same-origin worker path on the primary server as degraded mode not claimed isolated; prefer fail-visible logs over silent false isolation. Re-run the origin probe when WebView, bundler, server, or packaging dependencies change.

Real origin separation is implementable and tested at the HTTP handler layer in Bun. Packaged-host proof remains BLOCKED until a WebView2 smoke matrix records distinct authority, no shared storage or token, API denial from the sandbox origin, and CSP probes. Do not claim full sandbox isolation in release notes until that matrix is green. Plans 005 token and 016 quotas remain load-bearing layers; origin isolation is additive.

This ADR deliberately does not assert that the shipped WebView collapses authorities safely. Until packaged measurements exist, Plan 017 status is BLOCKED for full Done criteria while the code path of sandbox host protocol and token absence ships as defense-in-depth scaffolding.

docs.title: ADR-010: Shared semantic content capabilities
docs.summary: **Status:** accepted, 2026-07-25
docs.semanticSummary: Accepted ADR dated 2026-07-25 for shared semantic content capabilities. Context: Kit will eventually need more than one hundred content-editing operations; advertising every schema on every model request wastes context and hurts tool selection; implementing the same mutation separately in Kit and Workbench would allow drift. Filesystem is already the registry for formats and UI extensions, so content edits need the same drop-in property while canonical validation and escrow preservation remain mandatory. Decision: pure semantic operations live under src/entities kind capabilities; platform-specific operations may live under src/formats platform capabilities; one immutable catalog validates stable dotted IDs and supports deterministic metadata search; Kit keeps a complete runtime registry but exposes only direct tools and up to five successfully discovered deferred capabilities to the model; browser uses a generated import seam from the same folders never a second hand-maintained catalog; a capability produces a validated preview and never writes; Kit composes previews into a session-local draft while apply stale-revision checks persistence and verification are separate runtime responsibilities; Web UI imports the same pure operations and keeps presentation-only state locally. Consequences: add operations via drop-in and proof; small task-relevant tool sets; shared mutation meaning; capability IDs become compatibility-sensitive once shipped; live apply rejects stale drafts and reports only verified post-save receipts as applied.

anchors.summary: Kit will eventually need more than one hundred content-editing operations. Advertising every schema on every model request wastes context and makes tool selection less reliable. Implementing the same mutation separately in Kit and the Workbench would also allow their behavior to drift. The filesystem is already Hoplight's registry for formats and UI extensions. Content edits need the same drop-in property, while canonical validation and escrow preservation remain mandatory.

Pure semantic operations live under src/entities kind capabilities folders. Platform-specific operations may live under src/formats platform capabilities. One immutable catalog validates stable dotted IDs and supports deterministic metadata search. Kit keeps a complete runtime registry but exposes only direct tools and up to five successfully discovered deferred capabilities to the model. The browser uses a generated import seam from the same folders; the generated file is never a second hand-maintained catalog. A capability produces a validated preview and never writes. Kit composes previews into a session-local draft; applying, stale-revision checks, persistence, and verification are separate runtime responsibilities. The Web UI imports the same pure operations and keeps presentation-only state such as focus and undo locally.

Adding an operation means adding a capability drop-in and proof, not editing a central registry. Models receive small task-relevant typed tool sets instead of one huge static catalog. Kit and the Workbench can share mutation meaning without sharing surface state. Capability IDs become compatibility-sensitive once shipped. The live apply boundary rejects stale drafts and reports only a verified post-save receipt as applied.

docs.title: ADR-011: Exhaustive runtime schemas at canonical boundaries
docs.summary: **Status:** accepted, 2026-07-26
docs.semanticSummary: Accepted on 2026-07-26, ADR-011 makes exhaustive runtime decoding the canonical boundary contract while preserving handwritten domain interfaces. TypeScript alone cannot validate JSON from disk, HTTP, adapters, or Kit drafts, and the former central decoder accepted only a required floor. The decision adds one adjacent runtime decoder per content kind and routes every decoded object through defineExhaustiveShape<T>(), which infers concrete Zod schemas before demanding exact domain-compatible inputs and outputs. Missing or extra keys, narrowed unions, coercion, any at any nesting depth, and never fail typecheck. Six strict bodies compose the public discriminated union; unknown same-version keys fail outside declared open record bags; profiles validate as kind-matched shallow partial bodies. Adapter-corpus tests, fully populated fixtures, malformed-family matrices, and storage, HTTP, Kit validation, and final-apply tests prove adoption. Strictness forces explicit schema evolution while leaving declared escrow and extension bags lossless and inert. ADR-005's canonical superset, escrow envelope, and Round-Trip Law remain in force.

anchors.summary: Canonical entities use rich handwritten TypeScript interfaces under src/entities/<kind>/schema.ts, but TypeScript types disappear at runtime and cannot validate JSON arriving from storage, HTTP, format adapters, or Kit drafts. The former central decoder checked the common envelope and only a required subset of each entity body. Because loose objects did not exhaust optional field families, a parse could succeed while carrying values that contradicted the domain interface into durable storage or editing logic. Replacing every interface with a schema-inferred type would cause broad disruption and still would not prove that every producer and consumer crosses one shared validation boundary. The problem is therefore boundary completeness and adoption, not merely the syntax used to declare types.

Handwritten domain interfaces remain the internal semantic contracts. Each content kind owns an adjacent decoder at src/entities/<kind>/runtime-schema.ts. Every decoded object uses defineExhaustiveShape<T>(), which infers each concrete schema before requiring exact domain-compatible input and output types. Missing and extra keys, narrowed unions, coercion, any at any nesting depth, and never fail typecheck. src/entities/runtime-schema.ts composes six strict body decoders into the public discriminated canonical union. Canonical envelopes, bodies, profiles, and authored nested objects reject unknown current-version keys outside explicitly declared open carriers. Profiles use their kind's shallow partial body decoder. Adapter-corpus tests, fully populated per-kind fixtures, malformed-family matrices, and public-boundary tests prove adoption by format output, storage, HTTP save, Kit draft validation, and final Kit apply.

A successful canonical parse now proves the complete known shape rather than a required floor. Interface and decoder drift, including narrowed unions and coercing inputs, becomes a compile-time error, while malformed external values fail at one shared runtime boundary with bounded messages. Storage, HTTP, adapters, and Kit no longer need competing ad hoc validators. Adding a canonical field requires the interface, adjacent decoder, positive fixture, and malformed-value regression to change together. Rejecting unknown same-version keys makes evolution deliberate. Declared escrow, metadata, extension, and other record bags remain lossless and inert. ADR-005's canonical superset, escrow envelope, and Round-Trip Law remain accepted.

docs.title: Format support matrix
docs.summary: Auto-generated from live adapters (`bun run scripts/format-matrix.ts`). Canonical schema version: **1**. Generated: 2026-07-26.
docs.semanticSummary: Auto-generated format support matrix from live adapters via bun run scripts/format-matrix.ts, canonical schema version 1. It lists every registered adapter by content kind with id, writes extensions, and human labels. How to use shows Hoplight formats, inspect, convert, and validate, and names SillyTavern CCv3 as the default portable character shape for thin hosts such as C.AI Tools dumps and Crushon import. Characters currently has nine adapters including agnai, backyard, byaf, lumiverse, pygmalion, risu, rolecall, sillytavern, and vaud-json. Lorebooks has six: agnai, marinara, novelai, risu, rolecall, and sillytavern world info. Personas has four: lumiverse, marinara, rolecall, and sillytavern. Presets has four: lumiverse, marinara, rolecall, and sillytavern. Regex script sets has five: lumiverse, marinara, risu, rolecall, and sillytavern. Sprite packs has zero adapters; the studio edits the pack kind but no import or export format exists yet. Notes require content-sniff detection not extension alone, same-format lossless round-trips where fixtures prove them, honest cross-format drops, and Default CCv3 via sillytavern for skipped host-native bags. Samples lists per-platform fixture folders under samples/.

anchors.summary: Documents the primary CLI entry points for format work: bun run hoplight formats to list adapters, hoplight inspect on a card path, hoplight convert with --to for a target such as sillytavern, and hoplight validate on card JSON. The default portable character shape for thin hosts including C.AI Tools dumps and Crushon import is SillyTavern CCv3 through the sillytavern adapter.

Nine character adapters. agnai writes .json for Agnai Agnaistic. backyard writes .json for Backyard.ai or Faraday legacy json. byaf writes .byaf Backyard archives. lumiverse writes .json and .charx for ST plus modules. pygmalion writes .json and .png flat character. risu writes .charx zip with card.json and assets. rolecall writes .json for RoleCall v3 png or json cards. sillytavern writes .json for SillyTavern CCv2 and v3 png or json. vaud-json writes .json as Hoplight native. All are kind character.

Six lorebook adapters. agnai-lorebook writes .json Agnai memory books. marinara-lorebook writes .json native .marinara.json export. novelai-lorebook writes .lorebook for NovelAI native export or json. risu-lorebook writes .json RisuAI native export. rolecall-lorebook writes .json RoleCall v1 export. sillytavern-lorebook writes .json SillyTavern world info worldbook. All are kind lorebook.

Four persona adapters, all writing .json. lumiverse-persona is a Lumiverse account object. marinara-persona carries theming and stat bars sealed. rolecall-persona is rcpersona or RC persona-card export. sillytavern-persona is a SillyTavern personas backup where the default persona is primary and the rest ride sealed.

Four preset adapters, all writing .json. lumiverse-preset imports a wrapper and exports as an ST flat preset. marinara-preset is Marinara-Engine marinara_preset export. rolecall-preset is RoleCall preset export with ST grammar plus macros, choice groups, and readme. sillytavern-preset is SillyTavern completion preset as flat json.

Five regex script set adapters, all writing .json. lumiverse-regex is a versioned export file. marinara-regex is an API dump array. risu-regex covers .risum module or customscript array. rolecall-regex is a chat-pipeline find and replace set. sillytavern-regex is a bare array or card extensions.regex_scripts. All are kind regex.

Sprite packs currently list zero format adapters in the live matrix. The studio already edits the pack kind as a first-class content type, but no import or export format adapter exists yet. The table row is an explicit placeholder with kind pack, empty id, and no writes extensions until a format is registered.

Detection is content-sniff, not only extension; prefer hoplight label when unsure. Same-format round-trips aim for lossless where fixtures prove it, see adapter tests and samples/. Cross-format convert keeps what the target can express; use export honesty in the studio UI for drop notes. Dropped or skipped host-native bags such as Character.AI and Crushon should use Default CCv3 via the sillytavern adapter.

Lists sample fixture folders under samples/. sillytavern holds CCv2/v3 and Seraphina.png. rolecall has RC character plus lorebook. risu has .charx and card json. agnai, backyard .byaf, pygmalion classic flat, lumiverse ST plus Lumi extensions, chub ST plus extensions.chub, marinara lorebook envelope plus prompt preset, and novelai lorebook complete the corpus map.

docs.title: Convert a card
docs.summary: Take a card you have in one app's format and ship it out in another, and see plainly what crosses and what stays behind.
docs.semanticSummary: User guide for converting a card from one app's format to another. Most content crosses cleanly through one shared middle model, but private scripts and fields without a target home stay behind on purpose. Short workflow: import into Library with receipt, optionally edit on Workbench, stage for the Press, pick one target format, run the press and download a platform-named zip. Same-app round-trip keeps everything via the saved original file including private extensions layout and ids. Cross-app keeps only shared model fields; one app's private scripts never copy into another; scripts drop when converting to plainer apps like Agnai or legacy Backyard while name description and greetings arrive; use Risu .charx when the full rule pack must travel. Export honesty view lists keep note and drop lines before commit. Press batch stages many pieces one target per run with per-row printed skipped or failed results; staged characters bring linked lorebooks as riders. Tips stress same-app prefer, read drop notes, and fix lorebook keywords before export because empty keywords never fire and Press flags that in red.

anchors.summary: Five steps: import the card into the Library by drop or Import files reading the receipt and checking desired files; open on Workbench to edit or skip; stage for the Press via right-click or Press left rail, with staged characters bringing linked lorebooks; pick one target platform in the Press; click run the press then download the bundle as a single zip named for the platform.

Every convert passes through one shared model: read in then write out in the target shape. Same app round-trip keeps everything because the Library keeps the original file so private extensions layout and ids return from that saved copy. A different app keeps only what the shared model can express; if the target has no place for something it does not travel, and one app's private scripts are never copied into another as the safe choice. Example: converting a card with trigger scripts and regex to Agnai or legacy Backyard keeps name description and greetings but drops scripts; use Risu .charx to keep the full rule pack. Every export shows outcomes first via the editor Export honesty view listing what will and will not travel line by line before commit.

The Press converts a whole set in one go. Stage pieces via right-click Stage for the Press or left rail; the queue survives room switches. Pick one target, run once, every piece prints into a single zip. Each row reports printed with notes, skipped when the target has no format for that kind, or failed with error. A staged character travels as a bundle dragging linked lorebooks as riders; drop a rider from one run without unlinking. One target per run; for a second app run the press again with a different platform.

Prefer same-app round-trip to keep everything via the original file. Read drop notes keep note and dropped lines before export. Convert one piece from editor Export or a batch from the Press with the same honesty. If scripts matter pick a target that keeps them such as Risu .charx; plainer formats keep words not machinery. A lorebook whose entries have no keywords will never fire; Press flags that in red so fix keywords first.

docs.title: Edit a piece
docs.summary: Open a piece on the Workbench, change it through the Grid or Steps view, and save your draft explicitly before you close the tab.
docs.semanticSummary: User guide for editing pieces on the Workbench. A piece opens as its own tab filled from import or a blank template and stays a private draft until save. Characters get the deepest editor with Grid or Steps fill modes, platform lens preview of what a target keeps, and a scripts workshop; pack lorebook regex persona and preset use simpler editors with the same save mechanics. Short version: open from Library via Send to Workbench; choose Grid direct fields or Steps quiz style with Bento all-at-once or Playbill paged acts; change fields knowing platform tabs only change view not saved data; Save or ctrl+s with dirty-dot warning; close discards without confirm so save first. Editor panels cover Hoplight full card vs platform tabs with Lens count, Hide and Dim currently both hide fields, completion chips, Sealed Cargo read-only original, Variables macros, Fields/Workshop for scripts, and simpler pack lorebook binder regex persona preset forms. Save requires a name except packs fallback Untitled pack; whole draft write; close does not confirm. Tips cover dirty dot, platform tabs view-only, Sealed Cargo for lossless round-trip, toggles moving to Settings after tour, and Workshop only when scripts exist.

anchors.summary: Open from Library by right-click Send to the Workbench or stage and send bar; each piece is its own tab and already-open pieces do not reopen. Pick Grid for every field or Steps as a quiz, with Bento all fields at once or Playbill acts. Change fields; platform tabs preview what a target keeps and only change what you see never what is saved. Save or ctrl+s; dirty tab dot means unsaved. Close never confirms so save first.

Character editor has platform tabs above fields; Hoplight is full card; selecting platforms hides fields that platform cannot carry with a Lens count of surviving fields. Hide and Dim currently both drop fields; dim half is not built yet. Header has name scale Grid Steps Bento Playbill Save Export; toggles move to Settings under Workbench after tour once. Six completion chips track Portrait Name Core Prompts Greeting Tags Lens Check. Body cards include portrait with sprite links, Sealed Cargo holding original platform file whole read-only for lossless round-trip, Variables counting macros, and Fields/Workshop switch for scripting that does not retire to Settings. Other kinds: pack is name brief sprite grid; lorebook binder one entry at a time with TOC keys timing placement; regex personas presets closer to single form; all save the same way.

anchors.text: Saving, and what happens if you don't
anchors.summary: Every editor requires a name before Save does anything; blank name makes Save quietly do nothing with status a name is required before saving. Packs fall back to Untitled pack instead of blocking. Save writes the whole draft not just changes so untouched fields round-trip byte-for-byte. Ctrl+s saves from anywhere. While save is in flight you can keep typing; if you outrun it status says newer changes not yet saved. In Steps last Next becomes Complete and saves. Closing a tab with X or Delete does not ask first and discards unsaved work; the dirty tab dot is the only warning.

Watch the dirty tab dot as the unsaved work signal. Platform tabs change what you see not what you save; click Hoplight to clear selection and see the whole card. Sealed Cargo is read-only on purpose for same-app lossless round-trip. After first-run tour, layout and mode toggles move to Settings under Workbench; right-click Replay tutorials to restore header toggles. A piece with no scripts never shows the Workshop toggle.

docs.title: Export a piece
docs.summary: Send a piece out of Vaudeville Studios through the character editor's Export button, or a staged batch through the Press, and see exactly what travels before anything downloads.
docs.semanticSummary: User guide for exporting pieces from Vaudeville Studios. Two paths: character editor Export button for one piece with full honesty view of keep note and dropped lines and immediate single-file download, or staging for the Press for batches and for lorebook persona or preset alone. Short character path: open Workbench, Export, pick platform defaulting Risu or SillyTavern when available, read honesty lines, Export or Export anyway. Honesty checks whether the target carries Hoplight behavior shape for trigger scripts regex virtual script backdrop HTML and packaged modules; when it does scripts keep and Risu .charx re-packs modules; when not scripts drop and plain fields stay with pointer to Risu for rule packs. Example Agnai drops expression packs and maps lorebooks to MemoryBook with regex key warning. Press stages queue surviving room switches; linked lorebooks ride as bundles; one target; readiness not honesty showing keyword gaps red amber and filled field counts; run prints printed skipped failed then zip download. Tips: Press for non-character exports; Export anyway is soft warn; rename and flavor lock after result; fix zero-keyword lorebooks first.

anchors.summary: For characters open Workbench Export at top of editor; lorebook persona or preset skip to Press staging. Click Export, pick a platform from formats for this kind with Risu or SillyTavern chosen first if available. Read honesty lines that state facts or open with Note or Dropped. Click Export or Export anyway when anything needs a second look; one file downloads immediately no zip.

Every export checks whether the target carries Hoplight behavior shape: trigger scripts, regex, virtual script, backdrop HTML, and packaged module rows. When the target carries behavior, scripts keep; Risu .charx re-packs module scripts and lore whole while elsewhere the module blob may not survive intact. When it does not, scripts drop and plain fields stay with explicit dropped marks not silent loss; dialog points to Risu .charx if rules matter. Concrete case: export to Agnai drops expression pack and maps linked lorebook to MemoryBook with regex key survival warning; SillyTavern or Risu keep both. Media chips show portrait expression pack and named assets before platform pick.

Press is the only way to export a lorebook persona or preset alone and the only multi-piece single run. Stage via right-click Stage for the Press or left rail; queue survives rooms. Staged characters auto-bring linked lorebooks as riders; drop a rider from this run without unlinking. One target for the whole queue. Press shows readiness not honesty: lorebooks check keywords immediately red if none amber if some missing; characters need target then show filled vs empty platform fields. Open in editor preserves queue spot. Run the press settles rows as printed skipped or failed; download the bundle is always a zip even for one piece once any row prints.

Export is character-only; stage other kinds for the Press even alone. Export becomes Export anyway on Note or Dropped as a soft warn. Press readiness is not honesty. Rename or pick txt/md flavor before run; fields lock after a result. Zero-keyword lorebooks read red and never fire; fix keywords first.

docs.title: Frequently asked questions
docs.summary: Straight answers on where your files live, what a convert actually keeps or drops, which apps Hoplight reads and writes, and whether converting or editing a card can damage it.
docs.semanticSummary: FAQ for privacy, convert survival, supported apps, and whether convert or edit can damage cards. Content is private: local loopback server 127.0.0.1, plain JSON studio folder default Documents/Hoplight Studio, no account cloud or telemetry; scripts import as text never run; deep access refused; fail-closed parse with zip-bomb caps. What converts: plain card fields and lorebook entries keys placement; private extras only on same-app round-trip; different app keeps shared model only and drops scripts when target cannot run them with Risu .charx keeping full rule pack; honesty view before export. Supported apps: SillyTavern RoleCall RisuAI Backyard/Faraday Agnai NovelAI Pygmalion Lumiverse Marinara and Chub with kind gaps; Chub is ST-shaped with extensions.chub; NovelAI lorebook only; Marinara regex and personas only; native JSON is studio storage not a convert target. Convert cannot damage cards: writes new files only, originals kept, import never overwrites, Workbench save is only overwrite path, whole-piece save preserves untouched fields, broken lorebooks heal on import, cross-app drops are named not corrupted.

anchors.summary: Four short answers. Content is private via local server plain JSON on disk no account cloud or telemetry. Converts keep plain card and lorebook structure; private extras only on same-app round-trip. Supported apps are SillyTavern RoleCall RisuAI Backyard/Faraday Agnai NovelAI Pygmalion Lumiverse Marinara and Chub though not every app carries every kind. Convert cannot damage a card: only writes new files, original kept, export shows travel before commit.

Yes. hoplight ui starts a local server bound to 127.0.0.1 loopback only. Pieces store as plain JSON one file per piece in a studio folder default Documents/Hoplight Studio unless pointed elsewhere. No sign-up or account; interface requests go only to that local server; no telemetry is collected. Import does not trust files: trigger scripts and regex are saved as text never run; deep access requests are refused with receipt notice. Uploads parse through fail-closed readers with caps against zip bombs so hostile files stop at we could not read this.

anchors.text: What converts, and what stays behind?
anchors.summary: Every convert goes through one shared middle model never direct app to app. Same-app round-trip is lossless via kept original including private extensions layout ids. Different app only shared part crosses: name description personality scenario greetings example messages for characters; lorebook entries keys placement. Target without a place drops trigger scripts regex virtual script and backdrop HTML on purpose never as inert baggage. Risu .charx keeps the full rule pack; plainer Agnai or legacy Backyard keep words not machinery. Export honesty view lists keep note drop before download; Press readiness shows filled target fields instead.

Nine apps covering four kinds character lorebook persona and regex set; the support figure is ground truth not a wishlist. Chub has no own wire format and is SillyTavern CCv2/v3 with extensions.chub. NovelAI has no character-card concept only lorebook. Marinara ships regex and personas only. Hoplight native JSON is local studio storage for every kind lossless by construction and is not a convert target in the table because pieces already are that format before converting elsewhere. Formats are drop-in folders so the list can grow without touching existing formats.

anchors.text: Can a convert damage my card?
anchors.summary: No. Worst case is leaving something out and telling you before export. Original is never overwritten by convert or import; Library keeps whole file; re-import makes a second piece with -2 id not a refresh; only Workbench edit and save overwrites on purpose. Editor saves whole piece so untouched fields escrow behavior media stay byte-identical; save is explicit Save or Ctrl+S with dirty flag. Slightly broken lorebooks heal on import with receipt listing fixes. Cross-app conversion drops fields it does not corrupt them; honesty names lines before commit. Original file in Library is the safety net.

Prefer same-app round-trip for full keep via original file. Read honesty view or readiness line before export for exact keep note drop. Studio folder is plain JSON one file per piece easy to back up. If scripts matter pick Risu .charx; leaner formats keep words not machinery. Lorebook entries without keywords never fire; Press flags red before export so fix keywords first.

docs.title: Get started
docs.summary: Install Hoplight, get through the four-question setup wizard, learn the rooms the Dock puts in front of you, and bring your first file into the Library.
docs.semanticSummary: Getting started covers release or source installation, the one-time first-run wizard, everyday Dock rooms, specialist catalog apps, and the Library's import and blank-character paths. Release builds are the shortest install; source use requires Bun 1.3+, clone, install, and bun run dev for the primary loopback server at 127.0.0.1:8321. Optional remote listeners stay off until enabled. The studio folder defaults to Documents/Hoplight Studio or a custom hoplight ui path. Wizard asks theme, one or more kinds to make, publish targets, and a palette or custom accent; Skip all uses defaults. Settings retains theme, the first selected kind as the initial Library deck, publish targets, and accent rather than the complete ordered make selection. Dock rooms are Workbench, Library, and Press with Settings pinned below; Docs and CSS Workshop are catalog tools. Import receipts write only checked pieces, while Start fresh creates, saves, and opens a blank character.

anchors.summary: Download a platform build from GitHub Releases, or install Bun 1.3+, clone Hoplight, and run bun install for source use. Open the app or use bun run dev for the primary loopback address at 127.0.0.1:8321. Studio JSON defaults under Documents/Hoplight Studio or a custom path. Complete or skip the wizard, then import through the Library door or create a blank character through Start fresh.

Wizard appears once when the Studio finds no completed setup; after finish or skip it never returns on its own. Four questions: light or dark, default Dark; one or more kinds to make, where the first pick controls the first Library deck and an empty choice falls back to Characters; publish targets as a multi-select populated from known formats, with Not sure as default; and a house-palette or custom accent, default Rose. Skip all fills remaining defaults and jumps to the You're set recap. Theme, the initial Library deck, publish targets, and accent remain editable afterward; the complete ordered kind selection is not a Settings field.

Dock is the side column of everyday app tiles. Workbench edits character lorebook persona regex preset or pack; Library browses six decks with counts views and the import door; Press ships only a staged queue to one selected target. Settings is pinned in the foot. The app catalog exposes included specialist tools such as Docs and CSS Workshop plus future apps such as Company; catalog-only tools are not ordinary Dock tiles. The configured home app controls normal launch, while a reload restores the active room when possible.

Empty studio primary door accepts drop or click file picker; after pieces exist drop anywhere on Library for the same flow. Files are read before write. Headings are Pick what to keep when all clean or Here is what we read when some fail. Readable files show receipt with name, kind, and default-checked checkbox; unreadable files show a plain reason without a checkbox. Add more files appends the batch, Import N writes only checked pieces, and Not now writes nothing. The second empty-studio door creates and saves a blank character, then opens it in the Workbench.

Release builds are the shortest installation path; Bun 1.3+ is required only for a source checkout. Skip all fills defaults, and retained setup choices remain editable. The first selected make kind chooses the initial Library deck; later the Library remembers the last open deck. Attached character lorebooks arrive in one bundle receipt. An unreadable receipt means safe parsing failed because the file may be unsupported, malformed, or damaged; hoplight formats lists adapters. hoplight ui port path selects another studio folder.

docs.title: Import a file
docs.summary: Bring a card, lorebook, persona, or regex set into the Library by dropping it on the shelves or clicking Import, and see exactly what the receipt keeps before anything is written.
docs.semanticSummary: User guide for importing cards lorebooks personas or regex sets into the Library. Nothing is written until confirmed; each file shows as a receipt first. Short flow: drop files on shelves or use Import to be guided to drop; read per-file receipt of name kind platform or failure reason without blocking others; uncheck unwanted then Import with live count; find piece on matching deck. Brand-new empty studio drop zone is also a clickable file browser, the only place outside active import that opens a browser; once pieces exist Import does not open a file browser. What gets kept: original file whole with unmapped private layout ids escrowed; slightly broken lorebooks heal with receipt listing fixes; scripts saved as text never run; deep access refused on receipt; personas not filed as characters; import never overwrites so re-import makes second piece with -2 id while Workbench save overwrites on purpose. Batch import reports each file alone; Add more files accumulates before one write; shelves route by kind not open deck. Tips: Import button only navigates to shelves; failed reads can retry after fix; uncheck before Import; read extras for embedded lorebook scripts deep access; update via Workbench not re-import.

anchors.summary: Drop one or more files on Library shelves; from elsewhere click Import or right-click Import files to go to shelves and drop; once studio has pieces Import does not open a file browser. Each file returns a receipt with name kind and platform or failure reason without blocking others. Uncheck unwanted; click Import with live count; Select all resets batch; Add more files reads another round into same overlay. Saved pieces land on kind decks character lorebook persona or regex. Empty studio drop zone is also a file browser button, the only place that happens outside active import.

Import reads into the shared studio model so the receipt knows the piece before write. Original file is kept whole; private layout ids and unmapped fields stay alongside for same-app export later. Slightly broken lorebooks with missing name or wrong entry shape are healed not rejected; receipt lists fixes and entry counts. Scripts on cards are saved as text never executed; deep access requests are refused with plain receipt; personas are shelved as personas not characters. Import never overwrites: same file twice yields two pieces with -2 on the second id; update via Workbench save which overwrites on purpose.

Drop many files and each is read alone. Overlay is Pick what to keep when all clean or Here is what we read when some fail; failures never block successes. Add more files appends into the same overlay so you accumulate before one Import. Route is by kind: a lorebook dropped on Characters still lands on Lorebooks.

Corner Import only takes you to shelves to drop; it does not browse files. Failed read is not final: fix in the source app and retry or check unsupported format. Uncheck receipt rows to skip without blocking the rest. Read character receipt extras for embedded lorebook scripts or deep access lines. To update an existing piece edit and save on the Workbench; re-import always makes a second copy never a refresh.

docs.title: Browse the Library
docs.summary: Filter pieces by kind on the Library's deck chips, switch between Grid, Show, List, and the deck-specific views, and stage one piece or many for a single send to the Workbench.
docs.semanticSummary: Browse the Library covers shelves of pieces already in the studio: six decks by kind, view modes, and staging one piece or a batch to the Workbench. Import is covered separately. The short version is pick a deck chip with live count among Characters Lorebooks Personas Sprite packs Presets Regex sets; pick Grid Show List or a deck-specific view and drag the art slider to resize cards live; stage by click for tray accent ring and check, click again to drop, tray survives deck switches; send bar Send it to the Workbench or Send all N, or right-click one piece to send without staging or stage for the Press. The decks and their views keep every chip visible even at count 0; status line reports active deck share; empty Lorebooks Regex Personas Presets offer New while Characters and Sprite packs are import-only; Grid Show List and Shelf run everywhere with Lorebook on/off Split Copy drag-merge and Regex rule count description slow flags, and off books or sets are skipped on export. Staging and sending never opens on tap; open Workbench pieces refuse restage; send bar has count Send and Clear; sending opens tabs and may navigate per Settings. Tips cover tray clear rules, Grid fallback, Shelf search scope, Personas dual Shelf icons, and import-only decks.

anchors.summary: Pick a deck chip among Characters Lorebooks Personas Sprite packs Presets Regex sets; each chip shows a live count.
