Pick a view: Grid Show and List sit in the toolbar on every deck and some decks add one more suited to their contents; the art slider beside them resizes cards live as you drag in Grid List and Show. Stage what you want by clicking a piece, or in Show click Stage for the Workbench, to add it to the tray with accent ring and corner check; click again to drop it; switch decks and the tray stays full so a persona and characters can travel together. Send it to the Workbench from the send bar for one piece or Send all N for a batch; right-click a single piece instead to send without staging first or to stage it for the Press.

Every deck chip shows even when empty at count 0 so the full studio shape stays visible. The status line reports active deck share of everything in the studio. Empty Lorebooks Regex sets Personas Presets offer a New button on the shelf; Characters and Sprite packs are import-only with no blank start. Grid Show and List behave the same on every deck: Grid is portrait cards, Show is one piece with tagline and description, List is dense rows. Shelf also runs everywhere as spine cards with name-or-key search; Lorebooks spines add on/off Split Copy and drag-to-merge onto another book; Regex Sets view adds rule count, a computed one-line description, and a quiet slow-rule flag. Turning a book or set off is not cosmetic; an off one is skipped on export.

Tapping a piece anywhere in the Library stages it and does not open it. A staged piece wears an accent ring; a piece already open on the Workbench wears a quiet on the workbench tag instead, and tapping that one only repeats the tag rather than toggling. The tray survives switching decks so you can pick a character from one chip and a lorebook from another before sending. The send bar appears only once something is staged; it carries the live count, the Send button, and Clear that empties the tray without sending. Sending opens every staged piece as its own tab and, depending on Workbench follow setting changeable in Settings, may take you there right away. You do not have to stage to move a single piece: right-click Send to the Workbench opens immediately, or Stage for the Press queues it for export on a separate queue from this tray, covered in Convert a card.

A piece already open on the Workbench cannot be re-staged; tapping it only tells you it is already there. The staged tray persists across deck switches and only empties when you send it or click Clear. Switch to a deck your current view does not support and the toolbar falls back to Grid, not the prior view. The Shelf view search box narrows what is on screen; it does not touch the chip count or the deck actual total. Personas carry two toolbar buttons that both read Shelf; go by the icon not the label, person icon for the persona-tailored view and bookcase icon for plain spine search. Characters and Sprite packs have no New button on an empty deck; import is the only way in for those two.

docs.title: Build a lorebook
docs.summary: Add entries to a lorebook, give each one the keywords that trigger it, and decide where it lands in the assembled prompt.
docs.semanticSummary: Build a lorebook covers writing entries, keying them to fire, and placing them in the assembled prompt. Other apps call this world info, character book, or memory. The short version is create or open a lorebook, add a blank entry from the binder, give it Keys chips or switch Always on or By meaning, place it on the Where rail at World Character or a richer host stop, then Save or ctrl+s. Keywords and triggers fire one of three ways: Keywords default on recent chat, Always on every turn, By meaning by similarity only for Hoplight or SillyTavern; Advanced adds Only together with AND/NOT sets, regex chance, and min messages between activations; whole-word and case defaults inherit from Book rules with per-entry override; Keywords with no keys never fires and health flags it. Where it lands is after scan chance cooldown sticky delay and optional recursion budgets; World and Character are the portable floor; richer stops under Hoplight, subset on SillyTavern, World Character only on Chub Lumiverse Agnai, and Risu NovelAI force character floor; foreign positions stay marked and export to closest slot. Building the book covers TOC Always on and Entries with health pips, bulk Select, Book rules defaults, Writing for host lens that hides not deletes, and Knowledge rail Attach lorebook. Tips cover new entry defaults, Try a line, Wake map, Always on portability, and full check Fix all.

anchors.summary: Create or open a lorebook from the Library with New lorebook on an empty shelf or open one you already have. Add an entry in the binder with + New entry in the table of contents; a blank entry starts with no keywords so it will not fire until you give it one. Open the Keys card and type a word then Enter or comma to add a chip; switch the entry to Always on or By meaning instead if you do not want keyword dependence. Place it via When and where then Where and pick a stop on the rail: World, Character, or a richer position your target host supports. Save with the Save button or press ctrl+s.

Each entry Keys card holds primary keywords typed one at a time as chips. An entry fires one of three ways picked per entry: Keywords default when a key shows in recent chat; Always on skips matching and injects every turn; By meaning fires on similarity to chat rather than exact word and only survives writing for the Hoplight lens or SillyTavern since no other host on Writing for carries it. Switch Keys to Advanced for a second optional set under Only together with, combined against primary by AND any, AND all, NOT any, or NOT all; Advanced also exposes regex with flags, per-key chance, and a minimum messages wait between activations. Whole-word and case-sensitive matching default from Book rules and can be overridden per entry; each toggle cycles inherit, on, off. An entry set to Keywords with no keywords never fires; health check flags it; brand-new entries start that way so give at least one key or leave Keywords.

A key clearing the scan window is only the first gate. Chance, cooldown, sticky, and delay still must pass, and if recursion is on one entry text can wake another entry keys under the same rules. If the book token or entry budget is full a fired entry can still be cut. What survives lands at the Where rail position, with depth and role when that position is Depth or Append which behave the same. World and Character are the portable floor every write host keeps. Richer stops Scene Depth Append Top Bottom Before example After example are only under Hoplight; SillyTavern keeps World Character Depth Before example After example; Chub Lumiverse Agnai keep World and Character only; Risu and NovelAI have no placement dial and every entry lands on the character floor. Pick a position your host does not carry and the rail keeps it marked foreign so export lands at the closest slot instead of losing it.

The table of contents groups entries into Always on and Entries, is searchable, and reorders by dragging rows only while not searching or in Select mode. A colored pip shows health: green ready, amber worth a look, red problem, grey off. Click Select to pick several entries at once and turn them on or off, delete them, or move them into a new book. Book rules behind the header link hold book-level defaults every entry inherits: name description case sensitivity whole words recursion global scan depth token or entry budget and named categories. Writing for next to it switches which fields the binder shows to match the export host; it never deletes anything, only hides what that host cannot carry. A lorebook sits alone in the Library until you attach it to a character or persona on the Knowledge rail with Attach lorebook; reorder or detach there. A staged character brings attached lorebooks along automatically when you run the press.

A new entry starts on World at 100 percent chance with no keywords; nothing is broken, it just will not do anything until you key it. Use Try a line on the binder right rail to paste a sample chat line and see exactly which entries fire and why using the same matcher real chat uses. Wake map on the same rail shows which entries can wake your focused entry through recursion and which it can wake in turn. Always on works on every host; By meaning does not, so check Writing for before you rely on it. Open the full check from the rail to see every finding across the book at once, with Fix all where a fix is safe to apply automatically.

docs.title: Create and manage personas
docs.summary: Build a persona on the Workbench from identity and sections or flat text, set where it injects and what it links to, and know the few places it behaves differently from a character.
docs.semanticSummary: Create and manage personas covers building your side of the fiction, the identity a target app shows as user. Only name and text are required; tagline pronouns portrait colors linked lorebook and injection are optional. The short version is New persona on the Personas deck saves Untitled persona and opens Workbench; fill name tagline pronouns height age plus sections Appearance Body Personality Quirks History or flat Identity Text; Write for defaults Hoplight and can narrow the form without deleting; set Prompt Injection and Knowledge lorebook; Save; star as default and stage for Press to ship. What actually reaches the model treats Content as fallback: any filled section ignores Identity Text; Body folds into Appearance; Identity always leads; Brief never crosses; labeled colors compile as tags; Live Preview is the real compiler. Where it's injected, and what travels with it lists RoleCall or SillyTavern stops under Write for; platforms with no wire hide the card; foreign stops show dashed kept; Knowledge attaches lorebooks but export carries only the top reference as an id not entries, and staging a persona never pulls the book as a rider; default star is studio shelf only. Converting and exporting a persona has no editor Export button; stage and run Press as solo row; Agnai skips; SillyTavern backup keeps sealed siblings. Tips restate sections beat flat text, Brief shelf only, Write for hide not delete, first lorebook only, Press for files.

anchors.summary: On the Personas deck click New persona from the shelf tile or empty deck button; it saves immediately as Untitled persona and opens on the Workbench. Fill who you are with name tagline pronouns height and age, then write section fields Appearance Body Personality Quirks History or, if you have no use for sections, flat Identity Text. Narrow to one host if building for one: Write for in the header defaults to Hoplight the full card; pick a platform and the form drops to only what that wire carries without deleting. Set where it is injected and link a lorebook if needed in the right-hand Prompt Injection card and the Knowledge card on the left. Save with Ctrl+s or Save like any piece. Star it as default if you want the shelf to flag it, then stage for the Press when ready to ship as a file.

Content is the fallback not a second copy. Fill even one section and the compiler ignores Identity Text entirely; it only wakes once every section is empty. Body has its own card for physical specifics but folds into the Appearance tag when compiled and never gets a tag of its own. Identity always leads: pronouns tagline height and age are not a section; they compile first ahead of whatever section order you set every time. Brief never crosses: it is the library-card blurb on the Personas shelf only and never enters the injected block; voice lines belong in a section or Identity Text. Full sections leave old Identity Text inert not deleted. Switch Write for to Agnai and sections traits palette and injection leave the form; switch back and everything remains. Labeled colors compile one tag per color from the label. Live Preview always shows this exact output as the real compiler not a mock.

anchors.text: Where it's injected, and what travels with it
anchors.summary: The Prompt Injection card lists stops your Write for lens carries: RoleCall four World Character Scene Depth or SillyTavern five In prompt Note top Note bottom In chat None; a platform with no injection wire such as Lumiverse or Marinara hides the card. Depth and In chat both ask for a depth number; In chat also asks role system user or assistant. A stop set under a different lens shows dashed amber disabled labeled kept not carried here so foreign choices stay visible. None of this makes Vaud chat; it decides where the target app places the block on export. Knowledge attaches reorders and detaches linked lorebooks like a character; SillyTavern RoleCall and Lumiverse each carry a single lorebook reference not a list so only the top one crosses as an id the target should already have; entries do not ride in the persona file and staging a persona for Press never pulls the book as a rider. The star Set as default persona only flags the gilt Default badge on the shelf; nothing else in Vaud reads it automatically.

A persona editor carries no Export button unlike a character. To get a file out right-click Stage for the Press or click it on the Press left rail pick a target and run the press as in Convert a card. A staged persona always runs as its own solo row; it never bundles the way a character and linked lorebooks do. A target with no persona wire such as Agnai prints a skip row because Agnai has no persona format; its structured persona lives on a character card not as its own file. SillyTavern keeps every persona in a single Personas backup file not one file each. Import that backup and Vaud reads the default persona or the first if none marked as the editable piece; every other persona stays whole and sealed inside not shown as its own Library piece. Export back from that piece re-emits sealed ones untouched alongside your edit. There is currently no way to pull one sealed persona out on its own.

Sections beat Identity Text the moment any one of them has text; clear every section if you want old flat text gone not just hidden. Brief lives on the shelf only; keep the one-line blurb there and put real voice in a section or Identity Text. A Write for pick only narrows what you see; nothing is deleted; click Hoplight to see the whole card again. Only the first linked lorebook crosses on export; reorder the Knowledge card if a different book should travel. There is no Export button on a persona own editor; stage it and run it through the Press when you want a file out.

docs.title: Agnai
docs.summary: Bringing Agnai character JSON and memory books into Hoplight and back out.
docs.semanticSummary: Agnai also known as Agnaistic stores characters in its own JSON shape with a structured persona map, not SillyTavern shape. What Hoplight reads: character .json only no png option, and memory books as standalone or embedded .json; drop on Library for a plain-words receipt recognized by structured persona plus greeting shape. What comes across cleanly keeps the original whole and lifts name description version culture personality structured or plain scenario appearance greetings examples system post-history prefill one depth injection creator tags voice avatar or sprite recipe image-gen affixes structured response schema as data only and embedded memory book. What changes when you convert to another app: same-app round-trip keeps untouched fields byte for byte except persona always rebuilt from the editor so multi-block plain personality collapses to first; cross-app keeps shared character and drops sampler provider account layout private settings; no regex feature either way. Editing on the Workbench has dedicated controls for structured persona voice sprite image-gen and schema. Exporting back out stages through the Press as .json with embedded book riding; txt md available. Common questions cover round-trip exception no png structured persona location sprite voice and memory book pull-edit-put-back.

anchors.summary: Hoplight reads the two file types Agnai gives you. Characters as a .json file; Agnai does not embed a card inside a picture the way SillyTavern does so there is no .png option to bring in. Memory books Agnai name for lorebook or worldbook as a .json file either standalone or embedded inside a character. Drag the file onto the Library and drop anywhere; Hoplight shows a plain-words receipt of what it read and kept. It recognizes an Agnai character by its own shape a structured persona plus a greeting not by the file name. Full walkthrough lives in the importing guide.

Importing loses nothing. Hoplight keeps a complete original card then lifts editable fields: name description version label; culture or language for default voice; personality as plain text or Agnai structured persona map via W++ boostyle square-bracket or attribute list; scenario and separate appearance for image generation; first message alternate greetings example messages; system prompt post-history instructions assistant prefill; one depth injection with more editable on Workbench but only first travels to Agnai; creator tags voice selection; avatar image or layered sprite recipe; image-generation prefix suffix negative template; structured response schema as data only never run; embedded memory book entries keywords placement. Card picture when present is the piece portrait. Listed fields ready to edit; the rest held safely in the background.

anchors.text: What changes when you convert to another app
anchors.summary: Same-app round-trip keeps everything you did not touch byte for byte because Hoplight kept the original and only rewrites changed fields. One exception: Agnai persona is always rebuilt fresh from the editor so multi-block plain-text personality collapses to the first block even on straight Agnai round trip. Converting to another app drops Agnai-only extras on purpose. Core character name description personality scenario appearance greetings examples system post-history prefill creator tags come across as far as the target holds. Structured persona voice sprite image-gen affixes schema memory book and depth injection come across only if the target has matching slots. Sampler provider settings inside image config account id and saved layout stay on same-app and drop cross-app. Another app means SillyTavern RoleCall Risu Backyard Pygmalion and similar. Agnai has no regex-key feature so nothing carries either way.

Send a piece from the Library to the Workbench and it opens as a tab. Edit name description personality scenario first message and example messages the same as any character. Agnai extras get dedicated controls too: structured persona map voice sprite recipe image-generation affixes and response schema each have an editor so you are never stuck hand-editing raw JSON. When you save Hoplight writes the whole card back so parts you did not touch stay exactly as they were.

Stage a ready piece for the Press via right-click Stage for the Press or the Press rail. The Press works only staged pieces and each run exports to one target format you pick. Hoplight writes Agnai cards as .json the same shape Agnai exports. An embedded memory book rides along with the character automatically. You can also ask for plain .txt or .md when you just want to read the text. Choosing a different app as target applies the convert drop story above.

Will the card come back exactly as it was? Yes on export to Agnai except multi-entry plain-text persona collapses to first because persona is rebuilt from the editor. Agnai does not give a .png card; native export is JSON only so Hoplight never offers a picture for it. Structured persona still there: W++ boostyle or attribute map goes to structured persona editor while plain text lands in ordinary personality. Sprite voice and image-generation settings keep full on same-app round-trip and are editable; cross-app only if matching slots exist. Agnai has no regex scripts like SillyTavern so nothing carries either way. Embedded memory book is pulled for solo edit and put back on export to apps that support memory books or worldbooks.

docs.title: Backyard
docs.summary: Bringing Backyard.ai's two character card shapes, the older flat JSON export and the modern .byaf archive, into Hoplight and back out.
docs.semanticSummary: Backyard.ai formerly Faraday ships two character shapes and Hoplight reads and writes both. What Hoplight reads: older flat JSON with aiName aiPersona customDialogue keys, and modern .byaf zip of character scenarios and images; two separate adapters tell them apart by content not rename. What comes across cleanly keeps the original and lifts display name nickname description personality scenario system first message examples creator tags from flat JSON; from .byaf also alternate greetings portrait gallery background content rating as explicit or all-ages source dates; flat JSON rewrites single-brace placeholders to double braces while .byaf text is untouched. What changes when you convert to another app treats same-shape round-trip as full keep but moving between Backyard shapes counts as conversion like a different app so personality does not travel flat-to-byaf and byaf-only media rating dates drop on legacy; lore items not yet lifted to editable lorebook. Editing on the Workbench covers core fields with whole-card save. Exporting back out offers Backyard .byaf and Backyard legacy JSON as two Press targets. Common questions cover same-shape exact return, picture only on byaf, placeholder rewrite rules, and lore items stay escrowed.

anchors.summary: Hoplight reads both shapes Backyard has shipped. The older flat JSON export from Faraday-era versions is a plain .json with keys like aiName aiPersona and customDialogue. The modern .byaf archive is a zip that bundles the character one or more scenarios and any images together. These are not two names for the same thing; each has its own vocabulary and two separate adapters. Drop either on the Library; Hoplight looks inside a .byaf by zip signature and manifest shape and flat JSON by Backyard-only keys so renaming does not confuse it. Full walkthrough lives in the importing guide.

Importing loses nothing. Hoplight keeps a complete original then lifts editable parts. From older flat JSON: display name and separate nickname when short char name differs; description and personality as two fields; scenario system prompt first message example messages creator tags and optional version tag. From a .byaf archive: display name nickname single description no separate personality; scenario from primary narrative; system first message alternate greetings examples; avatar-labeled or first image as portrait other images as gallery; scenario background; creator source URL created and updated dates; content rating as explicit or all-ages only because byaf stores a plain NSFW switch so mature never comes from Backyard import. Across both shapes Backyard placeholders are single braces; flat JSON rewrites to double braces on the way in while .byaf text comes across exactly as written without rewrite.

anchors.text: What changes when you convert to another app
anchors.summary: Same-shape round-trip keeps everything: flat JSON to flat JSON or .byaf to .byaf because Hoplight kept the original and only rewrites changed fields. Moving between the two Backyard shapes counts as conversion not same-app: only listed shared fields cross. Personality is the clearest case; flat JSON keeps it but .byaf has one persona field so personality does not travel on export to byaf. Alternate greetings portrait gallery background content rating source dates keep on byaf round-trip and drop on flat JSON which has none of them. Lore items sampler generation settings prompt template grammar chat transcript and other Backyard extras without a canonical slot stay on same-shape and drop elsewhere. Lore items stay on the twin but are not yet lifted into an editable lorebook so they do not cross into another app lore fields. Another app includes SillyTavern RoleCall Agnai Risu and the other Backyard shape.

Send a piece from the Library to the Workbench and it opens as a tab. Edit name nickname description personality scenario first message and any alternate greetings and example messages. When you save Hoplight writes the whole card back so parts you did not touch stay exactly as they were.

Stage a ready piece for the Press via right-click or the Press rail. Each run exports staged pieces to one target you pick. Backyard shows as two targets: Backyard for modern .byaf and Backyard legacy for flat JSON. Hoplight writes .byaf as a zip and legacy as .json. Pick the target that matches where the card is going; the other applies the drop story like a different app. Plain .txt or .md copies are available for reading text only.

Will the card come back exactly as it was? Yes only when exported to the exact import shape; switching shapes follows the same crossing rule as a different app. Imported .byaf returns as .byaf only if you pick Backyard; Backyard legacy writes flat JSON and drops alternate greetings images background and content rating. Pictures ride on .byaf round-trip including gallery; flat JSON has no image archive. Flat JSON single-brace placeholders convert to double braces on read and only re-convert if you edited the field; .byaf text is never touched that way. Archive lore items stay attached on .byaf round-trip but are not yet lifted into an editable lorebook so they will not cross into another app lore fields.

docs.title: Chub
docs.summary: Bringing Chub character cards and lorebooks into Hoplight and back out.
docs.semanticSummary: Chub also called CharacterHub hosts SillyTavern-shaped Character Card v2/v3 files with an extensions.chub block for site extras. What Hoplight reads: character .png or .json recognized as SillyTavern shape plus chub extras, and lorebooks as bare character_book entry arrays standalone or embedded; origin labeled Chub when extras give it away. What comes across cleanly keeps the original and lifts core fields embedded worldbook expressions when present Chub extras background CSS bound preset related lorebook links plus id path Stages references escrowed not yet editable. What changes when you convert to another app: same-app Chub or SillyTavern round-trip keeps everything; cross-app drops Chub private extras; standalone Chub lorebook has no write-back twin and always exports as plain SillyTavern worldbook. Editing on the Workbench shows Chub-tagged cards CSS Workshop sealed preview and Write for Chub narrows lorebook placement. Exporting back out writes CCv3 JSON with chub bag; lorebooks not a Chub target. Common questions cover exact return JSON not PNG portrait extras worldbook and no byte-identical lorebook download.

anchors.summary: Hoplight reads Chub character cards as .png with text inside the image or plain .json. It does not treat Chub as its own wire format: it recognizes the SillyTavern shape underneath and keeps the extensions.chub block that rides along. Lorebooks arrive as .json embedded in a card or standalone from Chub lorebook shelf; standalone downloads are a bare character_book entry array not SillyTavern keyed worldbook map, and Hoplight recognizes that shape too. Drop on the Library for a plain-words receipt calling origin Chub CharacterHub when extras give it away; recognition is by inside content not filename. Full walkthrough lives in the importing guide.

Importing loses nothing. Hoplight keeps a complete original then lifts name description personality scenario greetings examples system post-history creator notes tags embedded worldbook expression images when present and Chub extras chat background custom CSS bound preset related lorebook links. Card picture becomes the piece portrait. Chub extras show as their own Workbench cards with a Chub tag. A few more bits ride along not yet editable: Chub id full path and Stages scenario-builder references; Hoplight keeps them on the twin for round trip. Standalone lorebook entries keywords and placement come across editable like any lorebook.

anchors.text: What changes when you convert to another app
anchors.summary: Character same-app round-trip keeps everything down to the byte because Hoplight kept the original and only rewrote changed fields. Converting to a different app drops Chub private extras on purpose: chat background custom CSS bound preset related-lorebook links Chub id path Stages. Core character and embedded worldbook come across as far as the target holds; expressions if the target has extra art slots. SillyTavern gets the identical result as Chub since they share file shape. Another app means genuinely different targets like Agnai Backyard RoleCall Risu Pygmalion. Standalone lorebook wrinkle: no back to Chub option and no twin because Chub never gave downloads a write-back wire format only borrowed character_book shape so Hoplight always writes plain SillyTavern worldbook or another lore format; entries keywords placement survive not the original wrapper.

Send a piece to the Workbench as a tab and edit core character fields the same as any card; save writes the whole card so untouched parts stay. Cards with a Chub bag show Chub-tagged cards for chat background bound preset and related-lorebook links. Custom CSS opens in the CSS Workshop sealed preview mocked to Chub chat-bubble classes never applied to Hoplight interface. Open a lorebook and Write for Chub narrows to character_book floor emphasizing priority secondary triggers and before-character after-character placement only; hiding never deletes fields.

Stage for the Press via right-click or rail; each run exports staged pieces to one target. Chub is a character target writing the same file SillyTavern would get: .json CCv3 with extensions.chub bag if present. Embedded worldbook rides automatically. Plain .txt or .md available for text. Chub is not a lorebook target; export standalone lorebooks as SillyTavern or another lorebook-capable app instead. Other app targets apply the drop story.

Will the card come back exactly as it was? Yes when exported to Chub or SillyTavern since both read the same shape. Imported .png returns as .json which both apps load like a picture. Character picture is kept as portrait and the original import file is held. Background and custom CSS stay with Chub extras and are not copied into another app. Embedded worldbook is pulled for solo edit and put back on export to worldbook-capable apps. Standalone Chub lorebook download never returns byte-identical; no save-back format so entries keywords placement write as plain SillyTavern worldbook.

docs.title: Lumiverse
docs.summary: Bringing Lumiverse character cards, expression archives, personas, and regex scripts into Hoplight and back out.
docs.semanticSummary: Lumiverse cards ride SillyTavern-shaped JSON or PNG plus Lumiverse-only expression images alternate faces text persona and regex export. What Hoplight reads: character .png or .json, .charx archive with expressions alternate faces and baked regex, persona .json dump, and standalone regex .json; detect by Lumiverse-only keys not filename. What comes across cleanly keeps the original and lifts core fields talkativeness linked world embedded worldbook portrait resolved expression images and alternate text or faces as variants; unresolved image refs stay plain text never guessed. What changes when you convert to another app: same-app JSON keeps fields unchanged and .charx may re-path files inside the archive; cross-app drops variants regex TTS LoRA databank ids layout while core and worldbook cross as far as target holds. Editing on the Workbench uses portrait variant strip Manage Sprites and Lumiverse-tagged extras with world-book ids read-only for later lore editor work. Exporting back out keeps container JSON or charx by default and refuses JSON when archive files would strand. Common questions cover round-trip paths expressions variants scripts and persona dump.

anchors.summary: Hoplight reads four Lumiverse outputs. Character cards as .png or .json like SillyTavern. A Lumiverse archive as .charx packing the card expression images alternate faces and any regex scripts as separate files inside rather than inline. A persona as a .json dump of one account persona with name title description and pronouns. A set of regex scripts as standalone .json separate from any card. Drop on the Library for a plain-words receipt. It tells Lumiverse from plain SillyTavern by Lumiverse-only keys inside data not by filename so renaming does not confuse. Full walkthrough lives in the importing guide.

Importing loses nothing. Hoplight keeps a complete original card and for an archive every file inside then lifts name description personality scenario greetings examples system post-history creator notes tags talkativeness linked world name embedded worldbook portrait art and expression images the archive carried plus alternate description personality scenario or face as variants. An expression image becomes editable art only when bytes are found embedded or in the same archive; a missing file reference stays plain text and Hoplight never guesses. Card picture is the piece portrait. Listed fields ready to edit; the rest held safely in the background.

anchors.text: What changes when you convert to another app
anchors.summary: Same-app JSON round-trip returns every field unchanged because Hoplight kept the original and only rewrote changed fields. A .charx round-trip keeps every image alternate face and script though paths inside the archive may be regenerated; Lumiverse reads its manifest so the card still opens. Plain JSON has no layout to shift so it comes back closer to original. Converting to another app drops Lumiverse private extras: alternate faces and text variants for now since no other write target reads variants yet; regex baked into archive; TTS voice LoRA hint attached world-book and databank ids alternate character name internal ids layout. Core character worldbook and resolved images come across as far as the target holds. Another app means SillyTavern Agnai Backyard RoleCall Risu. The drop is deliberate never blind-copy private scripts or settings.

Send a piece to the Workbench as a tab and edit core character fields like any card. The portrait card carries a variant strip with Base plus one tile per alternate version; click a tile to edit that variant text or art or add with plus. Manage Sprites opens the pack editor when expression images exist. Lumiverse-tagged fields sit alongside: alternate character name image-gen LoRA TTS voice attached world-book and databank ids read-only full lore editor is later work and a catch-all. Save writes the whole card so untouched parts stay.

Stage for the Press; each run exports staged pieces to one target. Export to Lumiverse keeps the container the card came in: .json stays .json and archive returns as .charx with edited images faces and scripts packed back. You can ask for the other container. Asking .json after an archive import refuses rather than silently drop stranded files; that check can still trip after removing fields that pointed at them. Plain .txt or .md is available for JSON output not for .charx. Other app targets apply the drop story.

Will the card come back exactly as it was? Yes on export to Lumiverse unedited: plain JSON fields unchanged; archive keeps image and script bytes though internal paths may regenerate which Lumiverse does not mind. Imported archive returns .charx by default; ask for .json and Hoplight refuses rather than drop archive-only files. Picture and resolved expression images come across as portrait and editable art. Alternate faces and text fold into variants on the portrait card and fold back on Lumiverse export. Regex baked into archive stay with the card and do not copy cross-app; standalone regex is its own piece. Persona .json dumps import name title description pronouns with everything else on the twin for round-trip.

docs.title: Marinara
docs.summary: Bringing Marinara-Engine regex scripts and personas into Hoplight and back out.
docs.semanticSummary: Marinara-Engine has no import export screen of its own; Hoplight takes server dumps of regex scripts and personas. Character cards are SillyTavern-shaped and go through the SillyTavern page with a Marinara tab not this page. What Hoplight reads: bare .json regex arrays matching GET regex-scripts and persona objects with sections theming and stats; detect by Marinara-only marks like targetCharacterIds order ai_output or nameColor personaStats. What comes across cleanly lifts full regex row fields with timestamps escrowed and persona name description sections comment avatar while theming stat bars crop tags scenario ride sealed. What changes when you convert to another app keeps same-app everything; regex crosses to apps with regex slots ST RoleCall Risu Lumiverse and skips Agnai Backyard; personas to ST RoleCall Lumiverse only with theming stats dropped. Editing on the Workbench narrows Writing for Marinara and flags Hoplight-only regex controls. Exporting back out writes .json only. Common questions cover exact return character path sealed theming Writing for hide and character targets.

anchors.summary: Hoplight reads two bare .json file types from Marinara-Engine. Regex scripts as an array one row per script matching GET /regex-scripts. Personas as an object with sections comment avatar theming and stat bars. A Marinara character card is different: SillyTavern-shaped so it comes and goes through the SillyTavern page with Marinara-only fields like stat bars and tracker colors under a dedicated Marinara tab not here. Recognition looks inside not name: regex dumps need targetCharacterIds order or placement values like ai_output or user_input that SillyTavern regex never has; personas need id name description personality plus at least one theming or stat key like nameColor or personaStats. Drop on the Library. Full walkthrough lives in the importing guide.

Importing loses nothing. For a regex script Hoplight lifts pattern replacement flags trim strings where it runs input output or both prompt-only depth window character limits on/off and order; row created and updated timestamps ride in the background only. For a persona it lifts name description first-person voice comment as short blurb appearance personality backstory sections and avatar. Marinara persona extras per-persona chat theming name dialogue box colors stat bars avatar crop tags and scenario have no shared home so they ride sealed in the background and return exactly on export back to Marinara rather than being dropped.

anchors.text: What changes when you convert to another app
anchors.summary: Same-app round-trip keeps everything for both kinds because Hoplight kept the original and only rewrites changed fields. Regex scripts cross as far as the target regex engine holds; timestamps drop cross-app. A regex only lands if the target has a regex slot: SillyTavern RoleCall Risu Lumiverse do; Agnai or Backyard do not so Press skips the piece for that run. Personas keep name description sections comment avatar on cross-app as far as the target holds; chat theming stat bars avatar crop tags scenario and Marinara persona id drop. Fewer apps take personas: only SillyTavern RoleCall Lumiverse; converting to Risu Agnai Backyard skips the piece. The drop is deliberate never blind-copy theming stats or scripts.

A regex set opens as one rule per page in a table of contents with pattern replacement flags where it fires and fine print for the rest. Writing for Marinara narrows fine print to depth window and character targets and hides controls with no place like macro substitution and run-on-edit. Three Hoplight-only controls show under every lens flagged not portable: first match only overlay and conditional chaining. A persona opens with name portrait section tiles appearance personality History for backstory full first-person text and live injection preview. Writing for Marinara narrows to name sections avatar and hides color palette and injection-position picker because Marinara wire has no place for them; sealed theming and stats only reappear on export back to Marinara. Save writes the whole set or persona so untouched parts stay.

Stage for the Press via right-click or rail; each run exports staged pieces to one target. Hoplight writes both Marinara regex sets and personas as .json the only shape Marinara understands. Plain .txt or .md copies are available for reading text. Choosing a different app applies the drop story: regex to apps with regex slots personas to apps with persona slots each dropping what the target cannot hold.

Will regex or persona come back exactly as it was? Yes on export to Marinara-Engine same app in same app out. Marinara character cards go through the SillyTavern page not this one including stat bars and tracker colors under a Marinara tab. Persona colors and stat bars still ride sealed in the background and return untouched on export to Marinara. Writing for strip narrows the editor to what the platform wire carries so you never fill fields thrown away on export; switch to Hoplight lens for every field. Character targets on regex are kept; empty list means applies to everyone same as the wire.

docs.title: NovelAI
docs.summary: Bringing NovelAI lorebooks into Hoplight and back out.
docs.semanticSummary: NovelAI has no character-card concept; the only portable file is a lorebook .lorebook plain JSON underneath. What Hoplight reads: .lorebook or same-shaped .json by version and entries list not filename; imports always land as standalone lorebook pieces never characters. What comes across cleanly keeps the original and lifts entry title passage keywords including inline /regex/ enabled always-on scan distance placement category book categories key-relative and non-story toggles context wrap budget settings and phrase bias groups; book settings folders ride in background. What changes when you convert to another app keeps same-app everything; cross-app keeps shared entry core and categories only where RoleCall Risu have them while NovelAI-only dials drop; scan distance number can cross into message units unchanged not a bug. Editing on the Workbench uses the lorebook binder and Writing for NovelAI surfaces private dials. Exporting back out writes .lorebook; reverse convert uses blank-entry defaults. Common questions cover exact return no character cards regex keywords unnamed books and private dials stay on NovelAI export.

anchors.summary: Hoplight reads NovelAI native lorebook export as a .lorebook file or plain .json with the same shape. It recognizes by looking inside at version number and entries list not by file name. Because NovelAI has no character card dropping one in never produces a character; it lands in the Library as a standalone lorebook piece. Drag onto the Library for a plain-words receipt of what it read and kept. Full walkthrough lives in the importing guide.

Importing loses nothing. Hoplight keeps a complete original lorebook then lifts each entry title and passage; keywords including inline /regex/ patterns; enabled and always-on; scan distance and placement order; category assignment and the book list of categories; two NovelAI-only activation toggles key-relative match and non-story fire; context wrap and budget settings framing text token budget trim behavior; phrase bias groups nudging words while active. Book-level settings and folder details ride safely in the background with the original file so nothing is thrown away even without a field.

anchors.text: What changes when you convert to another app
anchors.summary: Same-app round-trip keeps everything because Hoplight kept the original and only rewrites entries you changed. Converting to another app drops NovelAI private dials: key-relative and non-story toggles context wrap budget phrase bias book-level settings folders internal ids. Core entry title passage keywords enabled always-on scan distance placement order come across as far as the target holds. Category assignment comes across only if the target has categories or folders RoleCall Risu; dropped elsewhere. Another app means SillyTavern RoleCall Risu Agnai; plain apps without lorebook format like Backyard or Pygmalion are never offered as lorebook targets. Honest unit note: NovelAI scan distance is characters of story text; an app that counts messages reads the same number unchanged so 1000 characters can land as 1000 messages after convert, a unit mismatch not a bug.

Send a lorebook to the Workbench and it opens on its binder with a table of contents and the focused entry on the page. Edit title passage and keywords there. Save writes back only what changed so untouched entries stay exact. Pick Writing for NovelAI and NovelAI dials rise: activation toggles context wrap budget and phrase bias; fields other apps use fold away without deleting. Switch Writing for back to Hoplight and everything is still there.

Stage for the Press via right-click or rail. Since NovelAI has no character card a lorebook staged alone prints by itself; a lorebook already linked to a character rides with that character. Hoplight writes .lorebook. Choosing a different app applies the drop story. Reverse convert into NovelAI from another app builds each entry on NovelAI blank-entry defaults the same starting point NovelAI uses for a new entry so the file loads clean.

Will the lorebook come back exactly as it was? Yes on export to NovelAI with only touched entries rewritten. NovelAI has no character cards Hoplight can read; every import is a standalone lorebook. Inline /regex/ keywords are kept as regex not flattened. An imported book may show no name because NovelAI export carries no book-level name; name it in Library or Workbench and it sticks. Phrase bias and context wrap do not survive another app; they stay untouched on export back to NovelAI.

docs.title: Pygmalion
docs.summary: Bringing Pygmalion's classic flat character JSON into Hoplight and back out.
docs.semanticSummary: Pygmalion is the classic five-field flat character format before Character Card V2: name persona scenario greeting example dialogue as .json or text inside .png. What Hoplight reads: either container by true Pygmalion shape so SillyTavern PNG cards are not mistaken. What comes across cleanly keeps the original and lifts the five fields with persona also shown as description; PNG portrait kept; tool bookkeeping version timestamp tool name rides in background. What changes when you convert to another app keeps same-app everything including folding edits into a fresh PNG when imported as PNG; cross-app has little private extras to drop beyond tool stamps. Editing on the Workbench: description mirrors persona but edit personality to change how the character reads on export. Exporting back out writes .json or folds into PNG only from a Pygmalion PNG you gave it; fold failure falls back to JSON. Common questions cover exact return PNG rules recognition thresholds and bookkeeping drop.

anchors.summary: Hoplight reads Pygmalion classic cards in either container: a .json five-field document alone or a .png with the same text tucked inside the picture like SillyTavern cards. Drop on the Library for a plain-words receipt. Recognition looks inside not filename. A picture can hide several card shapes so Hoplight checks the tucked text is genuinely Pygmalion before claiming the file and never mistakes a real SillyTavern card for Pygmalion just because both hide text the same way. Full walkthrough lives in the importing guide.

Importing loses nothing. Hoplight keeps a complete original then lifts name; persona the one blob of who they are and how they act also shown as description so description-only views still have text; scenario; greeting opening line; example dialogue. If the card arrived as .png the picture is the piece portrait. Some exporters stamp version timestamp tool name bookkeeping with no field so it rides untouched in the background. After import the five fields are ready to edit and the rest is held safely.

anchors.text: What changes when you convert to another app
anchors.summary: Same-app round-trip keeps everything because Hoplight kept the original and only rewrote changed fields. If the card came as .png exporting back to Pygmalion folds possibly edited fields into a fresh copy of that same picture. Converting to another app drops little: classic wire never carried extensions scripts tags or system prompt so there is no large private pile. Core five fields come across as far as the target holds. Tool bookkeeping drops cross-app. Picture comes across if the target has a slot. Another app means SillyTavern Agnai Backyard RoleCall Risu. The drop is deliberate though for Pygmalion there is rarely much private to drop.

Send a piece to the Workbench as a tab and edit name personality scenario first message and example messages. Description mirrors persona for display but on a Pygmalion piece is read-only in effect: editing description alone without personality will not reach the card on export so edit personality when you mean to change how the character reads. Save writes the whole card so tool bookkeeping and untouched parts stay.

Stage for the Press; each run exports staged pieces to one target. Hoplight writes Pygmalion as .json five fields plus whatever rode along. If the piece history includes an imported .png exporting to Pygmalion folds current fields into a fresh picture; if fold fails it falls back to plain .json rather than a broken file. Converting a piece that started elsewhere to Pygmalion writes plain .json with no picture; Hoplight only produces Pygmalion .png from a Pygmalion .png you actually gave it. Other app targets apply the drop story.

Will the card come back exactly as it was? Yes on export to Pygmalion. Imported .png returns as .png only when fold into a fresh picture succeeds; otherwise plain .json not a broken file; other targets write JSON fields without picture. Portrait is kept on import and returns on Pygmalion export; cross-app picture only if target has a slot; converting a card that never had a picture never invents one. Name and greeting alone without persona or scenario is not enough: Hoplight needs at least two of persona greeting and scenario or name plus persona specifically. Tool bookkeeping rides on round-trip and drops cross-app.

docs.title: Platforms
docs.summary: A short map of every platform Hoplight reads and writes today, what each one hands over, and which guide page to open first.
docs.semanticSummary: Platforms is the index map of every platform Hoplight reads and writes today: ten platforms each with a same-shaped guide page covering what Hoplight reads, same-app round trip keep, cross-app drops, Workbench look, and common questions. The platforms table lists Agnai characters and lorebooks; Backyard characters; Chub characters and lorebooks; Lumiverse characters personas regex; Marinara personas regex; NovelAI lorebooks only; Pygmalion characters; RisuAI characters lorebooks regex; RoleCall and SillyTavern characters lorebooks personas regex. Handles means decks those files land on; blank kinds mean the platform never shipped that shape. Backyard covers flat JSON and .byaf on one page; Marinara character cards are SillyTavern-shaped so they go through SillyTavern while Marinara's page covers regex and personas only. If your platform isn't listed, Character.AI and Crushon hand SillyTavern-shaped JSON so import via that path; default shape if unsure. Exhaustive live list via bun run hoplight formats or the format reference from the adapter registry. Common questions cover why handle counts differ, convert losses spelled per page, and try import by shape not name.

anchors.summary: The table maps each platform to what it handles and its guide page. Agnai characters and lorebooks; Backyard characters; Chub characters and lorebooks; Lumiverse characters personas and regex sets; Marinara personas and regex sets; NovelAI lorebooks; Pygmalion characters; RisuAI characters lorebooks and regex sets; RoleCall and SillyTavern characters lorebooks personas and regex sets. Handles lists decks a platform own files land on among Characters Lorebooks Personas Regex sets. A blank kind means that platform never shipped a file of that shape, not that Hoplight is missing something. Two notes: Backyard reads older flat JSON and modern .byaf archive both on its one page; Marinara character cards are SillyTavern-shaped underneath so they come and go through the SillyTavern page while Marinara covers only regex scripts and personas.

A handful of apps never shipped a portable file worth its own page. Character.AI export tools and Crushon both hand plain SillyTavern-shaped JSON, so drop the file in and Hoplight reads it through the SillyTavern page the same as a real SillyTavern card. That is also the default shape to reach for if you are not sure what your app produces: most thin hosts copy it. For the exhaustive generated list of every adapter Hoplight has today, run bun run hoplight formats or read the format reference, the technical version of this page. It is built straight from the live adapter registry so it never drifts from what the app can actually do.

Why do some platforms handle fewer kinds than others? Because the platform itself does; Hoplight adapters mirror what each app actually exports, so a platform with no lorebook feature never gets a Lorebooks column. Will I lose anything moving between two platforms? Sometimes, always spelled out: each platform page has a what changes when you convert table with exact fields that stay and drop, and the converting guide covers the general rule. My app is not SillyTavern Chub or anything above? Try importing anyway; Hoplight recognizes a file by its shape not its name, and most roleplay apps without their own page still export a SillyTavern-shaped card underneath.

docs.title: RisuAI
docs.summary: Bringing RisuAI .charx cards, lorebooks, and regex scripts into Hoplight and back out.
docs.semanticSummary: RisuAI exports a character as .charx zip with card.json assets and sometimes module.risum of regex trigger and lorebook rows. What Hoplight reads: .charx cards lorebook .json or .lorebook and regex as .risum or bare JSON rows; detect by zip and card.json not filename. What comes across cleanly keeps the original and lifts core fields greetings group-only Risu additional text creator notes dates display settings bias words image-gen voice scripts as data never run privileged flag as warning only embedded lorebook; images ride as bytes and may not preview live because of internal refs. What changes when you convert to another app keeps same-app fields assets scripts though not guaranteed identical archive bytes; cross-app drops Risu behavior surface scripts display package ids. Editing on the Workbench has Workshop tab for script data; bundled .risum is look do not touch and edit blocks export. Exporting back out writes .charx with linked lorebook in character_book; media only survives same-app Risu round trip not foreign pictures yet. Common questions cover semantic exactness not byte identity preview scripts risum edit block and lorebook put-back.

anchors.summary: Hoplight reads RisuAI cards as .charx a zip holding card.json plus assets folder of images and sometimes a bundled module.risum package. Lorebooks export as plain .json or .lorebook. Regex scripts arrive as a .risum module with rule rows or a bare .json list of rows. Drop on the Library for a plain-words receipt. Recognition uses zip signature and card.json entry not filename so renamed exports still import. Full walkthrough lives in the importing guide.

Importing loses nothing. Hoplight keeps a complete original then lifts name nickname description personality scenario first message alternate and group-only greetings examples system post-history Risu additional text creator notes including per-language source license tags dates display settings view screen large portrait inlay utility bot lore plus bias words image-gen hints voice config regex trigger virtual script background HTML/CSS default variables module toggles prebuilt-asset config privileged flag as warning marker never executed and embedded lorebook. Script rows never run; Hoplight parses edits and writes them as plain data. Every image rides as background bytes; Risu internal image refs mean live Workbench preview is not always available though bytes export back. Bundled .risum package is kept whole.

anchors.text: What changes when you convert to another app
anchors.summary: Same-app round-trip keeps everything you can see and touch though not necessarily the same bytes: fields assets and script rows come back when exported to RisuAI. Converting to another app drops Risu private extras on purpose: display settings additional text and the whole behavior surface regex trigger virtual script background HTML/CSS default variables module toggles prebuilt-asset config privileged flag plus bundled .risum package internal ids bookkeeping. Core character and embedded lorebook come across as far as the target holds; bias image-gen voice only if matching slots. Another app means SillyTavern Agnai Backyard RoleCall Pygmalion. Never blind-copy scripts; they stay where they work. Fewer target slots drop on their side not yours.

Send a piece to the Workbench as a tab and edit name description personality scenario first message and example messages like any card. Save writes the whole card so untouched parts stay. Cards with Risu scripts get a second tab Workshop for regex rows trigger rows virtual script background HTML/CSS and default variables as data you read and edit never run. If a separate .risum package is bundled Workshop shows its contents as look do not touch for now: editing the package and exporting is currently blocked rather than risk a broken write-back. Leave it as imported and it exports whole.

Stage for the Press; each run exports staged pieces to one target. Hoplight writes RisuAI cards as .charx the same zip container Risu exports so it loads like any Risu export. A linked lorebook rides written into character_book the slot Risu reads on import. Plain .txt or .md available for reading text. Other app targets apply the drop story. Gap: if a piece picture came from a different app exporting to RisuAI currently leaves .charx with no images; media only survives same-app Risu round trip where original archive files ride untouched. A picture from elsewhere has nowhere to land in a Risu export yet.

Will the card come back exactly as it was? In every way that matters yes on export to RisuAI: every field asset and script row survives but exact .charx bytes are not guaranteed because Hoplight rebuilds the archive and re-prints JSON so spacing compression and entry order can shift. Imported .charx returns as .charx. Picture bytes always ride on same-app round trip; live Workbench preview depends on Risu internal refs. Regex and trigger scripts stay on the Risu card and are not copied cross-app; on Workbench they are data never run. Bundled .risum can be opened and looked at; leave alone to export whole; edit currently blocks export so change packages in RisuAI for now. Embedded worldbook is pulled for solo edit and put back into character_book on export to apps that read one.

docs.title: RoleCall
docs.summary: Bringing RoleCall character cards and lorebooks into Hoplight and back out.
docs.semanticSummary: User guide for RoleCall, Vaudeville's own roleplay client, covering character cards and lorebooks in Hoplight. RoleCall cards carry more than a plain sheet: casting card identity details, presentation layer colors background spoilers, and sprite pack ride with usual fields. What Hoplight reads: character cards as PNG with embedded text or plain JSON holding CCv2 or CCv3 plus RoleCall extras, and lorebooks as RoleCall JSON. Drop on Library for a plain-words receipt; character vs persona is told by inside-file marks not filename. What comes across cleanly: full original kept, editable fields include name tagline description casting details personality scenario greetings examples prompts creator notes tags rating genre fandom presentation depth injections sprites and embedded lorebook. What changes when you convert to another app: same-app RoleCall round-trip keeps everything including private casting and presentation; cross-app drops RoleCall-only layers on purpose never blind-copies them. Editing on the Workbench rewrites the whole card so untouched parts stay. Exporting back out stages through the Press as RoleCall JSON; linked lorebook rides along; other targets apply the drop story. Common questions cover exact return JSON not PNG portrait retention casting stay-private and embedded lorebook pull-edit-put-back.

anchors.summary: Hoplight reads the two file types RoleCall gives you. Character cards arrive as PNG where RoleCall tucks card text inside the image or as plain JSON; both hold Character Card v2 or v3 with an extra block for casting card, presentation layer, and sprite pack. Lorebooks arrive as JSON in RoleCall's own export format. Drag the file onto the Library and drop anywhere in the room; Hoplight reads and shows a plain-words receipt of what it read and kept. It tells a RoleCall character card from a RoleCall persona card even though shapes are almost identical by reading inside the file for what marks a card as a character, not the filename or a guess. Full walkthrough lives in the importing guide.

Importing loses nothing. Hoplight keeps a complete copy of the original card, then lifts editable parts into fields you see directly: name tagline description; casting card full name title age pronouns; personality and scenario; first message and titled alternate greetings; example messages; system prompt and post-history instructions; creator creator notes source link and public creator note; tags content rating as all hours late night or after dark genre and fandom; presentation signature and gradient colors named palette curated background field order and spoiler settings; depth-position prompt injections; sprite expression pack; embedded lorebook with entries keywords and placement if present. Card picture is kept and shown as the piece portrait. After import everything that was in the card is still there: listed fields ready to edit and the rest held safely in the background.

anchors.text: What changes when you convert to another app
anchors.summary: Same-app round-trip keeps everything: import RoleCall, edit, export to RoleCall returns everything down to the byte because Hoplight kept the original and only rewrote changed fields. Converting to a different app drops RoleCall private extras: casting card full name title age pronouns, presentation colors palette background field order spoilers, content rating genre fandom, and internal ids with no shared home. Core character name description personality scenario greetings examples system prompt post-history notes tags come across as far as the other app can hold them. Depth injections sprites and linked lorebook come across only if the target has places for them. Another app means SillyTavern Agnai Backyard Risu Pygmalion and similar. The drop is deliberate: Hoplight never blind-copies RoleCall private casting and presentation into another app file. Where the other app has fewer slots whatever it cannot hold is dropped on its side not yours.

Send a piece from the Library to the Workbench and it opens as a tab. There you can edit name description personality scenario first message and example messages. When you save Hoplight writes the whole card back so the parts you did not touch stay exactly as they were including casting presentation and escrowed original layers.

When a piece is ready to leave stage it for the Press: right-click Stage for the Press or drop from the Press rail. The Press works only staged pieces and each run exports to one target format you pick. Hoplight writes RoleCall cards as JSON; RoleCall reads JSON the same as PNG so import is fine. Linked lorebook rides with the character automatically. You can also ask for plain txt or md when you only want to read the text. Choosing a different app as target applies the convert drop story: shared character only RoleCall private layers left behind.

Will the card come back exactly as it was? Yes when exported back to RoleCall: same app in same app out nothing lost. docs.title: Security and privacy
docs.summary: What keeps your content and your keys on your machine, why a downloaded card cannot run code on its own, and the few places where a protection is partial and we say so.
docs.semanticSummary: User-facing security and privacy guide for a local-first Studio that opens untrusted cards, scripts, regex sets, PNGs, and archives. Your content stays under your control through a primary loopback listener, no accounts or telemetry, and plain inspectable studio files, while the guide names three deliberate network boundaries: provider-backed Kit turns, user-opened update and version-switch information, and explicitly enabled remote access. A card cannot run itself because regex is validated and budgeted, macros and triggers are analyzed, and Lua runs only in the opt-in Risu Test Bench with worker, WebAssembly, resource, and separate-origin defenses whose packaged-host isolation is not yet proven. The sandbox origin serves only the Lua worker, regex worker, and glue.wasm. Other files stay bounded by body, archive, parsing, and path rules. Converting never copies one app's code into another because only portable canonical content crosses formats while private fields stay escrowed. About API keys describes optional BYOP Kit vault storage, hop-by-hop provider destination checks, the missing non-Windows passphrase setup flow, and Studio's ephemeral mutation token.

anchors.text: Your content stays under your control
anchors.summary: Studio's primary listener binds the local-only 127.0.0.1 address, and Hoplight has no hosted account, telemetry, analytics, background content upload, or inference proxy. Canonical pieces remain readable JSON files under the chosen studio directory, making them portable and user-backupable but not encrypted at rest; anyone already able to read the user's files can read them. Network activity is deliberate and tied to visible actions: Kit sends model context to the configured provider when a turn is submitted, Updates reads fixed GitHub release endpoints during update or version-switch flows, and remote access creates only the separately enabled listener or tunnel after its approval flow. The private-mesh link also needs a helper program that is not bundled: pressing Download the extra piece fetches it from Hoplight's own releases and checks it against a fingerprint built into the copy before writing anything, discarding a file that does not match. It is the only download Hoplight turns into a program it runs, and LAN mode needs none. Import, editing, conversion, and deterministic analysis make no provider request.

Downloaded content is parsed rather than automatically executed. Regex rules are budgeted find-and-replace data, never eval; structurally dangerous patterns are rejected before execution because a timeout cannot reliably interrupt one pathological native match. Macros and Risu-style triggers are analyzed without evaluation, including calc expressions handled by a small numeric parser. Lua executes only after the user opens the Risu Test Bench, never during import, preview, or background work. The bench uses real Lua in WebAssembly inside a killable worker with time and memory limits, served from a second loopback origin that exposes only the Lua worker, regex worker, and glue.wasm, with no session token or API. HTTP-layer tests prove that boundary, but packaged Windows-host isolation remains unmeasured, so the guide claims opt-in limitation rather than complete isolation.

Untrusted files are constrained before they can consume unbounded memory, corrupt state, or escape storage. Uploads and request bodies have hard size ceilings. ZIP and PNG readers enforce bounded extraction so compressed archive bombs stop at configured limits rather than expanding indefinitely. Parsers fail closed on malformed content instead of producing partially trusted entities. Kit's gated apply saves and re-reads its target to verify intended canonical content, while Studio editors send expected revisions so stale writes are rejected. Piece identifiers are validated and resolved strictly beneath the selected studio directory; crafted traversal names fail before filesystem access can escape that root.
topics: Kit read-back and Studio revision checks

anchors.text: Converting never copies one app's code into another
anchors.summary: Cross-format conversion carries only the portable canonical content understood by both sides. Source-specific extension blocks, layout data, triggers, and executable-looking payloads remain in the saved piece's escrow rather than being copied into another platform's output. That escrow allows same-format re-export to preserve source-owned information while preventing a conversion from smuggling one application's private code into a different application's file. Hoplight reports content that cannot cross instead of silently pretending it was portable. The rule is structural: the shared readable core converts, while platform-private material remains attached to its source format.

Provider-backed Kit is optional and uses bring-your-own-provider credentials; import, conversion, inspection, validation, editing, and deterministic checks continue without a key. Windows uses the operating-system credential backend. A portable passphrase-encrypted backend exists, but the current settings flow does not collect or supply the passphrase, so first-run setup and unlock remain incomplete on non-Windows systems. Credentials authenticate the configured provider and stay out of messages, tool observations, canonical pieces, exports, transcripts, and privacy accounting. Provider requests validate the configured host before every hop and refuse cross-host redirects, HTTPS downgrades, and chains beyond five redirects. Separately, Studio creates a fresh local session token at launch to authorize mutations and does not persist it.

The guide avoids reassuring but unsupported claims. Current desktop binaries are unsigned, so SmartScreen or Gatekeeper warnings are expected; users should verify the SHA-256 checksums shipped with releases rather than treating the warning alone as evidence of tampering. The separate Test Bench origin has automated HTTP-layer proof but has not been measured inside the packaged desktop host. Canonical studio files are intentionally readable and are not encrypted at rest. Kit's portable vault still lacks a settings-driven passphrase setup and unlock flow. Security reports should go privately to chibiconeja@gmail.com, also listed in SECURITY.md.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.summary: The whole engine: the hub-and-spoke canonical model, escrow, the adapter contract, detection, folders-as-schema, bundles, and the CLI.
docs.semanticSummary: This reference maps Hoplight's implemented engine and tool architecture. Hub and spoke explains why every external format maps through one canonical model. The canonical entity defines the shared wrapper and superset rule; escrow preserves source twins and binary carriers without moving private or executable payloads across formats. The adapter contract uses a kind-discriminated open format system, attaches serialization-loss reports, and routes canonical JSON through strict per-kind decoders. defineExhaustiveShape<T>() demands exact schema input and output parity, rejecting drift escapes such as narrowed unions and coercion while leaving declared record bags open. Detection ranks confident kind-correct adapters, and folder discovery supplies the registry. Bundles extract and re-embed lorebook references. Semantic content capabilities define pure previews, progressive discovery, bounded reads and stored results, independently reviewed semantic docs, and explicit compare-and-save apply with re-read verification. Layering points dependencies inward; CLI remains a thin engine surface; source-of-truth links name the governing modules.

anchors.text: The one idea: hub and spoke
anchors.summary: Every external format maps to and from one canonical superset rather than converting directly to every other format. A pairwise mesh requires N times N minus one paths; hub and spoke needs only N adapters. Adding a format therefore adds one adapter without changing existing formats or core conversion logic. Import calls the adapter's toCanonical operation, export calls fromCanonical, and conversion composes those two steps. This is the architectural invariant behind adapter independence and honest interoperability.

src/core/canonical.ts defines the shared wrapper: schemaVersion identifies the canonical revision, kind selects the entity family, id is the stable identity, body contains interoperable content, profiles hold sparse per-platform overrides, and original holds source escrow. Character, lorebook, persona, preset, and regex are adapter-backed kinds; canonical schemas also define pack entities. Body details live in their entity folders rather than in the wrapper. The superset rule limits body fields to meaning represented by at least one real wire format. Values that exist only in one application's memory or have no portable producer remain in escrow instead of acquiring a misleading canonical slot.

children.summary: Canonical bodies contain only fields serialized by real formats. A field earns a first-class slot only when a wire producer exists. Application-only values, including five RoleCall lorebook fields, stay escrowed so Hoplight does not promise unsupported portability.

anchors.text: Escrow: semantic round-trips, contained cross-format loss
anchors.summary: Each imported entity keeps an original escrow entry containing the source format, parsed raw twin, and fields not mapped into the canonical body. On same-format export, the adapter clones that twin and re-projects edited canonical fields onto it. Untouched source-specific extensions, layout, identifiers, and scripts survive while edited values are re-encoded. This is a semantic and escrow-preservation guarantee; byte identity applies only where a format specification declares and tests a byte-level tier. Cross-format conversion intentionally carries canonical meaning only. It does not blindly copy private extension blocks, bespoke layout, trigger scripts, or other executable payloads into a different application's file; future extension mapping must be explicit per field. Escrow can also retain sourceMedia with base64 bytes and MIME type. Tavern-lineage PNG adapters use it to preserve the authored portrait carrier for same-format re-emission, while text inputs omit it.

src/core/adapter.ts defines a kind-discriminated union of open format plugins whose character, lorebook, persona, preset, and regex branches convert to and from matching canonical entities. Adapter output carries text or bytes, extension, and a SerializeReport naming escrowed, dropped, shadowed, and warning paths. Canonical JSON crosses storage and HTTP through src/entities/runtime-schema.ts, which composes six strict per-kind decoders. Each adjacent runtime schema uses defineExhaustiveShape<T>() to infer concrete schemas before requiring exact input and output parity; missing or extra keys, narrowed unions, coercion, any at any nesting depth, and never fail typecheck. Unknown same-version keys fail except in declared open bags such as raw, unmapped, extras, and structured metadata. Kind-matched profiles are shallow partial bodies whose present fields receive complete validation. Storage, HTTP save, format-corpus verification, and Kit drafts share this ADR-011 boundary.

src/core/registry.ts holds the in-memory adapter table. Detection runs every adapter, rejects scores at or below 0.5, and selects the single highest-confidence match. Scores encode specificity: a RoleCall card can score 1.0 and outrank the generic SillyTavern reader at 0.9 for the same compatible CCv3 payload. Because character and lorebook adapters share one registry, detectors also enforce a cross-kind firewall. A bare name is insufficient evidence for SillyTavern flat-v1 character data; at least one genuine character signal such as description, personality, scenario, first_mes, or mes_example is required, preventing a name-bearing worldbook from being misclassified.

src/core/loader.ts is the impure discovery edge. It scans src/formats/*/index.ts with filesystem primitives, dynamically imports each module, and registers its default export. Names beginning with an underscore, including _shared and _template, are ignored. A folder may export one adapter or an array when a format family supplies multiple entity kinds, as SillyTavern and RoleCall do for characters and lorebooks. FormatId is an open string rather than a central enum. Adding a format means copying the template, implementing detection and both canonical directions, and supplying proof; no core registry list or unrelated format file is edited.

anchors.text: Bundles: a card plus its lorebook
anchors.summary: CCv2 and CCv3 character cards can embed a character_book, but Hoplight models that book as a separate canonical lorebook referenced by the character rather than leaving an opaque nested blob. During import, shared bundle logic extracts the book, creates a CanonicalLorebook, and records its id in knowledgeRefs. During export, the character adapter receives resolved lorebooks through EmitContext and embeds the appropriate target-format representation. The resolved list is authoritative even when empty: removing a link or disabling all linked books clears stale embedded data from the escrowed source twin. convertFile coordinates extraction and re-embedding for ordinary same-kind conversions, keeping bundle behavior format-agnostic at the canonical layer.

Capability folders provide pure operations returning previews, changes, warnings, and platform impact without writing. Kit projects content, studio, transfer, and diagnostics into one catalog. Only pure content gets exact read-or-draft access; deferred apply and writable bridges fail closed until separate safety policy grants an exact name. Search exposes five matches, browse and describe progressively, hidden or duplicate descriptors fail, and deferred exposure resets each user turn while drafts persist. studio_read uses RFC 6901 pointers and paging; oversized values use result_query handles whose store enforces per-entry and aggregate UTF-8 byte caps, a count cap, oldest-first eviction, character paging, and direct-offset recovery beyond capacity. change_query retains proposals; read-effect tools return deterministic observations and are rejected for changing content or claiming changes. docs_query searches indexed metadata and reads authoritative Markdown without arbitrary paths or network. Summaries enter generated indexes only with independent hash-bound APPROVE receipts; source or summary edits invalidate approval. Focused checks validate an author's sidecar; global checks require every approval and current projections. Security classifies only exact catalog-derived names as preview-only; durable apply remains an explicit compareAndSave write with re-read verification.

Dependencies point inward: core has no application dependency, formats depend on core, and CLI or Studio depend on both. The engine does not import UI, database, or framework concerns.
