Conversion and adapters are proven before a surface wraps them. CLI, the Bun Studio server, and the React client share that engine. Studio uses a primary loopback listener, with optional remote listeners enabled separately.

src/cli.ts is a thin layer over the shared engine. convert writes a requested or extension-inferred target; inspect reports canonical identity and key fields; label reports detected format and origin; validate checks detection and canonical decoding; formats reads the live registry. ui launches the primary loopback Studio server, while optional remote listeners are enabled separately. Version and help expose release identity and usage.

The closing map assigns authority to concrete modules. src/core/canonical.ts owns the wrapper, escrow, and id policy. adapter.ts owns adapter kinds and EmitContext. registry.ts owns detection and lookup, while loader.ts owns filesystem discovery. convert.ts coordinates bundle extraction and re-embedding. src/entities/character/schema.ts and src/entities/lorebook/schema.ts define their canonical supersets. Contributors should change these owners rather than introducing parallel definitions in a UI, command, documentation generator, or format adapter.

docs.title: The audit suite
docs.summary: Runnable UI audits under `scripts/audit/`. They drive the real app in a real browser against a scratch studio seeded through the real adapters, and they **enumerate the live app at runtime**: the room list comes from the dock, deck and view
docs.semanticSummary: Reference for the runnable UI audit suite under scripts audit. Audits drive the real app in a real browser against a scratch studio seeded through real adapters and enumerate the live app at runtime: room list from the dock, deck and view lists from Library chip rows, lens lists from the editor select. Add an app deck view or lens and the next run walks it with no script edits. The one hand-grown file is walks promises.ts because behavior expectations are human knowledge; every new feature adds a row there act then observable effect. Runs table: audit everything in order; audit rooms every dock catalog app both themes; library every deck times view staging delete context; editors every kind write-for lens binder export book-rules folder inspector; setup first-run wizard steps theme accent; promises act-effect table; clicks every visible enabled clickable flagging dead-click suspects not auto-fail with Quit Restart external blocklisted; legibility dark light style only; watch reruns rooms plus promises on src ui change. The style audit every visited state checks tiny-text low-contrast naked-control plus page errors. Artifacts under audit-out run screenshots and ledger.json as coverage claim; non-zero on findings for CI. Honest boundaries: unrendered never audited; dead-click heuristic; unit suite carries non-promise behavior.

anchors.summary: bun run audit walks everything below in order. audit rooms walks every dock and catalog app both themes for style audit per room. audit library walks every deck times every view staging bar delete confirm context menu for style per state. audit editors opens one piece of every kind every write-for lens binder views export and book-rules dialogs and folder inspector. audit setup walks first-run wizard every step live theme flip custom accent final. audit promises walks the promise table act then observable effect covering import picker drop count delete staging lenses search updates theme create duplicate rename. audit clicks every visible enabled clickable flags no-effect as dead-click suspects eyeball list not auto-fail; Quit Restart and external links blocklisted. audit legibility dark or light pins theme for style only. audit watch reruns the quick set rooms plus promises whenever src ui changes.

Three exhaustive checks over the full DOM from page-audit.ts deliberately DOM-bound: the whole function is serialized into the page and runs there. tiny-text flags any text node under the 10px floor. low-contrast flags text under WCAG AA against effective background 4.5 to 1 or 3 to 1 for large bold text. naked-control flags any button or select wearing browser-default fonts instead of house tokens the unstyled-component regression class. Page errors thrown during a walk are ledgered too.

Each run writes audit-out run folder: one screenshot per visited state theme-stop png and ledger.json holding the visited-state list and every finding. The visited list is the coverage claim: anything not on it was not audited. A run exits non-zero when it found anything so runs can gate CI.

A state never rendered is never audited; coverage grows with the walkers and the ledger names exactly what was walked. Dead-click detection is heuristic because some no-ops are legitimate; its output is a suspect list for review. Behavior beyond the promise table is carried by the unit suite not these walks.

docs.title: CLI reference
docs.summary: Every hoplight command and flag, verified against src/cli.ts and src/cli-io.ts, with usage, behavior, JSON output shapes, and exit codes.
docs.semanticSummary: CLI reference for hoplight over the same canonical engine and format adapters as Studio. src/cli.ts dispatches, cli-validation enforces the exhaustive canonical runtime schema, and cli-io owns conversion I/O policy. Invocation works through source, package bin, or compiled output; bun run dev starts the primary Studio loopback listener. Commands cover convert, inspect, validate, label, formats, ui, version, help, no arguments, and unknown input. convert guards paths, detects and converts every same-kind adapter pair, checks container agreement, enforces its serialize report and optional strict-loss contract, then publishes atomically. inspect prints reachable kind-specific fields for character, lorebook, persona, regex, and preset; an internal media-pack formatter exists but no live format adapter can reach it. validate rejects unrecognized input, adapter failures, and invalid canonical output. ui blocks on the primary loopback server while remote listeners remain separately configured. Remaining JSON and positional inconsistencies are named explicitly.

anchors.summary: In the repo run bun run src cli.ts command args or package script bun run hoplight command args. package.json bin maps the hoplight command straight to src cli.ts so an installed or linked package exposes it directly. bun run build cli compiles a standalone binary to dist hoplight via bun build compile src cli.ts. bun run dev is hoplight ui 8321.

convert with optional to, yes, y, and strict flags converts and prints a loss report. inspect, validate, label, and formats cover file details, pass or fail, provenance, and adapter discovery. ui launches Studio's primary loopback server; remote listeners are configured separately inside Studio. version and help print their banners. No arguments equals help. Unknown first input names the error and exits 1.

Standalone v version and h help map to version and help commands. json works on version formats validate convert only; inspect label ui help stay human. convert-only to forces adapter id; yes y allows replace of existing out never input; strict refuses when dropped paths are reported or target coverage is undeclared.

Flags may appear anywhere after convert; parseConvertFlags scans the tail for yes y strict and to value leaving exactly two positionals; duplicates bad to unknown flags or wrong positional count exit 1 with usage. Before a byte is written, guardConvertOutput refuses same-file out as in and requires yes when out exists; registry detect fails listing known ids when unrecognized; resolveTarget prefers to format or extension via targetsForExtension and never guesses ambiguous matches; convertFile imports and exports with bundled lorebook extraction and re-embedding; assertContainerAgreement checks the adapter extension and payload shape; the command requires a serialize report; strict then refuses reported drops or undeclared coverage; publishAtomic writes a temp sibling, fsyncs, and renames while leaving the prior destination on failure. Only success honors json with ok, adapter and path fields, payload counts, and report details; undeclared coverage uses unknown with a null dropped count. Every failure prints plain text. Plain reports name confirmed drops, warnings, and unknown loss.

Detects the adapter, converts to canonical, validates the exhaustive runtime schema and matching adapter kind, then prints format id, adapter label, entity kind, and kind fields. Character prints greeting and tags; lorebook entries and budget; persona content and sections; regex rules; preset prompts, groups, and choices. The formatter contains a media-pack branch, but no live format adapter imports packs, so the CLI cannot currently reach it. Output is always human-readable. File is args1, so a preceding flag becomes the path.

Detects an adapter, converts through toCanonical, parses the result through the exhaustive canonical runtime schema, and requires the parsed kind to match the adapter contract in cli-validation before pass or fail. Unrecognized input, adapter errors, invalid canonical output, and kind mismatches are INVALID; otherwise OK prints format kind name. Exit is 0 or 1. Path is the first non-validate non-json arg. json shapes cover success, unrecognized failure, and recognized failure with format plus error.

Guesses a card spec and likely origin app without fully parsing into the canonical model via labelCard sniffContainer in character provenance. Source is best available: detected adapter escrowed raw else JSON parse of decoded text else undefined so label can still report unknown none on unrecognized files. Prints format as card spec chara_card_v3 v2 v1 agnai backyard or unknown not an adapter id; container png charx json or unknown; origin likely authoring app plus confidence or unknown; signals every fingerprint or none. Does not honor json. file is args1 same positional caveat as inspect.

Loads every adapter the loader discovers under formats star index and lists each id kind label and output extensions. Plain text also prints the doc path for the generated coverage matrix docs FORMAT-SUPPORT.md regenerated with bun run matrix and a reminder that a new format is a folder drop-in copy of formats template. json shape is schema 1 with adapters array of id kind label outputExtensions.

Starts Studio's primary loopback server through startUi and blocks until interrupt. Optional remote listeners remain a separate Studio configuration path. port is Number args1 or 8321; missing, non-numeric, or 0 values fall back. studioDir is args2, defaulting to the user's Documents/Hoplight Studio folder, and requires a port argument first because it is the third token. The command does not honor json.

hoplight version v and version flag forms are equivalent; the short and long version flags are checked before any other command match ahead of no-arguments and help fallback. Plain form prints just the version string. json shape is version string and schema 1.

help h help flag and bare no-arguments all print the same built-in HELP banner: usage line command table flag list one example block and a status line naming schema version and format-matrix doc path. No arguments falls through to the same branch as help. Does not honor json.

json is honored by version formats validate and convert, matching the HELP banner; inspect label ui and help remain human-only. Convert json only covers the success report; every failure branch prints plain text regardless of the flag. y is a working alias of yes that HELP does not mention. Every exit path is 0 or 1; there is no exit code 2 and no command writes to stderr; all output success or failure goes through console.log to stdout. Positional resolution differs: validate accepts path any side of json; inspect and label take args1 literally so a flag before the path is read as the path. label format column is the card spec from labelCard; inspect format column is the adapter id; same column name different value on two commands.

Command dispatch and HELP live in cli.ts; runtime validation and kind agreement in cli-validation.ts; conversion parsing, guards, and atomic publish in cli-io.ts. Registry detection and extension resolution use core/registry.ts. Schema, discovery, and bundle conversion use canonical.ts, loader.ts, and convert.ts. Provenance labeling uses entities/character/provenance.ts, UI startup uses ui/server.ts, and package.json defines invocation surfaces.

docs.title: Component catalog
docs.summary: Auto-generated by `scripts/hooks/component-catalog.ts` from exported UI entries under pre-commit gate (`--check`) fails the commit when this file drifts from the real exports.
docs.semanticSummary: Component catalog is the generated inventory of exported Hoplight UI entries. scripts/hooks/component-catalog.ts scans React components throughout src/ui plus exported create/build/swatch/inject helpers under src/ui/_shared. Authors do not hand-edit the markdown: regenerate it with bun run scripts/hooks/component-catalog.ts, and the pre-commit --check gate fails when live exports drift. Each row records Name, source File, TypeScript Signature, optional Doc blurb, and Styles class list. Before building a control, scan this catalog and reuse an existing entry rather than inventing a twin. The two tables distinguish React `.tsx` components from shared `.ts` UI helpers; that distinction is file shape and API role, not a claim that helpers are legacy or awaiting migration. Use the catalog as lookup authority for props and file homes; behavior and layout truth remain in reference/ui and the owning source.

anchors.summary: Primary table of React .tsx exports that power the studio under ADR-008. Rows span shell chrome (App, Dock, DropVeil, BootErrorScreen, FollowDialog, and the dirty-tab ClosePieceDialog/ClosePiecePrompt), shared components under src/ui/components (forms, dialogs, lens rail, export dialog, CSS workshop panes, sprite and expression tooling, write-for strip, bento cards, and many field editors), app-scoped presenters under src/ui/apps, and Settings sections including the remote-access helper card (HelperMissingCard, HelperInstalledLine). Workbench dominates: revision-aware character, lorebook, pack, persona, preset, and regex editors plus workshop rails, panes, bulk bars, health and changes surfaces, and mode chrome. Library contributes import and damaged-file notices plus lore and regex workshops; settings contributes LAN and update dialogs; docs contributes its room, navigation, contents, and table of contents. Each row is Name, source File, TypeScript Signature, optional Doc one-liner, and Styles class tokens. Prefer matching an existing name and file path over adding a parallel control; empty Doc cells still count as cataloged exports that the reuse rule covers.

Secondary table for exported TypeScript UI helpers under src/ui/_shared whose names begin create, build, swatch, or inject. These are ordinary `.ts` functions rather than JSX components; the table makes no deprecation or migration claim. It uses the same Name, File, Signature, Doc, and Styles columns as the React table. The current entry is buildTimeline from version-history, a pure helper actively consumed by the React Updates surface to derive release relations and behind counts. Regenerating the catalog adds or removes rows as matching exports change. Open this table when a UI task needs shared computation or construction logic, and open the React table when it needs a rendered control.

docs.title: Bundles
docs.summary: How a character card's embedded lorebook splits into two linked canonical entities, a CanonicalCharacter and a CanonicalLorebook joined by knowledgeRefs, extracted on import and re-embedded on export.
docs.semanticSummary: Bundles explain how a character card that embeds a lorebook becomes two linked canonical entities instead of one blob. On import the embedded book splits into a standalone CanonicalLorebook while the character keeps only body.knowledgeRefs id links; on export the target adapter re-embeds resolved lorebooks into its native slot. The page is the join mechanism and call-site lifetimes, not the CCv2/v3 wire map (see character-book) or the shared wrapper (see canonical-model). knowledgeRefs: the join field is an ordered id list distinct from worldName, which names an external worldbook by title. Import: extract at the boundary runs inspectBundle with shared extractCharacterBook or an adapter extractLorebook override such as Agnai. Export: re-embed at the boundary runs emitBundle with EmitContext lorebooks and multi-book merge when the wire has one slot. Two call sites, two lifetimes contrast the CLI one-shot convertFile path with Studio persist-resolve-export. Source of truth tables convert.ts, adapter contracts, studio bundle, and CLI wiring.

anchors.summary: CanonicalCharacter body.knowledgeRefs is an ordered string array of linked lorebook ids that export adapters embed when the format requires it. It is not worldName: worldName is the creator intent to auto-load an external worldbook by name, while knowledgeRefs links an embedded or library book by canonical id. The field is a list because KnowledgeRail lets authors attach, detach, and reorder multiple library books on one character; attachKnowledgeRef appends only if absent. Import extraction is narrower: a single card import yields at most one extracted book, so ConvertResult.lorebooks is zero or one entry per pass. Multi-book knowledgeRefs lists are therefore Studio-authored, never produced alone by one import, and they are exactly what forces export-side merge when the target wire supports only one character_book slot.

inspectBundle runs once per import. First source.toCanonical leaves any embedded book inside entity.original in the source raw shape. Extraction then chooses: if CharacterAdapter implements extractLorebook for a dialect the shared mapper cannot read, that override runs; otherwise extractCharacterBook on primaryOriginalRaw handles only CCv2/v3 character_book. Finally knowledgeRefs is set to the new lorebook id. Agnai is the concrete override case with native characterBook MemoryBook and its standalone lorebook codec; SillyTavern, RoleCall, and Risu fall through to the shared path. The shared extractor also escrow-stashes the raw book on the lorebook under key character-book, not the host format id, so later standalone export can still overlay that twin. Wire field mapping lives on the character-book concept page.

Extraction is shared; re-embedding belongs to the target adapter. emitBundle builds EmitContext with resolved lorebooks and passes it to target.fromCanonical. EmitContext is optional and cross-entity, resolved by CLI or Studio, never by core. Adapters that embed knowledge write context.lorebooks into their slot; formats without embedding or that only use worldName ignore it. Three-way contract: omitted lorebooks leaves the twin alone; nonempty list replaces the embedded book; empty list clears both CCv2/v3 slots so resolution stays authoritative without breaking direct same-format adapter round trips. When multiple linked books hit a single slot, lorebooksToCharacterBook collapses them: one ref overlays or encodes that book; many refs concatenate entries under the first book's settings and record names plus entry counts in extensions.vaud_source_books so the split stays recoverable.

knowledgeRefs is the same field, but resolution differs by caller. The CLI hoplight convert path is one ephemeral convertFile pass: inspectBundle then emitBundle in memory, no lorebook file on disk; if the target embeds knowledge the book rides inside the single output and CLI only reports entry counts. The Studio persists character and lorebook as separate Library entities. handleInspect returns both pieces; save-bundle writes lorebook first, rewrites knowledgeRefs on keep-both rename, then character. Later export resolves refs via resolveLorebooksFromStore and fails closed with 422 naming missing ids rather than exporting a silent book-less card. Disabled books are omitted with knowledgeRefs named as not carried so export is not a false success. App and CLI both re-embed through the same emitBundle primitive after their own resolution steps.

Ownership map for bundle code. convert.ts owns inspectBundle, emitBundle, convertFile, and rewriteKnowledgeRefs. adapter.ts defines EmitContext and extractLorebook. character-book.ts owns shared CCv2/v3 extract and re-embed. character schema owns knowledgeRefs and worldName. KnowledgeRail session ops attach and reorder refs. studio/bundle.ts persists lorebook then character. server-engine.ts wires Studio inspect export and fail-closed resolution. cli.ts wires convert. book-ops filters enabled books. Agnai index is the non-CCv3 override example.

docs.title: The canonical superset model
docs.summary: The one hub every format converts through, a versioned entity wrapper whose body is the union of what real formats express, governed by the superset rule that a field earns a canonical slot only when a real wire format serializes it.
docs.semanticSummary: The canonical superset model is the one hub every format converts through, never format to format. This page defines the shared wrapper and the superset rule that decides what body may hold; whole-engine hub-and-spoke context lives in architecture.md and per-kind body detail on entity pages. Structure lives in src/core/canonical.ts while per-kind fields live under src/entities. The wrapper is CanonicalEntity with schemaVersion, kind, id, body, optional profiles, and original escrow. The superset rule first-classes only fields a real supported wire format serializes; everything else rides escrow. Escrow: what the rule leaves out is original as Record of OriginalEntry with raw, unmapped, and optional sourceMedia for carriers. Profiles: one superset, many apps stores sparse per-FormatId Partial body overrides so authors set only deltas without full duplicate records. Source of truth lists canonical.ts, adapter kind union, character and lorebook schemas, and architecture map.

anchors.summary: CanonicalEntity is the stable shape every entity shares: schemaVersion fixed at 1, kind as a closed union of character lorebook persona or regex today, id as a storage-safe slug from canonicalId, body as the superset content, optional profiles as sparse per-FormatId Partial body overrides, and optional original as the escrow map. FormatId is intentionally an open string so drop-in adapters claim any id without core hardcoding the set. canonicalId normalizes names with NFKC, lowercases, collapses non-alphanumerics to hyphens, caps length, and falls back to character when empty so path policy always accepts the result. kind stays closed for compile-time safety across FormatAdapter; preset and pack schemas exist under entities without adapters yet. Formats are open; entity kinds grow only by union member plus entities folder.

Body is the union of what real formats express, not any one wire shape. A field earns a first-class canonical slot only if some real currently supported wire format serializes it; otherwise it rides original. Not serialized means no slot: platform and database baggage such as creator stats publishing timestamps and runtime state stay out of body, and in-memory-only residue such as RoleCall allowRecursion boostIds scanPreset probabilityMode verified absent from serializers stays in escrow. Single-platform is not a reason to relegate: if even one format serializes an authored field it earns a slot because the schema is the editor. Lorebook first-classes SillyTavern-only scan sources vectorized group toggles automation and displayIndex on that ground. The policed distinction is authored-and-serialized content versus derived-or-runtime state; character schema states the same gate.

anchors.text: Escrow: what the rule leaves out
anchors.summary: Fields that fail the superset rule are contained, not dropped. The wrapper original field is a Record keyed by FormatId of OriginalEntry values: raw source payload verbatim, unmapped fields canonical did not express, and optional sourceMedia for binary carriers such as PNG card pixels. Same-format round trips stay field-lossless; cross-format conversion is contained-loss by design. Superset rule and escrow keep body portable while nothing outside it is lost silently.

One superset body still allows per-app differences without full duplicates. profiles is a sparse Record of FormatId to Partial body, empty by default. Authors write the entity once and set only fields that should differ for a given app; the projected app version is body plus those overrides via the adapter. Both profiles and original share the open FormatId key space, so overrides and escrow residue thread the same format identity model across the wrapper.

canonical.ts owns the wrapper, schema version, id policy, escrow envelope, primaryOriginalRaw, and profiles. adapter.ts owns the closed entity-kind union. character and lorebook entity schemas state the superset rule for their bodies. architecture.md supplies whole-engine hub-and-spoke, escrow, and detection context for this model page.

docs.title: The embedded character_book
docs.summary: A card's embedded character_book is extracted into a standalone linked lorebook on import and re-embedded into the target format's book slot on export.
docs.semanticSummary: The embedded character_book concept explains how a card-carried lorebook becomes a linked CanonicalLorebook on import and is re-inlined into the target format book slot on export. Source is formats/_shared/character-book.ts with convert.ts orchestration; this implements architecture bundles for card-plus-book. A different dialect from the worldbook file covers CCv3 field names versus standalone ST world info, including dual-encoded position under extensions. Import: extract at the boundary finds, maps, escrows under character-book, and links knowledgeRefs, with Non-CCv3 dialects override the extractor for Agnai MemoryBook. Export: inline at the boundary uses EmitContext lorebooks and twin overlay, with Quirks preserved faithfully for use_regex and multi-book merge via vaud_source_books. End to end walks convertFile inspectBundle plus emitBundle for CLI and Studio callers. Source of truth lists mapper, adapter, enums, convert, and canonical files that own each concern for implementers reading the wire path end to end.

anchors.text: A different dialect from the worldbook file
anchors.summary: Embedded character_book is not the same wire shape as a standalone SillyTavern world info file. It uses CCv3 entry field names at top level and tucks ST-extended fields into each entry extensions bag: keys and secondary_keys instead of key and keysecondary, insertion_order instead of displayIndex and order, use_regex force flag plus inline regex, coarse before_char after_char strings with precise value in extensions.position, and depth role group probability selective_logic scan sources inside extensions. Because ST-extended fields can appear top-level or in extensions, entryToCanonical reads both with extensions winning via pick. Only selective logic, injection role, and character filter share worldbook codecs through lore-enums; position and keyword parsing stay local. Position is dual-encoded, not degraded so export writes coarse string and precise extensions.position together and import prefers extensions then falls back.

children.summary: On export positionToCoarse writes CCv3 top-level before_char or after_char while positionToExt writes the precise slot into extensions.position in parallel. Spec-only readers see the coarse floor; ST-family readers recover the exact slot. On import parseBookPosition reads extensions.position first and falls back to the top-level string only when extensions carries none, so encoding is lossless for any reader that understands extensions.

anchors.summary: When a character imports, a format-agnostic layer finds an embedded book and extracts it. findCharacterBook checks CCv3 slot, CCv2 extensions.character_book, and flat V1, returning raw so the caller controls escrow. characterBookToLorebook maps to LorebookBody. extractCharacterBook stashes raw under the new lorebook original key character-book, not the host format id, so dialect owns the escrow shape across host formats. inspectBundle sets knowledgeRefs to the lorebook id. Non-CCv3 dialects override the extractor via CharacterAdapter extractLorebook; Agnai embeds native characterBook MemoryBook and reuses its standalone lorebook mapper so embedded and file imports canonicalize identically.

children.summary: Shared extractCharacterBook understands only CCv2/v3 character_book. Formats with another dialect implement extractLorebook on CharacterAdapter; inspectBundle calls that override when present. Agnai is the case today: native characterBook MemoryBook mapped through agnai-lorebook so books read the same embedded or as files.

anchors.summary: Re-embedding is the target format job. Adapters that embed knowledge receive resolved lorebooks in EmitContext and call embedCharacterBook to write data.character_book and clear stale extensions.character_book. Empty resolved list clears both slots; omitted context leaves the raw twin intact. SillyTavern RoleCall Risu and Lumiverse use the shared helper; Agnai applies the same three-way rule to native characterBook. lorebookToCharacterBook overlays when a character-book twin exists so unedited books re-emit byte-true with residue preserved; without twin it full-encodes from canonical for cross-format paths. Quirks preserved faithfully covers entry-level use_regex only when every keyword is regex, and multi-book concatenation with vaud_source_books boundaries.

children.summary: use_regex is entry-level only when every keyword in both trigger lists is regex. Multi-book refs concatenate under the first book's settings with extensions.vaud_source_books recording each source name and entry count.

anchors.summary: convertFile runs the same-kind character path: inspectBundle extracts and links books, then emitBundle hands resolved lorebooks to target fromCanonical. CLI calls convertFile; Studio uses the same primitives with store-resolved knowledgeRefs so both re-embed through identical code and lorebooks survive format hops.

character-book.ts owns mapping extract and re-embed. adapter.ts owns extractLorebook and EmitContext. lore-enums.ts shares selective logic role and filter. convert.ts orchestrates inspectBundle emitBundle and convertFile. canonical.ts owns wrapper escrow and ids. VAUDEVILLE apps/rc notes are interop facts only for this dialect.

docs.title: Detection and the registry
docs.summary: How hoplight sniffs a file's format from its content, scores each adapter's confidence, keeps the single best match above a threshold, and stops any detector from claiming another entity kind's files.
docs.semanticSummary: Detection and the registry explain how Hoplight sniffs file content rather than trusting extensions. Every adapter scores AdapterInput confidence; registry.detect keeps the single best score at or above DETECT_THRESHOLD 0.5 or returns undefined. Content, not extension builds bytes always and text only for valid UTF-8 json or txt. The registry pass is one winner with strict-greater selection and deliberate score spread so order does not decide ties. Confidence scores ladder specific readers over generic shared shapes, with weak in-band and sub-threshold soft nos. Not detection: the origin labeler is a separate hoplight label pass after format choice. The cross-kind firewall forces zero on other kinds so worldbooks never steal character readers, backed by detection.test.ts and kind-discriminated convert. Adding a format never edits detection: folders-as-schema registers each detect locally without core changes. Source of truth maps registry adapter loader tests CLI and provenance ownership.

anchors.summary: Adapters receive AdapterInput with bytes for binary, text for JSON, and optional filename. Reads always fill bytes and decode text only for valid UTF-8 .json or .txt; extension never picks the winner. Binary detectors use magic and chunks; JSON needs text or returns 0. sniffContainer is a separate wrapper sniff under provenance.

registry.ts is the pure in-memory adapter table. detect walks every registered adapter, tracks the highest score, and returns that adapter only if score clears DETECT_THRESHOLD 0.5 inclusive; otherwise undefined. One pass one winner against the same input with no format-to-format probing. No match is real: callers report unrecognized rather than guess. Selection uses strict greater so equal later scores never displace earlier ones, which is why confidence ladders are deliberately spread. convert inspect validate and label CLI commands plus studio inspect all call registry.detect first.

detect returns 0 to 1; zero means not mine. Scores are hand-chosen so specific readers outrank generic ones on shared wire shapes. SillyTavern generic Tavern reader scores 0.9; RoleCall claims 1.0 only with extensions.rolecall and returns 0 on plain CCv3 so sillytavern wins. Backyard scores 0.9 on legacy cards but 0.55 on bare persona objects, a weak but intentional clear of the floor. vaud-json returns 1 for real canonical entities and 0.1 for other JSON, which never clears 0.5 and cannot win. Per-adapter rosters live on FORMAT-SUPPORT and format pages.

hoplight label runs a second scoring pass after detection already chose the format. labelCard guesses which app likely authored the card by testing app-namespaced extension blocks and reports the winning rule weight as 0 to 1 confidence. That answers origin heuristic where detect confidence answers which adapter reads the file. They are different numbers from different passes and must not be conflated.

Character lorebook persona and regex adapters share one registry pass, so each detector must return 0 on other kinds. Character-versus-lorebook is load-bearing: ST worldbooks are name-shaped JSON that would false-positive a naive V1 character path. The flat/v1 branch therefore requires real character signals description personality scenario first_mes or mes_example so worldbooks route to sillytavern-lorebook. detection.test.ts registers every format and asserts samples route correctly; new folders may add detectors but must not steal. A type-level complement is FormatAdapter kind-discriminated union with convertFile throwing on cross-kind pairs.

anchors.text: Adding a format never edits detection
anchors.summary: Each format folder owns detect. The registry never hardcodes formats; the loader discovers src/formats/*/index.ts default exports. Adding a format means writing detect in the new folder and choosing a score that fits the confidence gradient with no core edits. The firewall test is the safety net against scores that invade another format territory.

registry.ts owns the table detect and threshold. adapter.ts owns detect contract and kind union. loader.ts registers folders. detection.test.ts is the firewall property. convert.ts guards kind on conversion. CLI and server-engine build AdapterInput. provenance.ts owns the origin labeler. FORMAT-SUPPORT.md lists the generated adapter roster.

docs.title: Escrow and round-trip
docs.summary: How the escrow envelope, the canonical original field, makes a same-format round-trip lossless and keeps a cross-format conversion to contained loss by design.
docs.semanticSummary: Escrow and round-trip document how every canonical entity carries a lossless import twin in original so same-format round trips lose nothing and cross-format conversions lose only non-portable residue by design. The escrow envelope is Record FormatId to OriginalEntry with raw unmapped and optional sourceMedia, filled automatically under each adapter key, with primaryOriginalRaw selecting the source twin. A same-format round-trip loses nothing via toCanonical stash and fromCanonical three-state overlay onto the twin so only edited fields re-encode; scope is fields not bit-identical containers after pretty-print. A cross-format conversion is contained loss by design because targets read only their own original key and full-encode body without blind-copying foreign extensions or scripts. Per-kind coverage of the same idea points format pages for character lorebook persona and regex twins. Source of truth lists canonical adapter convert tavern-fields sillytavern and architecture ownership for the twin path.

anchors.summary: Escrow is per-source original on the wrapper: Record of FormatId to OriginalEntry. raw is the entire parsed source payload untouched as the exporter twin. unmapped holds source facts canonical does not first-class such as Tavern round-trip variant. sourceMedia is the binary carrier such as PNG card pixels kept as a raw-bytes twin, not body content. original fills automatically on import and is never hand-edited; each adapter stores under its own format id. primaryOriginalRaw reads the first entry raw so labeler and bundle layers cannot drift. Superset rule sends non-wire residue here rather than inventing body fields.

Adapter symmetry: toCanonical stashes the payload while reading; fromCanonical re-emits from that original for the round trip. SillyTavern character is the worked example storing whole card twin variant and PNG carrier then overlaying body onto a twin clone in the original variant. applyBodyToData three-state: equal values leave raw untouched, changed values write exact wire homes, values twin had but canonical dropped clear those homes. Absent both sides leaves raw alone protecting unrepresentable shapes and unknown keys. Lossless means every field including unexpressed ones survives from the twin and only edits re-encode. Pretty-printed JSON and PNG-to-JSON container changes are out of scope; no authored field is silently dropped or fabricated.

anchors.text: A cross-format conversion is contained loss by design
anchors.summary: convertFile same-kind paths pass the full entity but only the canonical body plus re-embedded lorebooks project into the target file. Per-id keying keeps the source twin under original source while the target adapter looks for original target, finds none on a fresh conversion, and full-encodes from body alone. Private extensions scripts layout and internal ids stay in escrow and are not written into another app file. This is safety: never blind-copy executable or private payloads; deny by absence with future opt-in field mappers only. PNG carriers likewise stay in escrow across formats as portrait yet restore on same-format re-emit. Loss is bounded to non-portable extras while the portable core crosses.

anchors.text: Per-kind coverage of the same idea
anchors.summary: Every entity kind carries escrow the same way. Format pages document where same-format is lossless and where cross-format collapses. SillyTavern covers character and lorebook twins, injection-slot collapse on cross-format lorebooks, and persona plus regex codecs that seal multi-record files so untouched records re-emit unchanged. Entity pages define what each canonical slot means for character and lorebook bodies.

canonical.ts owns original OriginalEntry and primaryOriginalRaw. adapter.ts states the stash and re-emit contract. convert.ts projects only body across formats. tavern-fields applyBodyToData is the three-state overlay example. sillytavern index stores and re-emits twins. architecture.md maps escrow in the whole engine diagram.

docs.title: Concept: the persona editor
docs.summary: The {{user}} sheet, wearing the CHARACTER editor's chassis on purpose (the kinship ruling, 2026-07-12): the same `.bento` three-column grid, `BentoCard` tiles, and `.lcard`/`.portrait` face plate from `editor-styles`. Source: `src/ui/apps/w
docs.semanticSummary: Persona editor is the Workbench {{user}} sheet that reuses the character editor chassis on purpose: same bento three-column grid, BentoCard tiles, and portrait face plate from editor-styles under src/ui/apps/workbench/persona. Left holds PortraitCard writing media.portrait as data-URI without character variant strip, plus KnowledgeRail for knowledgeRefs. Middle holds Identity with tagline pronouns BRIEF honesty line, section tiles Appearance Body Personality Quirks History, and flat Identity Text for section-less personas. Right holds shared SwatchRow and PaletteControl colors, Prompt Injection stops per Write-for via injectionsForProfile, LIVE PREVIEW from real core/persona/inject.ts, and default-persona star. Compiler test landmine: brief never injects and content never becomes the card blurb. Reuse law on this surface requires components catalog first before any new control. The shelf covers Library persona cards brief lines and Default badge. The wires cover rcpersona ST backup Lumiverse Marinara and Agnai limits without inventing extra formats.

anchors.summary: Every element on the persona editor was walked against the component catalog. Anything new on this surface must come from docs/reference/components.md first before inventing a twin control. The law matches house UI reuse: scan the generated catalog and share chassis pieces already used by character and regex editors such as WriteForStrip BentoCard and KnowledgeRail.

Library persona shelf lives in persona-shelf.tsx and persona-shelf-ops.ts. Cards show portrait or monogram, put the brief as the card line which is its one honest home, and surface pronouns section count and lorebook facts from the meta loader. A gilt Default badge marks the studio default persona preference.

Supported persona wires include rcpersona with RoleCall V2 side-channel export, SillyTavern personas backup that imports the default persona and seals the entire backup so others re-emit byte-true, Lumiverse account objects with pronoun triplet as data, and Marinara persona where theming and stat bars ride sealed. Codec headers document detection firewalls. Agnai persona has no real standalone file wire and is served by the structured-persona component on character cards.

docs.title: Concept: the regex editor
docs.summary: The Workbench surface for authoring a regex set. Source: `src/ui/apps/workbench/regex/` (one concept per file: `set-editor` chassis, `rule-toc`, `rule-page`, `phase-picker`, `fine-print`, ops in `session.ts`). Built by transcription from th
docs.semanticSummary: Regex editor is the Workbench surface for authoring a regex set under src/ui/apps/workbench/regex, transcribed from locked wireframes, with Library shelf in regex-shelf views. Everything shown about a pattern is engine truth from explainAst verified examples validate and travelLint; the UI never fabricates match claims. Three authoring modes, one rule keeps Guided Plain words and Pattern as lossless views on one pattern source. Platform honesty in the frame re-lenses Write-for phases fine-print fields and travel notes from capability matrices only. The full check (health) runs six linters with shadowing proven by real chain execution and safe duplicate fix. The recipe gallery offers thirty-seven engine-proven starters grouped by purpose. The test bench hosts live applyRules step cards and dialect import preview beside the editor. Fluid grammar collapses by pane container queries not viewport width. Source of truth is the workbench regex folder plus core/regex helpers shared with the engine page.

anchors.summary: Mode switch is per-rule and lossless: the pattern is the single source and modes are views. Guided uses quiz cards in binder grammar with three steps, an it-will-catch card from template plus verified examples and one computed miss, confession line, no raw pattern, and escape to Pattern. Plain words is RoleCall example-driven builder for match-these-words family analysis stems and match-by-example with syntax-colored slash readout token chips and inline try-it. Pattern is raw find flags replace with live plain-words reading under the box and an honest partial note when the pattern exceeds builder grammar.

Header Write-for tab strip re-lenses the whole editor per profile. Where it runs pills come from phasesForProfile so unsupported phases disappear and foreign phases already set show dashed amber. Fine-print fold shows only fields platformOwnsField. Travel-lint notes render dashed amber inline. All per-platform truth is read from capability matrices never hardcoded UI literals.

health-pane plus core/regex/inspect runs six linter checks over the whole set with problems first. Headline is shadowing detection: execution-verified examples per rule run through the real chain; a rule flags only when it provably never fires while an earlier rule did, and indeterminate runs stay silent. Duplicates get one-click safe fix switching the copy off in session until Save. Reordering advice is always fix by hand. Per-rule Health card shows that rule slice; heavy patterns wear quiet slow chips on TOC rows and N slow counts on Library shelf cards.

gallery-pane plus templates and template-catalog provide starter recipes opened from New rule. Thirty-seven recipes group Cleanup Guardrails Formatting Style Compatibility Roleplay. Each pitch includes Before After pairs the engine computed; catalog tests re-run every example so unproven recipes do not ship. Picking appends a pre-filled rule focused in Plain-words when the pattern fits words grammar otherwise Pattern with reading; Start blank keeps empty-rule path.

bench-pane hosts beside the editor never as a modal. A sample line runs through real applyRules on every keystroke with one step card per rule showing before after word diff, engine-span capture chips, overlay chips, or plain skip reason, plus a final what comes out card. Second tab is import preview: drop any of five dialects, see per-rule before after against the sample, and stage-pick rules into the open set. Narrow panes become full-screen takeover so the chain stays legible while editing.

Editor collapses by its pane width via container queries not viewport media queries. Below 34rem TOC becomes a Contents bottom sheet with pager, Write-for strip folds into head kebab, and bench takes full screen. Bench-open has its own 44rem stack point because two columns need less room than three.

docs.title: Concept: the regex engine
docs.summary: How hoplight actually RUNS a regex set. Source of truth: `src/core/regex/` (pure, no side effects). The entity it operates on is [entities/regex.md](../entities/regex.md); per-platform field/phase truth lives in `src/core/regex/capabilities
docs.semanticSummary: Regex engine documents how Hoplight runs a regex set in pure src/core/regex with no side effects. Rules are data executed as budgeted String.replace never eval or new Function; HTML-looking output only through SealedHtmlPreview and Risu cbs tokens stored then stripped before compile. The pipeline (`apply.ts`) runs applyRules in sortOrder with d-flag spans, per-rule and set budgets, condition chaining, overlay non-mutating matches, and firstMatchOnly, plus replace-ops group and case transforms. The AST layer (`ast/`) is a clean-room u-mode parser powering explainAst examplesFor analyzeRedos and dialect flag parsing. Travel honesty (`travel-lint.ts`) reports cross-platform lint for JS engines without forking parsers. The builder (`builder.ts` + `word-boundary.ts` / `word-family.ts`) turns word lists into verified patterns for Guided and Plain-words modes. Entity shape is entities/regex.md; platform phase truth lives in capabilities and platform-fields matrices, never as UI literals for pickers or the position-picker law itself.

anchors.summary: applyRules runs one deterministic pass in sortOrder. Every rule compiles with the d flag so match and group spans come from the engine as TraceMatch whole and groups for bench chips. Per-rule time budget and optional setBudgetMs skip over-budget rules with plain skipReason timeout set-budget phase off or condition never crash. condition chains on whether an earlier rule applied and matched in one pass without forward references. overlay true rules match without mutating and emit spans on a separate overlays channel. firstMatchOnly replaces only the first hit under g. Replacement text goes through replace-ops for dollar groups match sugar and case transforms with escape parity between runtime and travel lint. Replacement also runs JavaScript's own $& family, and those are the asymmetric tokens: this engine expands them and no other surveyed engine does, because none hands the template to String.replace, so a rule written to re-emit its match consumes it instead and every later rule keyed on that text stops firing.

Clean-room ECMAScript u-mode regex parser fuzz-checked against host RegExp as oracle, with spans on every node. explainAst supplies plain-words reading under Find, exhaustive over node kinds and honest about ASCII word boundaries. examplesFor generates matches each verified by executing the real regex before display so chips never invent hits. analyzeRedos detects catastrophic backtracking with culprit spans; validate delegates to it and falls back to heuristic only when the parser refuses. dialect.ts tolerantly parses flag tokens including gu cbs for imports from foreign wires.

All five platforms execute JS RegExp, so divergence is a lint, not a parser fork. travelLint reports with spans: replace and flag extensions the destination will not run, engine-only rule fields, and host-age risks. The dollar-ampersand family reports on every lens but this engine's own, because it works while a rule is edited and breaks once it travels. The editor shows these dashed amber under Write-for; nothing is blocked or mangled.

Plain-words layer under Guided and Plain-words modes: word and phrase lists become pattern plus explanation plus execution-verified examples. Unicode-aware boundaries handle space-less scripts and the whole-word toggle drops out honestly where word-boundary would lie. Structure atoms cover numbers anything-between and line anchors. Round-trips through explainPattern which carries full AST reading for any parseable pattern.

docs.title: Concept: safe content rendering (the render toggle)
docs.summary: Character fields carry authored markup: descriptions and greetings are Markdown, creator notes arrive as HTML, and short facts (version, creator, license) are plain text. The editor and the read-only inspector render that markup so a field
docs.semanticSummary: Safe content rendering explains how character fields that carry untrusted Markdown, HTML, or plain text are shown in the editor and inspector without dumping raw tags or running XSS. Authority lives in render-markup and render-policy plus the RenderBox and leaving-gate components. The pipeline (sanitize last) caps input, routes by format through marked or escape, and always finishes with DOMPurify before dangerouslySetInnerHTML. Hardening forbids script style iframe object embed and form controls, keeps sanitized style attributes, drops non-allowlisted hrefs, pins noopener blank targets, and memoizes results. The leaving-gate (external links) intercepts rendered anchor clicks, shows the real destination via a CustomEvent, and enforces open only through POST open plus safeExternalUrl with OS browser argv; recognition uses a local platform registry without network unfurl. The RenderBox component is the reusable toggle that takes value and RenderFormat, defaults render ON, and falls back to source for plain empty or editable blank fields.

anchors.summary: renderMarkup in render-markup.ts is the DOM shell and render-policy.ts holds pure decisions. Pipeline order is fixed: capInput truncates to RENDER_INPUT_CAP of 200k so giant fields cannot stall parsing; then format branches so markdown runs marked then sanitize, html sanitizes as-is, and plain HTML-escapes with no parsing; DOMPurify.sanitize is always the last step and its output goes straight to dangerouslySetInnerHTML with no post-mutation. The sanitizer is never hand-rolled because allowlist walks miss mutation-XSS. Policy purity enables unit tests without a DOM for isSafeHref http https mailto and relative only plus the input cap. The XSS battery in render-markup.test.ts runs real DOMPurify under jsdom and asserts sanitized output lacks script on handlers and javascript schemes rather than relying on alert absence.

Forbidden elements include script style iframe object embed and form controls while the style attribute is kept so authored text-align on notes survives after DOMPurify value sanitization. An afterSanitizeAttributes hook drops non-scheme-allowlisted anchor hrefs and pins target blank with rel noopener noreferrer so rendered links cannot share an opener or navigate the shell in place. The hook registers lazily on first render never at import so the module stays side-effect-free for desktop boot smoke that evaluates without window. Results memoize in a bounded map keyed on format plus raw so unchanged fields do not re-run marked and DOMPurify.

Rendered links are untrusted for destination and visible text so none navigate directly. RenderBox onRenderedClick intercepts plain left-clicks and routes to the full-window leaving-gate page that shows the real host and url and warns on externalLinkInfo mismatch when visible text names another host. Modified ctrl meta middle clicks stay native as deliberate open anyway. Because RenderBox and gate live in separate bundles the click crosses as a window CustomEvent via link-gate.ts not a shared module bus that would split-brain. Enforcement is server-side: POST only api open re-runs safeExternalUrl for http https normalized and spawns the OS browser with an argv array no shell. DOMPurify forbids form so content cannot auto-submit. Bare URLs in plain fields are linkifyEscaped through the same gate. Destination recognition uses a local curated platform-registry seed with monogram tile or neutral globe and never fetches favicons or unfurls which would be SSRF; widen by seed row only.

RenderBox under components render-box is the reusable surface with a per-box render toggle default ON. It accepts value and declared RenderFormat never a field id so field identity does not leak into the component; format is data-driven from characterFields InspectField tags and editor markdown for prose cards. Rendered mode shows sanitized HTML; source mode shows the raw editable textarea or raw text for read-only fields. plain fields have nothing to render so they show inline without a toggle. An empty editable field falls back to its source surface so editing a blank preview never costs an extra click.

docs.title: Concept: the tag taxonomy
docs.summary: Character tags arrive as free strings from every source format (`discovery.tags` is `string[]`); no format carries a category on the wire. The editor still colors each tag chip by KIND, so a pure classifier decides which category a tag stri
docs.semanticSummary: The tag taxonomy concept page defines how free-string character tags from discovery.tags become KIND-colored chips without any wire format carrying a category. Authority is pure categorizeTag in src/core/tag-taxonomy.ts with tests in the sibling test file; presentation colors and icons live only in workbench Editor TAG_CATEGORY_STYLE. Categories lists the eleven TagCategory values identity trait role genre theme setting pov mood kink warning and meta, each with coverage and editor color, after normalize folds hash lowercase and separators. Deliberately a seed, not the full taxonomy states the dictionary is a curated RoleCall-mirrored seed, unrecognized tags fall to meta slate, and the Open Tagsheet milestone widens SEED rows only never code branches so lookup stays one normalized Map.

anchors.summary: categorizeTag takes a tag string and returns TagCategory after folding to a lookup key by dropping a leading hash, lowercasing, and collapsing underscore hyphen slash and whitespace to single spaces, then reading a seed dictionary. Categories are identity for gender sexuality species cyan, trait for personality dere archetype violet, role for occupation dynamic relationship rose, genre indigo, theme for trope theme pink, setting for place era environment emerald, pov for narrative POV sky, mood for mood tone amber, kink red, warning for trigger content warning orange, and meta for authoring provenance plus the unrecognized fallback slate. Editor colors are presentation only; the pure classifier returns the category token.

anchors.text: Deliberately a seed, not the full taxonomy
anchors.summary: The dictionary is a curated seed of common tags mirroring RoleCall display categories, not the full roughly thousand-tag taxonomy. Unrecognized tags resolve to meta with neutral slate and are never mis-colored. The discovery milestone Open Tagsheet widens coverage only by adding SEED rows, never by adding code branches, so lookup remains a single normalized Map.

docs.title: Character entity
docs.summary: The canonical superset entity for a roleplay character: every CharacterBody field, its type, the formats that produce it, and its meaning.
docs.semanticSummary: Character entity is the field-meaning authority for CanonicalCharacter as CanonicalEntity character CharacterBody, with schema.ts owning types and this page owning what each field means and which formats produce it. How to read the field tables explains generated Field Type Producers Meaning cells from docs-fields. Composition lists eight always-present groups and optional presentation settings behavior plus bias worldName knowledgeRefs behaviorRefs variants. Identity covers name nickname and RoleCall casting attributes. Persona and voice holds personality scenario appearance Voice ImagePrompt and structured encodings. Prompts and injections covers system postHistory depth prefill additionalText and DepthInjection. Greetings and examples covers firstMessage alternate group greetings and mes_example. Media covers portrait assets Sprite visualKind faceLabel and MediaAsset. Presentation is casting-card color palette background spoilers. Settings and behavior first-classes dials and CharacterBehavior scripts never executed by converter. Attribution and discovery separates credit notes and ContentRating tags. Composition and variants defines body assembly links and CharacterVariant overlay. What rides escrow, not a field and See also close the map.

anchors.text: How to read the field tables
anchors.summary: Field tables are generated by scripts/docs-fields.ts and embedded verbatim; never hand-edit a cell, improve the schema doc comment and regenerate. Field is the canonical name with trailing question mark for optional. Type is the schema TypeScript type. Producers lists source formats from the doc comment or dash when untagged, including universal core fields whose provenance is prose. Meaning explains purpose; blank cells are self-evident primitives without schema annotation. Richer explanation lives only in surrounding prose never inside a cell.

CharacterBody groups fields into eight always-present sub-objects identity persona prompts greetings examples media attribution and discovery, plus optional presentation settings and behavior sub-objects and five standalone fields bias worldName knowledgeRefs behaviorRefs and variants. Grouping mirrors how a card is authored not any one app storage layout. Full CharacterBody and CharacterVariant tables live in Composition and variants at the end. Sections walk each group with tables pasted from docs/generated/fields.character.md.

Identity is who the character is: required name plus authored attributes. char macro resolves to name; nickname from CCv3 Risu Backyard overrides display without changing canonical name. tagline is a short one-liner. description is the main CCv2/v3 persona block. characterVersion is unannotated version text. RoleCall adds fullName title age as free text never int pronouns. Agnai culture drives default language and voice selection. Together these separate display casting metadata from the portable name slot.

Persona carries how the character behaves sounds and looks: personality scenario and Agnai appearance free-text, plus nested Voice for TTS selection not audio bytes, ImagePrompt for image-gen hints, and structured as a discriminated union that preserves attribute maps such as W++. Voice child covers provider voiceId rate pitch disabled and open extras. ImagePrompt child covers prompt prefix suffix negative template instructions emotionInstructions and labeled rows. Structured kinds text without attributes versus attributes wpp sbf boostyle requiring attributes so illegal states are unrepresentable. Other formats often fold appearance into description.

children.summary: Voice is the authored TTS selection and config, never model bytes which ride assets or escrow. provider is an open union including elevenlabs webspeechsynthesis novel agnaistic vits and more. Optional voiceId rate pitch and Agnai disabled keep config when voice is turned off. extras is an open Record for provider-specific knobs such as stability similarityBoost model seed and vits config.

ImagePrompt is creator text that steers image generation for the character. Sampler and provider knobs are platform config and are not modeled. Fields include Risu full base prompt, prefix suffix negative, Agnai template, Risu instructions and emotionInstructions, and Risu sdData-style labeled rows of label value pairs.

anchors.summary: Prompts and injections hold instruction-layer text sent to the model. systemPrompt is the universal system slot. postHistoryInstructions is SillyTavern jailbreak post-history. depthInjections is an array of DepthInjection entries. Agnai prefill prepends to the assistant reply common with Claude. Risu additionalText is a simple plain append not a depth injection. The DepthInjection child defines text depth optional role origin for re-export home and enabled toggle where undefined means enabled.

children.summary: DepthInjection places text at a fixed chat depth. Required text and depth; optional role system user or assistant. origin records which source mechanism produced the injection among depth_prompt rolecall_details and worldinfo so export re-emits to the original home. enabled is a creator toggle with undefined meaning enabled.

anchors.summary: Greetings and examples cover opening messages and example dialogue. firstMessage is the primary opening. alternateGreetings is an array of Greeting values. groupOnlyGreetings from CCv3 are group-chat-only and distinct from alternates. Greeting child is text plus optional title and format-local id for editing provenance that other writers drop, emitting only text and title. Examples child holds exampleMessages as the mes_example string slot.

children.summary: One greeting with optional creator title. text is required content. title is optional display labeling. id is stable editing identity and format-local provenance, not user-facing portable content; other format writers emit only text and title.
Examples holds optional exampleMessages as a single string corresponding to the wire mes_example dialogue block used for few-shot style character dialogue samples.

anchors.summary: Media holds image references and the Agnai composite-avatar recipe; bytes live in the asset store or data URIs. portrait is the main MediaAsset. assets from RoleCall and Risu carry extra images and expression outfit pose packs. sprite is the Agnai composite recipe when visualType is sprite. visualKind is open avatar or sprite mode. faceLabel prefers an expression-pack label for the body or variant and binds the portrait stage without a second asset store. MediaAsset child defines role name label primary ref mime. Sprite child is parts map plus gender eye body hair colors as recipe not rendered pixels.

children.summary: MediaAsset is one image reference and its purpose. role is portrait emotion outfit pose background or other. Optional name and RoleCall label for expression outfit pose variants. primary marks the main asset of its role. ref points into the entity asset store or a data URI. mime is optional content type.

Sprite is the Agnai builder-authored composite avatar recipe: named part selections in parts plus optional gender eyeColor bodyColor and hairColor. Rendered images are assets; this shape is only the authored recipe.

anchors.summary: Presentation is the optional casting-card visual identity omitted by formats without the concept. signatureColor holds a single solid RC or Risu color; a two-to-three color blend rides gradientColors instead as one concept two storage shapes. Account-level accent is not modeled. palette is Swatch arrays; background is Background with optional video rate. fieldOrder is creator display order. spoilers is RC reveal config with fields boolean map preserved not collapsed. mediaLinks are RC external reference links. Swatch child is label name hex. Background child is ref overlayOpacity videoPlaybackRate.

children.summary: Swatch is a named color in a card palette with optional label and name plus required hex value for the casting-card color system.
Background is a creator-curated backdrop reference with optional overlayOpacity and videoPlaybackRate when the asset is video, plus required ref into media storage.

anchors.summary: Settings and behavior hold authored inline dials and on-card behavior. Converter and editor NEVER execute any behavior payload: no eval require or DOM injection; execution only inside a later capability sandbox. Behavior re-emits only on its own format wire and is never blind-copied across formats. talkativeness is SillyTavern group turn weight 0 to 1. risu groups single-platform display toggles. responseSchema is Agnai structured-output config carried editable likely migrating to Preset later. CharacterBehavior child first-classes regexScripts as RegexScript twin, triggerScripts virtualScript background markup defaultVariables prebuiltAsset moduleToggles and privileged as warning and sandbox gate never execution. TriggerScript child is event conditions effects state machine rows.

children.summary: CharacterBehavior carries card scripts and background markup as editable data. regexScripts are card-embedded find replace twins using RegexScript from the regex entity with one definition and no separate table here. triggerScripts virtualScript backgroundHTML backgroundCSS defaultVariables prebuiltAsset and moduleToggles are mostly Risu payloads. privileged records that the card requested low-level script API as a UI warning and sandbox gating input never an execution trigger.

TriggerScript is a trigger state-machine script carried verbatim-editable with optional label, required event such as Risu type output input start, and conditions and effects as unknown arrays of condition and effect rows.

anchors.summary: Attribution and discovery cover credit provenance and how the card is found. Attribution fields include creator originalCreator source sourceUrl license creatorNotes as CCv2/v3 single-language notes creatorNotesMultilingual as CCv3 ISO map preferred over single-language and publicNote as RoleCall separate public from-the-creator note distinct from creatorNotes. createdAt and updatedAt are unix seconds. Discovery child holds free tags genre fandom ContentRating as all-ages mature or explicit kept out of free-text tags and contentWarnings as portable trigger warnings.

children.summary: Discovery categorizes the card for browsing. tags genre and fandom are free strings. rating is explicit ContentRating all-ages mature or explicit and must stay out of free-text tags. contentWarnings are optional portable trigger warnings on the card.

anchors.summary: Composition and variants is the top CharacterBody assembly of every group. worldName is SillyTavern intent to auto-load an external worldbook by NAME while knowledgeRefs links embedded lorebooks by canonical id. behaviorRefs links standalone regex script entities by id versus behavior which carries on-card CharacterBehavior content. bias is Risu NovelAI phrase weight pairs a different axis than lorebook loreBiasGroups. presentation settings optional. variants from RoleCall are CharacterVariant alternate versions. CharacterVariant child uses deep partial overrides via applyVariant with present keys counting as overrides including empty clear; mirrorBase true deep-overlays while false replaces whole defined sections.

children.summary: CharacterVariant is an alternate version of the character. overrides is DeepPartial of the body without nested variants; applyVariant in variant.ts deep-merges onto base so one field or a whole section may change. A field is overridden when its key is present including empty string clear; absent keys inherit. mirrorBase true or undefined is default deep overlay; false means each defined section replaces the base whole section while untouched sections inherit and name falls through when omitted. id is required; label optional.

anchors.text: What rides escrow, not a field
anchors.summary: Anything a single source keeps without a canonical field stays in escrow formatId raw and survives same-format round-trip. Cross-format conversion carries only the canonical body so private app data never copies into another app file. Escrow riders include RoleCall private ids, unmapped SillyTavern extension keys, app-local layout state, and source bytes such as PNG pixels in sourceMedia served as portrait. Authored on-card behavior does NOT ride escrow because it is first-classed in behavior as CharacterBehavior editable data re-emitted only on its own format wire and never executed by converter or editor.

Related authority pages close the character map. architecture.md owns the canonical model escrow hub-and-spoke and the adapter contract. entities/lorebook.md is the knowledgeRefs target superset. entities/regex.md owns behaviorRefs targets and the RegexScript shape of the card twin. concepts/character-book.md explains embedded character_book extract and re-embed. formats/README.md is the coverage matrix of every format and the fields it produces.

docs.title: Lorebook entity
docs.summary: The canonical superset entity for a lorebook (world info): every LorebookBody and LorebookEntry field, its type, the formats that produce it, and its meaning.
docs.semanticSummary: Lorebook entity is the field-meaning authority for CanonicalLorebook as CanonicalEntity lorebook LorebookBody, the superset for world info character book and memory formats baselined on RoleCall entry type. schema.ts owns types; this page owns meanings and producers. How to read the field tables repeats generated Field Type Producers Meaning rules from docs-fields. Composition is book settings plus flat LorebookEntry list and optional categories. Book settings covers identity globals budget and LorebookCategory folders. Entries is the large flat roughly 48-field entry with concern groups for identity triggers injection ordering recursion scan filters CharacterFilter side effects ST-lineage toggles NovelAI extensions EntryContextConfig LoreBiasPhrase LoreBiasGroup and metadata. What rides escrow, not a field lists RoleCall in-memory-only fields and wire twins. See also links architecture character character-book RoleCall NovelAI and formats matrix.

anchors.text: How to read the field tables
anchors.summary: Field tables are generated by scripts/docs-fields.ts and embedded verbatim; never hand-edit a cell, improve the schema doc comment and regenerate. Field is the canonical name with trailing question mark for optional. Type is the schema TypeScript type. Producers lists source formats from the doc comment or dash when untagged, including universal core content enabled triggers position depth. Meaning explains purpose; blank cells are self-evident primitives without schema annotation. Richer explanation lives only in surrounding prose never inside a cell.

LorebookBody is book-level settings for identity categorization matching defaults and budget plus entries LorebookEntry array and optional categories LorebookCategory array for folders. Unlike CharacterBody the schema keeps LorebookEntry as one flat interface of roughly forty-eight fields matching RoleCall in-memory entry type without named sub-interfaces. This page groups fields by concern for readability while schema and generated table stay flat. Tables come from docs/generated/fields.lorebook.md.

Book settings hold identity categorization matching defaults and injection budget. name description lorebookType as open world character scenario rules utility other genre fandom and tags identify the book. enabled is RoleCall shelf and Press export filter default true deny by absence elsewhere. globalCaseSensitive globalMatchWholeWords globalScanDepth and globalRecursion are book-wide matching defaults entries inherit when null. tokenBudget budgetMode token or entry and entryBudget set the active cap. entries and categories complete the body. LorebookCategory child is id name sortOrder optional enabled folder grouping via entry categoryId.

children.summary: LorebookCategory is a folder grouping entries within a lorebook. Required id name and sortOrder with optional enabled. An entry joins one category via categoryId referencing this id. Organizational only, unrelated to activation groups.

anchors.summary: A LorebookEntry is one triggerable chunk with stable id referenced by categoryId and escrow twin matching. The full flat field table is followed by concern groups not separate types. Identity and content covers title comment content enabled constant. Triggers and matching plus Trigger shape gate activation with selectiveLogic and null inherit globals. Injection and placement sets position depth role. Ordering timing and grouping separates sortOrder placement priority eviction displayIndex list sticky cooldown delay groups probability. Recursion and budget covers exclude prevent delayUntil ignoreBudget useMemo. Scan sources extend match targets. Filters and side effects plus CharacterFilter EntrySideEffect EntrySideEffects are declarative never executed. ST-lineage toggles first-class vectorized group scoring automationId displayIndex. NovelAI extensions include keyRelative contextConfig and lore bias groups with EntryContextConfig LoreBiasPhrase LoreBiasGroup. Metadata is the open bag.

children.summary: title is the display name mapping to SillyTavern comment. comment is a separate RoleCall internal authoring note with no ST home so ST import always nulls it. content is the injected text itself. Together with the table fields enabled and constant they form the entry identity and payload core.

triggers and secondaryTriggers are keyword or regex lists gating activation. selectiveLogic combines secondary with primary as and_any and_all not_any or not_all. triggerMode advanced when triggers carry per-trigger probability overriding entry fallback else simple. caseSensitive matchWholeWords and scanDepth are per-entry overrides of book globals where null inherits.

Trigger has required keyword and isRegex plus optional flags for regex g i m s u y, frequency as min messages before re-activation, and probability for advanced mode per-trigger chance 0-100 overriding entry fallback. Wire regex is slash pattern flags; canonical carries isRegex and flags structurally instead of a delimited string.

position chooses where content lands: world and character are the portable floor every format has as SillyTavern before after character definition; richer positions degrade to that floor on downcast to CCv2 character_book. depth applies when position is depth or append. role is system user or assistant for the injected message voice.

sortOrder is placement order in the assembled prompt the universal axis every format names differently. priority is eviction priority when budget is exceeded higher survives a separate axis. displayIndex is a third list-order axis detailed under ST-lineage. sticky cooldown and delay are turn-counted timing. groupName with groupWeight is activation mutual exclusion; categoryId is organizational only. probability is entry-level activation chance fallback for simple triggers.

excludeRecursion keeps the entry from being found by recursive scan of other entries so only direct matches apply. preventRecursion stops this entry content from triggering others. delayUntilRecursion activates only at recursion level N with zero as first pass. ignoreBudget always injects bypassing token budget. useMemo marks client-specific memo behavior.

scanCharacterDescription scanCharacterPersonality scanUserPersona and scanScenario extend keyword matching beyond chat to those character and user texts. scanCharacterDepthPrompt and scanCreatorNotes are SillyTavern-only extras where undefined means the format has no field not that scanning is off. scanCreatorNotes lacks its own producer tag because the schema comment covers both ST sources together; the SillyTavern lorebook codec confirms matchCreatorNotes round-trips like its sibling.

characterFilter whitelists or blacklists the entry to specific characters or character tags. sideEffects lists variable mutations to run when the entry activates. Both are declarative data shapes; Hoplight never executes them. Detailed field shapes follow in CharacterFilter EntrySideEffect and EntrySideEffects children.
CharacterFilter has names and tags string arrays plus isExclude boolean to whitelist or blacklist which characters an entry may activate for, matching by character name or tag membership.

EntrySideEffect is one variable mutation row: type among setvar addvar incvar decvar delvar, variable name, optional value for setvar, optional amount for addvar incvar decvar, and scope local or global. Declarative data only; converter and editor never execute.

EntrySideEffects wraps effects as EntrySideEffect array plus onlyOnFirstTrigger and clearOnDeactivate booleans controlling when mutations apply relative to activation lifecycle. Still declarative never executed by Hoplight.

vectorized groupOverride useGroupScoring automationId and displayIndex are authored SillyTavern-lineage fields first-classed under schema-is-editor even though only ST serializes them today. vectorized is the RAG setting not the vectors which stay escrow. groupOverride and useGroupScoring extend groupName groupWeight mutual exclusion. automationId binds Quick-Reply automation by id only automation set stays escrow. displayIndex is creator manual list order distinct from sortOrder; real cards diverge so it is never regenerated from sortOrder.

keyRelative makes keys match relative to the entry insertion point not story tail. nonStoryActivatable allows activation outside story text such as UI actions. contextConfig is NovelAI per-entry assembly prefix suffix trim and budget dials detailed in EntryContextConfig. loreBiasGroups carries NovelAI phrase bias groups applied while the entry is active or whenInactive not active.

EntryContextConfig is NovelAI authored per-entry assembly: prefix and suffix text, tokenBudget and reservedTokens, trimDirection doNotTrim trimBottom trimTop open, insertionType newline space token, maximumTrimType sentence newline token, and insertionPosition as signed offset within the target section not canonical depth. NAI budgetPriority is deliberately not modeled here because placement lives in sortOrder one home per axis.
LoreBiasPhrase holds optional sequence string sequences string array and type as NovelAI phrase type integer open enum on the wire for members of a lore bias group.

LoreBiasGroup is a NovelAI phrase bias group with enabled boolean, signed bias strength, phrases as LoreBiasPhrase array, and optional whenInactive generateOnce and ensureSequenceFinish controls for when and how the bias applies relative to entry activity.
