metadata is an open Record string unknown bag for format-specific data that has no first-class canonical home on the entry, extensible without inventing body slots.

anchors.text: What rides escrow, not a field
anchors.summary: Per the superset rule a field needs a real wire serializer. Rides escrow because no serializer emits them: five RoleCall in-memory-only fields allowRecursion boostIds boostAmount scanPreset and probabilityMode verified absent from packages/lorebook serialize and parser with hard-coded defaults and corroborated by this repo RoleCall lorebook codec never naming them. Format-specific wire bytes also ride raw twin for lossless same-format round trip: SillyTavern entry uid derives canonical id then re-emits from twin, RoleCall export envelope tree exportDate unsupportedFields and trigger runtime state. Does NOT ride escrow: ST extra scan sources vectorized groupOverride useGroupScoring automationId and displayIndex which are authored wire fields first-classed by schema-is-editor.

Related authority: architecture for canonical model escrow hub-and-spoke and adapter contract; character for knowledgeRefs linking; character-book concept for embedded character_book extract and re-embed; rolecall format as baseline of the canonical entry shape; novelai format as source of contextConfig loreBiasGroups keyRelative nonStoryActivatable; formats README for the producer coverage matrix.

docs.title: Pack entity
docs.summary: The canonical studio entity for a reusable expression/sprite pack: every PackBody field, its type, and its meaning.
docs.semanticSummary: Pack entity is the field-meaning authority for CanonicalPack as CanonicalEntity pack PackBody, a studio-only reusable expression sprite pack with no format adapter, no toCanonical fromCanonical, and no formats matrix row. schema.ts owns the PackBody type; this page owns meanings. How to read the field table notes every Producers cell is dash because fields are studio-authored not wire-imported. Composition is a flat name brief pack and optional groups map with no eight-group CharacterBody layout. Pack body table covers library name shelf brief the main SpritePackValue pack and Lumi-style multi-character groups. The sprite pack hub shape defines SpritePackValue and SpritePackItem in core media pack.ts shared with character media.assets role emotion including resolvePackFace defaults. What rides escrow, not a field states packs never carry original escrow. See also links architecture character Media and formats matrix.

anchors.text: How to read the field table
anchors.summary: The field table is generated by scripts/docs-fields.ts and embedded verbatim; never hand-edit a cell, improve the schema doc comment and regenerate. Field is the canonical name with trailing question mark for optional. Type is the schema TypeScript type. Producers are always dash on this page because pack has no adapter and fields are studio-authored not carried from a wire format. Meaning explains purpose; blank meaning cells do not occur here. Richer explanation lives only in surrounding prose never inside a cell.

PackBody stays flat with name optional shelf brief the pack SpritePackValue and optional groups map of named SpritePackValue entries. There are no always-present sub-objects like CharacterBody eight groups. pack and each groups entry share SpritePackValue the label-to-image hub that character media.assets role emotion also project through. SpritePackValue and SpritePackItem live in src/core/media/pack.ts not pack schema so docs-fields does not generate their table; prose covers them under The sprite pack hub shape. The body table comes from docs/generated/fields.pack.md.

PackBody fields: name is the library and tab name. brief is a short shelf card blurb never host wire. pack is the emotion pack as SpritePackValue label to image hub shared with character media. groups is optional Record string SpritePackValue for multi-character Lumi-style groups where the flat pack is the default group when groups is absent.

SpritePackValue in core media pack.ts is the label-to-image hub for character cards and library packs. items is SpritePackItem array of id label ref into asset store or data URI and optional mime. enabled is pack-wide on off. defaultLabel picks the resting face; resolvePackFace falls back to a face labelled neutral then the first item. packFromMedia and emotionAssetsFromPack convert character media.assets role emotion through this same shape. groups holds one full SpritePackValue per named member for multi-character scenes as Lumiverse expression_groups; absent groups means pack alone is the default group.

anchors.text: What rides escrow, not a field
anchors.summary: Pack is never a toCanonical fromCanonical target so it never carries a foreign source payload. Every save path PackEditor Workbench New pack and Save as library pack from Manage Sprites writes bare CanonicalEntity pack PackBody with no original entry; body is the whole record. Rides escrow nothing because there is no wire format and original never populates. Item refs are authored inline data URIs or asset store references not binary carriers beside fields like character PNG sourceMedia.

Related pages close the pack map. architecture.md covers the canonical model the adapter contract and escrow rules that packs never use. entities/character.md Media section documents the character-attached form of the same SpritePackValue hub shape. formats/README.md is the coverage matrix and notes pack has no listed adapter because it is studio-native only.

docs.title: Persona entity
docs.summary: The canonical superset entity for a user persona: every PersonaBody field, its type, the formats that produce it, and its meaning.
docs.semanticSummary: Persona entity is the field-meaning authority for CanonicalPersona as CanonicalEntity persona PersonaBody, the user identity counterpart to character sharing prompt injection but first person user not third person char. schema.ts owns types; this page owns meanings and producers. How to read the field tables repeats docs-fields conventions. Composition is flatter with required name content and optional nested shapes; four adapters RoleCall SillyTavern Lumiverse Marinara ship today with RoleOut PNG pending. Core content separates brief never inject from content inject text and keeps sections both. Identity covers free-text age and Lumiverse pronounSet. Presentation is RoleCall theming and imageUrl. Knowledge, rating, and chat injection links lorebooks ContentRating and dual position dialects. Attribution uses ISO createdAt. Media is studio portrait only. PersonaBody assembles all fields. What rides escrow, not a field and See also close multi-record and modeled fields.

anchors.text: How to read the field tables
anchors.summary: Field tables are generated by scripts/docs-fields.ts and embedded verbatim; never hand-edit a cell, improve the schema doc comment and regenerate. Field is the canonical name with trailing question mark for optional. Type is the schema TypeScript type. Producers lists source formats or dash when untagged including universal name content brief. Meaning explains purpose; blank cells are self-evident primitives. Richer explanation lives only in surrounding prose never inside a cell.

PersonaBody is flatter than CharacterBody: required name and content plus eleven optional fields. Six nest named shapes sections identity presentation chatInjection attribution media; the rest are scalars or reference lists. Full table is under PersonaBody. Four adapters produce personas today RoleCall two shapes SillyTavern Lumiverse and Marinara. Legacy RoleOut PNG and foreign-V2/V3-card-as-persona are specced in specs formats personas but have no shipped adapter and rolecall format lists them pending. Tables come from docs/generated/fields.persona.md.

Core content is the persona voice and shelf discovery. name is the canonical identifier. brief is the short library-card blurb and is NEVER the injected text. content is the full first-person text injected as user voice. Swapping brief and content was a live RoleCall production bug; every codec replicates the fix not the bug. sectionOrder is creator display order for sections; traits are RC personality-descriptor tags. sections is a structured alternative source for content; canonical keeps both unlike source formats content-wins rule so the editor can structure-edit flat sources. Compiling sections into content is codec serialize work in fixed order appearance body personality quirks history as Label text blocks. Sections child lists those five optional string fields.

children.summary: PersonaSections holds optional appearance body personality quirks and history strings that codecs may compile into content at serialize time in that fixed order as labeled blocks for structured editing of the user persona voice.

anchors.summary: Identity holds RoleCall casting-card attributes: tagline age as free text never int height pronouns as free-text display for RC ST round-trip and pronounSet as Lumiverse structured triplet additive elsewhere. Pronoun set child is subjective objective possessive strings engines can conjugate with, distinct from free-text pronouns.

children.summary: PersonaPronounSet is Lumiverse structured pronouns with required subjective objective and possessive strings for engine conjugation, additive and absent on other producers unlike free-text pronouns.

anchors.summary: Presentation is RoleCall visual identity: signatureColor, colors as character Swatch array, and imageUrl as external image URL for JSON export. PNG export instead carries the image as the file body itself using the same binary-carrier pattern architecture describes for character portraits.

knowledgeRefs links ordered canonical lorebook ids by reference never inline copy same as CharacterBody. rating reuses ContentRating; RoleCall wire is two-way all_hours after_dark so mature narrows to after_dark on RC export a documented one-way loss. chatInjection places content with position open union covering RoleCall world character scene depth and SillyTavern prompt author_note_top author_note_bottom in_chat none plus depth role and RC wrapper injection_prefix. Platform lens visibility is injectionsForProfile in core persona platform-fields never UI hardcodes.

Attribution holds credit and provenance for the persona: optional creator version createdAt and source. createdAt is ISO 8601 text not unix seconds because the rcpersona wire itself carries strings. source is an open origin platform tag such as rolecall sillytavern or custom. This is distinct from CharacterBody attribution createdAt which uses numeric unix seconds.

Media is studio-side only. media.portrait is the same slot CharacterBody media.portrait fills so the studio portrait resolver can read a data-URI MediaAsset from in-editor upload. Codecs map explicit fields only so this portrait never leaks into a foreign wire format.

PersonaBody assembles every field: required name and content; optional brief never inject; sections both kept with content; sectionOrder traits; identity presentation knowledgeRefs rating chatInjection attribution and media portrait. Table meanings restate brief content distinction sections compile rule knowledgeRefs reference-not-inline rating map and studio media. This is the top shape codecs and the studio editor read and write.

anchors.text: What rides escrow, not a field
anchors.summary: Unmodeled source facts stay in original formatId raw for same-format lossless round trip; cross-format carries only body. Rides escrow: RoleCall private ids and unmapped extensions.rolecall keys; every other persona in a SillyTavern personas backup because one entity per file imports only default or first persona and export overlays the edited one so the sealed rest re-emit byte-true; Lumiverse folder is_narrator metadata timestamps; Marinara whole game layer theming stat bars avatar crop tags and scenario with no canonical home. Does NOT ride escrow: pronounSet chatInjection sections identity presentation which are first-classed and survive cross-format.

Related authority pages: architecture.md for canonical model escrow hub-and-spoke and adapter contract; entities/character.md as the sibling superset sharing ContentRating Swatch and MediaAsset; formats/rolecall.md for both RoleCall persona shapes and the cross-kind firewall against character; formats/sillytavern.md for the personas-backup codec; formats/README.md for the producer coverage matrix.

docs.title: Preset entity
docs.summary: The canonical superset entity for a chat-completion prompt-manager preset: every PresetBody field, its type, the formats that produce it, and its meaning.
docs.semanticSummary: Preset entity is the field-meaning authority for CanonicalPreset as CanonicalEntity preset PresetBody modeling the SillyTavern chat-completion prompt-manager family of ordered prompt blocks samplers and settings that RoleCall Marinara and Lumiverse dialects center on. Other ST preset subtypes context instruct sysprompt text-completion reasoning are out of scope. PresetAdapter is in the FormatAdapter union and four adapters read and write presets (SillyTavern RoleCall Marinara Lumiverse); no dedicated CLI preset subcommand, presets ride the generic inspect and convert commands, and Library and Workbench also author PresetBody directly. LiveBuild preview orders enabled blocks and counts tokens chars/4 without resolving macros groups or choices and never evals. How to read the field tables and Composition introduce generated tables. Prompt blocks and groups cover PresetPrompt verbatim ids markers placement and Groups. Sampler and generation settings System prompts templates and behavior API and media options Choices walkthrough Full composition Linked regex sets What rides escrow not a field and See also complete the map.

anchors.text: How to read the field tables
anchors.summary: Field tables are generated by scripts/docs-fields.ts and embedded verbatim; never hand-edit a cell, improve the schema doc comment and regenerate. Field is the canonical name with trailing question mark for optional. Type is the schema TypeScript type. Producers lists wire formats verified for the shape even without a shipping adapter, or dash when untagged. Meaning explains purpose; blank cells are self-evident primitives. Richer explanation lives only in surrounding prose never inside a cell.

PresetBody requires name and prompts ordered manuscript plus twelve optional fields: groups and choices collections; samplers systemPrompts templates behavior apiOptions media generation settings sub-objects; description and enabled scalars; behaviorRefs link array. Grouping mirrors authoring not app storage. Full table lives under Full composition. Tables come from docs/generated/fields.preset.md.

PresetPrompt is one manuscript row mapping 1:1 to ST RC or Marinara sections. id is the VERBATIM source identifier never vaud-minted because order refs markers and isDefault key off it exempt from UUID regeneration. role is system user assistant. Per-block systemPrompt flag is not preset-level systemPrompts. placement follows position-picker law with relative in_chat append append_preset prepend_preset open union legality in platform-fields. marker structural placeholders use markerSlot. injectionDepth injectionOrder forbidOverrides injectionTrigger isDefault groupId wrapInXml xmlTagName extras complete the block. Groups child first-classes PresetGroup folders; ST derives divider ids from group id and escrows original divider only for imported ST groups so edits never invent escrow.

children.summary: PresetGroup is a category or folder of blocks first-class because Marinara groups and RC categories are authored. ST has no real groups and encodes dividers; the ST codec derives divider identifier deterministically from group id for vaud-authored groups and escrows original divider id only for imported ST groups so add rename move never invent escrow. Fields include id name optional content parentGroupId order enabled extras.

anchors.summary: Sampler and generation knobs are all optional: absent stays absent because round-trip forbids emitting values the source never had. Build applies defaults at compile time none stored on the entity. Surfaces match presets-core SamplerSettings and GenerationSettings. temperature topP topK topA minP penalties maxContext maxTokens promptPostProcessing contextMode tokens or messages and maxMessages when messages mode. Generation child covers seed completions maxContextUnlocked biasPreset.

children.summary: Generation settings include optional seed completions as number of completions presets-core n maxContextUnlocked boolean and biasPreset string. All optional following the same absent-stays-absent round-trip rule as samplers.

anchors.summary: Three optional sub-objects assemble requests around the manuscript with every nested field optional too. systemPrompts carries always-on utility prompts impersonation newChat newGroupChat newExampleChat continueNudge groupNudge assistantPrefill assistantImpersonation. Templates child has worldInfoFormat scenarioFormat personalityFormat Handlebars-ish card field strings. Behavior child has wrapInQuotes namesBehavior as ST numeric enum kept verbatim sendIfEmpty continuePrefill continuePostfix message-assembly flags.

children.summary: PresetTemplates holds optional worldInfoFormat scenarioFormat and personalityFormat Handlebars-ish format strings for card fields matching presets-core TemplateFormats used when assembling requests around the manuscript.

PresetBehavior message-assembly flags: wrapInQuotes, namesBehavior as ST names_behavior numeric enum kept verbatim not decoded to a named union, sendIfEmpty, continuePrefill, and continuePostfix. All optional.

anchors.summary: API and media options hold provider and request-level toggles as two optional sub-objects with every nested field optional too matching presets-core APIOptions and MediaSettings. apiOptions covers streamResponses for streaming replies, claudeUseSystemPrompt and useMakerSuiteSystemPrompt for provider system-prompt shapes, squashSystemMessages, functionCalling, showThoughts, reasoningEffort as a string dial, enableWebSearch, and requestImages. Media child covers imageInlining, inlineImageQuality string, and videoInlining for how media is embedded into provider requests. Absent fields stay absent under the round-trip law the same as samplers; nothing here is executed by the converter or LiveBuild preview.

children.summary: PresetMedia optional imageInlining boolean inlineImageQuality string and videoInlining boolean control how images and video are inlined into provider requests for the preset.

anchors.summary: PresetChoice unifies Marinara choiceBlock and RC ChoiceGroup: authored now run later when a run surface exists. Answers feed getvar key gate blocks via enablesPrompts or write scoped state via set. type one many toggle input with default shaped to match; options min placeholder suggestions separator randomPick sortOrder extras. Options child carries value enablesPrompts and set first-class so each source keeps its effect without dropping the others.

children.summary: PresetChoiceOption has id label optional description Marinara value for the choice variable RC enablesPrompts block ids gated while selected and RC set scoped state writes. All three effects are first-class; a source using one leaves others empty rather than collapsing shapes.

anchors.summary: PresetBody top shape: name description enabled shelf switch read as enabled not false so off presets skip export like off sets; prompts ordered real blocks never divider rows; groups categories; samplers systemPrompts templates behavior apiOptions media generation; choices walkthrough authored now run later; behaviorRefs linked regex ids. Dividers are never blocks; groups model structure.

behaviorRefs is the preset counterpart of CharacterBody.behaviorRefs: it names standalone regex/script pieces by canonical id instead of copying their rules, so the set stays one editable piece shared by every preset that links it. The link is canonical; embedding is decided per format at export. SillyTavern and RoleCall carry rows inside the preset file under extensions.regex_scripts, so their adapters embed a linked set. Lumiverse attaches by preset_id on the script instead, and Marinara has no preset-level attachment at all, so nothing rides inside those files. Each adapter's embedRegex owns its answer, and emitPresetBundle reports a set that could not ride rather than dropping it silently.

anchors.text: What rides escrow, not a field
anchors.summary: Design principle: model what the editor or domain authors canonically; escrow pure source-wire fidelity no editor touches. groups and choices are canonical not escrow because Marinara and RC author them. Rides escrow: ST per-character prompt_order overrides, Marinara variable layer, original divider identifier for imported ST PresetGroup, and extras bags on prompt group and choice sealed leftovers. Does NOT ride escrow: groups and choices themselves first-classed.

Related authority is architecture.md for the canonical model escrow hub-and-spoke and the adapter contract. That contract currently excludes preset from the FormatAdapter union so no toCanonical fromCanonical pair ships yet while Library and Workbench still author PresetBody directly through createAndOpenPreset and PresetEditorView.

docs.title: Entities
docs.summary: Index of the six canonical entity kinds, character, lorebook, pack, persona, preset, and regex, linking each one's field reference and the shapes they share.
docs.semanticSummary: Entities indexes the six closed canonical kinds every Hoplight convert path and studio path uses: CanonicalEntity Kind Body wrappers where body is the superset for one kind. STUDIO_ENTITY_KINDS in path-policy names character lorebook pack persona preset and regex alphabetically and grows only by union member plus src/entities kind folder. Four kinds have format adapters character lorebook persona regex while pack and preset are studio-authored only without toCanonical fromCanonical or formats matrix rows. All six store at studio kind id json via resolveStudioPath. Generated field tables explains each entity page embeds docs generated fields kind md from schema JSDoc via docs-fields.ts never hand-edited cells. Reference pages table links character lorebook pack persona preset and regex with what each covers. Cross-cutting ties sprite pack hub shape RegexScript twin knowledgeRefs behaviorRefs and persona as opposite-voice counterpart.

anchors.summary: Each entity page embeds its field table verbatim from docs/generated/fields.<kind>.md. That file is generated from live schema JSDoc by scripts/docs-fields.ts via bun run scripts/docs-fields.ts and verified with --check. Do not hand-edit a table cell on an entity page; improve the doc comment in src/entities/<kind>/schema.ts and regenerate so the published table stays the schema truth.

Index table of the six entity field references. Character covers identity persona voice prompts injections greetings examples media presentation settings behavior attribution and discovery. Lorebook covers world info entry set triggers position depth and per-entry per-book settings. Pack is a reusable expression sprite pack attachable to multiple characters with no format adapter. Persona is the user identity counterpart with name content sections and chat injection. Preset is a chat-completion prompt-manager preset with ordered blocks samplers and behavior studio-only. Regex is a named ordered find replace rule set covering the character-card twin and standalone script files.

Shared shapes span kinds. SpritePackValue and SpritePackItem in core media pack.ts are the hub for Character media.assets role emotion and Pack pack groups. RegexScript makes Character behavior.regexScripts the card-embedded twin of the standalone Regex set. knowledgeRefs and behaviorRefs let Character link standalone Lorebook or Regex entities by canonical id. Persona is Character opposite-voice counterpart sharing prompt-injection machinery as first person user versus third person char.

docs.title: Regex entity
docs.summary: The canonical find/replace-script entity for a portable regex set: every RegexRule field, its type, the platforms that produce it, and its meaning.
docs.semanticSummary: Canonical field reference for CanonicalRegexSet: CanonicalEntity of kind regex around RegexSetBody, the superset union of real find/replace-script formats. src/entities/regex/schema.ts owns the types; this page owns what each field means and which formats produce it. A set is a named ordered rule collection mapping to ST standalone or card bundle, RC script, Lumi folder or pack slice, Risu card or module list, or Marinara collection, stored under studio/regex id json. A rule is data applied as budgeted String.replace never eval; engine and editor concepts live on sibling pages. How to read the field tables explains generated docs-fields embedding and Field Type Producers Meaning columns. Composition frames RegexSetBody as small name description enabled rules, with nearly all surface on flat RegexRule identity content placement and vaud-engine-only controls plus nested RegexRuleCondition. The set table covers name description enabled and rules. The rule table stores find and flags separately, documents all 21 fields, and nests Rule chaining for condition ruleId matched. The character-card twin is CharacterRegexScript for Risu customScripts, re-exported as character RegexScript without full RegexRule alias. What rides escrow, not a field covers original format raw versus rule-level extras, and firstMatchOnly condition overlay as first-class non-escrow engine fields. See also links architecture character regex-engine regex-editor and formats README.

anchors.text: How to read the field tables
anchors.summary: Field tables are generated from the schema by scripts/docs-fields.ts and embedded verbatim; do not hand-edit cells, improve the schema doc comment and regenerate so docs follow. Field is the canonical name with trailing question mark for optional. Type is the TypeScript type in the schema. Producers are source formats named in the field schema doc comment; a dash means no specific producer tagged, covering universal core fields such as id label find flags replace phases enabled sortOrder or provenance described only in surrounding prose. Meaning is purpose; blank Meaning is a self-evident primitive without schema annotation, while non-obvious fields pull meaning from the schema comment. Richer explanation lives in prose around a table never inside a cell.

RegexSetBody is small: name, optional description, set-level enabled switch, and ordered rules list. Nearly all entity surface lives inside RegexRule, a flat interface whose 21 fields still group as three concerns: identity and content for what the rule is and does, placement for when and where it runs in the pipeline, and vaud-engine-only controls for behavior no wire format can carry. RegexRuleCondition is the small nested shape used by the single condition field. The composition figure and following sections walk each shape; every field table is pasted verbatim from docs/generated/fields.regex.md.

RegexSetBody is the top-level shape: the set name and description, its on/off switch, and the rule list. name and description are unannotated string primitives with empty Meaning cells. enabled is optional boolean set-level on/off matching the Library shelf enable switch and the lorebook enabled precedent; absent means on, always read as enabled not equal false; an off set skips export the way an off lorebook does; additive and optional so the risu character codec and in-flight set editor stay compatible without breaking older writers. rules is the ordered RegexRule array that holds nearly all of the entity surface.

find and flags store separately as Risu RC Lumi encoding; the SillyTavern codec folds and unfolds its single slash pattern flags wire string. flags are stored verbatim including Risu extension tokens such as gu cbs never stripped except at compile time. Reading the table: id through trimStrings is identity and content; phases through characterIds is placement; firstMatchOnly through overlay are three vaud-engine-only controls; enabled and sortOrder are membership state; extras is the escrow bag. Key fields include stable id, bare find without delimiters, default g flags, useFlags for Risu ableFlag, replace that may carry groups match sugar CBS or HTML rendered only via SealedHtmlPreview, trimStrings, phases, Lumiverse targets, substituteFind, min and max depth, runOnEdit, Marinara characterIds, firstMatchOnly condition overlay as engine-only with travel lint under every lens, and extras for per-platform leftovers. Rule chaining nests under condition: earlier-rule gate with ruleId and matched, one pass sortOrder never forward reference.

children.summary: condition is the only field that uses a nested shape. It chains a rule firing on whether an earlier rule in the same set did or did not apply on the same pass: one pass, sortOrder order, never a forward reference. A ruleId naming a rule that has not run yet or does not exist skips the carrying rule with an honest trace reason instead of guessing. Nested fields are ruleId string and matched boolean.

anchors.summary: CharacterRegexScript in the same schema file is the narrow card-embedded Risu customScripts shape: singular phase instead of phases, and no id enabled or sortOrder because the card wire has none. entities/character/schema.ts re-exports this type as its own RegexScript so there is one definition not two. It is deliberately not RegexRule itself: a full alias would change CharacterBehavior.regexScripts wire contract and break the Risu codec round-trip. It stays the small card-embedded twin until a real migration replaces customScripts with references to standalone regex entities. See character entity CharacterBehavior. Fields: optional label, find, replace, phase as open pipeline string union, optional flags and useFlags for Risu flag and ableFlag.

anchors.text: What rides escrow, not a field
anchors.summary: Anything a single source format keeps but no canonical field expresses stays in escrow formatId raw and survives same-format round-trip byte-for-byte under the shared entity doctrine. For SillyTavern this is original sillytavern-regex raw script rows for exact re-projection. A second finer-grained mechanism is rule-level extras: a canonical RegexRule field sealing per-platform leftovers with no first-class slot such as Lumi telemetry scope script_id or ST id uuid, re-merged untouched on export at row grain so edited or reordered rules keep their own leftovers rather than whole-file original replay. Does not ride escrow because modeled: firstMatchOnly condition and overlay have no wire home on any platform and travel-lint marks all three under every lens, but they are first-class canonical fields the Workbench can set and applyRules executes; export emits nothing for them on formats that cannot carry them.

Related authorities: architecture for canonical model escrow hub-and-spoke and adapter contract; character entity for CharacterBehavior.regexScripts and the RegexScript card twin defined here; regex-engine for how a set runs applyRules AST travel-lint; regex-editor for Workbench authoring three modes and test bench; formats README for coverage matrix of every format and fields it produces.

docs.title: Add a format adapter
docs.summary: Every format converts through one canonical superset model, never format to format directly; adding a format is one adapter, and it touches no other format and no core code (`architecture.md`, "The one idea: hub and spoke"). This page is th
docs.semanticSummary: Developer how-to for adding one format adapter under hub-and-spoke: every format converts through the canonical model, never format to format; one new adapter touches no other format and no core. A format is a folder under src/formats name; the loader scans the filesystem and skips underscore-prefixed folders such as _template and _shared; index.ts default-exports one adapter or an array for multi-codec families like SillyTavern. The contract in adapter.ts defines AdapterBase id label outputExtensions detect optional native generic coverage lens, then CharacterAdapter LorebookAdapter PersonaAdapter RegexAdapter with toCanonical fromCanonical and optional extractLorebook, discriminated as FormatAdapter on kind; AdapterInput and AdapterOutput are plain bytes text filename data not streams. Steps: copy _template so name is folder id and original escrow key; implement detect returning 0..1 with registry highest at or above 0.5 and reject sibling markers first; implement toCanonical with canonicalId and original raw or sourceMedia under the superset rule; implement fromCanonical clone-overlay twin or minimal object plus extractLorebook and context.lorebooks; declare coverage; done with loadFormats register and matrix regeneration. Declaring coverage explains CoverageDecl carries notes and path-prefix matching for honest platform lenses. Testing copies the Pygmalion suite shape. Non-negotiables ban core edits, demand the cross-kind firewall, escrow not blind-copy, and underscore only for inert folders. Source of truth tables the key core and template files.

anchors.summary: src/core/adapter.ts defines every format plugin. AdapterBase carries id as FormatId and escrow key, label, outputExtensions without dots, detect returning 0..1 confidence, optional native for hoplight storage never a publish target, optional generic for the plain family reader shown as Default, optional CoverageDecl, and optional lens false to hide from the editor platform strip. CharacterAdapter extends with kind character, toCanonical to CanonicalCharacter, fromCanonical with optional EmitContext, and optional extractLorebook. LorebookAdapter PersonaAdapter and RegexAdapter mirror the same shape for their kinds; FormatAdapter is the kind-discriminated union. AdapterInput is optional bytes text filename; AdapterOutput is optional bytes text plus suggestedExtension. Binary formats read bytes; text or JSON read text; fromCanonical returns what it writes plus an extension normally from its outputExtensions list.

Six steps complete an adapter. Copy src/formats/_template to src/formats name so name is folder, adapter id, and original name escrow key; pick kind default character. Implement detect 0..1: registry keeps the single highest score at or above 0.5 so specifics must outrank generics; reject sibling known markers before positive signals as Pygmalion does; wrong shape returns 0 never throws. Implement toCanonical: map to canonical body, mint id with canonicalId, stash parsed source at original name raw and PNG pixels in sourceMedia; only first-class wire-serialized fields under the superset rule. Implement fromCanonical: clone escrow twin when present, overlay edited body, fall back to minimal object for cross-format; optional extractLorebook for non-shared embedded books; re-embed via context.lorebooks. Declare coverage in a later section. Done with no core edits: loadFormats globs index.ts files and registers exports; bun run hoplight formats lists it; bun run matrix and matrix:check keep FORMAT-SUPPORT.md honest.

src/core/coverage.ts makes per-platform editor lenses honest: the editor knows zero platforms, so each format folder declares which canonical body path prefixes its wire reads and re-emits, and every lens state is computed from that claim. CoverageDecl has carries string path prefixes and optional notes as per-path tooltip remarks. Path prefixes match on dot boundaries only so greetings covers greetings.firstMessage never greetingsX. Add coverage.ts default-exporting CoverageDecl and set coverage on the adapter; Pygmalion is the whole pattern with identity persona greetings examples media paths and honest notes. Absent coverage is not an error: the lens marks the tab not declared and dims nothing, deny-by-absence. In this codebase every non-native character adapter declares coverage; lorebook persona regex codecs and native vaud-json do not. Coverage also feeds export dialog honesty lines, so undeclared coverage understates that dialog for your format.

Format tests live beside the adapter as src/formats name name.test.ts under bun:test. Copy the Pygmalion suite shape: shape guard accepts the real form and rejects every sibling; detect scores your format high and siblings zero on your fixture; toCanonical maps every field; same-format unedited round-trip is byte-identical; an edit reaches the wire; cross-format conversion to one other format keeps core text. bun run test covers formats; scope with bun test src/formats name. A lorebook-kind format additionally earns a round-trip fixture under samples/lorebooks name with real input plus expected canonical parse.

No core edits: adding a format changes only its own folder; if src/core or another format folder seems necessary the design is not drop-in. The cross-kind firewall holds: a character detector must never claim lorebook bytes or vice versa because both share one registry. Escrow not blind copy: only the canonical body crosses formats; extensions scripts and internal ids stay under the source escrow key and never copy into another format file. The underscore prefix means inert only for shared helpers fixtures or the template, never to half-ship a real format.

Authoritative files: _template/index.ts as starting copy; adapter.ts for contract kinds input output EmitContext; loader.ts for folders-as-schema discovery; registry.ts for detection 0.5 threshold and lookup; coverage.ts for CoverageDecl; canonical.ts for wrapper escrow and canonicalId; pygmalion index coverage and test as smallest worked example; format-matrix.ts for matrix and matrix:check; cli.ts for hoplight formats; architecture.md for whole-engine hub-and-spoke escrow and detection context.

docs.title: Agnai format
docs.summary: Agnai (Agnaistic) is a browser/self-hosted AI roleplay app with its own native JSON character shape. It is not Tavern-lineage: instead of a flat description block, its persona is structured, a `kind` plus an
docs.semanticSummary: Developer reference for the Agnai Agnaistic adapter family: native JSON character shape and memory-book lorebooks, not Tavern-lineage. Persona is structured kind plus attribute map, preserved in canonical persona.structured. Folder src/formats/agnai default-exports agnai character and agnai-lorebook codecs, both .json; schema facts come from Agnai source under AGPL as interop only with no code copied. Detection covers character score 1.0 when kind character persona object greeting string and schemaVersion body both absent to firewall vaud-json; lorebook scores 1.0 kind memory, 0.9 kind-less native entry keywords array, 0.7 standalone CCv3 character_book soft import, else 0. Field map Character maps name through settings.responseSchema and original.agnai.raw including culture appearance voice imagePrompt prefill single insert depth slot sprite visualKind and structured persona decode encode rules. Field map Lorebook maps MemoryEntry entry keywords weight priority and book-level scan fields with hardcoded lorebookType other. Escrow and round-trip details two-state character set overlay, always-rebuild persona multi-text collapse, three-state lorebook entryToWire, and extractLorebook applyLorebook for native characterBook MemoryBook not CCv3. Quirks list overlay differences, firewall, imageSettings per-key merge, single insert, embedded book mapper, and selectiveLogic ST residue. Source of truth tables adapter files schemas samples and Agnai interop paths.

anchors.summary: Registry keeps the single highest detect score above 0.5 so specific formats outrank generic ones. Character detect parses JSON and returns 1.0 only when kind is character, persona is a non-null object, greeting is a string, schemaVersion is undefined, and body is undefined; otherwise 0. The last two clauses firewall vaud-json which carries schemaVersion and body so Agnai never fights the native wrapper on the same file. Parse failure or missing text returns 0. Agnai scores 1.0 not 0.9 as a self-identifying shape no other adapter supersets. Lorebook agnai-lorebook uses coerceMemoryBook: 1.0 for kind memory, 0.9 for kind-less books whose entries array first entry still has native entry plus keywords, 0.7 for standalone CCv3 Chub character_book with keys or content re-exported as MemoryBook, else 0 including SillyTavern keyed-object worldbooks and Risu envelopes without top-level entries array.

children.summary: detect requires kind character, non-null persona object, string greeting, and both schemaVersion and body undefined. Those absences block vaud-json collision. Failure or missing text yields 0; success is 1.0 as a specific self-identifying shape.

coerceMemoryBook scoring: 1.0 with kind memory; 0.9 kind-less array entries whose first row has entry and keywords distinguishing native Agnai from CCv3 content keys; 0.7 standalone character_book soft import via shared mapper; 0 for ST object entries and Risu envelopes.

anchors.summary: Decode uses cardToBody and bookToCanonical; encode uses applyBodyToCard and canonicalToMemoryBook. Only string values survive character decode via tolerant str and strList; only defined values write back. Character maps name description characterVersion culture persona scenario appearance voice imageSettings affixes system postHistory prefill insert greeting alternates sampleChat avatar sprite visualType creator tags json and whole card to original.agnai.raw. Persona kind text lands personality plus structured text; boostyle wpp sbf attributes keep structured attributes with personality unset; encode rebuilds from structured unless text. Lorebook maps MemoryEntry entry keywords weight priority distinct from CCv3 content keys, book-level scanDepth tokenBudget recursiveScanning, lorebookType hardcoded other, and documents weight to sortOrder priority to priority matching Agnai memoryEntryToNative interop comments.

children.summary: Full character table: identity name description characterVersion culture; persona personality structured scenario appearance voice imagePrompt; prompts system postHistory prefill and insert as depthInjections zero only; greetings first and alternate text only; sampleChat examples; avatar portrait sprite visualKind; creator tags responseSchema; raw escrow. Persona decode encode rules preserve attribute maps and collapse multi-element text attributes to first element. applyBodyToCard always rebuilds persona from canonical.

MemoryEntry uses entry not content, keywords array not CSV, and explicit weight placement plus priority eviction. Maps title content comment enabled constant triggers secondaryTriggers selectiveLogic position sortOrder priority probability excludeRecursion and book scanDepth tokenBudget globalRecursion. lorebookType is other; per-entry caseSensitive matchWholeWords scanDepth are null. weight to sortOrder and priority to priority match Agnai memoryEntryToNative interop comments verified locally for the local mapping.

anchors.summary: Escrow is original keyed by format id: original.agnai for character and original agnai-lorebook for books. Export deep-clones raw or baseCard then applyBodyToCard and pretty JSON; unmapped keys like extensions _id userId survive the clone. Character set is two-state unconditional write or delete string array without twin decode compare; malformed non-string skipped values stay. Persona always rebuilds so multi-element text attributes collapse to first element even same-format. Lorebook entryToWire is three-state diff by id Map so untouched entries re-emit byte-for-byte including selectiveLogic; optional book fields preserve twin presence. Embedded characterBook is Agnai MemoryBook not CCv3: extractLorebook uses memoryBookToCanonical identically to standalone; fromCanonical re-embeds via applyLorebook twin-overlay; no book means no key; empty bundle deletes stale characterBook; inspectBundle uses this override not shared CCv3 extractor.

Two-state character overlay versus three-state lorebook overlay: same well-formed result different mechanism. Persona always rebuilt; multi-element text persona collapses on every round-trip. Detection firewall is absence of schemaVersion and body not their presence. imageSettings affixes reconcile per key with sampler provider knobs surviving from twin clone. insert is single fixed-depth slot; only depthInjections zero re-encodes; role origin enabled stay undefined on decode. Embedded characterBook is Agnai-native MemoryBook via adapter extract apply not shared character-book mapper. selectiveLogic is ST-import residue on ST numeric convention never authored by Agnai editor so fresh cross-format encode never emits it.

Authoritative files: character adapter index.ts for detect toCanonical fromCanonical extractLorebook; memory book lorebook.ts and shared mappers; coverage.ts; shared character-book soft-import path and lore-enums selectiveLogic; convert and adapter extractLorebook EmitContext for bundles; character and lorebook entity schemas; canonical escrow; samples/agnai and samples/lorebooks/agnai; Agnai common types paths cited as AGPL interop facts only with no code copied.

docs.title: Backyard format
docs.summary: How the Backyard.ai (Faraday) adapter family detects, maps, and round-trips legacy flat-JSON cards and modern .byaf archives through the canonical model.
docs.semanticSummary: Developer reference for Backyard.ai Faraday adapters: two unrelated character shapes in one folder src/formats/backyard exporting backyard legacy flat JSON with aiName era writing .json and byaf ZIP archives with manifest character scenarios and images writing .byaf. Neither is a Tavern superset. Detection Legacy JSON scores 0.9 on Backyard-unique string keys aiName aiPersona aiDisplayName customDialogue, 0.55 weak persona-only fallback guarded against description and Agnai kind character, else 0. BYAF scores 1 only when bytes are ZIP PK with manifest characters and scenarios arrays and characters zero string, no weak tier. Field map Legacy uses firstStr alias lists and brace placeholder conversion on text fields; models two names display versus char shorthand nickname; leaves most CharacterBody unset beyond mapped slots. Field map BYAF maps archive via archiveToBody with verbatim text no brace conversion, multi-scenario alternate greetings with deterministic byaf path ids, media data URIs, and loreItems sampler transcript non-primary fields escrow only. Escrow and round-trip cover original.backyard with non-bijective toTavern toBackyard fieldOut unedited raw preserve, original.byaf full archive twin packByaf applyBody media and greeting path resolution refuse hostile ids, and from-scratch minimal shell. Quirks cover two-names fix, no version fabrication, lossy mature rating, one character per archive, titled versus untitled alt homes, BYAF detect no weak tier, creator tags bypass conversion. Source of truth lists adapter container scenario coverage sample files.

anchors.summary: Registry keeps highest detect above 0.5. Legacy JSON detect reads only input.text: 0 if no text non-JSON or non-object; 0.9 if any of aiName aiPersona aiDisplayName customDialogue is a string; 0.55 if persona is string description is undefined and kind is not character so it misses flat cards pairing persona with description and Agnai cards with kind character; else 0. Both scores sit below 1.0 RoleCall Risu Agnai and the 0.9 Tavern reader on shared inputs; 0.55 clears threshold barely by design. BYAF detect reads only input.bytes: 0 unless ZIP PK signature then unzips only manifest.json requiring characters and scenarios arrays and characters zero a string; match scores 1 with no weaker tier because schema-shaped manifest ZIP is unambiguous.

children.summary: Text-only detect with two tiers: 0.9 on Backyard-unique string keys, 0.55 persona-only with description undefined and kind not character, else 0. Scores intentionally below 1.0 specialists and sit at or under generic Tavern 0.9 on shared inputs.
Bytes-only detect: ZIP PK then manifest.json with characters and scenarios arrays and first character id string scores 1; any failure returns 0. No ambiguous middle tier in the registry.

anchors.summary: Legacy JSON maps identity name nickname description version personality scenario systemPrompt firstMessage exampleMessages creator tags via first non-empty alias lists; converted text fields run brace placeholder conversion; nickname carried only when aiName differs from resolved name. Unmapped CharacterBody slots stay unset and survive only in escrow. BYAF maps through byaf-container then archiveToBody: displayName name persona narrative formattingInstructions firstMessages exampleMessages images background attribution discovery rating; text is verbatim without brace conversion; alternate greetings fold extra primary firstMessages and later scenarios with deterministic byaf path ids; loreItems sampler settings chat transcript and non-primary scenario fields stay escrow only.

children.summary: Canonical table for legacy wire aliases: name from aiDisplayName aiName displayName name; nickname from aiName when distinct; description personality scenario systemPrompt greetings examples creator tags. Converted fields run toTavern on import. Everything else in CharacterBody left unset; other source keys survive only through escrow. Two Backyard name keys are distinct authored fields modeled as name versus nickname.

archiveToBody maps displayName name persona narrative formattingInstructions firstMessages examples images background author timestamps isNSFW rating. persona.personality left unset because BYAF has no personality description split. Alternate greetings from extra primary firstMessages and secondary scenarios with byaf path ids for stable re-import. Media re-embedded as data URIs; missing image files skipped. loreItems not mapped to lorebook refs; sampler runtime transcript and non-primary scenario extras stay escrow only.

anchors.summary: original.backyard holds whole parsed raw for legacy; original.byaf holds full opened archive base64. Legacy placeholders single-brace to Tavern double on import via toTavern with lookaround safe char; inverse toBackyard only handles char and user so is lossy. fieldOut re-emits raw when unedited so non-bijection cannot corrupt untouched cards; edited fields write lossy inverse. BYAF export rebuilds archive from twin, applyBodyToArchive, packByaf; sampler transcript grammar ride untouched. Media unedited versus edited split; clearing images deletes archive files. Alternate greetings match by stable scenario path id with hostile id refusal; orphan secondary scenarios deleted; titled title match only without resolvable id. From-scratch character synthesizes minimal manifest character scenario shell without requiring a source archive.

Two names two keys: displayName name versus aiName nickname; earlier fold destroyed distinct aiName and was fixed with regression WB-1; BYAF applyBody same rule. No version fabrication at parse; export invents 1.0 only for from-scratch without twin. BYAF boolean isNSFW is lossy toward mature never produced on import; export only writes for exact explicit or all-ages else leaves twin; from-scratch defaults false unless explicit. One character per archive characters zero only per ahoylabs cap. Untitled alts fold into primary firstMessages; titled alts become secondary scenario files; retitle alone does not move homes. BYAF detect has no weak tier. creator and tags bypass placeholder conversion on legacy.

Authoritative files: legacy adapter index.ts for detect toCanonical fromCanonical plus coverage.ts; BYAF adapter byaf.ts; ZIP container open pack original twin in byaf-container.ts; scenario and greeting id mapping in byaf-scenarios.ts; byaf-coverage.ts; canonical.ts for escrow and id policy; samples/backyard ahoylabs byaf conformance archives; legacy JSON shape fixtured only in backyard.test.ts because no clean public sample was found.

docs.title: Lumiverse format
docs.summary: How the Lumiverse adapter family maps ST-shaped character cards, regex scripts, personas, and presets through the canonical model.
docs.semanticSummary: Developer reference for four Lumiverse adapters: an ST CCv2/v3 character wire with Lumiverse extensions and an optional modules ZIP, a versioned regex export, an account Persona object, and a block-based preset wrapper that exports as a flat ST preset. There is no dedicated lorebook codec; embedded character_book uses the shared bundle layer. Detection, field mapping, bounded archive handling, dual escrow twins, module packing, character variants, regex and persona behavior, and the preset wrapper's import-only asymmetry are documented with their source files.

anchors.summary: Registry highest score above 0.5; ties resolve by registration order not content. Character checks ZIP first: modules json scores 1; bare module.risum scores 0 ceding to Risu; card.json with Lumiverse fingerprint scores 0.96; PNG chara ccv3 fingerprint 0.95; plain V3 V2 flat JSON fingerprint 0.95. Fingerprints include expressions expression_groups alternate_fields alternate_avatars lora name world_book_ids databank_ids ttsVoice. Fingerprinted cards outbid ST 0.9; plain ST without fingerprint scores 0 here. A genuine modules ZIP ties Risu at 1 because Risu claims any ZIP with card.json, but sorted folder registration puts Lumiverse before Risu and the strictly-greater registry comparison retains Lumiverse. Regex claims only type lumiverse_regex_scripts with scripts array score 1. Persona claims name description and both subjective and objective pronoun strings score 0.95 outbidding ST character heuristic 0.9.

children.summary: Character detection checks modules ZIP first, cedes bare module.risum, then requires Lumiverse fingerprints for charx, PNG, or JSON. Modules ZIP ties Risu, but sorted registration and first-winner tie handling select Lumiverse.
lumiverse-regex claims only self-identifying envelope type lumiverse_regex_scripts with scripts array for score 1. Bare scripts array or wrong type scores 0. No other adapter reads this shape.

Claims object with name description and both subjective_pronoun and objective_pronoun as strings at 0.95. Pronoun pair is the signal that outbids SillyTavern flat character name plus description at 0.9.

anchors.summary: Character field map reuses shared tavern-fields dataToBody applyBodyToData and CCv3 assets with lumiverse dialect identical to ST emotion typing. Lumiverse-specific data lives under extensions as native not escrow but almost none lifts to body: alternate_fields and alternate_avatars bridge to body.variants via altsToVariants label merge and variantsToAlts wholesale overwrite; resolved expression and avatar data URIs become media.assets emotion or other. Other extension keys stay Workbench native panel only. Archive regex scripts decode to RegexRule arrays under extensions but never lift to behaviorRefs. Modules sidecar rehydrate merges expressions groups alternate fields avatars world_books regex_scripts into extensions with resolveAssetRef 64 MiB cap leaving bare paths for missing or oversized files.

children.summary: Shared ST data mapping plus two bridges: alternate fields and avatars to CharacterVariant overrides by label; resolved expression group and avatar URIs to media assets. Remaining extension keys stay native. Module regex lands as typed rules under extensions without behaviorRefs. Variants export overwrites alternate_fields and alternate_avatars wholesale from body.variants deleting keys when empty.

rehydrateCardData merges lumiverse_modules.json into cloned extensions: expressions and expression_groups produce emotion assets when resolved; alternate_fields feed variants; alternate_avatars produce other assets; world_books and regex_scripts land on private extension keys with regex decoded to RegexRule arrays. resolveAssetRef turns archive paths into data URIs under 64 MiB or leaves bare path strings.

anchors.summary: Two escrow buckets: original.sillytavern with hydrated extensions raw, unmapped variant, and optional PNG sourceMedia; original.lumiverse with modules, fromZip, and a base64 files map containing every ZIP entry, including card.json and lumiverse_modules.json. SillyTavern raw extensions are hydrated and not byte-identical to input card.json when imported from ZIP. Export clones the ST twin, overlays body and media, merges current extensions, folds variants, applies lorebooks, and chooses the requested or source container. packModulesFromExtensions rewrites the two structured JSON entries, uses deterministic asset paths and typed regex encoding, and preserves other files from the complete twin map. JSON export from a ZIP can conservatively refuse when original archive content would be lost. Plain-JSON unedited round trips are field-lossless; ZIP round trips are data-lossless rather than path- or byte-identical. Cross-format output carries canonical content while both twins remain escrowed.

All ZIP inflate uses unzipBounded CARD_ARCHIVE_BOUNDS shared with Risu and BYAF: 96 MiB archive, 512 entries, 64 MiB per entry, 96 MiB aggregate. Regex codec converges account RegexScript export and reduced archive regex_scripts on one RegexRule with extras sealing account fields; placement maps to phases including memory; unmapped placements and substitution modes are not fabricated. Persona maps title, pronouns, knowledge refs, and image URL; its twin seals folder, default, narrator, and metadata. A from-scratch persona materializes required description, subjective, and objective string keys while optional possessive stays absent. alternate_character_name is a prompt override. Lumiverse preset import converts blocks to ST preset wire; export writes ST flat preset and does not reproduce the wrapper.

Authoritative files: character adapter index.ts for detect toCanonical fromCanonical and container selection; modules.ts for rehydrate pack and fingerprint; variants-bridge for alternate fields and avatars to body.variants; regex.ts for both wire shapes; persona.ts; preset.ts; coverage.ts; shared tavern-fields assets png card-io; core archive registry and canonical; samples/lumiverse rich.extensions.card.json.

docs.title: Marinara format
docs.summary: How the Marinara-Engine adapters map regex scripts, personas, lorebooks, and presets through the canonical model.
docs.semanticSummary: Developer reference for four Marinara adapters: bare API data for regex scripts and personas plus native export envelopes for lorebooks and prompt presets. Tavern-shaped characters use SillyTavern while Marinara-only fields remain in the editor lens. Regex detection rejects overlapping ST rows before bidding 0.95; persona detection requires identity, authored text, and a theming/stat signal; unique lorebook and preset envelopes have structural gates. Field maps cover RegexRule, PersonaBody, native lorebook book/entry/folder semantics, and preset sections/groups/choices/parameters. Regex export rebuilds from canonical rules and extras. Persona, lorebook, and preset export overlay mapped changes onto sealed twins, retaining engine-only data. Empty persona sections are omitted on import, explicit clears survive export, and avatarPath is neither fabricated nor retained after an explicit clear. Lorebook nested folders and native entry exotica remain escrowed; preset string-encoded booleans, JSON fields, and unmapped variables/parameters survive.

anchors.summary: Detection follows the registry rule that every adapter's detect runs and the highest score above 0.5 wins. Regex bids 0.95 after four ordered gates over a non-empty object array: reject ST scriptName, require id and findRegex on every row, and require a Marinara signal among targetCharacterIds, order, or string placement. Persona bids 0.95 only with string identity and text plus nameColor, boxColor, or personaStats. Lorebook bids 1.0 for the unique marinara_lorebook envelope with data.entries. Preset bids 0.95 for marinara_preset with data.preset and data.sections; groups and choiceBlocks are optional, and raw database string encodings are accepted.

children.summary: detect returns 0.95 for a recognizable Marinara dump and 0 otherwise. The score is 0.95 not lower because SillyTavern's regex codec claims 0.9 on the shared findRegex replaceString shape, and even the ST-form fixture is named marinara-essentials. readMarinaraRows fails closed on the first of four gates: non-empty plain-object array; any scriptName rejects the whole file as ST dialect; every row needs string id and findRegex; at least one row needs targetCharacterIds, order, or placement ai_output or user_input. Real ST rows always carry scriptName so this adapter scores 0 and ST keeps its files.

detect returns 0.95 for a recognizable Marinara persona object and 0 otherwise. readMarinaraPersona requires all three: string id and name; string description and personality; and at least one theming or stat signal among nameColor, boxColor, or personaStats. The codec comment calls this combination disjoint from Lumi ST and RoleCall so a plain id name description object fails before any name-based disambiguation is needed.

marinara-lorebook scores 1.0 only for the unique marinara_lorebook envelope with object data and an entries array. Version, metadata, and folders remain tolerant payload fields rather than detection requirements.

marinara-preset scores 0.95 only for marinara_preset with object data.preset and array data.sections. Groups and choices are optional; string booleans and JSON-string nested fields match the engine export.

anchors.summary: Field map covers all four codecs. Regex maps each row to one RegexRule and derives set name from filename. Persona maps authored text, optional sections, brief, and image while sealing ids, themes, stats, crop, tags, and timestamps. Lorebook maps book budgets and recursion, plain-string keys with one useRegex flag, selective/matching/injection/timing/group/filter/source fields, order to sortOrder, and folder rows to flat categories while preserving nested parents. Preset maps sections to prompts, groups, choice blocks, supported samplers, and API options; string booleans and JSON strings are decoded, while conversation/game prompts, variables, metadata, and unmapped parameters remain in escrow.

children.summary: The wire row is MarinaraRegexScript, one row per canonical RegexRule. id maps to id, name to label, findRegex to find as bare pattern without delimiters, flags and replaceString to flags and replace, trimStrings empty as undefined, placement ai_output user_input to phases output input with dedup order preserved, promptOnly true to targets prompt, depths passthrough, targetCharacterIds to characterIds empty as undefined, enabled and order to enabled and sortOrder, createdAt updatedAt to extras only. The regex set itself has no Marinara wire home: name derives from filename; description and set-level enabled never touch a Marinara file.

The wire object has no spec or envelope name; shape recognition is the Detection gate. name maps to name, description to content as the full first-person user voice, comment to brief when non-empty after trim, appearance personality backstory to sections appearance personality history when non-empty, avatarPath to presentation.imageUrl when truthy, and attribution.source is always synthesized as the literal marinara because the wire has no attribution field. id scenario theming stats crop tags timestamps have no canonical slot and ride sealed in escrow.

The native lorebook envelope carries one book row, entry rows, and folder rows. Book mapping covers name, description, category, tags, enabled state, scan depth, recursion, token budget, and entry limit. Entries map plain primary and secondary keys plus one useRegex flag, selective logic, match settings, position/depth/role, order as canonical sortOrder rather than priority, timing, groups, folder, probability, recursion, character filters, and additional scan sources. Folder rows project to categories; nested parentFolderId and other engine-only fields survive in escrow.

Preset section rows map to prompts with role, enable and marker state, group, ordered or depth placement, XML wrapping, override refusal, and marker slot. Group rows carry parent, order, and enabled. Choice blocks carry question, variable, cardinality, JSON-string options, separator, random pick, and sort order. The parameters JSON string maps supported samplers and squash-system, show-thoughts, and reasoning-effort API options. Conversation/game prompts, variables, author metadata, and unsupported parameters remain on the raw twin.

anchors.summary: Escrow is the canonical wrapper original field keyed by format id. Regex seals the imported row array but rebuilds output from canonical rules and extras. Persona clones its twin and overwrites mapped fields; hub ids and Marinara business ids remain separate. Lorebook and preset also clone complete native envelopes, match rows by stable ids, and patch only mapped differences, retaining nested folder state, engine-only entry fields, preset variables, unsupported parameters, and metadata. Fresh entities emit minimal native envelopes. These are structural JSON round trips; whitespace and object-key order are not promised.

Quirks pin behavioral edges. Marinara regex detection outbids the overlapping SillyTavern shape through four gates. Whitespace-only persona sections are omitted on import, while an explicit empty section survives export. A fresh persona does not fabricate avatarPath; clearing an imported canonical image deletes the twin's key, while unchanged absence stays absent. Character cards still use the SillyTavern adapter and expose Marinara extras only through the editor lens. No dedicated Marinara design spec exists in this checkout.

Source of truth table maps regex to index.ts, persona to persona.ts, lorebooks to lorebook.ts, and presets to preset.ts. Shared regex mapping, filename naming, JSON readers, the character-side editor lens, canonical escrow, entity schemas, format tests, and the SillyTavern-dialect regression fixture are also listed.

docs.title: NovelAI format
docs.summary: How the NovelAI lorebook adapter detects, maps, and round-trips native lorebook exports through the canonical model.
docs.semanticSummary: NovelAI format is the developer authority for how Hoplight's single novelai-lorebook codec detects, maps, and round-trips native NovelAI lorebook exports through the canonical model. NovelAI has no character card, so the family is one lorebook reader writer under formats novelai writing .lorebook JSON. Detection scores 1.0 only when lorebookVersion is numeric and entries is an array, scoring zero on ST object-keyed entries, Risu wrappers, or version alone. Field map covers NAI entry names versus LorebookEntry including keys as inline slash pattern flags, forceActivation as constant, searchRange as scanDepth, budgetPriority as sortOrder, plus nested Enums are strings on the wire, the searchRange unit caveat, the contextConfig assembly block, and Phrase bias loreBiasGroups. Escrow and round-trip seals the whole raw book under original novelai-lorebook and overlays by uuid or index with merge replace and category rules, including Cross-format into NovelAI no twin shells. Quirks list no book name, dual bias casing, non-clearable categories, priority never serializes, no character adapter, and nothing executed. Source of truth maps codec schema fixtures samples and tests. No design spec exists; content is read from adapter tests and samples.

anchors.summary: detect returns 1.0 when parsed JSON has a numeric lorebookVersion and an array entries, otherwise 0. Unlike SillyTavern's generic 0.9 which yields the ceiling to a more specific reader, nothing else claims this exact pair so 1.0 is the plain top score not a collision defense. Three shapes score zero: ST worldbooks with object-keyed entries, Risu exports wrapped with type risu and no top-level lorebookVersion, and lorebookVersion alone without entries. Detection does not sniff the version number; 3 4 and 6 all pass the same typeof number check because only entry-level richness differs across versions not the top-level shape.

Field map documents NovelAI entry names versus LorebookEntry. keys use inline slash pattern flags via shared keywordToTrigger with forceRegex false so bare keys stay literal. text becomes content, displayName title, forceActivation constant, searchRange scanDepth, budgetPriority alone is sortOrder and is placement not eviction, categories become body.categories, book name and budgets stay empty or zero defaults. Secondary ST axes like selective recursion probability and position are fixed defaults because NAI lacks them. Nested subsections cover Enums are strings on the wire for trim and insertion fields, The searchRange unit caveat on character versus message units, The contextConfig assembly block for prefix suffix budgets and insertionPosition, and Phrase bias loreBiasGroups as first-class canonical with dual casing accepted.

children.text: Enums are strings on the wire
children.summary: trimDirection, insertionType, and maximumTrimType are plain strings in both real samples on hand, a v3 slice and a v6 export. The schema records them as an open string union rather than a closed enum on the assumption NAI may add values. The codec does no int-to-string decoding for these three fields; whatever string the export carries is read and written as-is.

NAI searchRange is measured in characters of story text; SillyTavern scanDepth is measured in messages. Both map to canonical scanDepth as the closest home for how far back to scan, and the exact number round-trips losslessly through escrow on a same-format NAI trip. Cross-format import into a messages-based format carries the number verbatim with no unit conversion, so NAI 1000 characters becomes 1000 messages downstream. That is documented drift not a bug and does not affect same-format NAI round-trip.

EntryContextConfig is read field-by-field skipping absent wire keys so deep equality against the twin re-decode stays stable. Mapped fields are prefix suffix tokenBudget reservedTokens trimDirection insertionType maximumTrimType and insertionPosition as a signed offset within the target context section, a different axis than canonical position and depth. budgetPriority is excluded from this block and lives in sortOrder alone so it has exactly one canonical home.

LoreBiasGroup arrays are first-class canonical not escrow. The reader tolerates two casings for whenInactive generateOnce and ensureSequenceFinish snake and camel. The real v6 sample confirms dual casing for generateOnce and ensureSequenceFinish while whenInactive appears only camel; the v3 fixture has no loreBiasGroups. Mapped fields include enabled bias phrases sequence sequences type and the three booleans. bias is signed strength defaulting to zero if missing or non-numeric; phrase type is NAI's numeric enum carried open.

anchors.summary: Escrow and round-trip store only the whole raw lorebook at original novelai-lorebook raw with no unmapped or sourceMedia. fromCanonical overlays the body onto that twin matching entries by id on v6 uuid or by array index on v3 v4. Flat scalars replace when changed; nested blocks differ: contextConfig merges so twin-only dials survive and you cannot unset by omit; loreBiasGroups is replace-or-delete and edits drop snake_case duplicates while untouched entries keep dual casing; categories can be added renamed or toggled but not bulk-cleared by empty list. Twin-only fields include lorebookVersion top-level order lastUpdatedAt category subcontext settings and advancedConditions. Tests pin v3 field-level fidelity and v6 bias and category edits with 4-space JSON. Cross-format into NovelAI no twin builds each entry on a blank NAI shell with default contextConfig and lorebookVersion 3.

children.summary: A canonical lorebook from SillyTavern Risu or CCv3 has no NAI twin, so each entry is built onto a valid shell instead of overlaid. contextConfig defaults match a real NAI blank-entry export: empty prefix, newline suffix, tokenBudget 2048, reservedTokens 0, budgetPriority from sortOrder, doNotTrim, newline insertion, sentence maximumTrimType, insertionPosition -1. searchRange defaults to 1000 and the book writes lorebookVersion 3. v3 v4 entries carry no wire id so cross-format entries get none; a v6 uuid only survives on a same-format twin.

anchors.summary: Quirks pin edges already detailed under Escrow. The book has no name field so body.name is always empty and canonicalId falls back to character for the entity id. contextConfig writes merge while loreBiasGroups writes replace and dual bias casing only survives untouched entries. Categories cannot be bulk-cleared through this codec. Priority never serializes: NAI is single-axis budgetPriority placement and a regression test greps that the string priority never appears in a serialized entry. No character adapter and no bundle path exists because NAI has no character card. Nothing is ever executed; the codec is pure JSON transform and advancedConditions always empty so far rides the twin only.

Source of truth maps concerns to files. The native lorebook codec for detect field map escrow and twin overlay is formats novelai lorebook.ts; folder default export is index.ts. Canonical lorebook schema including EntryContextConfig LoreBiasGroup and LorebookEntry is entities lorebook schema.ts with field meanings in entities lorebook.md. Shared keyword slash pattern flags decode is formats shared character-book.ts. Committed v3 fixture is reformatted 4-space test-only JSON; real untouched v6 sample is samples novelai crystal dragon with provenance in SOURCES.md. Adapter tests are lorebook.test.ts; canonical wrapper escrow and id policy are core canonical.ts.

docs.title: Pygmalion format
docs.summary: How the Pygmalion adapter detects, maps, and round-trips the classic flat five-field character JSON and its PNG chara chunk through the canonical model.
docs.semanticSummary: Pygmalion format is the developer authority for how Hoplight's single pygmalion character codec detects, maps, and round-trips the classic flat five-field character JSON and its PNG chara chunk through the canonical model. The wire is legacy snake_case char_name char_persona char_greeting world_scenario example_dialogue as standalone .json or PNG tEXt, not Tavern-lineage CCv2. Detection scores 1.0 after rejecting CCv2 vaud-json Agnai and Backyard shapes, then requiring classic field counts or char_name plus char_persona, with registry 1 beating SillyTavern's PNG chunk-only 0.9. Field map places persona into personality with description mirror, scenario greeting and examples, portrait from PNG carrier, empty prompts attribution discovery, and export overlay that prefers personality over description. Escrow and round-trip seals whole raw plus optional sourceMedia under original.pygmalion with no unmapped block, clones for lossless five-key overlay, and treats inline PNG portrait as carrier authority. Quirks cover display-only description mirror, never-invented name alias, overlay never clears, persona-required minimal detect, metadata in raw only, narrow PNG output, and no sibling codecs. Source of truth lists adapter coverage shared PNG helpers samples and tests.

anchors.summary: Detection follows registry highest score above 0.5. detectPygmalion returns 1 for a recognizable classic card and 0 otherwise, claiming full confidence because no sibling shares its wire vocabulary. isPygmalionCard rejects known shapes first: spec or data for CCv2 v3, schemaVersion or body for vaud-json, kind character for Agnai, aiName or aiPersona for Backyard. Positive signal needs at least two of char_persona char_greeting world_scenario or the minimal char_name plus char_persona; name plus greeting alone is not enough. readCardJson decodes PNG chara ccv3 or raw JSON so the same scan applies to both carriers. ST PNG scores 0.9 from chunk presence alone so registry 1 beats 0.9 on real Pygmalion PNGs; reverse path returns 0 when decoded payload is not Pygmalion shape so real ST PNGs are never misclaimed.

Field map wires the five classic keys into CharacterBody. char_name with name fallback becomes identity.name defaulting empty. char_persona maps to persona.personality and is mirrored into identity.description on import only for description-only UIs. world_scenario becomes persona.scenario, char_greeting greetings.firstMessage, example_dialogue examples.exampleMessages. PNG carrier pixels become media.portrait and may re-export as the PNG container when the portrait is inline PNG; metadata has no canonical slot and rides original raw. prompts attribution and discovery are always empty objects. Export applyBodyToCard writes only when canonical is not undefined; char_persona prefers personality and falls back to description only if personality is undefined so description-only edits after import do not reach the wire. Legacy name alias is written back only if the source already had a name key.

Escrow stores under original.pygmalion the whole parsed card as raw plus sourceMedia b64 for PNG input only. There is no unmapped entry because Pygmalion has one wire shape. fromCanonical clones raw when escrow exists or starts from baseCard five empty strings then overlays via applyBodyToCard so unedited same-format trips are byte-for-byte including metadata. Portrait authority is the current canonical media.portrait: inline PNG becomes chara-embedded .png output; clearing produces JSON; explicit JSON drops portrait; unsupported refs fall back to honest JSON; explicit PNG without usable inline PNG fails. Cross-format carries prose and usable inline PNG only; metadata stays escrowed and is not copied into other apps; remote non-PNG portraits are reported dropped not fetched.

Quirks pin behavioral edges. Description mirror is display-only: import sets both personality and description from char_persona but export prefers personality so description-only edits never reach the wire. name alias is never invented; classic char_name-only cards stay that way. Overlay writes never clear: undefined canonical leaves the last wire value unlike Tavern three-state overlay. Minimal detection needs persona specifically so name plus greeting alone fails. metadata tool provenance rides raw only. PNG output is deliberately narrow with no remote fetch or non-PNG transcode. One codec only: no Pygmalion lorebook persona or regex sibling because the classic wire never carried those concepts.

Source of truth maps concerns to files. Character adapter detect toCanonical fromCanonical live in formats pygmalion index.ts; coverage declaration is coverage.ts. Shared card JSON reader for PNG chara ccv3 or raw text is formats shared card-io.ts; shared PNG chunk read write is png.ts. Canonical wrapper escrow original and id policy are core canonical.ts. Samples live under samples pygmalion classic.native.json. Tests are pygmalion.test.ts. Research provenance is reference platform-native-fields.md under the Pygmalion heading.

docs.title: Formats
docs.summary: Every format hoplight reads and writes. A **format** is a folder in `src/formats/<name>/`; the loader discovers it automatically (see [../architecture.md](../architecture.md)). Each format family gets one
docs.semanticSummary: Index of every format hoplight reads and writes.
