A format is a folder in src/formats name discovered automatically by the loader; each format family gets one reference page under this directory with architecture for discovery context. Coverage matrix points exclusively to generated FORMAT-SUPPORT.md from the live registry via bun run matrix with matrix:check failing CI on drift; a hand-maintained matrix here rotted once by missing three shipped adapters and will not be repeated. Reference pages table ships dedicated docs for SillyTavern RoleCall RisuAI Backyard Agnai NovelAI vaud-json and Marinara with their covered kinds; adapters without a dedicated page yet such as pygmalion lumiverse and chub live in source folders and the matrix. Detection scores are detect confidence with higher winning and more-specific formats outranking generic Tavern; recognition threshold is 0.5. Cross-cutting links character-book extraction and re-embed. Not yet built planned tracks honesty gaps: Wyvern lorebook needs no codec because there is no verifiable standalone wire, only CCv2 PNG character export with Lexicon either in extensions.wyvern escrow or in-app only; wire-gate forbids codecs from wiki-inferred zero-byte formats. Lumiverse World Books need no dedicated codec either: import accepts only Risu-native and CCv3 entries shapes already emitted by risu-lorebook and sillytavern-lorebook; export is the same; rich LumiWorldBookEntry is a database row not a portable file except inside .lvbak account backup as a separate multi-entity concern.

anchors.summary: The exhaustive adapter list lives only in FORMAT-SUPPORT.md, generated from the live registry with bun run matrix; CI fails if it drifts under matrix:check. A hand copy in this README rotted once by missing three shipped adapters and does not get a second chance.

Family table links dedicated pages: SillyTavern for character v2/v3 png/json world info personas; RoleCall for character lorebook regex persona; RisuAI for charx native lorebook risum modules regex; Backyard Faraday for legacy json and byaf archive; Agnai for character and memory book; NovelAI for lorebook; Vaudeville native vaud-json for the canonical wrapper; Marinara for native lorebook prompt preset persona regex and characters as CCv3 plus extension fields. Adapters without a dedicated page yet, pygmalion lumiverse chub, are documented by source under src/formats and appear in the generated matrix. Detection scores are confidence each detect returns for its own format: higher wins; more-specific formats outrank the generic Tavern reader on the same card; threshold to be recognized at all is 0.5.

Points to concepts/character-book.md as the single cross-cutting reference for an embedded character_book: how a card lorebook is extracted on import and re-embedded on export. That shared bundle concern is not restated on every family page, so adapters that ship cards with inline books should follow the character-book concept doc rather than inventing a second path.

Tracks planned honesty so the matrix separates exists from coming. Wyvern lorebook: no standalone wire format and no dedicated codec; Wyvern character export is CCv2 PNG already readable; Lexicon is character-attached so it rides extensions.wyvern escrow via CCv2 or stays in-app like Janitor with no serialized file; zero real public export means wiki-inferred codecs would violate the wire-gate doctrine that a codec exists only when a real wire serializes it; revisit only if a real standalone export lands with open questions on standalone serialization and CCv2 extensions. Lumiverse World Books: already covered by risu-lorebook and CCv3/ST worldbook codecs; LumiRealm parseDirectLorebook accepts only Risu type risu data array and CCv3 entries object; export returns Risu-shaped loreBook arrays; rich LumiWorldBookEntry is a database row not a portable file; only .lvbak full-account backup would carry it as multi-entity restore, not a lorebook codec. A native LumiWorldBookEntry file codec would be dead surface.

docs.title: RisuAI format
docs.summary: How the RisuAI adapter family detects, maps, and round-trips .charx character cards, a native lorebook export, and regex script sets through the canonical model.
docs.semanticSummary: RisuAI format is the developer authority for how Hoplight's risu family detects, maps, and round-trips .charx character cards, native lorebook exports, and regex script sets through the canonical model. The folder exports three codecs: risu character for .charx ZIP with card.json assets and optional module.risum, risu-lorebook for native lore JSON, and risu-regex for .risum or bare customscript rows writing JSON only. Detection covers Character via PK magic and card.json at 1.0 with bounded unzip, and Lorebook via type risu data array at 1 or character_book extract at 0.75. Field map reuses shared Tavern data mapping plus first-class extensions.risuai behavior media and book extract for Character, and native key secondkey alwaysActive insertorder folder modes for Lorebook. Escrow and round-trip seals original.risu with raw assets module and safety flags and overlays lorebook twins; same-format is data-lossless not byte-identical ZIP. Quirks document always CCv3, millisecond dates, selective media cross-format, behavior never executed, risum edit-blocked re-encode, risu-regex scores and rows-only export, native role, and insertorder as sortOrder. Source of truth lists adapters rpack helpers and samples. Regex codec detail lives mainly under Quirks.

anchors.summary: Detection splits Character and Lorebook. Character detect returns 1.0 only for a ZIP whose first two bytes are PK and whose bounded inflate finds a card.json entry; bare JSON never wins, and spec contents are not inspected so V2-shaped data inside still scores 1.0. Every inflate uses unzipBounded CARD_ARCHIVE_BOUNDS with 96 MiB archive and entry caps rejecting oversized input before decompress. Lorebook returns 1 for top-level type risu with array data, unambiguous against ST object entries, and 0.75 for portable character_book extracts so real Risu native always outranks the shared fallback.

children.summary: detect returns 1.0 for a recognizable .charx and 0 otherwise via two steps: zip magic first two bytes PK or score zero immediately so bare JSON is never claimed; then a bounded single-entry inflate only card.json scores 1.0 if present else 0. Detection does not parse spec or spec_version; a charx with V2-shaped data still scores 1.0. Inflates use core unzipBounded with CARD_ARCHIVE_BOUNDS max archive 96 MiB, 512 entries, 64 MiB per entry, 96 MiB aggregate inflated, rejecting oversized entries before decompress.

risu-lorebook returns 1 for the native envelope, 0.75 for a portable character_book extract, and 0 otherwise. Score 1 requires a top-level object with type exactly risu and an array data; that shape does not collide with SillyTavern worldbook object-keyed entries. Score 0.75 is a Chub-style or card-extracted character_book with entries array of CCv3-shaped rows, the same fallback ST lorebook accepts, scored below native so a real Risu export always wins any tie.

anchors.summary: Field map covers Character then Lorebook. Character card.json data uses the shared Tavern V2 V3 mapper identical to SillyTavern; Risu delta is first-class extensions.risuai for license bias additionalText display settings imagePrompt vits customScripts triggerscripts virtualscript backgrounds variables prebuilt assets module toggles and privileged lowLevelAccess, plus millisecond date unit fix, assets to media roles, and character_book as bundle extract not Tavern map. Lorebook maps native loreBook rows where key and secondkey are comma strings, alwaysActive is constant, insertorder is sortOrder not priority, folder is categoryId, mode folder rows become categories, and book-level name settings stay empty because Risu keeps them on the character record.

children.summary: card.json data maps through shared tavern-fields dataToBody and applyBodyToData like SillyTavern. Risu delta is extensions.risuai fully first-class: license bias additionalText settings viewScreen largePortrait inlay utilityBot lorePlus imagePrompt from sdData and newGenData, vits voice, customScripts triggerscript virtualscript backgrounds defaultVariables prebuiltAsset moduleToggles and privileged as lowLevelAccess warning never execution. Dates above 1e11 normalize ms to seconds on import and restore raw ms on same-format export. assets map to media roles icon main portrait emotion outfit pose background other with bytes in escrow. character_book is bundle extract via knowledgeRefs and re-embed on export; resolved empty list removes both slots rather than keeping a stale twin.

Native field names differ from CCv3: key and secondkey are comma-joined strings split trimmed with slash pattern decode and useRegex force. comment maps to title and comment, alwaysActive to constant, activationPercent to probability, insertorder to sortOrder never priority, role kept as native-richer system user assistant, folder to categoryId, enabled always true. mode folder loreCache bookVersion ride escrow; mode folder rows lift to LorebookCategory. Envelope has no book name or settings so name empty and budgets zero. Native and charx-embedded Risu lore must canonicalize identically matching character-book insertorder path.

anchors.summary: Character twin is original.risu with raw full card.json envelope, unmapped assetFiles base64 for every non-card non-risum zip entry, moduleRisum bytes, optional structured OpenedRisumModule, and hasExecutableContent plus privileged safety flags. Export clones raw or baseCard V3, applies Tavern three-state overlay, media merge, risuai twin-diff, restores raw millisecond dates, re-stringifies card with 4-space JSON, restores asset bytes, re-emits unedited module.risum or refuses edited, and re-zips. Data is lossless including assets and module but output bytes need not equal input due to JSON and zip regeneration. Lorebook twin original risu-lorebook raw walks rows by id for field-for-field unedited re-emit, partial rewrite on edit, drop on delete, append on add; book-level name depth budget are not written because Risu keeps them on the character record.

Quirks pin Risu-specific edges. Always CCv3 never V2 via wrapV3 and baseCard. Millisecond dates normalize per field above 1e11 because samples mix units. Media crosses format selectively for data http and ccdefault refs; archive-relative refs need twin uri match; same-format keeps assets via assetFiles. Behavior is first-class editable never executed and never re-emitted by non-Risu codecs. module.risum is RPack opened into structured view; unedited re-exports original bytes; edited throws RpackEditedExportBlockedError until fixtures flip the verified gate. risu-regex detects 0.8 for risum with regex and 0.85 for bare customscript arrays while charx stays character; export is pretty JSON rows never repacked module; phases map editinput output display and request spellings with open unlisted types. Native role is richer than embedded path; insertorder maps to sortOrder for clean ST order conversion.

Source of truth maps concerns to files. Character adapter detect container escrow dates and safety flags live in formats risu index.ts; risuai scalar mapping in risu-fields.ts; native lorebook in lorebook.ts; regex codec in regex.ts. RPack container codec table module and index live under formats risu rpack; structured module open is open-module.ts. Shared Tavern field map assets and character-book helpers are formats shared. Coverage is coverage.ts; canonical escrow core canonical.ts; bounded zip core archive.ts. Samples under samples risu with SOURCES.md.

docs.title: RoleCall to SillyTavern presets
docs.summary: What converts mechanically when a RoleCall preset becomes a SillyTavern preset, what Kit reports about the parts that do not, and the four patterns for finishing those by hand.
docs.semanticSummary: How a RoleCall preset becomes a SillyTavern preset, separating what converts mechanically from the remainder needing human judgment. A RoleCall preset can carry a second program beside its prompts: a hook machine writing variables as text passes through, and conditionals reading them back. The page is one crossing on purpose while the machinery is not, since macros resolve through a canonical operation hub and no engine pair is written down anywhere. Converting without a decision: separator differences, indexed access lowering onto composed names, conditionals preserved rather than flattened, and macros nested in blocks or passed as arguments. Kit reports facts without deciding them, in a structure section carrying arrays, domains, wideVariables, pushHooks, choices and markerCandidates, plus stateLayer as read, absent or unknown. Four patterns follow: a choice group becomes a seeded variable, still author work; an inline cleanup macro is removed by guarding the appends that made it necessary, since regex scripts run over messages rather than prompt content and cannot replace it; a closed domain expands into a conditional, reported rather than applied; and a splice macro is promoted into a marker block by splitting its prompt. Hook machines are rendered as regex rules in declaration order, with authored values verbatim, while push is refused. Evidence is labelled unit-proven, integration-proven or code-read.
topics: canonical operation hub no pair table

anchors.summary: Handled in code, appearing in the transfer receipt only as rewrite entries. Separator differences resolve because each catalog declares the shape of its own forms, so roll with double-colon becomes roll with single colon without either engine knowing about the other. Indexed access lowers because SillyTavern has no arrays but an array of fixed slots is a set of variables whose names carry the index: getvarkey on propp_plan at 3 becomes getvar on propp_plan_3, and a computed index becomes a composed name, which works because a nested macro resolves before its consumer. SillyTavern documents exactly this shape itself. Conditionals are preserved rather than flattened because SillyTavern's current macro engine has if, else, closing tags, inversion and comparison; the target's own catalog decides this through the canonical flow.conditional operation, and an engine without conditionals still gets blocks flattened to their body with the condition kept as a comment. Macros nested inside a preserved block, or passed as arguments to a portable macro, are translated too; both were defects at one point and both are now covered by tests.

The engine computes facts and does not decide what to do about them. A preset transfer or export receipt carries a structure section: arrays answering which variables are addressed by index, which literal indices appear, and how many accesses use a computed index; domains for variables whose every written value was a short literal, with the value set; wideVariables for variables that are literal but too long or too many to expand inline, named rather than dropped in silence; pushHooks for hooks that append to a list, with the trigger regex verbatim; choices, each choice macro resolved against the choice group it names with that group's declared options and default; markerCandidates for dead macros whose name resembles a canonical marker slot; and stateLayer as read, absent, or unknown. stateLayer deserves attention because a RoleCall hook machine lives only in escrow and never in the canonical body, so a piece whose escrow was dropped reports unknown rather than zero hooks, since zero read as there are none is precisely the mistake this distinction exists to prevent.

anchors.text: Pattern 1: a choice group becomes a seeded variable
anchors.summary: The choice macro asks RoleCall for the option a user picked at load time, and SillyTavern has no such concept, so the macro is removed on the way out and the receipt records it. The choice group itself survives conversion as canonical data, so the receipt can hand you its options. Replace the read with an ordinary variable and seed that variable once at the top of the preset: a seed block placed first sets the variable to a value, and every former choice read becomes a plain getvar. The seed is the group's declared default when it has one. A person switching options edits one line instead of hunting every reference, which is the closest thing to the original behaviour a preset without a picker can offer.

anchors.text: Pattern 2: fix the producer, not the consumer
anchors.summary: The regex macro rewrites a value as a prompt renders and SillyTavern has no such macro. Regex scripts are not the counterpart: they run over chat messages and world-info entries, never over preset prompt content, so no arrangement of them reproduces it and emitting one gives a rule that runs, matches nothing and looks correct. The move is to stop needing it, and the converter now performs that repair for the shape it recognises. A list assembled by appending separator plus item onto an empty variable comes out with a leading separator; guarding each append on whether the variable already holds something means it never appears, and the cleanup is deleted rather than translated. Scope travels with the variable, since chat-local and global live in separate stores. Nothing is compiled: recognition is textual, and a cleanup that rewrites rather than strips, reads something other than a plain variable, or whose producer is elsewhere comes back unfixed with a reason.
topics: regex scripts are not the counterpart

anchors.text: Pattern 3: a closed domain expands into a conditional
anchors.summary: The upper macro has no SillyTavern equivalent. Applied to a variable whose values are unknown it is unfixable; applied to one whose value set is closed it is a lookup. This is why the receipt reports domains: when every write is a short literal the full value set is known, so the uppercase form can be written beside the value, after which the upper read becomes a plain getvar. Check the receipt first, because the pattern needs a literal assignment site and only works for a variable listed under domains; in the preset measured here upper was applied to a computed variable, where the fix is Pattern 2. Domains counts every write form, not just setvar: shorthand assignment, addvar, incvar and decvar all open a domain, since a value derived from the current one cannot be enumerated. Three variables there looked like the closed set containing zero until the arithmetic writes driving them were counted; they are counters, and expanding one into a constant would badly mislead.
topics: paired upper write at assignment site
every write form opens a domain

anchors.text: Pattern 4: a macro becomes a marker prompt
anchors.summary: The message_history macro splices the transcript; SillyTavern does the same job with a marker prompt, a prompt-list entry named chatHistory that the builder fills during assembly. There is no macro to rewrite it to, so the conversion is a structural edit and the converter now performs it: the block carrying the macro is split, keeping the text before and after on either side of a new marker block. Order of operations is the whole trick, since the translator removes a macro with no home on the target and would leave nothing to promote; promotion therefore reads dead tokens off the original body and restructures first. Promotion happens only when the slot is unambiguous: exactly one shared-word match promotes, zero or several leave the token for a person, because content moved to the wrong slot reads as odd behaviour rather than a conversion error. A macro the target can still run is never touched. Every split is reported under promotions.

RoleCall's macro_engine_yaml is regex-triggered hooks: a trigger, flags, a placement of user_input or ai_output, an optional strip, and actions that set, unset, append or push. They line up with SillyTavern regex scripts, whose replacement is macro-substituted after capture groups fill in, so a replacement containing a setvar really does write state. A dialect-changing crossing now returns hookRules: the hooks as rules the target can run, in declaration order, triggers verbatim because both engines share regex syntax. The authored value crosses verbatim too, which is load-bearing: RoleCall writes templates woven around two capture groups and writes an empty value to clear, so guessing would discard a group or turn a clear into a write. sortOrder preserves declaration order because a hook that clears state must precede the hooks that write it. Push is still refused, since its rule count comes from how the preset reads the array. Hoplight still seals the YAML as escrow and never executes it, and placing the rules into a target remains a separate act.
topics: hooks and regex scripts are one mechanism

anchors.summary: Claims are backed at different strengths and the difference matters. Unit-proven covers separator rewriting, indexed-access lowering, block preservation, nested-argument translation, every field of the structure report, the observations in explanation, the rendered hookRules, marker promotion and producer repair. Integration-proven covers a RoleCall preset crossing to SillyTavern through the real adapter registry, resolving its dialect from escrow and carrying structural findings, promotions and rendered rules into the receipt. Code-read covers SillyTavern's regex replacement path calling substituteParams, its placement values, its marker prompt identifiers, and the surfaces regex scripts actually run over, all read from that project's source. Pattern 1 remains a recommendation and says so. Patterns 2 and 4 were recommendations when the page was written and are now performed; Pattern 3 is reported rather than applied, since expanding a closed domain is still the author's edit.

docs.title: RoleCall format
docs.summary: How the RoleCall adapter family maps character cards, lorebooks, personas, regex scripts, and presets through the canonical model.
docs.semanticSummary: Developer reference for five RoleCall adapters: CCv2/v3 character cards with extensions.rolecall, a v1 lorebook envelope, persona and regex JSON exports, and a RoleCall-flavored flat preset. Character detection bids 1.0 only for the RoleCall extension and steps aside for persona exports; lorebook detection recognizes its dedicated wrapper without colliding with SillyTavern world info. Character mapping covers identity details, titled greetings, depth injections, presentation, media, and embedded lorebooks. Lorebook mapping flattens RoleCall's nested trigger, matching, injection, timing, grouping, scan-source, and advanced settings into canonical entries. Character export overlays canonical edits onto the sealed source while preserving native fields, including a documented depth-injection write asymmetry. Lorebook export preserves source dates and conditionally writes budget fields. Persona handling keeps brief and content distinct across two supported shapes. Regex handling models the live chat pipeline with open placement values. Preset handling shares the flat SillyTavern grammar but requires RoleCall fingerprint fields and preserves native YAML as sealed data. The source table identifies all five codecs, shared helpers, schemas, design specs, and constructed samples.

anchors.summary: Detection follows registry highest score above 0.5. Character detect returns 1.0 for CCv2 or V3 cards that carry extensions.rolecall whose type is not the literal persona, outranking SillyTavern 0.9 on the same card. Cross-kind firewall: RC persona exports reuse the CCv2 V3 shape with type persona so character returns 0 and toCanonical throws pointing at rolecall-persona instead of tying. Lorebook detect returns 1.0 for a RoleCall v1 export envelope with schemaVersion containing 1.0.0 as a substring and a lorebook object with an entries array; exportDate is optional. No firewall is needed versus ST because ST has a top-level entries object and no lorebook wrapper.

children.summary: detect returns 1.0 for a CCv2 or V3 card carrying extensions.rolecall and 0 otherwise. Requirements are spec chara_card_v3 or chara_card_v2, a data object, and rolecallExt whose type is not the literal persona. Score 1.0 outranks SillyTavern generic 0.9. Cross-kind firewall: RC persona-export route emits the same CCv2 V3 shape with type persona; character detect returns 0 and toCanonical throws pointing at rolecall-persona so the adapters never tie at 1.0 on the same file.

detect returns 1.0 for a RoleCall v1 export envelope with a schemaVersion string containing 1.0.0 and a lorebook object whose entries is an array, else 0. exportDate is optional for detection and import. The version match is a substring rather than exact equality, so beta tags pass; a nonmatching version scores zero even though the direct structural parser does not hard-reject it. The envelope does not collide with a SillyTavern worldbook, which has a top-level entries object without a lorebook wrapper, so no firewall is needed between the two lorebook codecs.

anchors.summary: Field map covers Character RC deltas then Lorebook nesting. Character reuses shared Tavern data mapping and adds extensions.rolecall tagline genre fandom content_rating mapped all_hours late_night after_dark to all-ages mature explicit, source_url creators_note, details full_name title age pronouns, titled alternate greetings, prompt_depth_injections concatenated with depth_prompt origin, presentation casting-card colors fieldOrder background media_links, and assets with expression as emotion; unmapped loadout links ride escrow. Lorebook flattens RoleCallEntryV1 nested groups triggers matching injection priority timing grouping advanced scanSources characterFilter and unsupportedFields ST toggles into flat LorebookEntry; book settings metadata categories map at book level; scanPreset has no v1 wire slot.

children.summary: Shared Tavern data mapping is documented on sillytavern; this table is RC layer only. extensions.rolecall maps tagline genre fandom content_rating with exact three-way rating, source_url creators_note, details full_name title free-text age pronouns, alternate_greeting_titles merged by index into alternate greetings, prompt_depth_injections as origin rolecall_details concatenated before depth_prompt, and presentation signature gradient palette fieldOrder background spoiler media_links. assets use shared assetsToMedia dialect rolecall with expression as emotion; PNG carrier bytes live in original.rolecall.sourceMedia. character_book is shared bundle re-embed; empty resolution removes stale twin book. id nsfw image urls loadout recommendations trackerPreset linked lists ride whole-card escrow.

Canonical LorebookEntry is flat; RC v1 wire nests each entry into named groups and the codec flattens on import and re-nests on export. Groups cover triggers mode primary secondary selectiveLogic, matching case whole-words scanDepth, injection position depth role, priority sortOrder priority, timing sticky cooldown delay, grouping name category weight, advanced recursion memo ignoreBudget, scanSources four RC toggles, top-level characterFilter probability sideEffects metadata, and unsupportedFields for ST-origin vectorized groupOverride useGroupScoring automationId matchCharacterDepthPrompt matchCreatorNotes as first-class canonical. Book settings metadata categories map at book level; scanPreset has no RC v1 wire slot.

anchors.summary: Character twin stores whole parsed card in original.rolecall.raw plus PNG sourceMedia when input was PNG. Export clones raw or fresh V3, applies Tavern overlay, media dialect rolecall, then applyBodyToRcExt three-state for presentation fields gradientColors palette background fieldOrder distinguishing untouched edited cleared while rebuilding nested details; scalars write when defined and cleared values on twin stay rather than delete. Depth-injection asymmetry: import concatenates rolecall_details and depth_prompt origins but export only rewrites depth_prompt via shared applyBodyToData; applyBodyToRcExt never writes prompt_depth_injections so details array re-emits from twin. Lorebook twin original rolecall-lorebook raw overlays by id; budgetMode entryBudget write only when twin had them or from-scratch differs from defaults; exportDate preserved from twin and only regenerated from-scratch, which differs from source product always minting fresh exportDate in the design spec.

Quirks pin RC edges and summarize preset persona and regex codecs. rolecall-preset shares SillyTavern's flat grammar but requires native fingerprint keys; a from-scratch export writes a neutral empty choice_groups array so it stays distinguishable and self-readable. V3 source as object array is unread by shared Tavern string[] decoder so object form rides twin; greeting titles omit key when all untitled; background keeps customUrl or backgroundId slot; real sprites use type expression mapped to emotion. Persona codec claims 1.0 on rcpersona envelope and chara_card_v2 lookalike with type persona; brief never swaps with content; sections compile or fold unfold description; after_dark omitted when not mature explicit; no rcpersona PNG keyword path in code despite design specs. Regex codec models live find_pattern pipeline only at 0.9 for single script with rules; placements map to phases open-union; no substituteFind on this wire; unknown keys ride extras. coverage.ts is editor lens only not round-trip.

Source of truth maps character to index.ts and lorebook, persona, regex, and preset codecs to sibling files. Shared Tavern mapping, lore enums, assets, PNG and card readers, coverage, canonical escrow, persona schema, design specs, and constructed samples are also listed.

docs.title: SillyTavern format
docs.summary: How the SillyTavern adapter family detects, maps, and round-trips Character Card V1/V2/V3 cards and world info books through the canonical model.
docs.semanticSummary: SillyTavern format is the developer authority for how Hoplight's sillytavern family detects, maps, and round-trips Character Card V1 V2 and V3 cards plus standalone world info through the canonical model. The card rides JSON or a PNG base64 text chunk; adapters always write JSON. One folder exports four codecs: sillytavern character PNG or JSON, sillytavern-lorebook JSON, sillytavern-regex bare RegexScriptData arrays or card extensions.regex_scripts, and sillytavern-persona ST personas backup files. This page documents character and lorebook in full; regex and persona are summarized under Quirks. Detection scores character 0.9 not 1.0 so RoleCall can outrank on extensions.rolecall, with PNG chara or ccv3 chunks and JSON V3 V2 or flat v1 paths plus a cross-kind firewall requiring a real character signal beside name. Lorebook scores native entries object 0.9 and character_book 0.85. Field map uses shared tavern-fields for CCv2 V3 data, lore-enums for integer selectiveLogic role position, and character_book as bundle extract. Escrow and round-trip seals original.sillytavern raw variant and sourceMedia with three-state overlay so same-format is byte-lossless while cross-format carries only the canonical body. Quirks cover V2 versus V3 drops, dual PNG chunks, talkativeness tolerance, world by name, displayIndex, and the regex and persona codecs. Source of truth lists adapters shared helpers coverage and samples.

anchors.summary: Detection follows registry highest score above 0.5 so more specific formats outrank generic ones. Character detect returns 0.9 for a recognizable card and 0 otherwise, not 1.0, because SillyTavern is the generic Tavern reader and RoleCall claims 1.0 on CCv3 with extensions.rolecall. Two recognition paths: PNG with chara V2 or ccv3 V3 text chunks scores 0.9 and non-card PNG falls through to JSON; JSON detectCard accepts chara_card_v3 or v2 with data, or flat objects with name plus a real character signal for V1 flat. Flat v1 is the cross-kind firewall so a worldbook name object never false-positives as a character. Lorebook returns 0.9 for native top-level entries object keyed by string index with entry-shaped values, 0.85 for portable character_book with entries array, and 0 otherwise so native wins any tie.

children.summary: detect returns 0.9 for a recognizable card and 0 otherwise. Score is 0.9 not 1.0 so RoleCall on extensions.rolecall wins when present; plain CCv3 without that block is read by sillytavern. PNG path scores 0.9 when bytes carry chara V2 or ccv3 V3 text chunks; a non-card PNG falls through because real JSON reads carry both bytes and text. JSON detectCard recognizes chara_card_v3 with data, chara_card_v2 with data, or flat with name plus V1 core fields description personality scenario first_mes mes_example or V2-era alternate_greetings system_prompt post_history_instructions creator_notes extensions character_version. V2-era fields mark variant flat otherwise v1; worldbooks carry none so they never score positive.

sillytavern-lorebook returns 0.9 for a native worldbook, 0.85 for a portable character_book, and 0 otherwise. Score 0.9 requires top-level entries as an object keyed by string index not an array, which would be RoleCall or Agnai, whose first value looks like an entry via key keysecondary comment or content. Score 0.85 is a Chub-style or card-extracted character_book object with an entries array, portable as ST but scored below native so the native file wins any tie.

anchors.summary: Field map covers Character shared Tavern data then Lorebook enums and entry wires. Character data mapping lives in tavern-fields dataToBody and applyBodyToData shared with Risu: identity name nickname description characterVersion, persona personality scenario, greetings first alternate group-only, examples mes_example, prompts system post_history depth_prompt, attribution creator notes source multilingual dates, discovery tags, settings talkativeness, worldName, assets to media, character_book via bundle knowledgeRefs, and PNG pixels in original.sillytavern.sourceMedia. depth_prompt talkativeness and world are first-classed from extensions; empty depth prompt maps to no injection. Lorebook uses lore-enums for selectiveLogic role position integers; entries map comment content disable keys order group match toggles vectorized automationId displayIndex; embedded character_book uses CCv3 dialect with ST extensions bag.

children.summary: Shared Tavern data mapping covers data.name nickname description character_version to identity, personality scenario to persona, first_mes alternate_greetings group_only_greetings to greetings, mes_example system_prompt post_history_instructions, extensions.depth_prompt as origin depth_prompt, creator creator_notes source creator_notes_multilingual dates, tags, extensions.talkativeness with tolerant string or number, extensions.world as worldName not embedded book, assets to portrait and media, and character_book via bundle extract into knowledgeRefs not tavern-fields. PNG carrier pixels live in original.sillytavern.sourceMedia. Empty depth_prompt.prompt maps to no injection so depth and role ride the twin; role is carried only when authored. Resolved empty knowledgeRefs removes both primary character_book and legacy extensions.character_book so clearing a link cannot resurrect the twin book.

ST world info encodes selectiveLogic role and position as integers via shared lore-enums: selectiveLogic 0-3 and_any through and_all, role 0-2 system user assistant, position 0-4 world character before_example after_example depth. Entry highlights map title from comment, content, enabled as not disable, triggers from key with inline regex decode, secondaryTriggers keysecondary, sortOrder from order, priority defaults 100 with no ST eviction axis, groupName group, scan match toggles including depth prompt and creator notes, vectorized groupOverride useGroupScoring automationId displayIndex. Embedded character_book uses CCv3 top-level keys secondary_keys insertion_order use_regex coarse before_char after_char with ST-extended fields in extensions, extensions winning when both present.

anchors.summary: Escrow is the wrapper original Record keyed by format id; the character twin lives at original.sillytavern with raw entire parsed card, unmapped variant v2 v3 v1 or flat, and sourceMedia b64 png only for PNG input. Same-format round-trip is byte-lossless: fromCanonical overlays the body onto a clone of raw and preserves the original variant wrapper. Overlay is three-state against the twin decode via applyBodyToData: equal leaves raw untouched, changed writes, missing clears at the exact wire home; unknown keys and non-representable raw stay. Cross-format carries only the canonical body; raw extensions unknown keys and PNG stay in escrow uncopied. Lorebook collapses richer positions append append_bottom to depth 4, prepend_top to 0, scene to before_example 2; triggerMode always simple on read. Unedited entries re-project from raw twin by id so ST to ST stays byte-lossless; only edited entries re-encode and take the collapse. Raw-only uid vectors loreCache ride escrow untouched.

Quirks pin ST edges and summarize regex and persona codecs. CCv2 versus V3: V3-only nickname source multilingual dates group_only_greetings assets round-trip only in V3; V2 export drops group_only and multilingual; media present upgrades non-V3 twin to V3 because V2 has no portable assets. PNG embedding uses chara V2 or ccv3 V3 tEXt; V3 normally writes both with reader preferring ccv3 wherever present. Flat v1 needs name plus character signal as the cross-kind firewall. Talkativeness tolerates string or number on read and writes number while three-state leaves unchanged string twin. World is by name not knowledgeRefs; embedded book is character_book. displayIndex is a distinct axis never fabricated from sortOrder. Regex codec scores 0.9 for bare RegexScriptData array and 0.85 for card extensions.regex_scripts with findWrapped extras for delimiter style. Persona codec scores 0.95 on personas backup, imports default or first, and seals the entire backup so export overlays only the edited persona.

World info codec is lorebook.ts; regex and persona codecs are sibling regex.ts and persona.ts. Shared Tavern field map is tavern-fields.ts; lore int-enum decoders are lore-enums.ts; embedded character_book mapper is character-book.ts; CCv3 assets to media is assets.ts; PNG chunk read write is png.ts. Coverage declaration is coverage.ts. Canonical wrapper escrow original and id policy live in core canonical.ts. Samples under samples sillytavern include CCv2 and v3 JSON plus Seraphina.png.

docs.title: vaud-json format
docs.summary: How the vaud-json adapter serializes the canonical character entity straight to plain JSON with no wire translation, and why it always wins detection on its own files.
docs.semanticSummary: vaud-json is Hoplight's native character format: the canonical entity written directly to plain JSON with no wire translation. It serializes schemaVersion, kind, id, body, profiles, and original unchanged, making it the lossless local save and interchange format. The codec is native, so import and conversion use it while publish surfaces omit it. Detection parses through the exhaustive canonical runtime schema and scores 1.0 only for a valid character; invalid JSON, unsupported versions, malformed bodies, and other entity kinds score 0. Import uses the same parser and kind narrowing, eliminating a second partial validator. The field map is one-to-one, and export pretty-prints the whole entity. Existing escrow entries pass through untouched because vaud-json does not create its own twin. Quirks cover bounded parse errors, pure JSON media, and native exclusion from coverage. Source of truth lists the adapter, its tests, the shared runtime schema, registry, canonical wrapper, adapter contract, and UI publish filters.

anchors.summary: detect parses input through parseCanonicalEntity and returns 1.0 only when the complete result is a character. Missing text, invalid JSON, unsupported schema versions, malformed required or optional fields, unknown authored keys, and other entity kinds return 0. toCanonical uses the same exhaustive parser and then narrows to character, so detection and import no longer maintain separate validation rules or accept a fixture-shaped partial body.

There is no wire translation to tabulate. On-disk JSON is the canonical entity one to one: schemaVersion kind id body profiles and original map to themselves. Every CharacterBody field the eight always-present sub-objects identity persona prompts greetings examples media attribution discovery plus optional presentation settings bias worldName knowledgeRefs behavior behaviorRefs variants is written verbatim under body. The adapter has no opinion on field meanings; see entities character for semantics. fromCanonical is JSON.stringify entity null 2 with suggested extension json. It writes the whole entity including any original and profiles the entity carries with no filtering or re-projection.

vaud-json is the one format where same-format round-trip is lossless exact and unconditional rather than reconstructed from an escrowed twin. Because it serializes the canonical entity directly, vaud-json to canonical to vaud-json returns the identical entity same body original and profiles untouched, proven by the adapter round-trip test and the registry-level round-trip test. Relationship to escrow differs from app adapters: those fill an original entry keyed by their own id on import so private fields survive same-format round-trip. vaud-json neither reads nor writes an original entry keyed to itself; it carries whatever original the entity already holds straight through because toCanonical and fromCanonical never inspect that field. A card imported from SillyTavern then saved as vaud-json keeps original.sillytavern.raw intact in the file ready to re-project if later exported back to SillyTavern.

Detection and import both use the exhaustive canonical parser. Hand-edited files with unsupported schema versions, missing required sections, invalid optional fields, unknown authored keys, or another entity kind fail at the adapter boundary. Invalid JSON and invalid canonical character failures use separate bounded messages. Exports remain two-space pretty JSON. The format has no PNG or ZIP container; media stays in canonical refs or data URIs. native keeps the adapter off Press, export publish lists, and the platform coverage API while conversion and Workbench editing still use it.

Source of truth maps the adapter to formats vaud-json index.ts, its regressions to vaud-json.test.ts, and exhaustive parsing to entities/runtime-schema.ts. Registry selection lives in core/registry.ts; canonical wrapper and escrow in core/canonical.ts; adapter flags in core/adapter.ts; and character fields in entities/character/schema.ts. Press, export dialog, and setup publish filters exclude native adapters. FORMAT-SUPPORT.md carries the generated matrix row.

docs.title: Kit reference
docs.summary: Kit's conversational runtime, semantic content capabilities, and change-draft lifecycle.
docs.semanticSummary: Kit reference is the short index for Hoplight's conversational terminal surface. Kit uses the same canonical entities and Studio store as the Web UI, so terminal and browser share one model of truth. Content tools documents the capability catalog, progressive model exposure, and the implemented canonical content bundles. Kit can search and read catalog-declared Hoplight user and developer documentation through the read-only docs_query model tool without arbitrary filesystem paths. UI reference covers terminal shell behavior users can run today. Architecture documents semantic content capability ownership and dependency direction between entity pure layers and Kit runtime adapters.

docs.title: Kit content tools
docs.summary: Kit's shared workflow discovery, traversable results, semantic drafts, and Hoplight docs query.
docs.semanticSummary: Kit content tools separates runtime tools from terminal slash commands. Its lifecycle connects six canonical capability bundles through pure previews, one four-domain discovery catalog, complete draft evidence, guarded-mode semantic review, documentation query, whole-piece reads, and bounded result handles. Twenty direct tools begin each turn, studio_delete among them, plus the preset-authoring belt (block_lookup, preset_verify, regex_lab), the shared-folder pair (folder_search, folder_import), rail_open, studio_art, and ask_choice. Search may reveal up to five deferred schemas, collapsed browse reveals none, and exact describe reveals one. Studio lifecycle contains typed creation for character, lorebook, persona, preset, regex, and media pack without an existing target, plus duplicate and delete. studio_transfer serializes a piece through another platform adapter and reports dropped fields, escrowed fields, and dead macros without writing any file. Macro compatibility is computed by the engine from per-engine catalogs, never inferred by the model, and is name-level only: a surviving token is not a semantic guarantee and an unmodeled engine reports unchecked rather than clean. Normal pieces up to 64,000 characters return in one read. Guarded mode hands apply to the application review card. Atomic create-only apply refuses occupied IDs and verifies storage. Unit and integration proof exists; live terminal verification remains required.

anchors.summary: Built lifecycle connects six canonical capability bundles to Kit. entities capabilities owns ids, search and exposure; kit capabilities adapts them into one registry. Six lifecycle tools draft creation without a write; duplicate carries body, profiles and original escrow forward. studio_delete is the only tool that destroys canonical content, carries no discovery descriptor because the runtime refuses deferred applies, and reports a miss as stale without writing. studio_transfer serializes through another adapter without writing. block_lookup explains a kind of prompt block; preset_verify renders through the real engine; regex_lab tries, races, explains and lints patterns while storing none. folder_search reads inside shared folders and the studio, reconciling each resolved path against its real path. folder_import is the one-way door into the studio, drafting every piece a file contains or none. rail_open opens a preset and reports what is on the rail; studio_art shows a piece card art without the bytes reaching the model; ask_choice hands the user a list the shell renders. kit changes retains baseline, escrow and warnings.

A content capability is a pure semantic operation declaring a stable dotted ID, kind, navigation metadata, platform applicability, Zod input, effect, exposure, concurrency key, and preview. Preview returns a complete canonical entity, changes, warnings, platform impact, and optionally a deterministic read observation. It never writes. The composer rejects identity or original escrow changes. The read adapter also requires a canonically identical entity and empty changes, preventing analysis from creating a mutation draft.

The safety subsystem owns exact-name access classification and never trusts prefixes, discovery metadata, or a claimed runtime effect. Pure content capabilities derive read or preview-only draft access from validated catalog metadata. Each of the six creation workflows has a separate safety-owned exact-name draft classification. Guarded apply pauses in an application-owned semantic review card. Update apply compares the expected revision under a per-path lock. Create apply uses a distinct atomic create-only operation that refuses an occupied ID rather than overwriting or minting a sibling. Stale state and collisions write nothing. Both modes re-read and verify canonical fields and non-Studio escrow. Unreadable or mismatched verification reports failure without retry.

Progressive exposure keeps a large catalog out of every prompt. The runtime registry holds every adapted capability and deferred workflow so dispatch can resolve a selection, and twenty direct tools begin each turn, among them ask_choice, block_lookup, folder_import, preset_verify, rail_open, regex_lab, studio_art, studio_delete and studio_export. Those last two are direct for a structural reason: the deferred path classifies a tool from discovery metadata, and the runtime refuses to let that path describe an apply effect, so a destructive or file-writing workflow cannot be discovered into existence and must be granted by exact name in the trust map. Routing removal through draft and apply would require ChangeDraftMode to grow a remove arm, a core authority change deferred to its own design pass. One catalog accepts content, studio, transfer, and diagnostics domains; transfer is populated by studio_transfer while diagnostics remains a declared but empty slot. Only pure-content capabilities derive safe access from catalog metadata. Search reveals at most five ranked matches, browse exposes no schemas, describe reveals one. Hidden descriptors never appear. The deferred set clears each turn while drafts persist.

children.summary: studio_read defaults to one complete canonical entity. A normal piece up to 64,000 characters returns inline in one observation, avoiding forced section traversal. It can still outline immediate children as RFC 6901 JSON Pointers or read one selected value with offsets and limits. Invalid pointers fail closed. Larger whole pieces enter a session-local store and return an opaque result-N handle plus a 4,096-character peek. Other result-producing tools retain the shared 4,096-character inline threshold. result_query provides stat, bounded read, and literal case-insensitive search. Handles reveal no path and expire with the session. Storage caps are 24 entries, 1,000,000 UTF-8 bytes per entry, and 4,000,000 UTF-8 bytes total with oldest-first eviction. Content beyond the store cap remains recoverable through direct studio_read offsets.

Every composed operation retains validated input, changes, warnings, and platform impact, while the draft aggregates warning and impact evidence over one immutable baseline. change_query list returns compact state and counts. show returns operations, baseline, complete proposed entity, warnings, and platform impact, using a result handle or explicit offsets for large proposals. validate re-parses canonical shape and compares the live stored revision without mutating draft state or writing. Per-operation rollback remains excluded until deterministic replay is specified.

anchors.summary: studio.character.create needs no existing target. It accepts a safe optional ID or derives one, then builds a canonical character from identity, persona, scenario, greeting, examples, tags, portrait, and additional media. Portrait and media schemas describe data URI, HTTP(S), and existing asset references, MIME types, roles, labels, and primary selection. It returns structured application-Gate review and uses atomic create-only verified apply. Existing characters retain ten preview-only capabilities covering identity, prompts, greetings, metadata, presentation, media, links, variants, settings, and embedded behavior scripts. Script payloads remain sealed data and original escrow remains non-editable.

studio.lorebook.create builds a new book and optionally typed initial entries with content, literal or regex triggers, selective logic, insertion position, depth, role, and defaults for the remaining canonical activation fields. Existing drop-ins are settings.update, entries.update, entries.reorder, entries.enable, and entries.remove. Duplicate, separate entry-create, trigger-specific update, placement-specific update, and broad bulk operations remain future additions. The Web UI retains local selection, focus, generated-ID, and undo behavior.

Persona creation separates shelf brief from injected content and accepts sections, traits, identity, rating, and portrait. Preset creation accepts prompt blocks, sampler values, and media-inlining settings. Regex creation accepts stored rules with patterns, flags, replacements, phases, depth bounds, and ordering but never executes them. Pack creation accepts expression items with IDs, labels, refs, MIME types, enabled state, and default label. Existing capabilities continue editing each kind through shared entity reducers.

Macro translation across engines states that a preset crossing to another engine is translated rather than only reported on, because refusing over one imperfect token leaves the job unfinished and authored prose outweighs a macro that was never going to fire. The engine computes every equivalence and the model explains it, never the reverse, since a model reasoning from names alone is confidently wrong when names collide but meanings do not follow them. There is no engine-pair table: project rule 1 forbids format-to-format conversion for macros as it does for codecs, because five engines would mean twenty directed pairs. Each catalog instead declares what its own macros mean through canonical operations, and every cross-engine answer is a join on that meaning. Crossings produce portable, collision, absent or flatten verdicts. A gate asserts no shared name diverges in shape without a declared operation. Risu, Agnai and unverified SillyTavern annotations are named as honest limits.

children.text: Hub and spoke, the same as formats
children.summary: Hub and spoke explains why macros have no engine-pair table. Project rule 1 forbids format-to-format conversion for macros as it does for codecs, because five engines would mean twenty directed pairs and each new engine would multiply the work. Each catalog instead declares what its own macros mean through canonical operations, and every cross-engine answer is a join on that meaning. Adding an engine is one annotation pass. Operations attach per entry rather than per name, because one name can mean different things at different argument counts: RoleCall reads random as a range at two arguments and a pick at three or more. Annotation is partial by design, since unannotated entries fall back to name matching.

A crossing produces one of four verdicts. Portable means both engines perform the operation and the token is re-spelled in the target's punctuation. Collision means the same name performs a different operation, so it is left as authored and flagged rather than silently kept. Absent means the target has no macro for the operation, so it is removed with same-family candidates. Flatten means a block the target cannot express, where the body is kept and only the scaffolding removed. Random with two arguments crossing RoleCall to SillyTavern is the worked example: a range meets a pick, and the collision is derived rather than listed anywhere.

children.text: The gate that keeps it honest
children.summary: The gate is a function returning any macro name that several engines share with differing argument shapes where at least one side has not declared an operation, paired with a test asserting that list stays empty. This is what keeps the hub trustworthy as engines are added: a shared name spelled differently, whose meaning nobody has written down, is exactly where a silent mistranslation hides. Because divergence is detected mechanically rather than by reading, the system reports which annotations are owed instead of leaving a person to hunt for them, and a contributor cannot introduce a silent mistranslation by adding an engine and forgetting to declare what one of its macros means.

Honest limits names what the translation layer cannot currently prove. Risu with its bracket CBS dialect and Agnai with its named-slot templates are not modeled at all, so an unmodeled target reports unchecked, which a caller must render as unknown and never as clean. SillyTavern's catalog is the only one with no oracle to verify against, so its annotations are the least grounded of the four, while RoleCall, Lumiverse and Marinara are machine-checked against their real registries by the macro oracle. Flag-prefixed tokens resolve to no name and are therefore never flagged, because the same prefix character means different things on different engines and stripping it would trade a false negative for a false positive.

anchors.summary: docs_query is a direct read-only meta-tool with four actions. browse lists collections and pages from index metadata only, with root or immediate children, limit 12 cap 25, offset pagination, and slash-separated collection ids that never path-escape. outline returns a semantic page overview and collapsed H2 map without loading Markdown; a returned section slug expands only that branch and its H3 summaries. search ranks body text plus title, short summary, semantic summary, topics, and headings with in-memory BM25. read alone returns authoritative source prose: omit the section for a whole document or select a slug for a targeted nugget. Bounded responses provide continuation offsets so long documents can be read completely across calls. Whole-document reads are preferred around located answers to preserve qualifications, failure conditions, and current-versus-planned distinctions. Semantic navigation merges only from docs/summaries sidecars with current independent APPROVE receipts bound to source and semantic-summary hashes. Authoring discovery is folder-derived from docs/. New and edited pages require authoring, stamping, focused checking, and independent review. Global check requires every page APPROVED. No embeddings or network.

anchors.text: Serving the belt to another client
anchors.summary: hoplight mcp serves the same tools over MCP on stdio, so Claude Code, Cursor, Zed or Codex can read and edit the studio; register it once with the client own command. A studio directory is the first non-flag argument. The subcommand exists so nothing needs to know where the source lives: a compiled binary has no main file to point at, and a path that worked from a checkout failed silently for an installed copy, answering without tools. Two postures differ only in who holds the gate. Registered by a person, their client prompts before every call, so the full belt is safe and is the default. Spawned by Kit for the Claude subscription provider the client prompt is off and Kit gate cannot cross a process, so that path passes --read-only and gets read-effect tools only, filtered by building the dispatcher from the reduced set so a filtered name is unknown rather than run. The belt comes from discoverTools and the schemas from the tools own Zod, with no MCP SDK dependency.

Verification status separates proof from gaps. Unit and integration tests cover discovery, creation preview, draft evidence, collision and stale refusal, one-save apply, and post-save verification. Lifecycle and transfer add delete safety, escrow-carrying duplication, structural export containment, create-only refusal, and a RoleCall to SillyTavern preset journey onto a real filesystem. An oracle checks macro catalogs against each engine registry; SillyTavern alone lacks one. Live verification against a real provider remains outstanding.

docs.title: Marinara agents, tools, and regex
docs.summary: Agent phases abilities result types, Memory Recall and Roleplay/Conversation summaries, custom tools Static Result Webhook Script, regex trim test apply modes depth scoped chats, Professor Mari, and maps pointer.
docs.semanticSummary: Documents Marinara agents, Memory Recall and summaries, custom Functions, regex scripts, Professor Mari, and the map boundary at the pinned Engine docs for Kit retrieval. Agents cover activation, phases, abilities, result types, tools, and dynamic package inventory. Memory distinguishes semantic message chunks from Roleplay and Conversation summarization. Functions cover names, parameters, Static Result, Webhook, Script, hidden context, enable lists, import and export, and server restrictions. Regex covers placement, mode, scope, order, depth, import, and safety blocks. Professor Mari covers supported creation and editing, guided chips, selected connections, attachments, Skills, separate history, reversible saved-data edits, and its powerful install-folder command boundary. Hierarchical map semantics route to the dedicated page. Hoplight imports codecs and sealed data without executing Marinara assistants, tools, scripts, or maps.

anchors.summary: Agents are per-chat helpers enabled in Chat Settings. Official packages are mode-limited while custom agents run in all modes. Copy official packages to edit rather than mutating stock. Import export packages where documented. Phases are Pre-Generation Parallel and Post-Processing and result types may force phase. Post may optionally read Turn Data Access of pre-generation injections and parallel results. Abilities opt-in include create edit lorebooks target one book edit messages trackers frontend styling image generation vectors embeddings and main prompt edits. Result types include Context Injection Text Rewrite Lorebook Update Character Tracker Persona Stats Custom Tracker Game State Image Prompt Prompt Patch Frontend Style. Activation keywords skip irrelevant turns. Attach custom tools. Built-in inventory is dynamic from built-in agents docs and Marinara-Agents repo so static Hoplight pages must not freeze the list.

Memory systems two are distinct product features not short-lived agent notes. Memory Recall works in all modes and is the only memory system in Game with no summaries. It runs semantic search over past messages with per-chat enable defaults on in Conversation and on in Roleplay or Game with active Scene else off. Embedding source is on the connection or local sidecar. Memories for This Chat modal shows Vectorized Waiting or Embedding unavailable chunks with export marinara json import merge rebuild clear and per-chunk forget. Chunks need at least five new messages similarity may return none and rebuild after model change. Storage can continue when the toggle is off if embedding is available. Lite may hide Memory Recall. Summaries are Roleplay Chat Summary compressing old messages and Conversation Automatic Summarization. Different jobs that can combine with Memory Recall.

Custom tools Functions live under Presets Functions. Name is lowercase snake_case one to one hundred characters description one to five hundred for the model unique with reserved built-in names blocked. Admin secret required for remote manage. Export ZIP import ZIP or JSON. Parameters are name type string number boolean array object Required description empty names dropped and invalid imported params can skip the tool at generation with server log only. Execution types exact are Static Result fixed string empty becomes OK Webhook POST JSON tool and arguments to URL reply at most five hundred twelve KB default sixty seconds https only private localhost blocked unless admin allows failures return error result and Script server JS with args JSON Math Date must return off by default until CUSTOM_TOOL_SCRIPT_ENABLED true greyed when disabled. Include hidden chat context default off for Webhook and Script adds mode persona characters chat variables game state without AI-passed args. Chat Settings Enable Tool Use off default. No explicit list means all globally enabled tools adding any tool restricts to that set.

Regex scripts live under Presets Regexes. Find without slashes Replace with dollar captures and case transforms flags g i m s u y d Trim Strings after replace Live Test pattern only not placement enable scope or depth. Macros allowed in find replace trim. Apply To AI Output and or User Input at least one. Apply Mode Only Display default Only Prompt or Both. User Input plus Only Display or Both rewrites the saved or sent message with no pure display-only for outbound user text. Execution Order lower first default auto-assigned. Depth Min Max from newest zero empty means any min greater than max blocks save. Specific Characters toggle or character Advanced Regex Scripts after save. Per-chat Scoped Regex Scripts Disabled default Exclusive or Chat with per-script toggles. Prompt-side scripts follow generating character. ST card import Character only or Global empty or unsafe patterns skipped. Safety blocks nested quantifiers ambiguous quantified alternatives oversized patterns over one thousand chars and multi broad wildcards slow run skips that message only.

Professor Mari is Marinara's Home-screen assistant for explanation, agent-catalog comparison, and creation or editing of characters, personas, lorebooks, themes, agents, prompt presets, avatars, sprites, and backgrounds. Guided chips ask one focused question and fill editable drafts. Existing-data edits save then show a ten-minute Review Mari's changes card: Keep confirms and Restore reinstates the previous snapshot; new items usually skip it, and character or persona history is a second recovery path. It remembers a selected text connection, opens Connections when absent, accepts images PDFs and common text up to 20 MB, and needs vision for image reading. Custom Skills have upload, edit, enable, and delete lifecycle. Restart archives separate Mari chat history; Stop cancels work. Its repair authority may inspect or modify only the install folder and run short-lived commands there, never directly write saved data through that path. Remote edits require remote access. Hoplight does not import that command ability.

The dedicated Maps and game content page owns the full Hierarchical Maps authoring, draft, enable, save, exact-location lore, one-move travel, import, archive, and Game-binding lifecycle. Agent Game State and tracker result types cannot bypass the map's current-location or save rules.

Hoplight currently provides Marinara regex and persona codecs for this cluster. Imported scripts remain sealed data. Hoplight does not run Marinara custom Functions, agent pipelines, Professor Mari install commands, or map updates during import or conversion. Unsupported behavior stays platform-owned and must not be inferred from documentation coverage.

docs.title: Marinara chats and group chats
docs.summary: JSONL and non-reimportable Text export, bulk zip, mode-tab import, branch import reuse, reasoning-export privacy, group Roleplay/Conversation modes, disabled-member fallback, connected chats, and chat-setting ownership.
docs.semanticSummary: Documents Marinara chat interchange, group behavior, connected-chat relationships, and per-chat setting ownership. JSONL is re-importable while Text is not; single export offers either, bulk export is JSONL-only, new-chat import takes the open mode tab, and branch import reuses the open chat's characters, persona, connection, and prompt preset. Hidden reasoning is excluded from all exports by default. Group chats form at two characters: Roleplay provides Merged or Individual generation with Sequential, Smart, or Manual order, while Conversation provides Reply When Mentioned and Character Exchanges. Disabling every member reactivates all as a safety fallback. Connected Chats is a one-to-one asymmetric Conversation-to-story link, distinct from automatic Cross-Chat Awareness, with influence, durable note, and ooc transfer tags plus disconnect cleanup. Chat Settings and reusable Chat Settings Presets own bounded per-chat configuration without rewriting library artifacts. Hoplight requires an implemented adapter before claiming chat conversion.

anchors.summary: File formats state that JSONL is the default re-importable chat form accepted for Marinara and SillyTavern JSONL interchange, while Text txt is a human-readable transcript that cannot be re-imported. There is no separate undocumented Marinara-native chat container beyond JSONL and Text as documented. Kit must not invent binary or proprietary chat carriers when advising export paths.

Single export uses the open chat Switch branch panel to download JSONL or Text for the open chat including its messages. Authors choose format per download. This per-chat export surface is separate from the mode-tab bulk selection path and ZIP workflow.

Bulk export runs from the mode tab CONVO RP or GM after selecting chats then Export. The result is a zip of JSONL only with one file per selected chat of that mode. Text bulk export is not this path. Mode membership of the selection follows the open tab not a mode field inside each file itself.

Import as new chat uses the chat list import control whose tooltip names SillyTavern or Marinara chat JSONL. Import creates a new chat in the currently open mode tab CONVO RP or GM rather than reading a mode encoded in the file. Success reports imported message count and switches into the chat. Wrong open tab yields the wrong mode for the new chat container.

Import as branch uses Branch panel Import of JSONL to create a new branch of the open chat. The branch reuses that chat characters persona connection and prompt preset rather than inventing new membership from the file alone. Use this path when continuing an existing chat container rather than starting a new mode-tab chat session.

Reasoning in exports is controlled by Settings Advanced Message Tools Include reasoning in exports which defaults off. Off strips hidden thinking from both JSONL and Text for single and bulk exports. On includes reasoning; leave the toggle off before sharing exports that must not leak chain-of-thought content.

Group chats form when two or more characters are present without a separate group button. Conversation and Roleplay support them; Game uses its party system. Creation may select several characters, add a folder roster, or use Dice pick. Chat Settings supports add, remove, drag reorder, and per-chat eye-disable; disabling every character re-enables all as a zero-speaker fallback. Roleplay provides Merged Narrator or Individual with Sequential, Smart, and Manual response orders, Color Dialogues, Add Turn To Prompt, Name Prefix History, and chat-local Scenario Override. Conversation instead defaults to multi-character replies and provides Reply When Mentioned plus Character Exchanges under Autonomous Messaging.

children.summary: Roleplay group settings choose Merged Narrator default versus Individual. Merged optional Color Dialogues uses character Colors tab. Individual Response Order is Sequential list order Smart hidden AI pick with mention override and possible multi-queue or Manual Trigger Response only. Individual toggles Add Turn To Prompt default on and Name Prefix History default off. Scenario Override can replace card scenarios when present.

Conversation group speaking does not use Roleplay's Group Chat panel. Default replies may voice several characters with automatic speaker coloring. Reply When Mentioned makes members wait for an at-name mention or manual Trigger Response selection. Character Exchanges, off by default, allows members to talk to one another only while the browser app remains open and consumes the autonomous daily-message allowance. Schedules, presence, and per-chat member disable state further constrain participation without creating Sequential, Smart, or Manual Roleplay order.

anchors.summary: Connected Chats is a deliberate one-to-one link between one Conversation and one Roleplay or Game chat. Conversation automatically reads recent story messages; the story side does not automatically read Conversation. Character-emitted influence sends one-turn steering, note stores durable story-side prompt notes, and ooc posts Roleplay text back to Conversation. This differs from default-on Cross-Chat Awareness among sibling Conversations sharing a character. Links start from Conversation or Game, exclude already-linked chats, add bidirectional toolbar switching, and disconnect or chat deletion clears pending influences and saved notes. Story Chat Settings provides per-note deletion and confirmed Clear all.

Chat settings ownership places lorebook pins, agent enables, budgets, persona override, group modes, scoped regex, tool use, autonomous messaging, and Advanced Parameters on one chat. Reusable Chat Settings Presets may capture connection, prompt preset, agents, tools, translation, memory, and generation overrides, but omit characters, persona, lorebooks, sprites, summary, tags, scene prompt, and Roleplay Scenario Override. Library cards and prompt presets remain separate; the built-in Default preset cannot be renamed, overwritten, or deleted.

Hoplight does not convert Marinara chat JSONL unless an adapter exists. Kit must not invent chat codecs from this interchange page. Export privacy and mode-tab import rules describe upstream product behavior, not proven canonical interchange or round-trip support inside Hoplight.

Profiles route to Convo Display Name, About Me defaults and chat overrides, update_about_me scopes, Behavior insertion modes, and Conversation-only macros. The four-step new-chat wizard owns name and connection, prompt preset, participants, and Automation with autonomous messages, schedules, and package-contributed command families. Schedules include chat and character caps, tuning, timing, daily blocks, AI draft actions, temporary status, and user presence. Custom media covers portable emoji export, sticker send modes, Giphy limits, gallery scope, and semantic/random/tool-call selection. Calls document required audio pipeline, four input modes, per-chat versus global settings, answer lifecycle, soundboard, reusable video clips, and history summary.
