docs.title: SillyTavern character authoring
docs.summary: Field semantics and lifecycle of SillyTavern character cards, including permanent definitions, greetings, prompt overrides, examples, metadata, lore links, and portability.
docs.semanticSummary: Defines a SillyTavern character as both a portable Character Card and a runtime prompt component, with character name as the only required authoring field. Identity and permanent definitions separates always-sent name, description, personality, and scenario from conditional material, explains their context cost, and preserves authored prose rather than normalizing writing styles. Greetings and dialogue examples covers First Message as a style demonstration, Alternate Greetings as opening swipes, and START example blocks that may leave context as budget tightens. Advanced definitions and metadata distinguishes Main Prompt and Post-History Instructions overrides composed with original, depth-based Character's Note, group talkativeness, and non-prompt attribution fields. Lore, attachments, and platform links separates embedded books, named World Info links, chat lore, Data Bank attachments, tags, and installation state. Character expressions (sprites) documents per-emotion files under the character folder, ZIP packs, classifiers, custom labels, multi-sprite naming, folder override, and the rule that PNG cards do not carry the full expression grid. Import, export, and Hoplight boundaries explains JSON and PNG card layers, canonical mapping plus escrow, cross-format loss reporting, and the rule that scripts and installation-specific links remain sealed rather than transplanted or executed.

anchors.summary: Identity and permanent definitions states that name supplies character identity and the char macro, description carries broad durable facts, personality summarizes traits, and scenario establishes circumstances. SillyTavern sends all four on every generation, so their tokens reduce space available for history, examples, World Info, and retrieved documents. Authors should reserve them for stable required facts and move conditional material into lore, Author's Note, or depth-based injections. The prose fields accept free text, structured lists, and pseudo-dialogue without a mandated mini-language; actual effect depends on the model and surrounding template. Hoplight preserves authored strings without converting one writing method into another.

Greetings and dialogue examples distinguishes three teaching layers. First Message starts a new chat as the initial assistant turn and strongly demonstrates voice, markdown or HTML markup, pacing, and desired response length. Alternate Greetings provide additional opening swipes and may be selected when initiating group conversations so one card can host several entry scenarios. Example Messages use START blocks plus user and char labels; SillyTavern replaces the marker with the active example separator or utility prompt. Examples are budget-sensitive and can fall out block by block unless settings force retention, so they should demonstrate style rather than contain indispensable facts.

Advanced definitions and metadata separates behavioral instructions from attribution. Main Prompt and Post-History Instructions may override global values when the corresponding preference is enabled, while the original macro composes the default into an override instead of fully replacing it. Character's Note is a role-tagged static injection whose depth controls recency (depth zero after the most recent message; larger values earlier), and talkativeness changes natural-order group response probability rather than prose style. Creator, character version, creator notes, source references, and embedded tags support attribution or discovery and are normally not inserted into the model prompt, so conversion must not fold them into description prose merely because another platform has fewer metadata slots.

Lore, attachments, and platform links distinguishes an embedded character book that travels inside a compatible card, a named World Info link that depends on a separate book in the receiving installation, and chat lore owned by one conversation. Character-scoped Data Bank attachments are stored locally and do not export with the card. Tags may be assigned on the card, imported from embedded Tags to Embed, or bulk-edited; Manage Tags holds local colors, order, and bogus folder modes, while tag backup JSON is installation-specific. Import can create local tags, attach matches, import all, or import none. Filtering toggles include, exclude, or ignore tags. Character locks, chat history, favorites, and UI layout remain installation state and must not be rewritten into description prose during conversion.

Character expressions (sprites) stores per-emotion images under data user-handle characters character_name, separate from the single card avatar. Authors upload per emotion or a flat ZIP sprite pack that does not rename files to match emotions. Manual display uses click, expression-set, or Quick Reply; automatic change uses Local classifier (one-time model download; 28-label default or 6-label via extensions.models.classification), Main API LLM classification (Limited or Full Context), WebLLM, or deprecated Extras classify. Custom Expressions add author-named labels; Local and Extras classifiers know fixed sets unless trained or LLM sees defaults plus customs. Formats include PNG, webp, and animated gifs. Fallback may be an expression, No Fallback, or Default emojis. Multi-sprite naming uses expression name then a suffix after a dot or hyphen. Sprite Folder Override or costume command selects image sets. Portable PNG cards must not claim to carry the full expression grid.

Import, export, and Hoplight boundaries describes portable Character Card JSON and PNG carriers imported from files or URLs. Image pixels are presentation while encoded card data is the semantic record. Hoplight maps supported fields into a canonical character while retaining the complete source snapshot in escrow for same-format restoration of SillyTavern-specific fields that lack a canonical editing surface. Cross-format output carries only target-supported semantics and must report losses. Regex scripts, automation identifiers, local World Info names, and other installation-specific links cannot be copied merely because another platform offers a vaguely similar field. Imported scripts remain sealed data and never execute during import or conversion.

docs.title: SillyTavern chats and group configuration
docs.summary: SillyTavern chat file interchange (JSONL vs TXT), checkpoints, group reply strategies, generation handling modes, mute/force/auto, and scenario overrides as stored authored configuration.
docs.semanticSummary: Treats SillyTavern chats and group chats as re-importable creative artifacts documented at pin 70e5e4d3c239253fca4692fe82e3936cb9c4b1b1 via chatfilemanagement and groupchats sources. Solo versus group chats contrasts one-card solo chats with Create New Chat Group multi-member shared history. Chat import and export covers Import sources from Character.AI and other tools, Export as JSONL as re-importable metadata-bearing files excluding images, Export as TXT as human-readable non-reimportable dumps, and Checkpoints and rename including Create Branch, Create Checkpoint, parent links, and rename breakage. Group reply order strategies enumerates Manual, Natural Order with talkativeness and self-response rules, List Order, and Pooled Order. Group generation handling always shares history and selects Swap character cards or Join character cards with mute force auto, Allow Self Responses, Group Chat Scenario Override, Peek Character Definitions, and membership edits. Hoplight boundary states Hoplight does not host SillyTavern chat runtime, documents interchange for Kit understanding, keeps chat JSONL conversion out of scope without a future adapter, and leaves talkativeness on the character card.

anchors.summary: Solo versus group chats states a solo chat opens from one character card. A group chat is created with Create New Chat Group and holds multiple member cards that share history while reply drafting and card-assembly rules apply. The distinction is structural: group mode introduces reply order strategies, generation handling, mute force auto controls, and scenario overrides that do not apply to a single-card solo conversation. Authors must treat group membership and shared history as part of the stored chat artifact, not mere temporary UI selection.

Chat import and export separates re-importable structured interchange from lossy human dumps and branching clones. Import sources lists Character.AI via CAI Tools plus TavernAI, oobabooga text-generation-webui, Agnai, KoboldAI Lite, and RisuAI with source-dependent fidelity. Export as JSONL produces re-importable files with metadata but excluding images and file attachments, leaving privacy scrubbing to the sharer. Export as TXT is human-readable and cannot be re-imported; metadata is lost. Checkpoints and rename covers Create Branch (clone and switch), Create Checkpoint (clone name without switch), parent links by chat file name, Back to parent chat, and the failure mode that renaming breaks checkpoint links that stored the old file name. Default names use start date and time; rename via the pencil control.

children.summary: Import sources states SillyTavern can import chats from Character.AI via the CAI Tools extension and from tools including TavernAI, oobabooga text-generation-webui, Agnai, KoboldAI Lite, and RisuAI. Import formats and fidelity depend on the source tool. Do not assume byte-identical or field-complete transfer across every origin.

Export as JSONL is available from Manage chat files for each chat. The export produces a re-importable .jsonl including metadata but excluding images and file attachments. Privacy scrubbing before share is the user's responsibility. Treat JSONL as the portable chat interchange format when re-import is required.

Export as TXT is a plain-text download intended for human reading. It cannot be re-imported into SillyTavern as a chat. Metadata is lost. Never present TXT as a lossless interchange path for chat history, checkpoints, or group configuration.

Checkpoints and rename defines Create Branch as cloning the chat up to a message and switching to the clone, and Create Checkpoint as cloning up to a message, naming it, without switching. Checkpoints link to the parent by chat file name; Back to parent chat returns from a checkpoint. Renaming a chat breaks checkpoint links that stored the old file name. Default chat file names use start date and time; rename via the pencil control.

anchors.summary: Group reply order strategies enumerates four stored modes. Manual: the user picks the speaker via menu or trigger; empty user input can trigger a random unmuted member; user messages do not auto-trigger replies. Natural Order: extract whole-word name mentions from the last message (self-mentions ignored unless Allow Self Responses); then activate by Talkativeness where 0 percent never unless mentioned, 100 percent always, default 50 percent; if none activated, pick random. List Order: draft strictly by member list order. Pooled Order: pick a random member who has not spoken since the last user message; when all have spoken, pick randomly until the next user message. These strategies are group configuration, not character prose.

Group generation handling always shares history among members. Card assembly modes are Swap character cards (default: only the active speaker's card enters context) and Join character cards (combine all members' cards in list order, hurting isolation and risking identity confusion). Join sub-modes include or exclude muted members. Combined fields are Description; Scenario unless chat override; Personality; Message examples; Character notes and Depth prompts. Join Prefix and Suffix can separate fields; macros and char and FIELDNAME replacement apply. Mute disables replies; Force Talk triggers one member even if muted; Auto-mode chains generations with a five-second delay and disables when the user types though queued gens may continue; Allow Self Responses affects Natural Order self-mentions; Group Chat Scenario Override replaces each card's scenario for the group and branches inherit then can diverge; Peek Character Definitions edits the card itself; members can be added, removed, or reordered.

Hoplight boundary states Hoplight does not host SillyTavern chat runtime. The page documents interchange and group configuration so Kit understands what stored artifacts mean. Conversion of chat JSONL is out of scope unless a future adapter exists. Character talkativeness remains a card field documented on Characters rather than a free-floating group-only value. Do not claim Hoplight can run group generation, auto-mode chains, or re-import ST chats without an explicit adapter contract.

docs.title: SillyTavern macro syntax and operators
docs.summary: Complete operational guide to SillyTavern macro parsing, argument forms, nesting, scoped content, conditionals, flags, comments, escaping, variable identifiers, shorthand operators, return values, and legacy markers.
docs.semanticSummary: Complete operational model of the pinned SillyTavern macro parser. It specifies case-insensitive brace tokens, single and multi-argument separators, legacy colon syntax, ignored definition whitespace, inner-first nesting, scoped final arguments, trimming and dedenting, preserved whitespace, truthiness, inversion, else branches, implemented and planned flags, comments, and literal-brace escaping. Variable sections distinguish chat-local and installation-global prefixes, identifier restrictions, nested assigned values, and every shorthand operator with mutation, comparison, fallback, lazy evaluation, and return behavior. Full-form equivalence covers get, set, add, increment, and decrement, while existence and deletion remain named macros. Legacy angle markers map to modern forms without authoring-time normalization. The safety contract makes field registry and processing stage part of semantics and keeps all macro payloads sealed during Hoplight import and conversion.

anchors.summary: Tokens, arguments, whitespace, and nesting defines case-insensitive double-brace names, space-separated single arguments, recommended double-colon multiple arguments, and backward-compatible single-colon syntax. Whitespace around names, separators, and arguments does not affect parsing. Nested expressions resolve from the inside outward, allowing a computed character name or other result to become an outer variable key or value. That order is behaviorally important because nested random choices or state-changing macros can affect the consumer rather than remaining inert text.

Scoped blocks and whitespace preservation lets any argument-taking macro receive its final argument from text between opening and closing tags. The slash flag closes the named block. Default processing trims leading and trailing whitespace and removes shared indentation based on the first non-empty line, making multiline prose readable in source. The hash flag on the opening form preserves every newline and indentation character. Scoped content is semantically equivalent to an inline final argument after any earlier arguments and is appropriate for long or multiline values.

Conditions, inversion, and else specifies `if` blocks over no-argument macro names, nested expressions, variable shorthands, or literal values. Empty text, false, zero, off, and no are falsy. Prefixing the tested value with exclamation inverts the result, while `else` selects an alternate block when the first branch is false. The exclamation inside an `if` condition is logically distinct from the separately documented but unimplemented immediate flag, so parser context must be retained when explaining or editing the expression.

Flags, comments, and escaping separates two implemented flags from four planned forms. Slash closes a scoped block and hash preserves whitespace. Immediate exclamation, delayed question mark, re-evaluate tilde, and filter greater-than are documented plans, not current syntax. Single-line and scoped comments produce no output, with the scoped closing form using three slashes. Backslashes escape literal braces so authored text can display a macro-shaped token without resolving it. Kit must not advertise planned flags or accidentally unescape literal source.

Variable scopes and identifier rules assigns dot-prefixed shorthand to chat-local storage and dollar-prefixed shorthand to installation-global storage. The characters are prefixes rather than flags or parts of the stored name. Standard identifiers begin with a letter, continue with letters, digits, underscores, or hyphens, and cannot end in underscore or hyphen. Nonconforming keys require full variable macros. Assigned values may contain nested macros, and whitespace around operators is ignored. Both scopes support the same operators but differ materially in persistence and reach.

Variable shorthand operator table records all operations and return rules. Get returns the value; set, add, and subtract mutate and return empty text; increment and decrement return the new value. Add performs numeric addition or non-numeric string concatenation, while subtract requires numbers. Falsy and undefined fallbacks differ, as do their assignment variants, and fallback expressions evaluate lazily. Equality uses strings and treats missing, null, and empty alike; greater and less comparisons are numeric. Every comparison returns literal true or false text suitable for `if`.

anchors.text: Full variable macros and shorthand equivalence
anchors.summary: Full variable macros and shorthand equivalence maps dot and dollar get, set, add, increment, and decrement expressions to their named local and global macro forms. It preserves return behavior while showing that the prefix selects storage scope. Existence and deletion use `hasvar`, `deletevar`, `hasglobalvar`, and `deleteglobalvar`, since no shorthand operator replaces them. Comparison, fallback, and conditional-assignment shorthand also lack a one-token full-macro counterpart and should not be rewritten through an assumed mechanical equivalence.

Legacy markers maps USER to the user macro, BOT and CHAR to character, GROUP to group, and CHARIFNOTGROUP to the solo-character form. SillyTavern still recognizes these angle-bracket forms during processing for backward compatibility, but current authoring should use braces. Hoplight preserves legacy source during same-format round trips instead of performing cosmetic rewrites, because exact or tiered source stability may matter and another platform may interpret the text differently.

Evaluation and safety contract states that grammar validity does not prove a macro is registered in a particular field or processed at the expected stage. Variables, deletion, random choice, banned-word controls, and extension macros can alter state or generation behavior rather than merely returning text. Hoplight therefore treats every macro payload as sealed during import, inspection, conversion, and export and never runs it to infer meaning. Cross-format conversion preserves supported literal text, reports unrepresentable dialect behavior, and refuses name-only substitutions between superficially similar languages.

docs.title: SillyTavern documented macro catalog
docs.summary: Complete catalog of every built-in macro named by the pinned official SillyTavern macro manual, organized by content domain with signatures, returned values, mutation behavior, and scope notes.
docs.semanticSummary: Complete pinned catalog of every macro named in SillyTavern's official macro manual rather than a family-level sample. Authority and limits distinguishes the static documented set from extension-provided runtime registrations and field-specific availability. The catalog then enumerates participant, card, persona, message, swipe, clock, variable, random, model-state, prompt-template, Instruct, reasoning, image-generation, whitespace, input, banned-word, and World Info outlet macros with signatures, values, mutation behavior, and scope qualifications. Structural `if`, `else`, comment, block, and flag behavior routes to the operator reference. Runtime discovery requires `/? macros` or autocomplete for one live installation while using this page for pinned documented semantics. It warns that a known name is not proof of universal field support and that state-changing expressions remain sealed in Hoplight during import, inspection, conversion, and export.

anchors.summary: Catalog authority and limits defines completeness against the pinned official macro page, not against every future extension or local installation. SillyTavern's runtime registry can add names, while `/? macros` and autocomplete expose the live set and arguments. The tables use recommended modern signatures and qualify scope, return value, or mutation. Because fields are processed at different stages, catalog membership does not guarantee resolution everywhere. Hoplight treats state-changing or otherwise executable macro text as sealed and does not evaluate it during content operations.

Names, participants, cards, and personas individually catalogs user, character, group, non-muted group, solo-character, and other-participant values, then all documented card and persona fields. It distinguishes description, personality, scenario, persona, character prompt overrides, depth note, creator notes, version, formatted and raw examples, greetings, alternate greeting index, and original override composition. Scope notes preserve group and solo behavior, metadata distinctions, and empty-value cases. The section also warns that character-to-persona conversion may reverse `user` and `char` roles rather than safely retaining literal tokens.

anchors.text: Chat history, messages, time, and date
anchors.summary: Chat history, messages, time, and date enumerates latest message, latest user or character message, message indexes, context-window start, displayed-window start, current and final swipe indexes, full chat range, and extension-provided summary. Clock values cover local and UTC-offset time, short date, weekday, ISO time and date, custom formatting, idle duration, and two-value time difference. These results are runtime state rather than portable card data and can change across previews, branches, generations, installations, context fitting, display windows, and local clocks.

Variables, randomization, and runtime state catalogs complete local and global variable operations: get, set, add or append, increment, decrement, existence, and delete, with mutation and return behavior. Random rerolls from a list, pick stays stable for its chat position until rerolled, and roll evaluates dice syntax. Runtime lookups expose prompt, context, and response token limits, selected model, mobile state, latest generation kind, and extension availability. The section stresses that random is not a numeric range and that global writes affect installation state beyond one conversation.

anchors.text: Prompt, Instruct, reasoning, and image templates
anchors.summary: Prompt, Instruct, reasoning, and image templates catalogs the active and default system prompts, active, character, and default Author's Notes, Story String wrappers, user, assistant, and system role wrappers, separator, first and last role variants, stop sequence, filler, system-instruction prefix, example-chat separator, and chat-start marker. It also names reasoning prefix, suffix, and separator plus character positive and negative image-generation prompt prefixes. These values belong to model assembly stages and cannot be flattened into character identity or assumed equivalent to similarly named fields on another platform.

Utility and World Info values enumerates single and counted newlines, single and counted spaces, empty noop output, newline trimming, string reversal, current input, backend-dependent banned words, and named World Info outlets. It distinguishes text-returning utilities from actions with backend effects. Outlet lookup is case-sensitive and evaluation-stage dependent: content remains withheld until a compatible later field requests its exact key, and the form does not resolve inside World Info content, early card fields, or Author's Note. Outlet keys are therefore not automatically portable.

Conditional and structural forms identifies `if`, `else`, and comment expressions as language control forms rather than value lookups. Their complete truthiness, inversion, block, whitespace, and escape rules live in the operator reference. The section distinguishes implemented closing and preserve-whitespace flags from planned immediate, delayed, re-evaluate, and filter flags. Kit must not infer that planned syntax works merely because the official manual names it, and must keep structural meaning alongside the ordinary macro catalog.

Runtime discovery rule tells Kit how to answer without confusing a pinned manual with live installation state. For a cataloged name, the reference supplies documented semantics. For existence or support in the user's installation or field, Kit should direct them to `/? macros` or field autocomplete because extensions and field registries change the available set. Claims must be labeled as pinned documentation or observed runtime behavior, and absent snapshot evidence must not be converted into certainty about a user's environment.

docs.title: SillyTavern macro language
docs.summary: Authoring reference for SillyTavern macro syntax, arguments, nesting, scoped and conditional forms, variables, common macro families, and portability hazards.
docs.semanticSummary: Explains SillyTavern macros as a runtime expression language used across prompts, cards, World Info, Quick Replies, regex configuration, and scripts, with availability depending on field and evaluation stage. It routes exhaustive lookup to the companion documented-name catalog and complete operator reference. Core syntax covers double-brace names, arguments, nesting, scoped blocks, whitespace, conditionals, comments, escaping, and implemented versus planned flags. Variables describes chat-local and installation-global stores, full and shorthand operations, lazy fallbacks, and state mutation. Value families span participants, card and persona fields, runtime and random values, prompt templates, utilities, and extension-provided registrations. Portability hazards include order-dependent outlets, persona role reversal, regex substitution, script contexts, legacy markers, and platform semantic differences. Hoplight preserves exact source and keeps macros sealed rather than evaluating or translating them through superficial replacement.

anchors.summary: Core syntax and composition defines modern case-insensitive double-brace macros, a space for one argument, and `::` for multiple arguments; single-colon syntax is legacy. Whitespace around names and separators is ignored, inner expressions resolve before outer consumers, and scoped blocks provide a final dedented argument unless `#` preserves whitespace. `{{if}}` supports truthiness, inversion, and else branches; comments and backslash escapes preserve non-output or literal braces. Only closing `/` and whitespace-preserving `#` flags are implemented in the pinned source, so Kit must not present documented future immediate, delayed, re-evaluate, or filter flags as available.

Variables and state separates chat-local variables from installation-global variables. Full macros can get, set, add, increment, decrement, test existence, and delete values in either scope, with values sometimes containing JSON-like data. The experimental shorthand uses `.name` locally and `$name` globally and supports assignment, arithmetic or string addition, fallbacks, conditional assignment, equality, inequality, and numeric comparisons; fallback operands resolve lazily. Because expressions such as setvar mutate stored state during expansion, macro-bearing text is not necessarily passive. Hoplight never expands it while importing, inspecting, summarizing, converting, or exporting.

Common value families groups macros by purpose. Participant values identify user, character, groups, and speakers. Card and persona values expose definitions, prompt overrides, notes, versions, examples, and greetings. Runtime values expose messages, swipes, time, model limits, generation type, extension state, and summaries. Random forms provide rerolled choice, stable chat choice, and dice. Template values expose active system and Author's Note text plus Instruct wrappers, stops, and reasoning markers, while utilities manipulate whitespace, strings, input, banned words, or named World Info outlets. Extensions can register more, so runtime help and field autocomplete remain authoritative for one installation.

Evaluation and portability hazards explains that the same valid macro may behave differently by processing phase. World Info outlets do not resolve within early character fields, World Info content, or Author's Note. Character-to-persona conversion may reverse user and character roles, regex fields choose disabled, raw, or escaped macro substitution, and scripts provide pipe or variable contexts absent from prompt prose. Platforms that share brace syntax can still disagree on names, arguments, truthiness, and timing. Hoplight preserves same-format text exactly, reports unsupported cross-format behavior, avoids execution, and retains escaped, nested, or legacy markers required by the source round-trip tier.

docs.title: SillyTavern personas and Data Bank
docs.summary: Creation and portability model for SillyTavern user personas and retrieval documents, including prompt placement, locks, backups, attachment scopes, ingestion, and vectors.
docs.semanticSummary: Explains two user-controlled SillyTavern context systems that differ in ownership and portability: personas represent the user's chat identity, while Data Bank documents provide retrievable reference material. Persona identity and description covers display metadata, prompt-bearing description, placement choices, and the limited character-to-persona conversion with macro-role reversal. Persona connections and backups describes chat locks, character associations, defaults, temporary selection, immutable historical attribution, explicit synchronization, backup omissions, and Hoplight's selected-persona import plus whole-source escrow. Data Bank documents and scopes distinguishes global, character, chat, and message-level material, inventories extractable text sources, and rejects the assumption that local attachments travel with a card. Vectorization and retrieval separates authored documents from generated, model-specific embedding indexes and identifies chunking, overlap, thresholds, query window, and insertion limits as retrieval controls. Hoplight can explain these systems and preserve supported persona semantics, but Data Bank is not yet a canonical entity and neither system should be silently folded into a character.

anchors.summary: Persona identity and description defines a persona as display name, avatar, optional title, and optional prompt-bearing description. The title remains UI metadata. Description placement is saved per persona and may be disabled, expanded through Story String or Prompt Manager, placed around Author's Note, or injected into chat history at a chosen depth and role; therefore position must remain structured metadata. Character-to-persona conversion copies only useful identity fields, not scenario, personality, or greetings, and may require swapping `{{user}}` with `{{char}}` because their roles reverse.

Persona connections and backups defines selection precedence: a chat lock wins, then character association, then default persona, while a temporary choice lasts only until reopening. Past user messages retain their original persona attribution; switching identity does not rewrite history, and synchronization is a separate action. Optional multiple connections require a choice. Backups include names, descriptions, and character connections but omit images and chat connections, carry internal links, and are not public interchange packages. Hoplight imports one selected persona while escrowing the complete backup for same-format restoration.

Data Bank documents and scopes treats documents as retrieval sources rather than card fields. Global attachments apply everywhere, character attachments apply while that character participates, and chat attachments belong only to the active conversation; character attachments remain local and do not export with the card. Sources may be authored notes, extractable local files, readable web pages, video transcripts, or extension scrapers. PDF text, HTML, Markdown, ePUB, structured text, and source code can be converted when plain text is extractable, while unreadable binary input is rejected. A one-message file attachment does not imply a durable Data Bank entry.

Vectorization and retrieval describes Vector Storage as a generated index over document chunks. A selected embedding provider turns chunks into model-specific vectors, and recent messages form a query that retrieves related chunks for prompt insertion. Chunk size, overlap, score threshold, query-message count, and insertion limits affect recall, precision, and context cost; changing source content or embedding model requires recalculation. Vectors are cached indexes stored separately from authored documents, not portable source truth. Hoplight should preserve source documents and supported retrieval settings separately, and must not claim current character import includes Data Bank because no dedicated canonical Data Bank entity exists.

docs.title: SillyTavern prompts and presets
docs.summary: How SillyTavern assembles model context and separates Text Completion templates, Chat Completion Prompt Manager entries, character overrides, Author's Note, and generation presets.
docs.semanticSummary: Explains SillyTavern prompt construction as layered runtime assembly rather than one universal preset file. Prompt layers and precedence covers main or system instructions, character definitions and overrides, persona, World Info, Data Bank, examples, history, Author's Note, current input, and post-history instructions. Text Completion separates Context Template Story String from Instruct wrapping, while Chat Completion Prompt Manager models ordered role-bearing messages. Preset boundaries distinguish sampler presets, Context and Instruct templates, system prompts, Prompt Manager configurations, Quick Replies, and extension settings. CFG is multi-scope generation control. Tokenizer selection distinguishes overridable Text Completion from provider-bound Chat Completion, downloadable fallback, and Token Padding including negative values and trimming risk. Reasoning coverage includes token cost, display, acquisition, reinsertion, regex ephemerality, and provider effort controls. These are upstream product semantics; current Hoplight adapter capabilities remain governed by the format reference.

anchors.summary: Prompt layers and precedence inventories the runtime request: general instructions, character and persona definitions, World Info, Data Bank retrieval, summaries, external results, example dialogue, chat history, the current user message, and final instructions. Position and role affect priority as much as prose. Main Prompt or System Prompt supplies broad behavior, while Post-History Instructions near generation commonly exert stronger immediate pressure. Character cards may replace either when user preferences permit, and the original macro composes the global value into a character override rather than fully replacing it. Author's Note can sit after Scenario or inside history at a selected depth and frequency. When a distant system change fails against established history, authors should open a new chat, repair contradictory turns, use examples, or place a narrow reminder closer to the generation boundary.

Text Completion templates are governed by Advanced Formatting. A Context Template Story String arranges system prompt, character description, personality, scenario, persona, and other macro-expanded components. Instruct Mode wraps story, system, user, and assistant content in model-specific sequences and can define story-string prefix and suffix, role prefixes and suffixes, first or last message variants, separators, stop sequences, and alignment filler. Include Names and wrapping options decide whether participant labels are authored into the serialized request. These values describe wire formatting for a model, not character identity. Custom stopping strings and reply prefill are adjacent generation controls: a stop array may be provider-limited, while Start Reply With may become a final text prefix or assistant-role prefill. A portable preset must keep these controls typed rather than concatenating them into one prompt block.

Chat Completion Prompt Manager represents context as ordered messages with roles rather than one flat string. Utility prompts include format templates, new-chat and new-example markers, group nudges, continuation nudges, and empty-message replacements. Editable entries carry a name, role, trigger conditions, enabled state, position, depth, and order, and may sit at a relative position or an in-chat depth. The manager also controls character-name handling, continuation postfix or prefill, system-message squashing, inline media, reasoning requests, function calling, and provider-dependent system-role use. The visible list is an assembly plan: removing, disabling, or reordering one entry changes the request even when every prose block stays identical. Hoplight must preserve ordered prompt blocks and their roles rather than flattening a Chat Completion preset into a single string.

Preset and interoperability boundaries separates sampler presets, Context Templates, Instruct templates, system prompts, Prompt Manager configurations, Quick Reply presets, and extension-specific settings as distinct artifacts even when the UI groups them. Similar UI adjacency does not make them one file format. Hoplight's canonical preset models sampler settings, prompt blocks, and groups where adapters provide a semantic mapping. Platform-only ordering or provider controls may remain in escrow for same-format export. When converting to another platform, report unsupported roles, triggers, template sequences, and extension settings instead of presenting a partially flattened prompt as lossless. Inspect the final prompt when diagnosing behavior: an authored block may be valid but absent because its trigger did not fire, its position was disabled, context budget removed it, or a character override replaced the global value.

Classifier-free guidance (CFG) mixes differences between positive and negative guidance streams as LLM prompt mixing, not Stable Diffusion negative tags. Supported backends named by the pin include oobabooga textgen WebUI, NovelAI, and TabbyAPI. VRAM rises because more than one prompt is ingested; OOM recovery is reduce context, use a smaller model, or disable CFG. Access sits alongside Author's Note. Four scopes are Chat CFG, Character CFG, Global CFG (overrides model preset CFG), and CFG Advanced Settings (formerly Prompt Cascading) to combine scopes and set insertion depth. Guidance scale 1 is off and sends nothing CFG-related; scale above 1 increases strength; scale below 1 inverts emphasis toward the negative stream; about 1.5 is a suggested start. Positive and negative prompts are optional. Group chats remove Character CFG and add Use Character CFG Scales and Character Negatives. Insertion depth defaults to 1; depth 0 can dominate and is not recommended with cascading. Treat CFG as runtime generation control, not character-card prose, unless a format explicitly stores it.

Tokenizer selection and padding sources Usage Prompts tokenizer at the pin. Tokenizers split text into tokens roughly three to four characters. Best match follows API family. Text Completion is overridable NovelAI Clio NerdStash Kayra NerdStash v2 API tokenizer if supported else Llama KoboldAI Classic AI Horde Llama KoboldCpp model API. Chat Completion is non-overridable OpenAI tiktoken Claude WebTokenizers OpenRouter families Gemma downloadable models fallback GPT-3.5 turbo. Text Completion overrides include None rounded up Llama Llama 3 NerdStash Mistral Yi Gemma DeepSeek API tokenizer ooba koboldcpp TabbyAPI Aphrodite. Downloadable Qwen2 Command-R Mistral V3 Nemo DeepSeek chat download once unless enableDownloadableTokenizers false with manual JSON under data cache Llama 3 fallback when uncached downloads disabled. Token Padding is Text Completion only; Chat Completion always matches its tokenizer. Padding reserves room near max context so definitions are not truncated. Negative padding can exceed stated max tokens and raise prompt-trimming risk.

Reasoning and chain-of-thought blocks notes that hidden reasoning can consume Max Response Length, so incomplete or empty answers often need 1024 to 4096 response tokens on reasoning models. Blocks appear collapsible; Auto-Expand and Show Hidden are Advanced Formatting options; edit and copy work when expanded. Adding reasoning covers manual lightbulb edits, extensions writing extra.reasoning, the reasoning-set command, backend Request model reasoning for named sources, and Auto-Parse with Prefix and Suffix for unparsed streams. Prompting with reasoning defaults to not resending thoughts, describes Add to Prompts wrapping with Max Additions, and notes Continue may resend incomplete reasoning-only messages. Regex and effort covers Regex Affects Reasoning, ephemerality modes, and Reasoning Effort Auto through Maximum as connection configuration mapped to provider budgets, never a character-card field.

children.summary: Adding reasoning can be Manual via the message edit lightbulb or extensions writing extra.reasoning; Command via reasoning-set with optional at message id defaulting to the last message; Backend via Request model reasoning in AI Response Configuration when the source supports it (for most sources this only toggles request where the API allows and does not fully disable thinking). Named pin sources include Claude, DeepSeek, Google AI Studio/Vertex, OpenRouter, xAI, AI/ML API, Z.AI, Pollinations, MistralAI, Electron Hub, Chutes, NanoGPT, and Moonshot, with source-specific disable and effort caveats. Parse uses Auto-Parse with Prefix and Suffix (DeepSeek-style think defaults) for unparsed streams such as MiniMax or Perplexity.

Prompting with reasoning defaults to not resending prior reasoning into later turns. Add to Prompts wraps content with Prefix, Suffix, and Separator; Max Additions counts from the end of the prompt. Providers often discourage multi-turn chain-of-thought resend. Continue may resend incomplete reasoning-only messages without requiring Add to Prompts so the model can finish thinking and then emit content. Authors must treat reinsertion as an explicit opt-in with token cost rather than an automatic memory of all hidden thoughts.

Regex and effort notes that Regex Affects can include Reasoning. Ephemerality modes are none for permanent rewrite, run-on-edit to re-apply, alter display only, and alter outgoing prompts only. Reasoning Effort in the Chat Completion AI Response panel maps Auto, Minimum, Low, Medium, High, and Maximum to provider-specific budgets or keywords (Claude token budgets or adaptive thinking; OpenAI, OpenRouter, xAI, Perplexity, and NanoGPT keywords; Google thinkingBudget or thinkingLevel tables for 2.5 and 3.x models). Auto usually omits the parameter. Effort is connection configuration, not a character-card field.

docs.title: SillyTavern authoring reference
docs.summary: Curated map of SillyTavern content authoring concepts that Kit can use when creating, explaining, importing, editing, and exporting compatible pieces.
docs.semanticSummary: Curated entry point for Kit's SillyTavern authoring knowledge. The collection covers portable and behaviorally significant content rather than installation, hosting, providers, or ordinary chat controls. Collection map routes character cards including sprites, chats and groups with JSONL versus TXT, World Info, personas and Data Bank, prompts and presets including CFG and reasoning, macro language semantics, an exhaustive pinned macro catalog, complete macro operators, regex and STscript automation, and an auditable source-coverage contract to focused pages, requiring whole-page reading around a search hit because prompt order, scope, and timing qualify isolated matches. Authority and provenance identifies independently organized Hoplight text, pins official SillyTavern-Docs commit 70e5e4d3c239253fca4692fe82e3936cb9c4b1b1 retrieved 2026-07-26 with the same pin as 2026-07-25, and preserves AGPL license and contributor links. How Kit should apply it separates upstream behavior, current adapter behavior, and authoring advice, making the format adapter page authoritative for implementation claims and forbidding invented adapter support from upstream alone. Refresh policy limits updates to content types, workflows, prompt contracts, or interoperability and requires revision comparison, regenerated semantic summaries, and independent review while excluding routine UI, install, and provider churn.

anchors.summary: Collection map routes Characters card fields greetings advanced definitions metadata tags expression sprites permanent versus conditional prompt content Chats and groups re-importable chat JSONL versus lossy TXT checkpoints group reply strategies join modes mute force auto scenario overrides World Info lorebooks activation insertion recursion grouping timed effects outlets vector matching Personas and Data Bank user identities prompt placement connections backups attachment scopes retrieval documents Prompts and presets final request Text Completion templates Chat Completion Prompt Manager Author Note CFG reasoning blocks tokenizer selection and padding portable preset boundaries Macros evaluation Documented macro catalog Macro operators Regex and automation scripts STscript Quick Replies and Source coverage for every evaluated upstream authoring page. Use the narrow owning page then read surrounding constraints because features interact through prompt order scope or evaluation timing.

Authority and provenance declares these pages independently organized Hoplight documentation rather than a verbatim mirror or upstream replacement. It pins SillyTavern/SillyTavern-Docs to commit 70e5e4d3c239253fca4692fe82e3936cb9c4b1b1 retrieved on 2026-07-26 (same pin as 2026-07-25), and states every page links its principal upstream sources. Upstream documentation is licensed under AGPL-3.0; Hoplight is also AGPL-3.0-or-later. Upstream copyright and contributor credits remain available in the official documentation repository, including its license file and LicenseCredits document. The pin, retrieval date, and attribution together make later audits and refreshes reproducible for Kit and maintainers.

How Kit should apply it requires distinguishing three claim kinds. Upstream behavior describes what SillyTavern does with a field or artifact. Hoplight format behavior describes what the current adapter can preserve or emit. Authoring advice explains how fields interact but does not prove every target format can carry them. For interoperability decisions, read this collection with the SillyTavern format page; if they differ, the format page governs current Hoplight implementation and this collection governs upstream meaning. Kit must never invent adapter support from an upstream feature description alone.

Refresh policy states SillyTavern evolves quickly. A future refresh should compare the pinned upstream revision, update only the affected Hoplight pages, regenerate their semantic sidecars, and obtain a new independent review. New upstream features should join this collection only when they change a content type, authoring workflow, prompt contract, or interoperability decision. Routine UI rearrangements, installation changes, provider lists, and transient defaults stay outside the collection. When exact current UI labels matter, follow the linked official page rather than treating this corpus as a live UI screenshot.

docs.title: SillyTavern regex and automation
docs.summary: Content model and safety boundary for SillyTavern regex scripts, STscript, Quick Replies, World Info automation identifiers, execution scope, persistence, and portability.
docs.semanticSummary: Defines SillyTavern regex scripts and STscript as authored content with executable effects inside SillyTavern while Hoplight only inspects, edits, and round-trips their text as data. Regex script records cover display name, find expression, replacement with complete match and capture groups, trim strings, enabled state, source scopes, macro-substitution mode, depth bounds, run-on-edit, ephemerality, JavaScript-style flags, global versus character scope, export JSON portability, Affects selectors for user input AI response slash values World Info and reasoning, and empty-selector plus depth constraints. Ephemerality and visible truth separates persistent chat JSONL rewrites from display-only and prompt-only modes, creating three truths of stored, rendered, and model-bound messages that both ephemerality flags must preserve, plus find-expression macro modes disabled raw or regex-escaped and the requirement for bounded terminable testing. STscript and Quick Replies describes pipe-batched slash commands, variables, conditions, generation, World Info mutation, QR presets and qrset, properties, a.b cross-preset calls, management commands, auto-execute triggers including World Info Automation ID, and installation-dependent extension commands. Hoplight safety and interoperability seals imported payloads, forbids execution during import or conversion, limits regex testing to the isolated user-invoked terminable worker, escrows same-format script fields, requires explicit semantic mapping for cross-format movement, and routes execution-condition edits through Gate review.

anchors.summary: Regex script records include a display name, find expression, replacement, optional trim strings, enabled state, source scopes, macro-substitution mode, depth bounds, run-on-edit behavior, and ephemerality settings. Replacement supports the complete match and capture groups. JavaScript-style flags control global, case-insensitive, dot-all, multiline, and Unicode behavior. Global scripts live in installation settings; scoped scripts live in the active character card. Exported JSON can move a script between installations, and scripts can move between global and character scope. Name is operational because slash commands and STscript may target it. Affects selectors include user input, AI response, slash-command values, World Info content, and reasoning. An empty selector set prevents normal chat activation but may still allow an explicit script call. Min and max depth constrain eligible chat messages and do not apply to utility or system prompts in the same way.

Ephemerality and visible truth states that with neither ephemerality option selected, a regex script can rewrite values stored in the chat JSONL, a persistent and possibly irreversible mutation. Display-only changes alter what the user sees without changing the outgoing prompt. Prompt-only changes alter what the model receives without changing display. Selecting both changes display and prompt while leaving stored chat text untouched. This creates three distinct truths: stored message, rendered message, and model-bound message. An editor must preserve both ephemerality flags rather than reducing them to one enabled switch. World Info scope also depends on outgoing-prompt behavior. Macro substitution in the find expression may be disabled, raw, or regex-escaped; raw values can change pattern meaning when names contain metacharacters, while escaped substitution treats the value literally. Testing must use bounded, terminable execution because user-authored patterns can be computationally expensive.

STscript and Quick Replies describes STscript as pipe-separated slash command batches executed sequentially with pipe-passed values. The language includes named and unnamed arguments, macros, local and global variables, arrays and objects, conditions, closures, loops, math, generation calls, prompt injections, message access, character navigation, World Info mutation, text processing, and extension commands. Quick Replies store scripts behind buttons or hidden procedures; presets group replies and switch via qrset by name. From the pinned STscript reference: autocomplete on chat input and the large QR editor, slash-colon listing scoped variables and QRs, QR properties label message/script tool tip and debugger with breakpoint, cross-preset procedure calls as a.b with literal labels winning first, management commands including qr-create qr-delete qr-update qr-get and preset and context-menu helpers, and auto-execute at app startup user message AI message chat load group reply or matching World Info Automation ID. Extensions add installation-dependent commands. Scripts can call a model, modify messages and lore, change variables, navigate UI, or invoke extensions and are not static macro templates. Official docs warn users to inspect scripts before execution.

Hoplight safety and interoperability requires that imported regex, macro, Lua, and STscript payloads remain sealed text. Hoplight does not execute STscript, resolve Quick Reply procedures, follow Automation IDs, or apply a regex during import or conversion. Regex testing is available only through Hoplight's isolated, user-invoked test bench and its terminable worker. Same-format export can restore platform-native script fields from escrow. Cross-format movement is allowed only when a target adapter has an explicit semantic mapping; a target that merely has scripts does not prove compatible scope, lifecycle, persistence, or command semantics. Kit should describe executable consequences before proposing an edit. It must not imply that a disabled list switch, an internal disabled field, an empty Affects set, and ephemerality are interchangeable. Changes to any execution condition belong in the semantic Gate review even though the payload remains sealed.

docs.title: SillyTavern authoring source coverage
docs.summary: Path-level coverage map from the pinned SillyTavern-Docs tree to Hoplight platform references, with individual inclusion verdicts and no wildcard exclusions for authoring material.
docs.semanticSummary: Auditable path-by-path coverage map for all 92 Markdown files at SillyTavern-Docs commit 70e5e4d3c239253fca4692fe82e3936cb9c4b1b1, retrieved 2026-07-26 under AGPL-3.0. Twenty-one included authoring sources route character cards, tags, chat interchange, groups, personas, Data Bank, World Info, prompt assembly, CFG, reasoning, tokenizers, macros, regex, STscript, Quick Replies, and expression images to owning Hoplight references. Seventy-one individually named exclusions cover provider setup, installation, administration, ordinary navigation and settings, runtime-only extensions, contributor workflows, and repository metadata with a reason per path. Dynamic installation authorities remain live macro help, field autocomplete, extension slash commands, and expression classifiers; Hoplight never executes imported automation to discover them. Refresh requires pin comparison, destination updates, macro coverage tests, fresh semantic summaries, and independent review.

anchors.summary: Pinned source identifies the exact upstream documentation snapshot: SillyTavern/SillyTavern-Docs at commit 70e5e4d3c239253fca4692fe82e3936cb9c4b1b1, retrieved 2026-07-26, licensed AGPL-3.0. Paths in the coverage tables are repository-relative to that tree so audits can open the same files the Hoplight authoring corpus claimed to evaluate. The pin is the authority for inclusion and exclusion decisions on this page; later docs commits require an explicit refresh rather than silent drift. License and commit together make provenance reproducible for Kit and human maintainers.

Included authoring pages table maps Characters index design Author Note tags chatfilemanagement groupchats personas data-bank worldinfo Prompts index advancedformatting context-template instructmode prompt-manager CFG reasoning tokenizer macros Regex STscript and Expression-Images to Characters Chats Personas World Info Prompts Macros Regex destinations. Tokenizer selection and padding routes to Prompts and presets. The claim that every markdown file is classified depends on tokenizer remaining in this include table or a defensible exclusion which this corpus does not use. Preserve these rules in Kit answers without inventing adapter support.

Evaluated exclusions classifies 71 pinned files one row at a time with no directory wildcards. The table names chat navigation and branch UX, every provider-connection page, ordinary settings and onboarding, each installation and migration guide, every administration page, runtime-only audio image retrieval translation avatar and utility extensions, contributor workflows, and repository metadata. Each row states why it does not define a selected portable authoring contract. Together with the 21 inclusion rows, the manifest accounts for all 92 Markdown files. Macro names and operators remain governed by the stronger exhaustive catalogs rather than inferred from this coverage table.

Hoplight never executes imported automation, STscript, or sealed scripts merely to discover what an installation can do. Capability claims must not be reverse-engineered by running untrusted content; they come from static documentation, adapters, and user-invoked sandboxed benches only.

Refresh requires comparing the next SillyTavern-Docs commit to the pinned hash, updating inclusion and exclusion destinations, re-running macro coverage tests, rewriting affected semantic summaries, and obtaining independent review after those summary rewrites. Do not advance the pin without reconciling every path-level verdict and regenerating author-valid sidecars for changed pages.

docs.title: SillyTavern World Info authoring
docs.summary: Operational model of SillyTavern lorebooks, including book attachment, keyword and vector activation, entry selection, prompt placement, recursion, groups, outlets, and budgets.
docs.semanticSummary: Models SillyTavern World Info as conditional knowledge and prompt injection rather than a passive dictionary. Books, links, and entry identity distinguishes global, character, chat, embedded, and named-link scopes, organizational memos, content, enabled state, character filters, generation filters, and extra scan sources. Activation and selection covers constants, primary and secondary keywords, selective logic, probability, inclusion groups, group scoring, and vector similarity with remaining eligibility checks. Placement, order, and prompt budget separates insertion position, chat depth, order, outlets, scan depth, minimum activations, and context budget. Recursion, timing, and automation covers recursive activation controls, sticky, cooldown, delay, branch state, and executable Automation IDs. Interoperability rules distinguishes portable character books from standalone World Info dialects, requires canonical mapping plus original escrow, and demands explicit loss reporting when another platform lacks recursion, grouping, timing, vectors, outlets, trigger filters, or scan-source controls.

anchors.summary: Books, links, and entry identity distinguishes availability from activation. Books may be global, character-linked, chat-linked, embedded in a card, or referenced by an installed name. Entries retain a memo for humans, model-bound content, enabled state, and ordering metadata; memo and keys are not stable identity substitutes. Character or tag filters narrow eligible speakers, generation filters distinguish Normal, Continue, Impersonate, Swipe, Regenerate, and Quiet, and optional scan sources extend matching into character, persona, and creator fields.

Activation and selection covers constant entries, primary keys, secondary keys, selective any, all, not-any, or not-all logic, and global or per-entry case and whole-word behavior. Probability filters an otherwise qualified entry. Inclusion groups then resolve competing entries using weight, deterministic order priority, or matched-key group scoring. Vector similarity can replace keyword qualification but does not bypass probability, filters, groups, or token budget; retained keywords still permit ordinary activation, and embedding retrieval is less deterministic than explicit keys.

Placement, order, and prompt budget keeps insertion position, chat depth, and sort order as independent axes. Entries may land around definitions, examples, Author's Note, or a role-tagged chat depth. Outlet entries wait for an exact case-sensitive `{{outlet::Name}}` in a compatible later-processed prompt field; outlets cannot nest or resolve in early card fields, World Info content, or Author's Note. Context percentage or token budget limits combined entries, scan depth defines recent key input, and Min Activations may search farther within Max Depth.

Recursion, timing, and automation explains entry chains activated by keywords inside other entry content. Per-entry controls may block recursive activation, stop further propagation, or delay eligibility to a recursion level, while Max Recursion Steps bounds passes and conflicts with Min Activations. Sticky, cooldown, and delay create message-counted chat-local state that branches inherit and edits clear. Automation IDs can execute matched Quick Reply or STscript behavior, so Hoplight treats those bindings as sealed executable metadata and never follows them during import.

Interoperability rules distinguishes the portable character-book schema from SillyTavern's richer standalone World Info wire dialect, including extension-carried settings. Hoplight maps represented behavior into canonical lorebook entries and retains the complete source for same-format restoration. A cross-format target may lack recursion, inclusion groups, timed effects, vectors, outlets, generation filters, or alternative scan sources. Conversion must report each unsupported behavior rather than flattening it silently, with the format adapter reference governing the exact supported field and enum map.

docs.title: Safe archive handling: .charx and .byaf
docs.summary: How hoplight bounds a .charx or .byaf ZIP before and after inflation to resist a zip bomb, and where entry names are (and are not yet) checked for path traversal before they can become a filesystem write or a re-exported archive path.
docs.semanticSummary: Safe archive handling covers how Hoplight bounds .charx and .byaf ZIP bytes as untrusted until parsed with two properties proven to different degrees. Decompression limits against a zip bomb are real shared and unit-tested via unzipBounded and CARD_ARCHIVE_BOUNDS used by Risu and BYAF thin safeUnzip wrappers: reject before unzip pre-inflate per entry post-inflate backstop fail closed error wrap detection-only selection and module.risum RPack non-expansion. Path-traversal safety on entry names notes fflate does not sanitize names ingestion never turns a name into a filesystem write the one checked BYAF greeting id path via resolveGreetingPath and two unchecked re-export name carriers for BYAF images and Risu assets. What is not yet proven lists the untested lying-header backstop and the two unguarded export name paths so archive handling must not be called fully sandboxed against hostile archives.

anchors.text: Decompression limits against a zip bomb
anchors.summary: Decompression limits against a zip bomb share one helper. The shared bound is CARD_ARCHIVE_BOUNDS 96 MiB archive 512 entries 64 MiB per entry 96 MiB aggregate used by Risu and BYAF safeUnzip wrappers. Reject before any unzip call checks full compressed length first. Pre-inflate per entry uses fflate filter for total-entry compressed original and aggregate checks with missing originalSize falling back to compressed. Post-inflate as a backstop rechecks actual bytes but cannot undo allocation already done and lacks a lying-header test. Fail closed on any read error rewraps non-limit throws as ArchiveLimitError with Risu detect soft and toCanonical hard while BYAF open returns null. Detection is bounded too via only card.json or manifest.json. The module.risum aside is ordinary ZIP entry then fixed RPack substitution that cannot expand.

children.summary: CARD_ARCHIVE_BOUNDS is the budget both charx and byaf unzip under: 96 MiB max archive size 512 total entries 64 MiB max per selected entry compressed or inflated and 96 MiB max aggregate inflated across selected entries. Risu safeUnzip and BYAF container safeUnzip are thin wrappers that pin bounds CARD_ARCHIVE_BOUNDS and forward to the same unzipBounded. Neither format reimplements the check; both call the one helper in core archive.ts.

The full compressed archive length is checked first against maxArchiveBytes before unzipSync is called at all. An archive over 96 MiB never reaches fflate so hostile bulk payloads die at the outer gate without decompression work.

unzipBounded passes fflate an UnzipFileInfo filter that runs during extraction. Inside the callback before inflate: running total-entry count against maxEntries before selection so hostile directory counts still bound; compressed size and declared original size via entryOriginal fallback against maxEntryCompressed and maxEntryOriginal for selected entries; running sum of declared originals against maxAggregateOriginal. only-filter misses skip size budgets but already consumed total-entry budget and never inflate.

After unzipSync returns unzipBounded rechecks actual byteLength against maxEntryOriginal and actual aggregate against maxAggregateOriginal and maxEntries to catch understated originalSize. By then inflate already allocated; recheck discards and throws but cannot stop the spike. maxEntryCompressed plus practical DEFLATE ratio bounds the worst case. No streaming mid-decompress reject. No archive.test constructs a lying originalSize so this path is review-proven not test-proven.

children.text: Fail closed on any read error
children.summary: Anything unzipSync throws that is not already ArchiveLimitError is rewrapped as ArchiveLimitError archive could not be read safely. No partial-success path: fully bounded Record or throw. Risu detect catches everything as not this format while toCanonical lets ArchiveLimitError propagate. BYAF openByaf catches and returns null so bombs surface as generic not a valid byaf Error not ArchiveLimitError. Both fail closed under different error shapes.

Format detection never inflates a whole archive to check shape. Risu detect calls safeUnzip with only card.json so every other entry is skipped before inflation while directory entries still consume total-entry budget and the match passes size checks. BYAF detection reads only manifest.json the same way through readManifestBytes. A large hostile archive being probed cannot force full inflate or unbounded directory scan.

A charx can carry module.risum as one ordinary ZIP entry under the same CARD_ARCHIVE_BOUNDS with no separate inflate step. Extracted bytes run only through RPack byte substitution a fixed 256-entry table one byte at a time into a same-length output buffer not a compression codec. It cannot expand so it adds no zip-bomb surface beyond the entry cap it already sits under.

anchors.summary: Path-traversal safety on entry names is proven unevenly. fflate does not sanitize names so unzipBounded can return literal ../ keys within size budgets. Ingestion never turns a name into a filesystem write: entries become original twin base64 maps or basename-only sprite labels with no writeFile using zip names. The one place a name becomes a fresh write and it is checked is BYAF greeting ids through resolveGreetingPath byaf prefix no dots no leading slash no backslash plus knownPaths membership with hostile-id tests. Two places that are not checked the same way are BYAF image row paths returned verbatim into pack entry keys and Risu charx asset filenames re-emitted unmodified. Residual risk is downstream tools unzipping re-exports not same-process zip-slip.

children.summary: fflate unzipSync returns each entry name exactly as stored in the ZIP directory. There is no dot-dot backslash or absolute-path filtering in unzipBounded or fflate. A charx or byaf can legally contain ../../../evil.json and unzipBounded returns it under that literal key if size and count budgets pass.

children.text: Ingestion never turns a name into a filesystem write
children.summary: Nothing in core archive Risu or backyard joins an entry name onto a real OS path and writes it. Names are keys into in-memory Records base64-encoded onto original twin assetFiles or BYAF files map or reduced to basename for sprite-pack image checks so a ../ prefix is inert. No Bun.write writeFileSync or fs.writeFile in src takes a zip entry name as target path. Classic zip-slip has no extract-to-disk code path today.

children.text: The one place a name becomes a fresh write, and it is checked
children.summary: Export can write a new file into a re-packed byaf. Alternate greeting ids can name archive-internal scenario paths. resolveGreetingPath is the only function allowed to turn an id into a path: requires byaf prefix non-empty remainder no .. no leading slash no backslash and membership in knownPaths from the twin. Hostile ids cannot mint new paths; freshScenarioPath never derives from user input. Test hostile greeting id is never used as an archive path feeds ../../../evil.json cases and asserts clean scenarios/ outputs.

children.text: Two places that are not checked the same way
children.summary: Two spots carry untrusted archive names into freshly-built output entry tables without resolveGreetingPath or hostile tests. BYAF pathForLabel returns existing image row path verbatim into arc.files then packByaf zips keys unmodified; only fallback filenames are sanitized. Risu charx assetFiles import path is written back unmodified then zipSync. Neither becomes a real filesystem write here; residual risk is a less careful downstream tool unzipping the re-export. Call it verified unguarded and untested not safe by design.

anchors.summary: Proven and enforced: pre-inflate archive-size selected-entry size total-entry count and selected aggregate caps in unzipBounded exercised by archive.test.ts; fail-closed wrapping of unzip errors into ArchiveLimitError; only-mode selection plus total-entry cap for cheap detection on hostile archives; and resolveGreetingPath traversal-and-known-path gate on the one BYAF export write path with a hostile-id test. Not yet proven: post-inflate size backstop has no test fabricating understated originalSize; BYAF image-row path and Risu charx asset filename carry no traversal check before export entry names and no hostile tests. Do not describe archive handling as fully sandboxed against a hostile archive or as path traversal solved in general; it is solved and tested for one specific write path.

docs.title: Security threat model and defense layers
docs.summary: The assets hoplight protects, the untrusted inputs it faces, and each defense layer with its honest tested or scaffolded status.
docs.semanticSummary: Developer threat model for a local content forge that protects provider credentials, remote join secrets and approvals, filesystem state, trusted UI authority, and machine availability from hostile files and explicitly approved remote clients. The layers document canonical parse-not-execute conversion with semantic Round-Trip guarantees, bounded archives, pre-compile ReDoS rejection plus runtime budgets, sanitized rendering and CSP, capability-starved Lua with worker termination and value-only messages, a three-asset sandbox origin whose packaged proof is blocked, the primary loopback API plus separately gated remote listeners, and Kit's encrypted BYOK vault. Honest gaps include packaged-host sandbox measurement, malformed-vault recovery, the absent non-Windows passphrase flow, and provider redirects that are not revalidated after the initial host check. Each layer names its enforcement and test boundary so scaffolded behavior is not presented as packaged proof.

anchors.summary: Protected assets are provider credentials and connection secrets, remote join secrets and device approvals, host-only controls, the local filesystem and user-owned studio folder, the trusted UI origin and per-launch bearer, and machine availability. The adversary includes untrusted imported content and, when Remote access is explicitly enabled, approved remote clients and the remote listener. The primary server remains a loopback forge. Trust ends at every file and request, so input is parsed once, capabilities are absent unless deliberately supplied, and gates fail closed. Named soft edges at this boundary are unmeasured packaged-host origin separation plus Kit vault recovery and non-Windows setup; provider redirect limits remain documented with the provider egress layer.

The layers combine structural prevention with bounded execution and explicitly scoped evidence. 1. Parse, not execute keeps private payloads opaque and conversion canonical. 2. Decompression caps on archives bound selection and inflation. 3. ReDoS-guarded regex rejects dangerous AST shapes before native execution. 4. Sanitized rendering applies DOMPurify, pure policy, and CSP. 5. The Lua sandbox and its resource budgets remove host capabilities, cap state, and kill workers. 6. Distinct-origin sandbox isolation adds a second HTTP-tested listener whose packaged proof remains blocked. 7. The token-gated primary local server and separately enabled remote listeners protect API authority with request gates, join secrets, device approval, and host-only controls. The tunnel also carries the only path that turns a download into an executable, host-only and verified against a committed SHA-256 before the bytes reach disk. 8. The BYOK provider vault encrypts configurations while documenting passphrase, redirect, and recovery limits.

children.summary: Every format enters and leaves through the canonical superset rather than converting directly to another platform. Source-specific scripts, extension blocks, and layout remain opaque escrow data. Cross-format exports carry only canonical content, preventing one application's executable payload from being copied into another, while typed adapter contracts prevent cross-kind writers. The engine and server do not evaluate imported scripts; the user-invoked Lua Test Bench is the sole execution exception. Same-format Round-Trip requires semantic preservation unless a format specification explicitly declares and fixtures prove a byte-level tier.

unzipBounded handles untrusted charx, byaf, Lumiverse, and sprite archives with checks before and after inflation. It limits total entries, selected compressed and declared sizes, per-entry output, and aggregate output; missing originalSize remains bounded by compressed size and actual post-inflate length. Card containers allow 96 MiB archives, 512 entries, 64 MiB per selected entry, and 96 MiB selected total, while packs use tighter 48 MiB and 256-entry ceilings. Violations throw ArchiveLimitError and required entries are never silently omitted.

Because one synchronous native RegExp call cannot be interrupted, validateRule is the primary defense: it rejects excessive complexity and dangerous structures such as nested unbounded quantifiers, star-overlapping alternation, and quantified backreferences before compilation. Runtime execution adds per-rule and set budgets plus a 1,000-match ceiling, but its timeout observes only between native calls and cannot rescue a pathological match already running. The editor's structural ReDoS lens is advisory rather than authoritative. Validation, application, and AST warning behavior have separate suites.

Stored markup passes through marked and then DOMPurify as the final transformation before innerHTML. Active, form, embedding, style, media-fetching, and script tags are forbidden; data attributes and surviving fetch attributes are removed, and links receive scheme, target, and rel hardening. A DOM-free policy independently enforces a 200k input limit, http/https/mailto links, constrained inline-style properties, and rejection of url, var, import, and expression indirection. Sealed previews and portrait responses add restrictive CSP, sandbox, and nosniff headers. Pure policy and DOM rendering tests cover separate halves.

children.text: 5. The Lua sandbox and its resource budgets
children.summary: Lua executes only when the user invokes the Risu Test Bench. Wasmoon opens a deliberately small pure-library set, excludes io, os, debug, and package, then removes loaders and host-reaching globals. Typed ceilings cover wall time, heap, source, wire data, and host state; release maxima include five seconds, 64 MiB heap, and 2 MiB source and state budgets, and callers cannot raise them. Each run occurs in a Worker that is terminated at deadline. Its versioned value-only protocol accepts plain data, rejects functions, exotic prototypes, forbidden keys, and secret-shaped fields, and never receives the API bearer.

ADR-009 places sandbox assets on a second ephemeral loopback listener that serves only the Lua worker, regex worker, and glue.wasm, with no API, index, studio paths, or session token. This adds an origin boundary beyond a killable same-origin Worker. Bun tests prove the HTTP allowlist, CORS, protocol rejection, and token absence, but do not measure how packaged WebView2 treats the two authorities, storage, crossOriginIsolated, or credentialed API access. Plan 017 therefore remains blocked for full proof. Bind failure falls back to a degraded same-origin worker and must not be called isolated.

children.text: 7. Token-gated local server and opt-in remote access
children.summary: The primary Studio listener binds 127.0.0.1 and creates a random per-launch bearer. API requests receive Host validation against DNS rebinding; mutations require an allowed Origin and constant-time token comparison, while GET and HEAD use Sec-Fetch-Site cross-site refusal because browser subresource reads cannot attach the bearer. Missing mutation Origin fails closed. Streaming readers cap inspect bodies at 64 MiB and JSON at 32 MiB with 413 on overflow. Remote tunnel and LAN modes are separate, explicitly enabled boundaries with join secrets, device approval, and host-only control routes documented in the remote-access threat model.

Kit encrypts the complete provider configuration list, credentials included, into one vault file and holds plaintext only after opening it in process. Saves seal a private temporary file and atomically replace the previous document. Windows uses DPAPI. A portable passphrase backend exists and sealed blobs retain backend identity, but current settings do not collect or supply the passphrase, leaving non-Windows first-run setup incomplete. Provider egress normalizes the endpoint and validates the initial request host, but runtime redirects are not revalidated. Credentials stay out of messages, tools, content, exports, transcripts, and privacy receipts. Malformed outer-file recovery is also incomplete, and Kit remains source-preview only.
