anchors.summary: The generated status figure condenses the preceding defense layers into a scan of what is enforced, what has automated code-layer evidence, what remains scaffolded, and what is blocked on packaged-host measurement. It is a navigation aid rather than a substitute for each layer's caveats and source references.

anchors.text: What this document does not claim
anchors.summary: The document does not call the Lua environment fully isolated because its second-origin behavior is proven at the Bun HTTP layer, not inside packaged WebView2. It does not claim exploitation is impossible; controls reduce blast radius as defense in depth. Regex time budgets cannot interrupt one catastrophic native call, so structural rejection remains essential. Kit's vault lacks complete malformed-envelope recovery and a settings-driven portable passphrase flow, Kit is absent from current release binaries, and provider redirects are not revalidated after the initial host check. A same-origin sandbox fallback is explicitly degraded and receives no isolation claim.

docs.title: ReDoS defense in the regex engine
docs.summary: Vaud parses every card-authored find pattern into an AST, screens it for catastrophic-backtracking shapes before it is ever compiled, refuses the dangerous ones with an exact culprit span, and surfaces the rejection reason as plain text in two places, with the coverage gaps in that screen documented here.
docs.semanticSummary: Canonical reference for ReDoS defense when untrusted card-authored find patterns enter the regex engine. JavaScript RegExp is synchronous and uninterruptible on its thread, so Hoplight uses two layers: structural AST screening before compile, and Studio previews in a disposable worker terminated at a 750 ms wall clock. The AST layer never executes anything: parseRegex builds a typed tree under unicode-mode grammar, returns errors as values not throws, and never constructs RegExp. The screen walks unbounded quantifiers for three structural culprits with exact culprit spans: nested unbounded quantifiers, overlapping alternation under a quantifier, and backreference inside unbounded repetition; severity is safe, suspicious, or dangerous, precision over recall. The gate validateRule length-caps find and replace at 10000, rejects empty find, native-compiles under the rule flags, then analyzes: dangerous refuses and never compiles; suspicious still ok with complexity floored toward the heavy-pattern chip. Enforced on every run not just at save: applyRule validates every enabled rule before compile; rejected rules leave text unchanged. User rejection surfaces show plain-text RuleValidation.error only; culprit span is computed but not rendered. Guided mode hit miss chips are a separate feature, not a rejection report, and their preview compile skips the gate while stored rules still hit applyRule. Known gaps: core timeout is not preemptive; fallback heuristic when AST parse fails is weaker; v-flag set notation likely falls through; character-set overlap is coarse; culprit underline unwired. Source of truth maps each concern to files under core/regex, sandbox regex worker, and workbench UI.

anchors.text: The AST layer never executes anything
anchors.summary: parser.ts is a clean-room ECMAScript parser parseRegex that turns a pattern string into a typed node tree under the unicode-mode u-flag grammar regardless of the rule flags string. It never throws: syntax failure returns { error, at } as a value. ast-types states the tree is DATA describing a pattern, never executable; compilation and matching stay in apply.ts. No AST-layer file including the ReDoS analyzer ever constructs or runs a RegExp. A narrow Annex-B-only legacy class is out of scope by design and returns an honest parse error instead of a silently different parse: lone open brace, bare close bracket, \p as literal p, octal \8, or quantified lookaround. The v-flag set-notation grammar nested class operators -- and && is staged and unimplemented: parseClass has no branch for them and V_MODE_ENABLED is false. ReDoS implications of that staging appear under Known gaps.

redos.ts walks every unbounded quantifier max null in the parsed tree and checks three shapes, each producing a finding with exact RedosFinding.culpritSpan. Nested unbounded quantifier via hasAmbiguousInnerLoop catches (a+)+ and (.+)+ while (a+b)+ with a mandatory separator is safe. Overlapping alternation under a quantifier via alternationOverlap catches (a|a)+ and prefix ambiguity (a|ab)+; disjoint (a|b)+ is safe. Backreference inside unbounded repetition via containsBackreference catches (a)\1+ while unquantified (a)\1 is fine. Severity is safe, suspicious, or dangerous: literal prefix or equality ambiguity is dangerous; coarse first-set overlap on complex alternatives like (\d|\w)+ is only suspicious; nested quantifier and quantified backreference findings are always dangerous. Detector is precision over recall: false positives cry wolf while misses fall through to existing guards. Character-set membership is a coarse sample-based approximation; dot and Unicode-property atoms are wide true and can only push toward suspicious or dangerous. Mandatory disjoint separators are proven safe via nullability and first-set reasoning over the AST.

validate.ts turns analyzeRedos into refusal. Order: length caps reject find over MAX_PATTERN_LENGTH 10000 or replace over MAX_REPLACEMENT_LENGTH 10000 first; empty or whitespace-only find rejects; native new RegExp under jsFlagsForRule with the same flags apply.ts will use; then parseRegex without flags because flags do not change ReDoS shape. When the pattern parses the AST branch is authoritative: severity dangerous returns ok false with nested quantifiers catastrophic backtracking error, complexity COMPLEXITY_HARD_CAP, and culprit span, and the pattern is never compiled for real; numeric complexity is display only here not re-thresholded. Severity suspicious still ok true but complexity floored at COMPLEXITY_HARD_CAP minus 10 (40) to clear inspect SLOW_COMPLEXITY 20 so it runs with a heavy-pattern nudge not a block. Culprit attaches whenever analyzeRedos found something even on ok true; safe leaves culprit unset. When parse fails Annex-B-legacy-only, fallback estimateComplexity uses NESTED_QUANTIFIER regex plus flat costs; only on this path complexity >= COMPLEXITY_HARD_CAP 50 is itself rejection. Verbatim error strings cover length empty replacement invalid native and nested quantifiers.

anchors.text: Enforced on every run, not just at save
anchors.summary: applyRule calls validateRule unconditionally for every enabled rule on every engine pass after cheap skip-reason checks and before real compilation. There is no save-time-only path: the same gate runs from live Quick Try preview, test bench, and real content passes regardless of Guided, Plain-words, or raw Pattern authorship. Rejection yields applied false with the validation error string and leaves text unchanged. Accepted patterns still budget: compile with d flag for match spans; runReplace checks elapsed against timeoutMs default 100ms capped 500ms before and between matches. That budget is between-steps not preemptive; the synchronous match or matchAll call cannot be stopped once started. Studio callers add a preemptive outer boundary: run-in-worker posts to sandbox regex-worker.js and terminates the worker on timeout cancellation completion or error. The sandbox worker caps requests at 200000 text characters and 500 well-shaped rules before applyRules. A core caller that invokes applyRules directly does not receive this outer boundary.

anchors.text: What the user actually sees when a pattern is rejected
anchors.summary: Two UI surfaces read RuleValidation.error as plain text; neither currently renders the culprit span. The per-rule Health card in rule-rail calls validateRule and when not ok shows health.error or Check this pattern, the exact refusal string while editing. The whole-set linter in inspect calls validateRule on every enabled rule and on failure pushes a broken-pattern finding whose message embeds v.error; broken rules are excluded from duplicate and shadowing checks for that pass. redos describes itself as underline source for QOL row 22 editor highlights culpritSpan, and RuleValidation.culprit is populated on the dangerous path with tests; the suspicious path shares culprit attach by code inspection not test. As of this reading no file under src/ui reads .culprit; only the two plain-text surfaces consume validateRule in the UI. Exact-span underline is computed and tested but not yet wired to a rendered highlight.

anchors.text: Guided mode's hit/miss chips are a separate feature, not a rejection report
anchors.summary: guided-feedback.ts is easy to mistake for a second rejection surface because it touches user examples and a compiled RegExp; it is not. guidedMiss builds the Guided quiz it will catch preview from author examples and the pattern buildFromExamples derived, substituting one unseen word struck only if the compiled pattern truly rejects it. It never reports validation failure and has no severity or culprit. It skips the ReDoS gate: compile builds new RegExp without validateRule or analyzeRedos and swallows failure as null. Safety is read-only String.test never eval, not the ReDoS screen. The preview pattern comes from buildFromExamples not raw author regex; this page claims nothing about that builder. Not an execution bypass: when the guided wizard writes find and flags, the stored pattern hits the same validateRule-before-compile gate on every applyRules pass. The gap is only the wizard preview compile on every keystroke, ahead of the downstream gate.

Honesty posture from validate and redos. Core timeout is not preemptive: an AST false negative under precision-over-recall can hang inside one synchronous RegExp match or matchAll; timeoutMs is checked only between steps. Studio terminates the disposable worker; direct core callers must supply their own terminable boundary for untrusted patterns. Fallback heuristic when AST parse refuses is materially weaker: classic nested-quantifier text only, no overlapping-alternation or quantified-backreference bombs, which AST catches only when the strict grammar parses. v-flag set notation likely hits that weaker path because validate never passes real flags into parseRegex and parseClass lacks set operators; grammar read not a measured live pattern. Character-set overlap is coarse not full algebra, only pushes toward suspicious or dangerous, heuristic not proof. Culprit underline is not rendered; do not assume exact span beyond the plain-text error. Patterns that reach the core gate are analyzed before compile; AST-dangerous never runs. Remaining gaps: direct core, fallback syntax, v-flag, culprit UI.

Maps each concern to its authority file. ECMAScript AST parser that never executes is parser.ts; node shapes and spans are ast-types.ts; structural ReDoS analysis culprit spans and severity are redos.ts; the gate validateRule length caps complexity and fallback heuristic is validate.ts; flags derivation shared between gate and runtime is dialect.ts; runtime validate-before-compile and per-rule timeout match-count budget is apply.ts; Studio worker shell wall-clock termination is run-in-worker.ts; value-only regex execution worker and request caps are sandbox regex worker.ts; whole-set linter broken-pattern and slow-pattern findings are inspect.ts; per-rule Health card plain-text rejection is rule-rail.tsx; guided hit miss chips are guided-feedback.ts and mode-guided.tsx; fixtures for every severity tier and exact culprit span are redos.test.ts and validate.test.ts.

docs.title: Remote access: Tailscale and LAN
docs.summary: How hoplight lets you reach the studio from another device over a private Tailscale link or the local network, and the gates that keep everyone else out. Two listeners (trusted loopback, untrusted sidecar-fed), an owner-only Tailscale gate, and a connect-code + per-device-approval LAN gate. Off by default; driven entirely from Settings, never a terminal.
docs.semanticSummary: Canonical security reference for reaching the studio from another device without exposing it to the open internet. Remote access is off by default, driven only from Settings greater than Remote access never a terminal, with two independent modes: Tailscale private encrypted tailnet link and LAN connect-code plus per-device approval on the local network. Containers and SSH forwarding use the printed startup receipt with Studio port and optional sandbox port; browsing the server IP is refused by the trusted Host gate; one-port is enough for ordinary Studio work but both ports are required for Lua and regex benches; this guidance does not broaden hostAllowed or weaken token Origin checks. Two listeners one trust boundary: trusted 127.0.0.1 default 8321 with Host Origin and per-launch session token; untrusted 127.0.0.1:8788 only for the Tailscale sidecar with per-boot shared secret required on untrusted and refused on trusted. Tailscale owner gate admits only the studio owner's numeric user id fail closed. LAN gate uses CSPRNG connect code argon2id hashed never sent, per-IP throttle, pending approval with caps and 15 minute TTL, self-signed TLS; session cookie is HttpOnly SameSite Lax without Secure. Host-only surface blocks remote management, open, shutdown, restart, and settings writes. Owner can kick devices. The sidecar is not bundled: three locations are checked, and none reports the unavailable phase rather than a dead Enable control. The aux package fetches it from a release asset, verified against a baked SHA-256 pin before any bytes land. Sidecar lifecycle exits on parent death and kills orphans. What is proven lists unit tests and live end-to-end verification.

anchors.summary: Container or headless use does not need a browser inside that environment. The hoplight ui startup receipt prints the local Studio URL, one copyable SSH command for the Studio port, and when the isolated Lua regex listener started a second forward for its random sandbox port. Run it on the browser machine, replace user@server, keep the tunnel open, browse localhost with the printed ui-port. Browsing the server or container IP is refused by the trusted Host gate. HTML may arrive before api/settings is refused, so the browser turns that 403 into localhost and SSH instructions with Studio, Settings Remote access deep link, and one-port recovery copy buttons; host-only API gates still decide whether controls may change anything. One-port is enough for ordinary Studio work; Lua and regex benches need both ports because ADR-009 uses a second ephemeral loopback origin. Tailscale and LAN serve the approved Studio surface only and do not make the sandbox listener a general remote endpoint. This does not broaden hostAllowed, expose a new listener, or weaken token and Origin checks.

The app binds two loopback listeners in server-remote and server. Trusted 127.0.0.1 port default 8321 is the local owner's browser, gated by loopback Host Origin check plus a per-launch session token on state-changing requests via checkApiRequest in server-security. Untrusted 127.0.0.1:8788 is the ONLY thing the Tailscale sidecar reverse-proxies already-owner-gated remote traffic to; gated by a per-boot shared secret the sidecar stamps on every forwarded request checkRemoteApiRequest plus the session token on writes. The shared secret is a CSPRNG value generated once per launch in setupRemoteAccess, passed to the sidecar via environment variable never argv because argv is world-readable in the process table. The untrusted listener REQUIRES the secret so a local process or DNS-rebinding page without it fails closed. The trusted listener REFUSES the secret on any path before routing: a request carrying the sidecar secret is by definition sidecar-proxied remote traffic and has no business at the local door in createHandler.

The sidecar embeds Tailscale via tsnet and for every remote request calls WhoIs on the caller tailnet address, admitting only the studio owner's own account. Identity is compared by numeric user id who.UserProfile.ID equals Self.UserID via resolveOwnerID and newProxy; login-name strings are not used because tsnet can return an empty login for the owner node while the numeric id is populated. Fail closed everywhere: unresolved owner id zero denies everyone; unidentifiable caller with no WhoIs is denied; a caller whose node has no stable id is denied because a device that cannot be tracked or kicked will not be served. Identity headers forwarded upstream X-Tailscale-User and X-Tailscale-Node are taken from WhoIs never from client-supplied headers so a forged header cannot survive. These properties are unit-tested against a fake resolver in sidecar main_test.go.

anchors.text: The LAN gate: connect code + per-device approval
anchors.summary: Without tailnet identity, LAN gates on two stranger-proof checks in lan-host. Connect code the owner reads off screen is CSPRNG with rejection sampling, argon2id-hashed via Bun.password, and never sent to the connecting device. Wrong guesses throttle per IP with exponential backoff never a global lockout. Right code makes a pending session served nothing until host approval; pending is capped per IP and expires after 15 minutes so the code alone cannot flood approvals or leave stale entries. Listener binds 0.0.0.0:8790 with self-signed TLS in lan-server so code and traffic never cross clear; cert puts LAN IP and loopback in subjectAltName, regenerates if cache misses current IP, private key chmod 600 best effort with Windows ACLs; owner verifies shown sha256 fingerprint. Nested why the session cookie is not Secure: approved cookie is HttpOnly SameSite Lax Path slash without Secure because self-signed is not a secure context in some browsers that silently drop Secure cookies.

children.text: Why the session cookie is not `Secure`
children.summary: The approved-session cookie is HttpOnly SameSite Lax Path slash with no Secure attribute in lan-server. The listener is HTTPS-only, but a self-signed cert is not a secure context in some browsers, which then silently DROP a Secure cookie and leave the device stuck re-entering the code forever. SameSite Lax lets the cookie ride the reload navigation; HttpOnly still stands.

anchors.summary: Whether a device tailed in over Tailscale or was approved on the LAN, it may USE the studio but must never reach management or host control. isHostOnlyRoute in server-remote refuses for any remote or LAN-served handler every api/remote route that turns access on or off or kicks devices, api/open that opens a browser on the host, api/shutdown, api/restart, and settings writes. Those belong to the local owner alone.

The owner can remove any connected device from the host. Over Tailscale the app writes a kick command to the sidecar stdin; the sidecar blocklists that node stable id and denies it on the next request even though it is the owner own account via deviceTracker in main.go. On LAN the session is dropped.

anchors.text: Where the sidecar binary comes from
anchors.summary: The sidecar is compiled Go and is not inside Hoplight.exe. sidecarCandidates in server-remote checks three locations in order: the repository sidecar folder that bun sidecar/build.ts writes, a sidecar folder beside the running executable, and the aux-package cache where a requested download installs it. None present reports unavailable, its own RemotePhase distinct from off and error, because off is a switch the owner can flip and error invites a retry while a build with no helper can do neither; the panel says so up front and offers no Enable control instead of spawning a path that is not there. LAN mode needs no helper. The beside-the-executable candidate is load-bearing: deriving the path from import.meta.url alone is correct from source and meaningless once compiled, resolving onto the Bun virtual filesystem, so every packaged studio failed to start remote access and surfaced a raw uv_spawn ENOENT. Pinned by server-remote.test.ts.

anchors.text: The aux package: fetching the helper on request
anchors.summary: The helper is about 31 MB, so it ships as a release asset the owner fetches with an explicit click. A SHA-256 pin is the integrity control and it is committed in sidecar-pins.ts, pinned like a dependency: scripts/pin-sidecar.ts reads a release's published SHA256SUMS, re-downloads each asset to confirm it matches, and rewrites the module for review. Computing it during the build was the earlier design and it split the product in two, because only a CI-built binary carried a hash, so the download worked for packaged users and silently did not from source. Committing it works because the helper is not tied to an app version: the coupling is to the stdio protocol, not the version number, which is also why there is no staleness signal. Verification runs on bytes in memory before anything reaches the path the spawner reads, and the install renames from a sibling staging file, so no tampered or torn download leaves a runnable binary. HTTPS only with every hop inspected, the size cap applies while reading, and the routes are host-only.

The sidecar is a background process that speaks only over stdio pipes: status events out, kick commands in. It watches stdin; when the parent app dies stdin hits EOF and the sidecar exits so a crashed app never leaves an orphan carrying a stale secret. On startup the manager also sweeps any orphan from a prior run before spawning a fresh one via killOrphans in sidecar-manager. The binary is built as a Windows GUI-subsystem executable with bun sidecar/build.ts -H=windowsgui so spawning from the window-less packaged app never pops a console; parent-provided pipes still work as handles independent of any console. Spawns also pass windowsHide as a second layer.

The Tailscale owner gate and its fail-closed cases are unit-tested in sidecar main_test.go. The LAN code format, per-IP throttle, pending cap, and TTL are unit-tested in lan-host.test.ts. The trusted-port secret refusal and the host-only route block are tested at the handler in server-remote.test.ts, including that a guest cannot trigger a helper download. The three binary locations, the unavailable phase, and the refusal to persist an on that cannot happen are unit-tested there and in sidecar-manager.test.ts, with the packaged path resolution confirmed against a real compiled executable. Every aux-download refusal is unit-tested in aux-download.test.ts: pin mismatch, truncation, a non-GitHub or plain-http hop, a lookalike host, redirect loops, and a body exceeding the cap while streaming. The checksum reader that writes the committed pins is unit-tested in sidecar-pin-format.test.ts. That the release builds and uploads a helper for every pinned platform, and that every committed pin names an asset the release publishes, is pinned by ci-sidecar.test.ts, covering workflow shape only; the Go cross-builds succeeding is proven by a real release run. The LAN and Tailscale paths have been verified live end-to-end.

docs.title: Safe rendering: sanitizing card HTML and CSS
docs.summary: Specifies exactly what DOMPurify allows and strips on the two surfaces that render card-authored HTML and CSS, the sealed iframe and scoped CSP the riskier surface adds on top, and what is proven only at the string level versus what is not measured at all.
docs.semanticSummary: Sanitizer spec of record for card-authored HTML and CSS: complete allow and forbid lists for both places the app turns untrusted markup into DOM. Concepts safe-rendering covers prose UX RenderBox and leaving-gate; this page covers the higher-risk Risu behavior.backgroundHTML and backgroundCSS surface and what is proven only at string level. Where card HTML and CSS enter the app: CharacterBehavior carries them verbatim, Risu maps unchanged, flagged hasExecutableContent until a behavior entity exists; regex replace HTML also reaches only the sealed preview; ordinary prose uses renderMarkup and dangerouslySetInnerHTML without iframe. Two rendering surfaces two boundaries: prose sanitizes with DOMPurify into the document relying on ambient CSP and a strict forbid list; backdrop preview uses narrower DOMPurify then a srcDoc iframe with scoped CSP as the load-bearing egress barrier; both run DOMPurify last and cap input. What DOMPurify allows and strips: ALLOW_DATA_ATTR false, script forbidden, prose forbids media and style form controls; backdrop keeps style and img and leans on CSP; afterSanitizeAttributes on prose only strips fetch attrs, isSafeHref, pins noopener, narrows styles. CSS sanitizeBackdropCss is defense in depth not a parser; Workshop CSS sanitizer is separate and more permissive. Iframe sandbox empty is most restrictive without allow-same-origin; scoped CSP default-src none; ambient app CSP covers prose. What is tested and what is not: jsdom string and HTTP header assertions only; no packaged WebView2 claim of full isolation.

anchors.text: Where card HTML and CSS enter the app
anchors.summary: CharacterBehavior carries optional verbatim backgroundHTML and backgroundCSS. The Risu field mapper reads and writes them unchanged with no transform either way. The module header calls this the executable behavior surface, not original-forever, carried on the raw twin and flagged at import via hasExecutableContent until a dedicated behavior entity models it. Nothing in the canonical model parses or interprets this HTML and CSS; it rides as data until a render call touches it. Regex replace effects can produce HTML strings; that output is never rendered inline and reaches the screen only through the same sealed preview. Ordinary prose fields description greeting creator notes are lower risk: markdown or HTML tagged by RenderFormat, rendered through renderMarkup with dangerouslySetInnerHTML, and no iframe between that output and app chrome.

Prose fields via render-markup and RenderBox sanitize with DOMPurify and inject into the current document with no iframe; isolation is only the app shell ambient CSP, so the forbid list must block auto-fetch elements outright. The backdrop preview sealed-html-preview wired from workshop code-pane for backgroundHTML and backgroundCSS sanitizes with a narrower DOMPurify config then loads into a srcDoc iframe carrying its own scoped CSP. The component header states sanitizing is not isolation; the iframe plus CSP are the load-bearing egress barrier. Both surfaces run DOMPurify last after any markdown-to-HTML conversion and both cap input before parsing: RENDER_INPUT_CAP 200000 characters, BACKDROP_HTML_CAP 200000, BACKDROP_CSS_CAP 100000.

Both configs set ALLOW_DATA_ATTR false and add back only target on anchors. DOMPurify default empties script content and strips handlers and javascript or vbscript URIs; both also explicitly forbid script. Baseline is tested: script, onerror, SVG onload, javascript href, and a mutation-XSS payload come out clean. Prose forbid list removes style script iframe object embed form controls link meta base and all auto-fetch media including SVG image because there is no CSP of its own for network egress; verified remote media stripped. Backdrop forbid list drops script iframe object embed form controls link meta base frame frameset but not style or img; scoped CSP img-src data blob and connect-src none carry network egress. Prose afterSanitizeAttributes registered lazily strips FETCH_ATTRS, drops unsafe href unless isSafeHref http https mailto or relative then pins target blank rel noopener noreferrer, and narrows style to six props rejecting url image-set import expression behavior moz-binding var. buildBackdropSrcDoc does not install that hook; its guarantees come from own FORBID_TAGS CSS sanitizer and iframe CSP never from hook order which is untested.

anchors.text: CSS: `sanitizeBackdropCss` is defense in depth, not a parser
anchors.summary: behavior.backgroundCSS as the css prop distinct from style tags inside backgroundHTML goes through sanitizeBackdropCss. Header states defense in depth only: sealed-preview CSP is the load-bearing egress barrier; this helper must not claim to be a complete CSS parser. Regex passes in order: neutralize close-style breakout, blank residual markup, strip import and font-face blocks, neutralize expression behavior and moz-binding, rewrite non-data url to about:blank, wipe bare http https substrings outside url. All verified at string-output level including four varied close-style breakout payloads. CSS Workshop uses separate sanitizeWorkshopCss not a reuse; it overlaps on import font-face expression behavior moz-binding and non-data url rewrite but omits CLOSE_STYLE neutralization and bare http https strip. Workshop CSP is more permissive img-src data blob https http versus backdrop data blob only. Workshop sanitizes CSS the user types against fixed mock HTML, a lower-stakes boundary not otherwise covered here.

anchors.text: The iframe sandbox and the scoped CSP
anchors.summary: Backdrop preview uses iframe sandbox empty srcDoc with referrerPolicy no-referrer. Empty sandbox is the most restrictive HTML form: scripts forms popups pointer lock and top navigation disabled; without allow-same-origin the frame has a unique opaque origin not the app origin. srcDoc carries meta Content-Security-Policy SEALED_PREVIEW_CSP: default-src none, images and media data and blob only, script-src none, connect-src none, frame-src none, object-src none, base-uri none, form-action none, style-src unsafe-inline so inline style can apply. Policy is asserted as a literal string; tests confirm generated document has no http https after close-style breakout attempts. Tests do not run a real browser or WebView2; jsdom has no CSP implementation. Surviving claim is generated markup has no literal remote reference and the CSP string is present and well-formed, not cannot exfiltrate. ADR-009 records the same class of gap for Lua sandbox: pack measure BLOCKED; by the same posture this page does not claim full isolation or full sandbox in packaged Windows, only what code enforces and what tests exercise.

anchors.text: The ambient app CSP covers the prose-field surface too
anchors.summary: Prose fields have no iframe but are not undefended past DOMPurify. Every HTML response including the shell carries a CSP from htmlSecurityHeaders: default-src self, script-src self plus exact sha256 hashes of served inline scripts computed from the HTML so hashes cannot rot, style-src self unsafe-inline, img-src self data blob, connect-src self, worker-src self blob plus sandbox origin when set, font-src self, frame-ancestors none, base-uri none, form-action none. server applies this to every served index HTML. No unsafe-inline on script-src means even a script past DOMPurify could not run from inline source; connect-src self means a surviving element could not fetch or beacon externally. Asserted against a real HTTP Response header in server.test proving the header is served correctly not that a browser enforces every directive. Prose DOMPurify media forbid is intentional defense in depth with img-src self data blob: either layer alone would stop a remote img; they fail differently by removing the node versus blocking the network request.

anchors.text: What is tested, and what is not
anchors.summary: Prose DOMPurify stripping scripts handlers active tags unsafe hrefs styles and fetch attrs is verified by render-markup.test on jsdom sanitized strings not a real browser or packaged WebView2. Ambient app CSP well-formed and served on every HTML response is verified by server.test real HTTP Response header not live browser enforcement. Backdrop DOMPurify plus CSS regex strip of active tags and known CSS breakout is verified by sealed-html-preview.test jsdom string assertions on srcDoc not CSP network enforcement. Backdrop iframe sandbox empty without allow-same-origin blocking scripts and granting opaque origin is standard HTML sandbox specification not packaged WebView2 measurement for this component; no measurement pass exists unlike the Lua-worker ADR-009 gap it mirrors. Do not read this page as absolute cards cannot smuggle active markup. Read it as two sanitizer passes, ambient CSP, and sandboxed iframe with second CSP each remove a tested payload class with intentional cross-layer cover, and no claim of confirmation against packaged Windows WebView2.

docs.title: The Lua script sandbox
docs.summary: How hoplight runs an untrusted card script in a terminable worker on a distinct loopback origin, behind a versioned value-only wire protocol and resource budgets that clamp downward only, with an honest account of what is enforced versus what is not yet measured.
docs.semanticSummary: How Hoplight runs untrusted card scripts only when the operator deliberately stages them on the Workshop Test Bench, never on import. Layered sandbox: terminable worker, distinct loopback origin, value-only versioned wire protocol, resource budgets that clamp downward only. Scripts are data until staged: classifier and import receipt save text and never auto-run. Worker isolation is the kill switch: per-run Worker with host terminate and in-VM functionTimeout; same-origin worker is availability not origin boundary; stale runId responses dropped. Distinct sandbox origin ADR-009 serves only worker and wasm glue, never api or session token; readSandboxOrigin requires http 127.0.0.1; same-origin fallback is degraded not claimed isolated; origin code is defense-in-depth not evidence of a current exploit. Wire protocol version 1 is value-only with key allowlists and FORBIDDEN_KEYS including credentials and prototype keys; token never on the wire. Resource budgets RELEASE_LUA_LIMITS clamp never upward across host worker and engine; over-budget yields resource result without allocating attacker-sized state. Lua engine hardening deny by absence: openStandardLibs false, SAFE_LIBS only, STRIPPED_GLOBALS removed, no DOM fetch filesystem network. Privileged lowLevelAccess flag is a warning never an execution trigger. What is not yet proven: packaged WebView2 origin probe and related measures not run; do not claim full sandbox isolation until ADR-009 matrix is green; token and resource quotas are load-bearing proven layers.

anchors.text: Scripts are data until you stage them
anchors.summary: Card behavior rows are classified never executed. The classifier core splits a condition or effect row into a known or advanced shape and nothing more: nothing here executes anything; rows are data. The import receipt tells the operator the same: a card that carries scripts is flagged and the scripts are saved as text and will never run unless you put them on the test stage.

Each run happens in its own Worker and the real stop mechanism is termination. runLuaSandboxed is documented never hang never throw: it spawns a module worker, arms a host wall-clock timer, and on completion or deadline calls worker.terminate before resolving. If the deadline fires first the worker is terminated mid-run and the result is timeout. Timeout is enforced twice: inside the VM wasmoon functionTimeout aborts a pure-Lua infinite loop with LuaTimeoutError; outside the host timer terminates the whole worker thread regardless of what Lua is doing. Per ADR-009 a same-origin worker is an availability boundary killable thread not an origin boundary; the termination path holds independently of the origin question. Each run carries a monotonic run id; a response whose runId does not match the run in flight is dropped as stale or spoofed generation.

Worker bundle and wasm glue are served from a second loopback listener on an ephemeral port, a distinct origin from the UI and api paths. That sandbox-only server serves only GET sandbox worker.js, regex-worker.js, and glue.wasm and must not expose api, studio paths, index HTML carrying the session token, or source maps. Sandbox origin is published as meta vaude-sandbox-origin; per-launch API token stays only in meta vaude-session and trusted apiFetch. readSandboxOrigin accepts a value only when it starts with http://127.0.0.1. workerHref loads from that origin when present; when meta is absent it falls back to same-origin sandbox worker.js marked degraded not claimed isolated. Intent is blast-radius reduction if a future bug exposed web capabilities; defense-in-depth not evidence of a current same-origin exploit. Distinct-origin design is real and tested at Bun HTTP and handler layer but not yet measured in packaged WebView2; that gap is stated fully under what is not yet proven.

Only JSON-like values cross the worker boundary. Protocol is a versioned tagged union SANDBOX_PROTOCOL_VERSION 1; wrong version is rejected. Every message is runtime-validated both ways and fails closed on any schema violation via parseRunRequest and parseRunResponse. Three checks: value-only assertJsonLike allows null finite numbers strings booleans arrays and plain objects only and rejects functions symbols bigint undefined non-finite non-plain prototypes and nesting deeper than 32 so no functions DOM handles ports proxies object URLs or app objects ride across; key allowlists per message type via assertAllowlistKeys with state restricted to chatVars chat meta log; credential keys forbidden including token authorization cookie password secret vaude-session bearer and siblings plus assertNoForbiddenKeys against __proto__ constructor prototype. Before post the host runs messageContainsForbiddenKeys as a second pass and refuses to send. API token is never placed on a message and the protocol has no field that could carry it, enforced by construction and unit-tested per ADR-009.

RELEASE_LUA_LIMITS is the authoritative ceiling: wall-clock timeout 5000 ms, Lua heap 64 MiB via setMemoryMax, script source 2 MiB, request and response wire 4 MiB each, aggregate host state 2 MiB with per-field caps under it. Byte caps are UTF-8 via TextEncoder inclusive: exactly maxBytes accepted, maxBytes plus one rejected. Heap is VM-only so separate source wire and host-state caps exist for host JS. Budgets clamp downward only: resolveLuaRunLimits merges overrides under the release ceiling via clampInt so higher requests clamp to max and lower adversarial values pass; missing fields take release defaults. Clamp applies independently at three layers so a hostile postMessage cannot raise a ceiling: host before send, worker re-resolve documented re-clamped, engine again when built. Worker runs Lua on the same authoritative deadline as the host kill switch with no 120s leash above release max. Enforcement at edges: source host-state and request wire asserted before post, re-asserted in worker, response wire before parent accept. Over-budget yields bounded resource result with machine reason and never allocates attacker-sized state first.

Lua VM is wasmoon PUC-Lua 5.4 built fresh per run and hardened by opening nothing by default. Created with openStandardLibs false and injectObjects false, then only pure side-effect-free SAFE_LIBS load: base table string math coroutine utf8. io os debug and package are never opened. After safe libs load, base globals that reach the host or load bytecode are deleted: load loadfile dofile loadstring require collectgarbage as STRIPPED_GLOBALS. Memory ceiling uses setMemoryMax with traceAllocations true. Host capabilities are the only things a card can reach, injected as named Lua globals; anything not injected does not exist deny-by-absence. On the Test Bench the injected surface is JSON helpers plus the Risu host API bound to the run state and budgets. There is no DOM fetch filesystem or network global; those were explicitly out of scope for the sandbox per ADR-009.

anchors.text: The privileged flag (a warning, not a trigger)
anchors.summary: A Risu card can request low-level script API lowLevelAccess. Hoplight surfaces that as a boolean and does nothing else with it. The canonical field is a warning marker for the UI and a sandbox gating input, never an execution trigger. The reader states scripts must never auto-run; the import receipt says deep access is not granted. Surfaced never honored: the flag grants no capability and starts no execution.

Mirrors the codebase STOP honesty posture; do not read anything above as a claim of full isolation. Proven and enforced: worker kill switch host terminate plus in-VM timeout, three-layer resource clamp and byte caps, value-only wire protocol both ways, absence of any token field on the wire, and sandbox-host handler allowlist worker and wasm only with api and traversal 404. ADR-009 records these as automated. Not yet measured per ADR-009 table: packaged WebView2 origin probe not run in this implementation pass; self.crossOriginIsolated and storage visibility not measured; credentialed API fetch from sandbox-origin worker in packaged host not measured. Because of those gaps, distinct-origin isolation is implemented and tested only at Bun HTTP and handler layer, and same-origin fallback is degraded not isolated. ADR-009 conclusion: packaged-host proof remains BLOCKED and do not claim full sandbox isolation until that matrix is green. Origin-isolation code ships as defense-in-depth scaffolding; token layer Plan 005 and resource quotas Plan 016 are the load-bearing proven layers and origin isolation is additive on top.

docs.title: Secrets, provider credentials, and local API authority
docs.summary: How Kit encrypts BYOK provider configurations, constrains provider egress, and how the Studio gates its local API with a per-launch bearer plus Host and Origin checks.
docs.semanticSummary: Three current authority boundaries with limitations stated beside them. Kit is a source-checkout BYOP preview, not a release artifact. Its implemented vault encrypts the complete provider list and active id in ~/.hoplight/kit-vault.json rather than splitting metadata and secrets. Windows uses CurrentUser DPAPI end to end; a portable scrypt plus AES-256-GCM passphrase backend is unit-proven but the settings flow does not yet collect or pass a passphrase on macOS or Linux. Environment-variable providers remain cross-platform and unpersisted. Vault writes use temp plus rename and best-effort mode 0600 but no fsync; valid sealed envelopes fail loudly on backend or authentication errors, while malformed outer JSON or an invalid envelope is currently treated as no vault; there is no recovery, export, backend migration, or rotation flow. Provider egress rejects unknown or unkeyed providers and initial request URLs outside the one fixed or configured host; redirects are runtime-managed rather than hop-validated. Credentials go only as provider authentication, while conversation and tool observations are the model payload; privacy receipts retain provider and token counts, not bodies or keys. The Studio server binds loopback, mints a per-launch bearer, checks Host on every API method, rejects cross-site reads, requires Origin plus token for POST and PATCH, and caps bodies. Ordinary assets are ungated, but the ungated index HTML also contains the bearer and relies on loopback reachability rather than bearer authentication for confidentiality. Its second sandbox listener allowlists worker assets and withholds the bearer; Bun HTTP behavior is proven, packaged WebView separation remains unmeasured, and same-origin fallback is degraded.

anchors.summary: Current Kit BYOP boundary, not the obsolete packages/ai design. Offline import edit inspect validate convert and deterministic analysis need no key. Provider-backed turns use a discovered built-in or OpenAI-compatible endpoint; unknown providers and keyed providers without keys fail before request. Kit runs from a source checkout with bun run kit. The private package exposes that entry, but current GitHub Releases contain Hoplight.exe and hoplight CLI binaries only. The implemented vault, its three platform backends including the local key file fallback that keeps non-Windows machines encrypted rather than blocked, host-locked egress, and explicit recovery gaps are shipping source-preview behavior.

children.summary: Saved providers live in ~/.hoplight/kit-vault.json or HOPLIGHT_HOME. Current code does not split public metadata from secret state: it encrypts the complete Vault object, including every ProviderConfig API key base URL headers options and label plus activeId. Disk holds only version backend and opaque payload; round-trip coverage proves neither key nor provider name appears in plaintext. The decrypted vault is cached in process memory. Writes seal a temporary sibling, attempt mode 0600, then rename over the vault, protecting the prior file from a partial write but without fsync of file or directory.

The registry prefers Windows DPAPI, then the local key file, then the master passphrase. Opening follows the backend tag on the blob and never silently falls back. DPAPI pipes base64 plaintext through hidden noninteractive PowerShell, binding recovery to the same Windows user. The local key file is the universal fallback where no OS-native backend runs: a generated 256-bit key in a versioned 104-byte blob with HMAC integrity and owner-only mode, encrypting the vault with AES-256-GCM. It is re-read per operation, never cached, so a file removed underneath a running Kit is noticed. It is deliberately weaker and labeled so, since its key sits beside the vault. macOS Keychain and Linux Secret Service are unimplemented. Passphrase reports unavailable, never auto-selected.
topics: weaker than DPAPI and labeled so

children.summary: All provider spokes receive guarded fetch. Built-in spokes fix a host; custom and local spokes derive one host from configured baseURL. Unknown providers, missing required keys, and request URLs outside that host fail before network; model discovery uses the same gate. Credentials necessarily travel to the configured endpoint as authentication but are not inserted in conversations tools transcripts canonical entities or exports. The model receives conversation plus tool and docs observations needed for the request. Privacy records provider and token counts only. The current gate validates the initial request URL but delegates redirects to runtime and does not revalidate each hop.

Valid sealed envelopes fail loudly on an unknown backend, DPAPI failure, wrong passphrase, or GCM authentication failure, and DPAPI binds the blob to the Windows user. There is no vault export, recovery key, backend migration, or credential rotation flow. One documented exception: a structurally invalid local key file already holds an unrecoverable key, so failing closed protects nothing while trapping the user. Kit sets the damaged file and the unopenable vault aside under dated names, writes a fresh key, and returns an empty vault with a notice naming both paths; neither is deleted. I/O failures may succeed on retry and are surfaced, not treated as damage. Tampered ciphertext under a healthy key still throws untouched.

anchors.summary: Shipping code with automated Bun tests. The default visual app binds 127.0.0.1 only, and uploaded scripts remain data. A random per-launch bearer is injected into index HTML for trusted apiFetch and never handed to the sandbox. The api gate runs before every api handler, checks Host on every method, refuses cross-site GET and HEAD, and requires Origin plus token for POST and PATCH. JavaScript wasm CSS and icons are non-secret ungated assets. Index HTML is also ungated but contains the bearer, so its confidentiality relies on loopback reachability; any client that reaches the listener can read it. Reads remain weaker than mutations. Body caps are 64MB inspect and 32MB JSON.

children.summary: A fresh bearer is minted once per launch as randomBytes(32).toString base64url in createSecurityContext marked never log or persist. injectSessionMeta puts it into served index HTML as an escaped meta name vaude-session which trusted apiFetch reads for API authentication. The token is never handed to the sandbox origin. The index document itself is not bearer-gated, so the default listener's loopback bind limits which machines can fetch it; any local client that reaches the listener can read the bearer.

Every api route runs through checkApiRequest before its handler. JavaScript wasm CSS and icons are non-secret and ungated. Index HTML is also ungated but is not non-secret: createHandler injects the bearer before serving it, so confidentiality relies on the default loopback bind and any client reaching the listener can read it. The api gate returns 503 before security context completion, checks Host on every method, and rejects attacker hostnames resolved to loopback. GET and HEAD carry no token but reject Sec-Fetch-Site cross-site. POST and PATCH require a loopback-equivalent non-null Origin and a timingSafeEqual token. Other methods return 405.

children.text: What the gate does not do
children.summary: Stated plainly because overclaiming would be a defect. localhost and ::1 on the correct port are accepted not rejected; only wrong port or foreign hostname fails closed. All three loopback spellings resolve to the same bound interface so rejecting localhost would paper-cut bookmarks while protecting nothing; the gate stops attacker hostnames not loopback aliases. GET and HEAD are not token-gated: a header-less client curl or older browser with no Sec-Fetch-Site passes the read gate. The read gate is deliberately weaker than the mutation gate. Reads that expose entity data rely on the loopback bind and cross-site refusal not on the bearer.

Request bodies stream with a hard byte cap and 413 on overflow: INSPECT_BODY_MAX 64MB JSON_BODY_MAX 32MB. readBodyCapped checks Content-Length early when present and enforces a running total as it reads so a lying or absent length header still cannot exceed the cap. Same fail-closed posture the upload adapters use against zip bombs.

anchors.text: The sandbox origin (shipping code, packaged proof BLOCKED)
anchors.summary: Untrusted Lua from the Risu Test Bench runs in a Worker from a second loopback listener on an ephemeral port, a distinct origin from UI and api. Defense-in-depth: same-origin Worker is a killable thread not an origin boundary so a future WebView or bundler bug would widen blast radius if same-origin. Fails closed by construction: serves only sandbox worker.js regex-worker.js and glue.wasm; every other path 404 with locked CSP; no api no index HTML no session token no traversal. CORS limited to exact UI origin plus loopback aliases so only trusted UI constructs the cross-origin module Worker. API token is never injected into anything this host serves. What is proven and what is not: allowlist CORS value-only wire API denial and token absence proven at Bun HTTP layer; packaged WebView2 isolation not measured; Plan 017 BLOCKED; do not claim fully isolated; same-origin fallback degraded not claimed isolated.

children.text: What is proven, and what is not
children.summary: Scaffolding additive to token Plan 005 and resource quotas Plan 016 not a replacement. Proven: allowlist CORS value-only wire API denial and token absence by Bun HTTP and handler tests. Not measured: packaged WebView2 origin isolation, whether WebView collapses two loopback authorities, crossOriginIsolated and storage separation, and credentialed API fetch from sandbox origin; Plan 017 BLOCKED until a WebView2 smoke matrix records those. Do not call the sandbox fully isolated sandboxed or exploit-proof. Until the matrix is green it is defense-in-depth with tested HTTP behavior and unmeasured in-WebView separation. Sandbox bind failure falls back to same-origin Worker explicitly degraded and not claimed isolated.

docs.title: Cards and files as untrusted input
docs.summary: Cards, PNGs, and zip containers are parsed once into the canonical model without ever executing a card-authored script, and a cross-format conversion carries only the portable body, so one app's scripts and payloads never reach another app's file.
docs.semanticSummary: Layer 1 of the threat model: cards lorebooks regex sets and zip containers charx byaf risum are author-controlled content the user opens never something Hoplight fetches. Guarantee: each file is read by exactly one tolerant parser into the canonical model; nothing on that path evaluates a script; cross-format conversion carries only the portable body so one app scripts never reach another app file. Boundary: this page covers getting content past the door import inspect convert export; deliberate run isolation lives on script-sandbox and running is never automatic. Parsed once into a known type: JSON PNG and zip readers are total functions returning null or empty on bad input never throw or eval; unzipBounded caps archives; risum decode returns null without executing. Two script surfaces neither runs on import: declarative triggers classified as data pure TS runDataTriggers only on Test Bench Run; real Lua opaque text only via runLuaSandboxed on explicit click; privileged lowLevelAccess is warning never trigger with deny-by-absence host. Escrow never blind-copies scripts across formats: only Risu adapter emits body.behavior and export honesty names drops; original twin never crosses. What this page does not claim: regex hang safety sandbox isolation completeness decompression tuning details. Source of truth maps concerns to files.

anchors.text: Parsed once, into a known type
anchors.summary: Every import reader is a total function over untrusted bytes: parse into a known shape or fail to a known empty value. None throw on bad input and none evaluate what they read. JSON readers readCardJson readJsonAny readJsonObject wrap JSON.parse in try catch and return null on non-parse or wrong shape; no eval or lenient parser. PNG extractCharacterJson only reads tEXt iTXt after the 8-byte signature; safeExtract catches corrupt chunks and returns empty array; ccv3 preferred over chara so V3 is never silently downgraded. Zip containers charx byaf risum go through unzipBounded checking compressed size per-entry size entry count and aggregate inflated size before and after inflation; card caps 96 MiB archive 512 entries 64 MiB per entry 96 MiB aggregate with ArchiveLimitError on breach not silent truncate. risum openRisumModule decodes into typed records with script bodies as plain strings and returns null on any decode failure never throwing; nothing executes script bodies; raw module bytes kept for lossless export so failed structural decode never loses the source file.

anchors.text: Two script surfaces, neither runs on import
anchors.summary: Two authored script kinds treated the same at the door: classified as data never evaluated until an operator explicitly stages one. Declarative trigger rows become TriggerScript arrays of event conditions effects; classifyCondition and classifyEffect only sort shapes; nothing executes. The only interpreter runDataTriggers is pure TypeScript comparisons calc arithmetic and setvar with no eval Function or wasmoon; impersonate and command effects are only console text lines. It runs only when the operator clicks Run on the Workshop Test Bench; import convert and export never call it. Real Lua virtualscript triggerlua and risum script bodies ride as opaque text or bytes; CharacterBehavior states converter editor NEVER executes any of this no eval require or DOM injection. Only explicit onRunPackage hands code to runLuaSandboxed; execution never on import never during conversion never without opening Test Bench and clicking Run. lowLevelAccess becomes privileged boolean warning marker never an execution trigger; receipt says deep access not granted; no sandbox file reads privileged and host bridge never implements network filesystem or app access deny-by-absence.

anchors.text: Escrow never blind-copies scripts across formats
anchors.summary: Every canonical entity keeps a lossless twin keyed by source format; cross-format conversion hands the target only the canonical body never that twin. Scripts use two mechanisms. Body carries scripts but only the RisuAI adapter emits them: applyRisuToBody lifts triggerscript virtualscript backgroundHTML CSS defaultVariables and lowLevelAccess onto body.behavior and convertFile hands that body to targets so scripts exist in memory; only risu-fields reads body.behavior while SillyTavern RoleCall Agnai Backyard BYAF Lumiverse Pygmalion never look so triggers virtual script backdrop and privileged flag are never written to their wire. Declared not accidental: only Risu coverage lists behavior with scripts ride as DATA never executed here. Export honesty buildExportHonesty names what will not travel for targets that omit behavior and drops packaged risum module contents; import receipt says scripts saved as text never run unless staged. The raw twin never crosses: original is keyed per source format and a target only reads its own key; on fresh cross-format that key is empty so source raw payload and risum bytes under original.risu never reach the output even if a future adapter read body.behavior.

anchors.text: What this page does not claim
anchors.summary: Regex execution safety: card-embedded regex is a plain find replace data row never compiled or applied on import; applying is a regex replace never an eval; whether a pattern can hang at runtime is a separate question covered by regex-safety. Sandbox isolation completeness: this page states execution requires explicit operator action and makes no claim about isolation once staged; origin separation is tested at Bun HTTP layer only; packaged WebView2 is not measured and ADR-009 acceptance is BLOCKED Plan 017; do not read this page as fully isolated or cannot be exploited; see script-sandbox. Decompression-bomb tuning: exact archive size caps and rationale live in archive.ts and security README; this page only relies on enforcement before card JSON is read out of a zip.

Maps each concern to its authority file. Tolerant JSON is card-io.ts; PNG chunks png.ts; bounded zip archive.ts; risum structural decode open-module and rpack module; trigger classification behavior.ts; TriggerScript CharacterBehavior privileged schema.ts; pure TypeScript trigger interpreter run-data-trigger.ts; Risu import hasExecutableContent isPrivileged module decode index.ts; scripts onto body risu-fields.ts; Risu behavior coverage coverage.ts; only canonical body crosses convert.ts; escrow envelope canonical.ts; export honesty honesty.ts; import receipt receipt.ts; Test Bench run wiring workshop view.tsx; deny-by-absence host bridge risu-api.ts.

docs.title: The visual app (hoplight ui)
docs.summary: uses. Optional remote listeners are separately enabled and gated. One engine, two shells - no format logic exists in the UI layer.
docs.semanticSummary: Complete contributor map of the primary loopback Studio, its separately gated remote listeners, and its source-preview terminal companion. Kit terminal shell covers composition, discovery, sessions, providers, documentation and capability tools, staged review, and responsive presentation. Folder-derived apps, setup, context menus, and in-app docs define extension points. Infrastructure includes development reload, provenance chips, storage, receipts, and HTTP routes, including revision-checked editor writes and host-only remote-access and update families. Library owns importing and staging and visibly reports damaged files without changing them; Workbench owns persistent editors and split panes; Press owns staged export runs with explicit unknown-loss reporting when a target has no coverage declaration. Settings derives Appearance, Studio, Workbench, Remote access, Updates, and About from modules. Shared components centralize color and paint controls. Security distinguishes the primary loopback listener from opt-in remote boundaries while retaining fail-closed parsing, scripts-as-data, and sanitized app marks.

anchors.summary: Kit is a terminal shell: multiline composer, paste cards, a bounded follow-up queue, draft-preserving history and search, interruptible streaming, and a palette that completes command arguments. Right-click pastes text; alt+V, ctrl+G, /image and a text-free ctrl+V all paste a picture, with alt read from both the Kitty protocol and the older ESC-prefix convention. Whether a picture is SENT is the provider declared answer, per spoke, absent meaning no; the caption says which. A path written into a message becomes reachable for that file alone, drawn as a link. Atomic sessions support resume, rewind, fork and export. /rail keeps a preset block list beside the conversation, sized and stepped by its reader, riding in each turn ambient context. /gallery lays card art along the bottom with the rail same keyboard contract; /art and studio_art show one piece. The tool loop replaces model save prose with a revision-checked REVIEW CHANGE gate; a conversion gets REVIEW CROSSING, and a third answer holds a call instead of running or denying it.

UI applications are drop-in folders exporting a HoplightApp manifest and component. Bun discovery skips private underscore folders, bundles apps on demand, puts ordinary apps on the Dock, and keeps catalogOnly tools available through the catalog without a central roster. Apps receive AppContext and may reach engine or filesystem behavior only through its API; the shell owns global navigation, tabs, theme, and status. Visual law comes from one token sheet rather than app-local colors or fixed layout. Bright accents remain marks, borders, and spines; any labeled accent fill uses a generated deep companion with stage-white text. Rose, house accent, deck, and per-piece pairs share tested deepening logic.

First run is assembled from drop-in SetupStep folders, each declaring its question, options, settings key, optional widget and stage treatment, and recap language. The wizard derives order, progress, defaults, skipping, stage zones, and final summary from discovery; pure selection and sentence logic is tested separately. Settings are an open record parsed fail-closed per known key and persisted under the studio directory. Missing setupComplete opens the wizard; completion applies theme and house accent and follows the manifest-selected first landing, while later starts choose the lowest-order app. Theme changes use View Transitions when appropriate, retain an immediate reduced-motion fallback, persist server-side, and use localStorage only for pre-paint. Serialized PATCH operations ensure concurrent control changes merge rather than overwrite stale documents.

One shared context-menu service grows through registration. Surfaces attach typed targets and data to elements, with the deepest matching element winning and a shell-level target always available. Features register any number of item providers for a target type; each provider contributes a section, an empty result denies by absence, and cleanup receives an unregister function. Shell providers currently cover entity actions such as send, show, open beside, split close, and Workbench removal, plus Dock-app and shell navigation actions. A new feature contributes one provider instead of editing a central switch, preserving room-independent behavior for common entity operations.

The Dock's Add app control discovers the manifest-marked catalog instead of naming an id, and the catalog derives cards from the running app roster. catalogOnly tools such as CSS Workshop and Help/Docs remain bundled without occupying everyday Dock space. Help/Docs reads the committed corpus through the generated docs index, which can merge frontmatter, semantic page summaries, retrieval topics, and nested section anchors. Navigation separates user workflows and platforms from developer API, architecture, data, format, security, extension, and decision material; ADR filenames remain canonical while titles are reader-friendly. Markdown uses the shared sanitizer, figures and images are restricted to generated or committed docs assets, the right rail follows current headings, and packaged content matches GitHub. External GitHub viewing passes through the leaving gate and URL allowlist.

Development Studio watches src/ui and broadcasts changes to every open page over the /dev/reload server-sent-event stream. Browser bundles are rebuilt per request, so a save produces fresh code instead of a cached build. Packaged executables serve baked assets, return 404 for the development stream, and let the client become quiet without a separate dependency.

Library summaries derive sourceFormat and sourceVariant from the first non-Hoplight escrow record. Labels come from the live format registry rather than a duplicated UI map: platform-specific adapters show platform and variant, generic Tavern/CC content shows Default, and pieces authored without a source adapter display no chip. The badge therefore describes provenance without inventing one for native drafts.

Canonical Hoplight JSON is the local database: each entity lives at studioDir/kind/id.json as a portable file. Storage never replaces a different piece at the same id; it creates a numbered sibling, enforcing Keep both at persistence. One inventory pass returns healthy summaries and separate bounded records for safe-id JSON files that fail parsing, canonical schema, kind, or id checks. Damaged files are never modified or quarantined.

The server renders one plain-language import receipt for both shells, ensuring terminal and visual users receive the same explanation. It uses recognizable platform names, a we-read/we-kept voice, and emits conditional lines only when engine evidence supports embedded books, scripts-as-data, or privileged warnings. Unknown files receive a warm failure message. Receipt rendering adds presentation, not new detection or format logic.

The HTTP surface serves the shell, token sheet, boot code, discovered app manifests and bundles, and setup-step modules. Settings supports read, replacement, and validated partial merge. Documentation routes expose the generated index, figures, catalog-declared Markdown, and committed assets. Formats, inspect, export, coverage, and Studio routes remain thin engine and storage boundaries. `/api/studio/inventory` returns healthy entities and bounded damaged-file records from one filesystem scan; `/api/studio/list` remains the healthy-only compatibility read. Editor reads can return the complete entity with its revision, and editor saves atomically compare that revision, returning 409 without overwriting newer data. Bundle saves validate the complete canonical batch before any write, then report genuine storage partials honestly. Host-only `/api/remote/*` routes control tunnel and LAN setup, devices, and approvals; `/api/updates/*` routes read release information and perform version switching.

anchors.text: The Library room (the shelves - deep browse)
anchors.summary: Library presents first-run doors when empty and, when populated, live per-kind deck counts, a drop-in proscenium view, portrait-backed covers, drop-anywhere import receipts, and the configured initial deck. It loads healthy summaries and damaged records together through one `/api/studio/inventory` filesystem pass and renders an expandable notice even when no readable pieces remain. The notice names each file and bounded reason, states that Hoplight did not change it, includes the local studio path when available, and offers manual restore-or-remove guidance. Grid, showcase, and list are DeckView modules behind the one browser registry seam; each receives consistent open and staged states. Tapping ordinary pieces toggles a staging set that survives deck switches, then sendMany moves the batch through one follow decision reporting the true newly opened count. Already-open pieces remain annotation-only, while the context menu preserves one-shot Send. A continuous, fail-closed 4-to-36rem art-size control updates CSS live and persists on release. View choice and size live in per-user Library preferences.
topics: drop-in grid showcase and list views

anchors.text: The Workbench room (home by default - the IDE)
anchors.summary: Workbench is the shell-owned tabbed IDE for character, lorebook, persona, preset, regex, and pack entities; editors retain local drafts and save explicitly. Each editor loads a complete-entity revision and saves only against that revision, so an external write leaves the draft dirty and reports a conflict instead of being overwritten. One shared editor-guard hook publishes dirty state, owns Ctrl+S and window-close protection, and routes tab, keyboard, editor-back, and context-menu closes through a shell-owned discard-or-keep dialog. send and sendMany share ask/always/never follow behavior, while create and open-beside gestures navigate directly. Recents combines import and open times, excludes current tabs, caps history, and can collapse. Character editing preserves untouched body fields, persistent prose order, dirty state, and variant semantics shared with Kit operations. Split view supports any two kinds with tested focus, promotion, and close rules. Pane container queries, not viewport queries, drive responsive collapse. Lorebook editing centers one entry with searchable groups, trigger modes, timing, placement, passage, platform-specific cards, fine controls, match testing, and honest token estimates. The shell also persists a marks-only Dock mode.

anchors.text: The Press room (batch export - the staged set prints)
anchors.summary: Press exports only a shell-owned staged queue assembled from Library or its unstaged-piece rail, so queue state survives app switches and the room does not duplicate a studio browser. Characters automatically gather referenced lorebooks from the whole studio; riders may be dropped for one run, and an already staged riding book is not exported twice. Readiness compares characters with the target's live field-coverage claims and identifies lorebook entries that cannot fire, offering editor repair links without manufacturing green status when claims are absent. Export reports preserve that distinction: undeclared coverage is unknown with a null dropped count rather than false zero loss. Each run chooses one grouped platform target, declares filenames, text flavors, and skips before work, reports printed, skipped, or failed outcomes per row, and emits one zip. Delivery history, saved jobs, reorder, byte rehearsal, and readiness dots remain explicitly deferred.

Settings tabs derive from section modules exporting id, label, order, and a component that receives AppContext. The section registry is the sole browser seam, so adding configuration does not require a central tab switch. Controls operate against current persisted settings and immediately repaint visual choices. Shipping sections are Appearance for theme and accent, Studio for home app, initial deck, and publish targets, Workbench for follow behavior, Remote access, now including the optional mesh-helper download, for tunnel and LAN setup, devices, and host controls, Updates for release checks and version switching, and About.

Shared visual controls are extracted once for setup, settings, and future editors. SwatchRow exposes the house palette as quick choices and optionally opens PaintPicker for a custom solid color. ColorPicker provides a branded saturation/value square, hue strip, and hex input while retaining HSV internally to avoid grayscale-state loss. Pure color math normalizes and converts values fail-closed and shares pointer fractions across color and gradient controls. The Paint model is a validated discriminated union for solid, linear, and radial output; gradients require at least two valid stops. PaintPicker composes color editing, stop add/drag/remove, angle adjustment, and curved previews behind allowed-mode gates. Solid accent use is live; tested gradient editing awaits its first entity or pack background consumer.

The primary Studio listener binds loopback. Optional remote listeners are separate, explicitly enabled boundaries with join secrets, device approval, and host-only controls. Uploads use the CLI engine's fail-closed format parsers and archive-expansion limits rather than a permissive UI parser. Scripts stored inside entities remain data throughout Studio workflows. Third-party manifest SVG marks are sanitized before Dock or catalog insertion, removing scripts, foreignObject content, and event handlers.

docs.title: Updates and version rollback
docs.summary: The Updates settings tab, a version timeline built from each release's commit log, and a one-button switch that updates OR rolls back. How the switch works for a source checkout vs an installed build, and the safety rails (refuse a dirty tree, single-flight, restart-outcome marker, refuse a data-losing rollback). Off-network except a button-press GitHub read.
docs.semanticSummary: Developer authority for Settings Updates: a newest-first version timeline from each release commit log and a one-button switch that updates or rolls back. Reads GitHub only when the page opens or a button is pressed; nothing runs on its own. The timeline is read-only and live-proven: fixed GitHub URL releases fetch with cache and ETag, pure version-history parsing from fenced commits blocks only, and compareVersions so bare versions match v-prefixed tags. The switch is built and unit-proven while the full apply path is not yet live-provable: host-only POST validates real release tags single-flight returns 202 with status poll; source checkout refuses dirty tracked trees names files restores prior ref on failure; installed build downloads allowlisted asset verifies SHA256SUMS and stages without auto-swapping the running executable. Restart-outcome marker confirms next boot via pending endpoint. Rollback safety refuses storage-shape schema bumps via classifyDataChange SCHEMA_BUMPS and a storage-shape tripwire hash; studio data folder is never touched by a switch.

anchors.summary: GET /api/updates/releases fetches the repo releases from a fixed GitHub URL with no caller input in host or path so SSRF is out of scope. Five-minute in-memory cache plus ETag prevents burning unauthenticated hourly limits; 403 or 429 answers with try again in N min from server-updates. Pure core version-history.ts parses the payload into the timeline. Commit data comes only from a fenced commits block each release ships emitted by the release workflow as shorthash subject lines; a release without the block renders commit log unavailable never a guess from install-guide prose. Every version comparison goes through compareVersions so the bare running version still matches its v-prefixed tag.

anchors.text: The switch (built + unit-proven; the apply path is not yet live-provable)
anchors.summary: POST /api/updates/switch is host-only refused to remote or LAN devices, validates a real release tag blocking force-shaped values before git argv, refuses current version, starts one switch behind single-flight lock, and returns 202 while the client polls switch-status. Source checkout refuses a dirty tracked tree and names files never stashes work, captures prior ref, checks out the tag, reinstalls, and relaunches; on failure restores prior ref and reinstalls. Installed build downloads the matching asset over https with GitHub-host allowlist on URL and every redirect hop plus size cap, verifies SHA256SUMS, stages and opens the folder, but does not swap the running executable because auto-swap can brick and is deferred. Restart-outcome marker is written before source relaunch so next boot confirms via GET pending which clears on read. Older rollbacks cannot show the popup so confirm becomes the receipt. Guard rails and timeline are live-proven; full apply is unit-tested not yet live-provable until shipped.

A rollback that crosses a release which changed how the studio is stored is refused by classifyDataChange and SCHEMA_BUMPS in switch-decision. SCHEMA_BUMPS is empty today because CANONICAL_SCHEMA_VERSION has never moved so no rollback is refused yet but the guard fails closed the day one lands. A storage-shape tripwire test pins a hash of the files that define on-disk shape so a storage change cannot ship without a deliberate schema bump or SCHEMA_BUMPS entry. The studio folder with pieces settings and keys is never touched by a switch; only the program changes.

docs.title: Roadmap
docs.summary: This roadmap separates code that exists in the repository from work that has passed a release bar. Detailed future designs live under `specs/`; a spec is not evidence that its feature ships.
docs.semanticSummary: Roadmap organized around evidence rather than historical milestone labels: repository code and detailed specs do not count as released behavior until the release bar is met. Current foundation inventories the canonical model and escrow, live format adapters, CLI and Studio import/edit/validation/conversion/export, local storage and editors, sealed script analysis and opt-in benches, and source-preview Kit with providers, staged changes, sessions, content capabilities, and indexed docs retrieval; Kit is run with bun run kit and is absent from current release binaries. Near-term release work covers quiet artifact-level verification, exact public contracts, authenticated and signed release artifacts, and making Kit distributable with complete content lifecycles and real-terminal tests. Product work after the release foundation sequences Script Doctor, Table Read, Test Stage and productions, and Archives and World Forge while preserving canonical storage, staged edits, sealed scripts, citations, and deterministic foundations. Release bars require real public behavior, boundary and regression tests, live installed-flow proof, current reference documentation, and smoke-tested release artifacts before any milestone is called complete.

anchors.summary: The implemented foundation includes a canonical content model with escrowed source data, live format detection and adapters represented by FORMAT-SUPPORT, and import, validation, conversion, and export through both CLI and Studio. Studio provides local storage and the editors documented in the UI reference. Lua and regex payloads remain sealed during normal work and are analyzed or run only in user-invoked benches. Source-preview Kit already includes provider setup, staged mutations, sessions, content capabilities, and indexed documentation retrieval. Exact behavior belongs to the support matrix and CLI/UI references. Kit currently starts from source with bun run kit and is not included in GitHub release binaries.

Near-term work is release engineering rather than a claim that repository features are already product-complete. Make verification complete and quiet by removing OpenTUI warning noise and exercising real Node and packaged artifacts. Make public contracts exact by synchronizing documentation and proving the round-trip fidelity each adapter claims. Make releases reproducible by embedding the sidecar, running the full wall, auditing dependencies, pinning build inputs, authenticating existing checksums, and adding signatures. Finish Kit as a distributable product by packaging it, completing native content lifecycles, retaining staged approval and validation, and testing providers, recovery, docs retrieval, and editing in supported terminals.

children.summary: Verification already discovers tests across src and scripts and lints both React surfaces. Remaining work removes noisy React act warnings from the OpenTUI harness so genuine regressions stand out, then makes Node and packaged-binary smoke checks execute the actual artifacts users receive. The goal is to close the gap between source-tree confidence and release confidence without listing already-shipped gates as future work.
