Architecture, security, CLI, and UI references must move with implementation. Canonical boundary validation and semantic-summary freshness are current foundation rather than future roadmap items. Remaining contract work centers on proving same-format semantic round trips at the fidelity tier each adapter advertises instead of relying on generic tests or broad claims.

Supported release artifacts must contain the remote-access sidecar instead of depending on a checkout. Tagging follows the complete verification wall and a transitive production-dependency audit. Build actions and tools are pinned exactly to prevent moving inputs. Releases already publish checksums; remaining work must authenticate those checksum records and add signatures, giving users verifiable identity and making a release repeatable rather than merely buildable on one maintainer's machine.

children.text: Finish Kit as a distributable product
children.summary: Kit must move from bun run kit in a source checkout to a supported packaged entry point. Native create and edit flows must cover every supported content kind. Mutations must retain composed previews, explicit user approval, revision checks, and deterministic validation. Provider setup and recovery, documentation retrieval, and complete content lifecycles need live testing in real terminals across supported operating systems before distribution is claimed complete.

anchors.text: Product work after the release foundation
anchors.summary: Product expansion follows the release foundation and reuses existing contracts instead of creating parallel systems. Script Doctor starts with deterministic field-cited analysis and keeps model treatments staged. Table Read turns interviews into ordinary canonical edits through the same validation, storage, and history paths as direct editing. Test Stage and productions extend assembly, replay, history, and multi-piece workspaces while leaving imported scripts sealed outside existing benches. Archives and World Forge derive characters and continuity knowledge from large conversation collections, with evidence attached to every derived claim. Their detailed designs live under feature and engine specs, but those specs are not shipping evidence.

children.summary: Script Doctor begins with deterministic content analysis so useful findings do not require a provider. Every finding identifies the affected canonical field. Optional model assistance may propose treatment plans, but edits remain staged for review rather than silently applied. The contracts under specs/features govern the future implementation and must be reconciled with the same validation and mutation paths used elsewhere.

Table Read is an interview-led authoring experience whose output is not a special conversational document. Answers become ordinary canonical edits, then use the same local storage, validation, and history mechanisms as direct Workbench changes. That shared path prevents interview-created characters and lore from drifting into a second content model or bypassing established mutation safeguards.

Test Stage and productions extend prompt assembly, replay, content history, and multi-piece workspace behavior. They must remain extensions of the canonical model rather than introducing production-only entity shapes. Imported Lua, macros, regex, and other executable-looking payloads stay sealed as content throughout those workflows, with execution permitted only through the already isolated, explicitly invoked Lua and regex test benches.

Archives and World Forge target evidence-backed extraction from large conversation histories and continuity work across multiple pieces. Summaries, character facts, lore, and contradiction findings derived from archives must retain citations to the source material that supports them. The citation requirement is part of the product contract, preventing generated continuity claims from becoming unattributed canonical facts.

anchors.summary: A milestone is complete only when behavior exists outside fixtures, boundary and regression coverage plus adjacent tests pass, user-facing flows work live in a real installation, reference pages describe the implementation without substituting future tense, and the actual release artifact passes smoke testing. Repository code, passing unit tests, or a detailed specification is insufficient alone. Historical jewel names and dates remain available through Git history for archaeology, but this roadmap deliberately does not use them as evidence of current status.
